channel.title: Tools on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Tools on Best of AI

item.title: Plimo
item.description:
Plimo puts image and video generation behind one account and one pool of credits. The template gallery is the main way in: each template comes with its prompt and settings filled in, so you mostly just add a photo. Categories include dance, outfit try-on, hairstyles, portraits, anime and cartoon styles, and effects such as a cinematic push-in.

Beyond templates it has the usual tools: text to image, image to image, photo editing, text to video, and image to video where you describe the motion. It runs models from several labs, including Nano Banana, GPT Image, FLUX and Seedream for images, and Kling, Veo, Seedance, Hailuo, Wan and Vidu for video. You can send one prompt to several models and compare the results. It also has its own model, Plimo Image 1.0.

item.title: SceneMixer
item.description: You upload a script or a novel, or have the AI write one, and SceneMixer breaks it into characters, sets, props and episodes. Before it generates any video it makes reference art for each character and location. Every shot is generated against those sheets, so faces, outfits and places should stay consistent from episode to episode. A World Model builds each set first, which keeps the geography the same when the camera cuts.

item.title: 3Shape
item.description:
A clinician scans a patient’s mouth instead of taking physical impressions, and the software builds a 3D model. AI features help with margin detection, automatic design suggestions, and treatment simulation. The Automate and Dental System products support labs.

Hardware and software are sold to practices and labs, with custom pricing.

iTero from Align and Medit are alternatives. 3Shape suits orthodontists and digital dentistry labs.

item.title: AAPC Codify
item.description:
Users search by code or description, see guidelines, and check edits and crosswalks. Subscriptions include updates when code sets change. Coders use it to verify what they assign.

It supports human coders and does not replace coding judgment.

Encoder tools from 3M and Optum are alternatives. AAPC Codify suits medical coders.

item.title: Ableton Live
item.description:
It includes instruments, effects, and MIDI tools, plus Max for Live for building custom devices. Newer versions offer stem separation and other assisted features. Live runs on Windows and macOS.

It is sold in several editions at different prices.

Logic Pro and FL Studio are alternatives. Ableton Live suits music producers who perform or work in loops.

item.title: Action Network
item.description:
Organizers build action pages, collect signatures, and send email to supporters. The platform tracks who took which action, which helps with follow-up. Nonprofits can use it at reduced cost.

It is meant for progressive causes and has simple tools compared with a full campaign CRM.

NationBuilder and Mailchimp overlap in places. Action Network suits campaign managers and community organizers.

item.title: Adalysis
item.description:
Adalysis is a PPC management platform for Google Ads and Microsoft Ads. It audits accounts for wasted spend and missed opportunities, monitors performance, and automates routine optimizations, with the aim of saving specialists time on checks they would otherwise run manually.

For newer campaign types, it offers tools for AI Max and Performance Max, plus smart bidding support. An MCP server lets AI assistants connect to live account data, so you can query your campaigns from an assistant you already use. PPC agencies, brand advertisers, and in-house specialists make up its user base.

item.title: Adobe Animate
item.description:
It supports frame-by-frame animation, tweening, and character rigs, and exports to video, GIF, HTML5 Canvas, and sprite sheets. It integrates with other Adobe apps, so artwork from Illustrator or Photoshop moves in easily.

It was once known for Flash, and the modern product focuses on video and HTML5 output. Animators who want a more traditional workflow sometimes pick Toon Boom Harmony instead.

Adobe sells it by subscription. Moho and Synfig are alternatives. Adobe Animate suits animators who make web and social content.

item.title: Adobe Substance 3D
item.description:
Substance 3D Painter lets artists paint directly on a model with layers, masks, and smart materials that react to the shape underneath. Designer builds procedural materials from node graphs, so one material can produce many variations. Sampler turns photos and scans into tileable materials, and AI features help with that conversion.

Game studios, film teams, and product designers use it to texture assets, then export to engines such as Unreal and Unity or to renderers like Arnold. PBR output is the default, so materials look consistent across tools.

item.title: Aegisub
item.description:
Users load a video, type lines, and set timing with audio waveforms. Styling uses the ASS format, which supports fonts, colors, and positioning. Scripts automate repetitive edits.

The interface is old but dependable, and development is community driven.

Subtitle Edit and Amara are alternatives. Aegisub suits subtitlers who need precise control.

item.title: Afresh
item.description:
The system looks at sales history, shelf life, and promotions and recommends order quantities. Store teams review suggestions on a tablet. Grocers use it to cut spoilage on perishable items.

It is an enterprise service for grocery chains.

Blue Yonder and Relex offer broader retail planning. Afresh suits grocery managers focused on fresh departments.

item.title: Aftershoot
item.description:
It reviews a large set of photos, flags the best frames, and groups duplicates. Users train personal editing profiles, and edits can be sent to Lightroom or Capture One. It also offers retouching and other tools.

It is a subscription product.

Imagen AI and Narrative Select are alternatives. Aftershoot suits photographers with high volume.

item.title: Agisoft Metashape
item.description:
Users load images from cameras or drones, align them, and generate dense geometry and textures. Archaeologists use it to document sites and artifacts, and surveyors use it for mapping. It can classify points and measure volumes.

Standard and professional editions differ in georeferencing and processing features. Good results depend on photo overlap and lighting.

Pix4D and RealityCapture are alternatives. Metashape suits archaeologists, surveyors, and conservators.

item.title: AirDNA
item.description:
AirDNA is a data provider for the short-term rental industry. It collects listing and booking signals from Airbnb, Vrbo, and other platforms and turns them into market metrics such as occupancy, average daily rate, revenue per available rental, seasonality, and supply trends for a chosen area.

Investors use its Investment Explorer to model returns on a property before buying, and hosts use it to benchmark their results against competitors. There is also API access for companies that want the data inside their own products, along with tools for monitoring competitors and checking regulations and demand in a market.

item.title: Aisle Planner
item.description:
Planners create event timelines, track payments, and share floor plans and documents with couples. Templates speed up repeated tasks. A website builder and design tools are included.

It is a subscription product aimed at professionals.

HoneyBook and Zola cover related needs. Aisle Planner suits wedding planners.

item.title: Alation
item.description:
It crawls databases and BI tools, then shows popularity, owners, and lineage. Analysts get search with context, and stewards manage policies. AI agents help document and answer questions about data.

Enterprise pricing applies.

Collibra and Atlan are alternatives. Alation suits data governance managers and analysts.

item.title: AllTrails
item.description:
Users search by location, difficulty, length, or trail type, then read reviews from people who walked it recently. The paid tier adds offline maps, wildfire and weather layers, and printable maps. Guides use it to scout routes and check current conditions before a trip.

Trail data comes partly from community contributions, so details can lag behind closures or washouts. Guides should confirm with land managers for permits and hazards.

Gaia GPS and Komoot are common alternatives. AllTrails suits guides and hikers who want quick route research.

item.title: Anki
item.description:
Users create cards or download shared decks, and the app shows each card just before they would forget it. Add-ons add features, and sync works across devices. The desktop app is free.

The iOS app is paid, and the interface is plain.

Quizlet and RemNote are alternatives. Anki suits students who need long-term retention.

item.title: Annalise.ai
item.description:
Annalise.ai builds radiology AI that looks for many findings at once rather than one condition per algorithm. Its chest X-ray product covers a long list of abnormalities, and its brain CT product targets urgent findings such as bleeds.

Results are shown to the radiologist with the suspicious area marked, and the tool can help prioritize urgent studies in a worklist.

It is sold to hospitals and imaging groups. Output needs radiologist review, and local validation matters. Alternatives include Aidoc, Lunit, Qure.ai, and Gleamer. Annalise.ai suits radiology departments that want broad coverage from one vendor.

item.title: Ansible
item.description:
Playbooks describe the desired state of a machine, and Ansible connects over SSH to apply it. It needs no agent on targets. Roles and a large collection of modules cover most common tasks.

The core is free, and Red Hat sells a platform with a controller and support.

Puppet, Chef, and Terraform serve other needs. Ansible suits sysadmins who manage fleets of servers.

item.title: Ansys
item.description:
Engineers set up a model, apply loads and boundary conditions, and solve to see stress, airflow, heat, or electromagnetic behavior. Machine learning features help speed up some studies. It is common in aerospace, automotive, energy, and electronics.

Licenses are expensive and aimed at companies and universities, and learning the products takes time. Synopsys acquired Ansys, so product branding may change.

Altair, COMSOL, and Siemens Simcenter are alternatives. Ansys suits engineers who need validated simulation for certification or design work.

item.title: AnyLogic
item.description:
Models can use discrete-event, agent-based, or system dynamics methods, alone or combined. Users run experiments, see animations, and analyze results. Java scripting allows custom logic.

A free version exists for learning, and professional licenses are paid.

Simul8 and Arena are alternatives. AnyLogic suits industrial engineers who run simulation studies.

item.title: Apache Airflow
item.description:
Workflows are Python files that define tasks and dependencies. A web interface shows runs, logs, and failures. Hosted versions exist from cloud providers and Astronomer.

Airflow handles orchestration, not the data processing itself. It takes effort to run well at scale.

Prefect and Dagster are newer alternatives. Airflow suits data engineers who orchestrate batch pipelines.

item.title: AppFollow
item.description:
Reviews can be tagged, translated, and routed to the right team. AI-assisted replies and review summaries help with high volume. Its keyword and competitor tracking supports store listing updates.

Subscription pricing depends on app count and features. It connects to tools like Slack and Jira so feedback reaches product teams.

AppTweak and Sensor Tower are alternatives. AppFollow suits app store optimizers and support teams that manage reviews.

item.title: Applied Epic
item.description:
Agents view a client, quote and bind policies, track renewals, and manage documents in one system. Accounting and carrier downloads reduce data entry. Reporting shows book of business and producer results.

It is used by mid-size and large agencies, with custom pricing.

HawkSoft and EZLynx are alternatives. Applied Epic suits insurance agents at larger agencies.

item.title: AppTweak
item.description:
Marketers use it to find keyword ideas, check search volume estimates, and monitor changes in ratings and reviews. AI features suggest metadata and summarize review themes. It covers Apple App Store and Google Play.

Plans are subscription based. Results depend on store algorithms, which change.

AppFollow and Sensor Tower are alternatives. AppTweak suits app store optimizers and growth teams.

item.title: ArborGold
item.description:
Arborists can build quotes from price lists, schedule crews, and send invoices from the field. Mobile apps let crews see jobs and update status. Customer history helps with repeat work and follow-ups.

It is aimed at small and mid-size companies. Features are practical rather than AI heavy.

Jobber and Housecall Pro are broader field service alternatives. ArborGold suits tree care businesses.

item.title: articy:draft
item.description:
Writers lay out flows, write dialogue, and manage characters and locations. Scripts export to Unity and Unreal. Teams can collaborate on the same project.

It is a paid tool for studios.

Twine and Yarn Spinner are lighter alternatives. articy:draft suits narrative designers.

item.title: arXiv
item.description:
Authors upload papers, and readers can search, download, and set up alerts. Cornell University operates it. Most papers in physics and math appear there first.

Papers are not peer reviewed by arXiv itself, so quality varies.

bioRxiv and SSRN serve other fields. arXiv suits physicists and mathematicians.

item.title: Atlan
item.description:
It connects to warehouses, BI tools, and pipelines, and builds a searchable catalog. Users tag assets, request access, and see downstream impact of changes. AI helps write descriptions.

It targets modern data stacks.

Collibra and Alation are alternatives. Atlan suits data governance managers on modern stacks.

item.title: ATLAS.ti
item.description:
It supports document coding, memos, networks, and co-occurrence tables. AI coding and summary features suggest codes and condense text, and researchers can accept or edit them. It runs on desktop and in a browser.

It is used in academic research, UX research, and market research. Licenses are sold in student, academic, and business tiers.

NVivo and MAXQDA are the main alternatives. ATLAS.ti suits researchers who want flexible coding and visual network tools.

item.title: Audacity
item.description:
It records from microphones, edits waveforms, and applies effects such as noise reduction and compression. Plug-ins extend it, and there are AI-based plug-ins for noise and transcription.

It runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. It is destructive in some workflows, so keep copies of originals.

Adobe Audition and Reaper are alternatives. Audacity suits narrators and podcasters who need a free editor.

item.title: AuditBoard
item.description:
Audit teams plan engagements, test controls, and track findings through remediation. SOX teams map controls to risks and gather evidence once for several frameworks. Newer AI features draft summaries and help search policies and past work.

Large and mid-size companies use it as a system of record for assurance work. Implementation takes planning, since control libraries must be set up.

Workiva and Diligent are alternatives. AuditBoard suits internal auditors and compliance teams.

item.title: AutoCAD
item.description:
It supports precise 2D drawings, 3D modeling, and sheet sets. Specialized toolsets add architecture, mechanical, and electrical features. Newer releases add AI-assisted features, such as smart blocks and markup import.

It is a subscription product and a long-standing standard for drawing exchange.

BricsCAD and DraftSight are alternatives. AutoCAD suits civil engineers and drafters.

item.title: Autodesk Civil 3D
item.description:
It builds on AutoCAD and keeps design objects dynamic, so changing an alignment updates profiles and sections. Tools cover surface modeling, pipe networks, and corridor design. It works with Revit and InfraWorks for coordination.

The learning curve is real, and licenses are paid.

Bentley OpenRoads is the main alternative. Civil 3D suits civil engineers and land developers.

item.title: Autodesk Revit
item.description:
Changes made in one view update plans, sections, schedules, and quantities. Teams coordinate architecture, structure, and building systems in a shared model. Dynamo supports scripted automation, and generative design tools can test layout options.

It runs on Windows and has a steep learning curve. Large firms rely on it for coordination.

Archicad and Vectorworks are alternatives. Revit suits architects and engineers who work in BIM.

item.title: Autopsy
item.description:
Examiners add a disk image and run ingest modules that find deleted files, web history, and keyword hits. Timelines and hash databases help organize findings. Plug-ins extend it.

It is used by law enforcement, corporate investigators, and students. Reports must be validated before use in court.

Magnet AXIOM and Cellebrite are commercial alternatives. Autopsy suits forensic scientists with limited budgets.

item.title: Avid Media Composer
item.description:
Editors work with large bin structures, shared storage, and detailed timeline tools. Collaboration features let several editors work on one project. Newer versions add AI-based transcription and script search (PhraseFind and ScriptSync).

It is sold by subscription or as a perpetual license, and a free first version exists with limits. The interface has a longer learning curve than consumer editors.

Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, and Final Cut Pro are alternatives. Media Composer suits film editors working on large productions.

item.title: Axon Draft One
item.description:
The system transcribes the recording and produces a first-person narrative in a standard report format. Officers must check facts, correct errors, and attest to the final report. Some agencies add flags that mark AI-drafted text.

It is sold to agencies, and some jurisdictions and prosecutors have set rules on its use.

Transcription tools such as Truleo and Rev serve related needs. Axon Draft One suits police officers who write many reports.

item.title: Backstage
item.description:
Casting directors search a talent database and review submissions, including self-tapes. Actors apply to open calls and manage profiles. The company also publishes industry advice and resources.

Free and paid tiers exist for talent. Quality of submissions varies.

Casting Networks is the main alternative. Backstage suits casting directors looking for talent.

item.title: BeeHero
item.description:
In-hive sensors track temperature, humidity, vibration, and sound. In-field sensors count bee activity in crops. Data flows through a gateway to an analytics platform that flags weak colonies and helps schedule pollination.

BeeHero works with commercial beekeepers and growers, mainly in crops like almonds and blueberries. Reports of results come from the company, so growers should ask for trial data.

Hobbyists will find it too large in scale. BeeHero suits commercial beekeepers and pollination managers.

item.title: BeerSmith
item.description:
Users build recipes from ingredient databases and see estimates of color, bitterness, and strength. It handles water chemistry, fermentation schedules, and shopping lists. Desktop and mobile versions sync.

It is a paid license.

Brewfather and Brewer’s Friend are alternatives. BeerSmith suits homebrewers and small commercial brewers.

item.title: BioRender
item.description:
Researchers drag icons into a canvas and edit them to build pathways, experimental workflows, and graphical abstracts. Templates speed up common layouts, and teams share a library. Paid plans allow publication use and export options.

Free accounts have limits on exports and icons, so check the license before publishing.

Illustrator and Inkscape give more freedom but take more time. BioRender suits biologists and biochemists.

item.title: BirdNET
item.description:
Users record a bird, and the model suggests species with confidence levels. Researchers analyze long recordings from field recorders. The project comes from the Cornell Lab of Ornithology and Chemnitz University of Technology.

Accuracy depends on recording quality and local species lists.

Merlin Bird ID also identifies birds by sound and photo. BirdNET suits wildlife photographers and biologists.

item.title: BlackLine
item.description:
Controllers use it to match transactions, certify reconciliations, and track close tasks. Rules clear high-volume items automatically. AI features help flag exceptions and estimate close risks.

It is aimed at mid-size and large companies, with custom pricing.

FloQast and Trintech are alternatives. BlackLine suits financial controllers and accounting teams.

item.title: Bloomberg Tax & Accounting
item.description:
Users search the code, regulations, and rulings, and read practice guides. Alerts track law changes. AI tools help summarize documents and answer questions grounded in the platform’s content.

It is priced for firms and corporate tax departments.

Thomson Reuters Checkpoint and CCH are alternatives. Bloomberg Tax suits tax lawyers and professionals.

item.title: Bookshop.org
item.description:
Booksellers can open a storefront on the site, curate lists, and earn a share of sales. Customers shop from the full catalog and the store receives a share. The platform handles fulfillment.

It is an alternative to selling through large online retailers. Store owners still need their own marketing.

Shopify stores and Ingram services are other options. Bookshop.org suits independent bookstore owners.

item.title: Brainomix
item.description:
Brainomix is a UK imaging AI company. Its stroke products assess non-contrast CT and angiography scans and give clinicians scores and maps that support treatment decisions.

It also offers lung software that analyzes chest CT for fibrosis, helping track disease over time.

Brainomix is sold to hospitals and health systems. Regulatory status varies by region, so check what is cleared where you work. Alternatives include RapidAI, Viz.ai, and Aidoc. Brainomix suits stroke services and respiratory clinics.

item.title: Brewfather
item.description:
It calculates color, bitterness, and alcohol, scales recipes to equipment, and logs fermentation readings. Integrations with smart hydrometers record gravity automatically. Paid tiers add features like more batches and sharing.

It is built for small-scale brewing rather than large breweries.

BeerSmith and Brewer’s Friend are alternatives. Brewfather suits homebrewers and nano breweries.

item.title: Brisk Teaching
item.description:
Teachers can generate lesson materials, adjust reading levels, and draft feedback on student writing. A student-facing feature lets pupils chat with an AI tutor under teacher guidance. It also supports quizzes.

A free plan covers basic features, and paid plans add more. Teachers should check output before using it with students.

MagicSchool and Diffit are alternatives. Brisk Teaching suits educators who work in Google Workspace.

item.title: Burp Suite
item.description:
A proxy sits between the browser and the site, so testers can inspect and change requests. Scanner, repeater, and intruder tools probe for issues such as injection and broken access control. Extensions add features, including AI-assisted ones.

A free community edition covers manual testing, while the professional and enterprise editions add automation.

OWASP ZAP is a free alternative. Burp Suite suits security analysts who test web apps.

item.title: Calligraphr
item.description:
Users print a template, write letters by hand, scan it, and upload. Calligraphr builds a font file with options for alternate letters and ligatures so text looks less repetitive. Paid plans allow more characters and variations.

Results depend on the quality of the scan and consistency of the writing. It suits casual script styles more than formal calligraphy.

Fontself and Glyphs are more advanced font tools. Calligraphr suits lettering artists who want a quick font.

item.title: CalTopo
item.description:
Users draw routes, add waypoints, and view layers such as slope angle shading and forecast data. Teams can share a live map during an operation. Maps print to scale, and the mobile app supports offline use.

A free tier covers basic planning, and paid tiers add advanced layers, printing, and team features. The interface is dense, and new users usually need a short tutorial.

Gaia GPS and AllTrails are alternatives with friendlier interfaces. CalTopo suits guides, avalanche professionals, and rescue teams.

item.title: Candid
item.description:
Users search funders by location, cause, and giving history, and see past grants and contacts. A free version offers limited searches, and paid plans give full access. Candid also runs GuideStar profiles of nonprofits.

Data comes from tax filings and funder reports, so recent changes may not show.

Instrumentl is a grant discovery alternative with tracking features. Candid suits grant writers who research funders.

item.title: Carta
item.description:
Founders issue options, model funding rounds, and share ownership with employees. Investors and funds use related products for reporting. The platform handles compliance paperwork.

Pricing grows with company size and features.

Pulley and Ledgy are alternatives. Carta suits startup founders raising capital.

item.title: CAS SciFinder
item.description:
Users search by structure, reaction, or keyword and see papers, patents, and suppliers. Retrosynthesis tools suggest routes to a target molecule. Results link to the CAS registry.

Access is by subscription, usually through institutions.

Reaxys is the main alternative. SciFinder suits chemists doing literature and synthesis research.

item.title: CaseWare
item.description:
Auditors use CaseWare Working Papers to plan engagements, document procedures, and tie financial statement balances to supporting files. CaseWare IDEA imports full data sets and tests them for gaps, duplicates, and unusual entries, which supports analysis beyond sampling.

Cloud versions let teams review work remotely. Firms of all sizes use the products, and staff generally need training before they are productive.

AuditBoard and Workiva cover related ground for internal audit and reporting. CaseWare suits external auditors and accountants.

item.title: Casting Networks
item.description:
Casting directors post breakdowns, filter submissions, and organize talent into lists. Self-tapes can be reviewed online and shared with producers. Scheduling tools help with callbacks.

Actors pay for profiles and submissions, which has drawn criticism. The directory covers the US and some other markets.

Backstage is another casting marketplace. Casting Networks suits casting directors and agents.

item.title: CCC Intelligent Solutions
item.description:
Photos from a claim are analyzed by AI to estimate damage and repair cost. Adjusters review the estimate, assign repairs, and track progress. Repair shops use the same system to submit estimates and supplements.

It is an enterprise platform with business pricing.

Mitchell and Tractable provide related estimating or AI tools. CCC suits auto claims adjusters.

item.title: CellarTracker
item.description:
Users add bottles to a virtual cellar, track what to drink when, and see aggregated notes from other members. Sommeliers use the community notes to judge how a wine is aging.

The service is free with optional paid features, and notes are user submitted.

Vivino has a larger casual user base. CellarTracker suits sommeliers and serious collectors.

item.title: CephX
item.description:
CephX automates cephalometric tracing. An orthodontist uploads a lateral ceph image, the AI places the landmarks, and a full set of measurements comes back within seconds instead of the manual tracing time.

It includes many standard analyses, so a practice can pick the one it already uses. For 3D work, it can build a 2D cephalometric view from CBCT scans and includes airway analysis.

CephX is a paid service. Landmark placement still needs a clinician’s review, and the accuracy claims come mostly from the vendor. Alternatives include Owandy Ceph Analysis, Invivo, and Diagnocat. CephX suits orthodontic practices that want faster, more consistent ceph analysis.

item.title: ChemDraw
item.description:
Users draw structures, predict properties like NMR shifts, and name compounds from drawings. It integrates with Revvity Signals tools and Microsoft Office. A web version supports sharing.

Licenses are paid, and many universities provide them.

MarvinSketch and Ketcher are alternatives. ChemDraw suits synthetic and medicinal chemists.

item.title: ChiroTouch
item.description:
Chiropractors record visits with templates and complete insurance billing in the same system. Reminders and patient portals cut no-shows. Reporting shows visit counts and collections.

It is built specifically for chiropractic, which means less flexibility for other clinics.

Jane and ChiroSpring are alternatives. ChiroTouch suits chiropractors.

item.title: Cision
item.description:
Communications teams search for reporters by beat, build lists, and send pitches. Monitoring tracks mentions across news, broadcast, and social media, and AI helps summarize coverage and sentiment. Reports show reach and tone.

It is priced for organizations, and contracts are often annual. Contact data can go stale, so teams still verify key names.

Muck Rack and Meltwater are close alternatives. Cision suits communications specialists and crisis managers.

item.title: ClinVar
item.description:
Users search by gene or variant and see classifications such as pathogenic or benign, plus the evidence and submitter. Entries show review status, so counselors can judge confidence.

Classifications can conflict between labs and change over time.

gnomAD and OMIM are related resources. ClinVar suits genetic counselors.

item.title: Clip Studio Paint
item.description:
It includes pen brushes with pressure control, panel layout tools, tone effects, and 3D poseable models for reference. Artists can export to print and web formats. It runs on desktop, tablet, and phone.

It is sold as a one-time purchase or subscription, depending on the edition.

Procreate and Photoshop are alternatives. Clip Studio Paint suits graphic novelists and illustrators who draw comics.

item.title: CodeSignal
item.description:
Candidates take timed tests in a browser editor. Recruiters see results and replay sessions. Interview tools and an AI assistant help run structured loops.

It is sold to employers by plan, and candidates can practice for free.

HackerRank and CoderPad are alternatives. CodeSignal suits technical recruiters.

item.title: Collibra
item.description:
Stewards assign owners to data sets, document definitions, and set approval workflows. Users search the catalog to find trusted data. AI features help with classification and documentation.

It targets large enterprises with custom pricing and needs organizational buy-in.

Alation and Atlan are alternatives. Collibra suits data governance managers.

item.title: CommCare
item.description:
Program teams design forms and workflows without coding. Workers collect data offline on a phone and sync when connected. Supervisors see dashboards, and case management supports reminders for visits.

A free plan is available for small projects, and paid plans add more users and features.

KoBoToolbox and ODK are open-source options for data collection. CommCare suits community health workers and the programs that manage them.

item.title: COMSOL Multiphysics
item.description:
Users define geometry, add physics, and solve. Modules cover chemical reactions, batteries, fluid flow, and acoustics. Surrogate models can speed up repeated studies.

Licenses are costly, and the learning curve is steep for new users.

Ansys is the main alternative. COMSOL suits chemical and process engineers who need coupled models.

item.title: Corsearch
item.description:
Attorneys run searches across registers, common law sources, and domain names to assess conflicts before filing. Watching alerts them to similar new filings. Brand protection tools find counterfeits and abuse.

It is a professional service with custom pricing.

Clarivate and Questel offer related services. Corsearch suits trademark attorneys.

item.title: CoStar
item.description:
Brokers, appraisers, and investors use it to look up buildings, find comparable sales, and see rents and vacancy trends. It also owns listing sites such as Apartments.com and LoopNet. Coverage is deepest in the US and parts of Europe.

Subscriptions are costly and aimed at professionals. Data quality depends on research teams and submissions, so appraisers still verify key facts.

Reonomy and Cotality are other data sources. CoStar suits appraisers and commercial brokers.

item.title: Covidence
item.description:
Two reviewers screen independently, and conflicts are resolved in the tool. It supports risk-of-bias assessment and data extraction forms. It records PRISMA-style counts as the review proceeds.

It is subscription-based, and many universities hold licenses.

Rayyan is an alternative. Covidence suits clinical researchers running systematic reviews.

item.title: Credo AI
item.description:
Teams register AI use cases, run assessments, and collect evidence for reviews and audits. Policy packs translate regulations into checks that product and legal teams can follow. Reports give leaders a record of what was reviewed and approved.

It suits organizations with several AI projects and formal oversight needs. Setup takes effort, since the value depends on teams actually logging their systems.

OneTrust and Securiti offer broader privacy and governance suites. Credo AI suits ethicists, risk teams, and compliance leads.

item.title: CSI ETABS
item.description:
Engineers build a building model, apply loads, and run analysis. The program checks members against design codes and produces reports. It links with Revit and other BIM tools.

It is a licensed product with a steep learning curve.

STAAD.Pro and Robot are alternatives. ETABS suits structural engineers designing buildings.

item.title: cubic
item.description:
cubic is an AI code reviewer that looks beyond the diff. It reads the wider codebase to judge whether a change is likely to cause problems, and it leaves inline comments on the pull request. A merge confidence score from one to five gives reviewers a quick signal about how much attention a change needs.

Other features reduce review load. Low-risk pull requests can be auto-approved, nightly scans look for bugs across the repository, and reviews can run from the terminal before you push. Teams use it to cut the queue of pull requests waiting for a human.

item.title: D5 Render
item.description:
It uses real-time ray tracing, so designers can adjust lighting and materials and see results at once. A library of models and materials is included, and AI tools help with texture generation and scene edits. It exports stills, video, and panoramas.

A free tier exists, with paid plans for more features. It requires a capable graphics card.

Enscape and Twinmotion are alternatives. D5 Render suits architects and visualization artists.

item.title: Dagster
item.description:
Developers define assets in Python and Dagster tracks lineage and freshness. A UI shows runs and dependencies, and tests run locally. Dagster Cloud offers a hosted service.

The open-source core is free. It differs from Airflow in structure, so teams moving over need to adjust.

Airflow and Prefect are alternatives. Dagster suits data engineers who want asset-based pipelines.

item.title: Datarails
item.description:
Datarails is aimed at finance teams that live in Excel and do not want to leave it. The platform consolidates data from hundreds of sources into a single governed layer, then lets analysts keep working in the spreadsheets they already know while the numbers update underneath.

Its modules cover FP&A, month-end close, cash management, and spend control, with audit trails and permissions so changes can be traced. A ticketing feature handles internal requests to the finance team. The AI Connector links the consolidated data to AI tools, so a CFO or controller can ask questions in plain language and get answers drawn from the company’s own figures.

item.title: DataSnipper
item.description:
DataSnipper started as an Excel add-in for auditors and has grown into an agent-based platform for audit and finance work. Its agents run standard procedures, including tests of details, controls testing, and financial statement checks, and a person reviews each result before signing off.

Evidence stays traceable. The work happens in Excel, with connectors to other systems, and each conclusion links back to the source document it came from. That matters for audit files, where a reviewer needs to see where a number originated, not only the number itself.

item.title: DBeaver
item.description:
Administrators and developers browse schemas, run queries, and export data from one interface. The paid editions add features such as visual query building and AI assistance.

The community edition is free and open source.

DataGrip and TablePlus are alternatives. DBeaver suits database administrators who work across systems.

item.title: Dentrix
item.description:
Hygienists and dentists chart exams, record perio measurements, and manage recall lists. The system connects to imaging and third-party AI tools. Reports track production and collections.

It is widely used in dental offices, and licensing varies.

Eaglesoft and Open Dental are alternatives. Dentrix suits dentists and dental hygienists.

item.title: Deque axe
item.description:
The free axe DevTools browser extension runs on a page and lists issues with the offending element and a suggested fix. The same engine, axe-core, plugs into test frameworks like Cypress, Playwright, and Jest, so teams can catch regressions in continuous integration. Deque’s paid products add guided manual testing and reporting.

Automated checks find only part of all accessibility problems, since things like reading order and meaningful link text need a person. Auditors usually run axe first and then test with a screen reader and keyboard.

item.title: Dext
item.description:
Clients photograph a receipt or forward an invoice by email, and Dext reads the supplier, date, amount, and tax. The extracted data syncs to platforms such as Xero, QuickBooks, and Sage, where it becomes a draft transaction ready for review. It can also fetch supplier bills automatically.

Practices use it to collect documents from many clients in one place and spend less time keying numbers. Extraction is good but not perfect, so someone still checks unusual or poorly scanned documents.

item.title: Diagnocat
item.description:
Diagnocat analyzes dental imaging. A clinician uploads a CBCT scan, panoramic radiograph, or intraoral X-rays, and the AI segments the teeth and bone and flags issues in a report organized by tooth.

For orthodontics, the 3D view helps with impacted teeth, root position, and airway or bone assessment, and the reports can be shared with patients or referring dentists.

Diagnocat is a paid service. Findings are decision support, so the dentist has to confirm them. Alternatives include Overjet, Pearl, and VideaHealth. Diagnocat suits practices that use CBCT regularly.

item.title: Diffit
item.description:
Teachers paste in a source and choose a grade level. Diffit produces a summary, vocabulary list, and questions. Resources can be exported to Google Docs and Slides.

The free plan has limits, and paid plans remove them.

MagicSchool and Brisk Teaching offer broader teacher tools. Diffit suits educators who differentiate reading materials.

item.title: Digitail
item.description:
Clinics use online booking, telehealth, and an app for clients. AI features help create clinical notes from visit conversations. Reports show performance.

It is subscription based.

ezyVet and Shepherd are alternatives. Digitail suits veterinarians at independent clinics.

item.title: Discord
item.description:
Community managers set roles, channels, and rules, and use bots for moderation and welcome messages. Voice channels and events support live sessions. AutoMod features filter spam and harmful content.

Free to use, with optional paid subscriptions. It works best for real-time chat, and information can get buried.

Slack and Circle are alternatives. Discord suits community managers running active chat communities.

item.title: Dolphin Imaging
item.description:
Clinicians trace cephalometric landmarks, plan surgeries, and simulate outcomes. Patient photos and 3D scans are stored in one place. Some tracing steps can be done with AI assistance.

It is a licensed product for practices.

CephX and Ortho2 are related options. Dolphin Imaging suits orthodontists.

item.title: DoorLoop
item.description:
DoorLoop puts the main landlord workflows in one platform: accounting, leasing, maintenance, rent collection, and communication with tenants and owners. It is used by landlords, property managers, and real estate investors with growing portfolios.

AI is built in as an assistant and as agents for specific jobs, including a receptionist, maintenance coordination, lease renewals, rent collection, and leasing. You set approvals so the agents act within limits you control. AI inspections help document the condition of units.

item.title: Dragonframe
item.description:
Animators see live view, onion skinning, and timing exposure sheets while shooting. It controls DSLR cameras and DMX lighting and supports motion control rigs for camera moves. Captured frames can be reviewed and exported as video.

It runs on Mac, Windows, and Linux and is sold as a license. Independent animators and schools often use it.

Stop Motion Studio is a simpler, lower-cost option. Dragonframe suits animators who need precise capture and timing.

item.title: Drake Tax
item.description:
Preparers enter data, run diagnostics, and e-file federal and state returns. Features include document management and client portals. It is known for good value and support.

It is licensed per firm, and is aimed at professionals rather than consumers.

Intuit Lacerte and UltraTax are alternatives. Drake Tax suits tax professionals at smaller firms.

item.title: Duetto
item.description:
Revenue managers see demand forecasts and recommended prices, and adjust rules for channels and customers. Reports compare pace and competitors. The platform considers total guest spending, not only rooms.

It is sold to hotel groups with custom pricing.

IDeaS and Atomize are alternatives. Duetto suits hotel revenue managers.

item.title: Dungeon Alchemist
item.description:
Users sketch a floor plan, and the software adds furniture, lighting, and details that fit the room type. Maps export to virtual tabletops like Roll20 and Foundry. 3D views help with visualization.

It is a paid program.

Inkarnate and Wonderdraft are other map tools. Dungeon Alchemist suits game masters prepping scenes.

item.title: Duotrope
item.description:
Writers search by genre, length, pay rate, and reading period. They log each submission and see response times from other users. Listings include submission guidelines and acceptance statistics.

It is a paid subscription with a trial. Statistics come from user reports, so they are estimates.

Submittable and Chills are related tools. Duotrope suits poets who submit work widely.

item.title: eBay
item.description:
Sellers use it to list antiques, collectibles, parts, and general goods. Seller tools include AI-assisted listing creation from photos and promoted listings. Completed sales are searchable, which helps with pricing.

Fees apply to sales, and rules differ by category. Resellers often use its sold listings as a quick price guide before buying stock.

Etsy, Shopify stores, and Facebook Marketplace are other ways to sell. eBay suits dealers, resellers, and anyone selling second-hand goods.

item.title: ECMWF
item.description:
Meteorologists use ECMWF forecast charts and open data to compare with other models. The centre also publishes the ERA5 reanalysis, a long record of past weather used in climate research. Its AI forecasting system adds machine learning models alongside traditional physics.

Some data is open and some is available to member states or by license.

NOAA GFS is another global model. ECMWF suits meteorologists who compare model output.

item.title: ElliQ
item.description:
ElliQ is a physical device, not an app. It sits on a table and talks with the person using it. Older adults can chat with it, ask for music and news, play games, do light exercise, and get reminders for medications and appointments. Family members can send photos that ElliQ displays.

The caregiver side matters for families. Caregivers receive alerts and can see how the person is doing, which gives some reassurance when they live far away. The product is meant to reduce loneliness and encourage routines, not to replace human contact or medical care.

item.title: ELSA Speak
item.description:
ELSA Speak is focused on spoken English. You speak into the app, and it analyzes your pronunciation and tells you which sounds need work. A personalized learning path sets lessons based on where you struggle, and progress tracking shows improvement over time.

Newer features add conversation practice. A bilingual AI tutor can explain mistakes in your own language, and role-play scenarios let you rehearse situations such as interviews or meetings. Learners include professionals, job seekers, students, and travelers, and there are versions for companies and schools.

item.title: Enscape
item.description:
Architects click a button and walk through their model with lighting, materials, and entourage in a live window. Changes in the CAD program appear in Enscape right away. It can export images, videos, and VR views.

It is sold by Chaos. The quality is good for design review, but final marketing images sometimes use dedicated renderers.

D5 Render and Twinmotion are alternatives. Enscape suits architects who want quick visualization inside their modeling program.

item.title: Epic
item.description:
Clinicians chart, order tests, and review results in one system. Patients use MyChart to see records and book visits. Epic has added generative AI features for drafting messages and notes.

Implementations are large projects run by health systems, and individuals cannot buy it directly.

Oracle Health and MEDITECH are alternatives. Epic suits health informaticists and hospital administrators.

item.title: Eventbrite
item.description:
Planners create event pages, sell tickets, and check in guests with a mobile app. Marketing tools send emails and promote events. AI helps write descriptions and event details.

Fees apply per ticket, and free events have a simpler plan.

Cvent suits large corporate events. Eventbrite suits event planners running public events.

item.title: ezyVet
item.description:
Vets write clinical notes, order lab tests, and send reminders to pet owners. Staff manage appointments and invoices in the same system. Reports track revenue and procedures.

It is a subscription product from IDEXX.

Digitail and Cornerstone are alternatives. ezyVet suits veterinarians at multi-site practices.

item.title: Felt
item.description:
Users import GIS files and spreadsheets, draw on the map, and add comments. Maps share by link and embed in websites. AI features can help style layers and transform data from a plain-language request.

It is lighter than desktop GIS and lacks some advanced analysis. A free plan has limits.

QGIS and ArcGIS offer deeper analysis. Felt suits planners and cartographers who share maps with non-specialists.

item.title: FFmpeg
item.description:
Broadcast engineers and developers use it to transcode feeds, create proxies, and automate batch tasks. Many video apps use it behind the scenes. Recent versions can run Whisper-based transcription.

It runs from the command line, so there is a learning curve.

HandBrake offers a simpler interface for conversion. FFmpeg suits engineers who automate media workflows.

item.title: Fiix
item.description:
Fiix is maintenance management software used in manufacturing, oil and gas, food and beverage, and heavy equipment. Teams use it to schedule preventive maintenance, create and track work orders, manage assets and spare parts, and see where downtime comes from. It is a product of Rockwell Automation.

The AI features include Fiix MAX, an assistant for maintenance questions and tasks, plus work order insights, asset alerts, and a parts forecaster. These aim to help technicians find problems earlier and keep the right parts on hand. Mobile access lets technicians update work orders in the field.

item.title: Final Draft
item.description:
It handles scene headings, dialogue, and page counts automatically. Writers can use outlining tools, revisions, and collaboration features. Scripts export to PDF and common production formats.

It is a paid program, and its AI features are limited. Some writers prefer Fade In or Highland.

Fade In and WriterDuet are alternatives. Final Draft suits filmmakers and writers who need standard format.

item.title: Final Round AI
item.description:
Final Round AI covers interview preparation from practice to the real thing. You can run AI practice interviews, set goals, and get automatic debriefs that point out where your answers were weak. The prep side is useful on its own, even if you never use the live features.

The headline product is Interview Copilot, a desktop app for macOS and Windows. During a live interview it listens and suggests answers privately, and Screen Help reads questions from your screen. A stealth mode hides its windows from screen sharing. Some employers treat live AI help as cheating, so read the rules of the interview before using it.

item.title: Findmypast
item.description:
Users search census, parish, and military records, and view images of the original documents. Family trees are shared and linked to records. Hints suggest matches.

It is a subscription service.

Ancestry and MyHeritage are alternatives. Findmypast suits genealogists with British and Irish ancestry.

item.title: FL Studio
item.description:
The pattern-based step sequencer and piano roll make it quick to sketch ideas. It comes with synths, samplers, and effects, and includes stem separation. Image-Line has a lifetime free updates policy.

Editions differ by feature set and price.

Ableton Live and Logic Pro are alternatives. FL Studio suits producers who start from beats.

item.title: Flair AI
item.description:
Flair AI replaces much of a product photo shoot. You upload a product image, place it on a 3D canvas, and describe or choose the scene around it. The tool produces styled images that look like they were shot in a studio or on location, and it can place products on AI-generated human models for on-model shots.

Beyond stills, it makes product videos and ad creative. Templates let you reuse a scene across a whole catalog, a brand asset library keeps colors and logos consistent, and team collaboration features let several people work in one workspace. An API is available for stores that want to generate images programmatically.

item.title: FlightAware
item.description:
Free users can check flight status and history. Business products include APIs for flight data and tools that help operators with planning and alerts. Its data combines radar feeds, satellite data, and ground receivers.

Operations staff use it to monitor delays and trace aircraft. Like other public trackers, it is informational and not a substitute for official air traffic systems.

Flightradar24 is the main alternative. FlightAware suits dispatchers, operators, and developers who need flight data.

item.title: Flightradar24
item.description:
Each aircraft shows altitude, speed, and registration details where available. Subscriptions add longer flight history, weather overlays, and extra data. The site also covers airports with arrival and departure boards.

Aviation professionals use it to follow traffic and verify flight status, though coverage varies by region and it is not an official air traffic source.

FlightAware is the main alternative. Flightradar24 suits controllers, dispatchers, and aviation fans who want a quick traffic picture.

item.title: Floranext
item.description:
Designers take phone and web orders, print tickets, and schedule deliveries. Customer records track occasions for reminders. Online stores are built into the system.

It is a subscription product for flower shops.

Lightspeed and Shopify can work with extra setup. Floranext suits floral designers who run a shop.

item.title: Foundry Virtual Tabletop
item.description:
It offers dynamic lighting, scripting, and a large library of community modules and system packs. It is bought once, rather than by subscription, and runs on a PC or server.

It takes more setup than browser-based tabletops.

Roll20 is a hosted alternative. Foundry VTT suits game masters who want customization.

item.title: Frame.io
item.description:
Reviewers comment directly on frames, and comments appear in Premiere Pro and other editors. Camera-to-cloud features upload footage from set. Version stacking keeps cuts organized.

A free plan exists, with paid plans for storage and teams.

Vimeo Review and Wipster are alternatives. Frame.io suits videographers who need client approval.

item.title: Fresha
item.description:
Salons manage calendars, take payments, and send reminders. Clients find and book services on a marketplace. Reports track sales and staff performance.

The software is free to start, with fees on payments and some features.

Vagaro and StyleSeat are alternatives. Fresha suits cosmetologists and salon owners.

item.title: Frontify
item.description:
Brand managers publish guidelines online and share approved assets. Templates let non-designers create on-brand materials. AI features help tag assets and search the library.

It is aimed at mid-size and larger companies, with custom pricing.

Brandfolder and Bynder are alternatives. Frontify suits brand managers who need consistency across teams.

item.title: Gaia GPS
item.description:
Users record tracks, plan routes, and layer maps such as satellite imagery, slope angle, and weather. The paid plans include more map sources and offline use. It runs on phones and in a browser, and routes sync between them.

Outdoor guides, hunters, and search and rescue volunteers use it to plan trips and share routes. A phone battery is still a risk, so many users carry a backup map or battery pack.

item.title: GeoGebra
item.description:
Users draw geometric objects, define functions, and drag points to see relationships change. It includes graphing, spreadsheet, and 3D tools. A large library of shared activities covers school topics.

It runs in a browser and on phones and tablets.

Desmos is a close alternative for graphing. GeoGebra suits mathematicians and teachers who explore ideas visually.

item.title: GitHub Actions
item.description:
Workflows are YAML files that call reusable actions from a marketplace. Hosted runners run on Linux, Windows, and macOS, or teams can run their own. Secrets and environments control deployments.

Public repositories use it free, and private ones get a free allowance with paid usage after.

GitLab CI and CircleCI are alternatives. GitHub Actions suits DevOps engineers on GitHub.

item.title: Gleamer
item.description:
Gleamer is a French radiology AI company known for tools that find fractures on X-rays and for a chest X-ray product. Findings appear as marked overlays inside the radiologist’s viewer.

Its products are grouped in a suite for emergency and routine imaging, and the company has expanded toward other modalities such as MRI.

Gleamer is sold to hospitals and imaging centers. Overlays are an aid, not a diagnosis. Alternatives include Annalise.ai, Qure.ai, Lunit, and Aidoc. Gleamer suits emergency and musculoskeletal imaging workflows.

item.title: Global Fishing Watch
item.description:
Users see vessel tracks, fishing effort, and protected areas. Fishery managers and enforcement agencies use it to check activity near marine reserves and to spot suspicious behavior. Data downloads and an API support research.

Coverage depends on vessels broadcasting their position, so some boats are invisible.

Windward and Spire provide commercial maritime data. Global Fishing Watch suits fishery managers and conservation scientists.

item.title: Goalbook
item.description:
Teachers pick learning targets, choose research-based strategies, and build goals aligned to standards. Teams use shared planning tools to track progress. Some AI features help draft IEP language.

Schools and districts license it. Teachers should check AI-drafted language against the student’s data.

Frontline and SpEd Forms are IEP software alternatives. Goalbook suits special education teachers.

item.title: Godot
item.description:
It uses a scene and node system and its own scripting language, GDScript, and also supports C#. There are no licensing fees or royalties. The community adds plug-ins and tutorials.

It has fewer built-in features for large 3D projects than Unreal.

Unity and Unreal Engine are alternatives. Godot suits indie game developers who want open source.

item.title: Goodreads
item.description:
Users shelve books as read, reading, or want to read, and follow friends. Bookstores and authors use it to see which titles readers talk about. Its data is a handy signal for what is popular.

Amazon owns it, and the interface has changed little in years.

StoryGraph is an alternative. Goodreads suits bookstore owners and readers.

item.title: Google Analytics
item.description:
GA4 uses an event-based model and offers reports for acquisition, engagement, and revenue. It links with Google Ads and BigQuery. Machine learning predicts audiences and flags anomalies.

The standard version is free, and the 360 version is paid. Privacy rules affect what data can be collected in some regions.

Plausible, PostHog, and Matomo are alternatives. Google Analytics suits marketing analysts who need a common baseline.

item.title: Google Classroom
item.description:
Teachers create classes, share materials from Drive, and grade submissions. Students see due dates and turn in work. Gemini features help teachers draft lesson plans and quiz questions in education plans.

It is free for Google Workspace for Education accounts and works well with Docs and Meet.

Canvas and Schoology are fuller learning management systems. Google Classroom suits educators who already use Google tools.

item.title: Google Earth Engine
item.description:
It hosts decades of satellite and climate datasets, such as Landsat and Sentinel. Users write scripts in JavaScript or Python to compute change over time, such as forest loss or sea ice. Results export to maps and tables.

It is free for research and education, with commercial plans for business use.

QGIS and ArcGIS work with local data. Earth Engine suits climate scientists and geospatial analysts.

item.title: Gradescope
item.description:
Students submit scans or online work. Graders mark answers by clicking rubric items, and changing a rubric item updates every submission that used it. AI-assisted grouping clusters similar answers so one grading decision can apply to many students. Code assignments can be autograded.

It is common in university STEM courses with large enrollments. Regrade requests and grading analytics are built in, and it connects to most learning management systems.

Institutions pay for access. Canvas SpeedGrader and Crowdmark are alternatives. Gradescope suits instructors and teaching assistants who grade many similar assignments.

item.title: GraphPad Prism
item.description:
Users enter data in tables, choose analyses such as t-tests, ANOVA, survival curves, or nonlinear regression, and get publication-style graphs. It guides non-statisticians with explanations of results. Dose-response and kinetics fitting are common uses.

It is a paid license, often provided through universities. It is less flexible than R or Python for custom work.

R, Python, and JMP are alternatives. Prism suits bench scientists who want a quick path from data to figure.

item.title: HackerRank
item.description:
Recruiters build tests from a question library and review code, scores, and plagiarism checks. Live interviews share a code editor. Developers use the free practice site to prepare.

Hiring plans are paid, and test results are one signal among others.

CodeSignal and CoderPad are alternatives. HackerRank suits technical recruiters.

item.title: HawkSoft
item.description:
Agents keep policy data, notes, and documents together and automate renewal reminders. A phone integration pops up client records during calls. Reports help with retention and cross-selling.

It is a subscription product.

Applied Epic and EZLynx are alternatives. HawkSoft suits insurance agents at smaller agencies.

item.title: HeartFlow
item.description:
HeartFlow analyzes coronary CT angiography. Its software builds a 3D model of the heart arteries and estimates how blocked vessels affect blood flow, and a plaque analysis service quantifies buildup.

The goal is to give cardiologists more information from a noninvasive scan so fewer patients need invasive angiography.

It is a paid clinical service, typically ordered through hospitals. Alternatives include Cleerly and Tempus’s cardiac tools. HeartFlow suits cardiology teams that already use cardiac CT.

item.title: Hebbia
item.description:
Hebbia is built for work where the answer sits in hundreds of documents. Investors, bankers, lawyers, and consultants use it to extract and compare information across filings, contracts, and financial data, instead of reading each file by hand.

Matrix lays out analysis in a grid, with documents or companies in rows and questions in columns, so you can run the same questions over many sources at once. It works with sources such as SEC filings and FactSet. Max is a deal-team assistant that acts as an AI analyst and supports collaboration across a firm.

item.title: HEC-RAS
item.description:
Users build a terrain model, define channels and structures, and simulate steady or unsteady flow. Results include water surface profiles, inundation maps, and sediment transport. It works with GIS data.

The interface is technical and expects hydraulic knowledge.

MIKE and TUFLOW are commercial alternatives. HEC-RAS suits hydrologists and civil engineers.

item.title: Helium 10
item.description:
Helium 10 is one of the best known tools for people who sell on Amazon. It also supports Walmart and TikTok Shop. The suite covers product research, keyword research, listing optimization, advertising, and inventory, so a seller can run most of the day-to-day work from one account.

The AI layer includes Helium Agent, an assistant that completes tasks inside your dashboard, and Listing Builder, which generates product listings from your inputs. Helium MCP connects Helium 10 data to assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT, so you can ask questions about your catalog and market from the chat window you already use.

item.title: Hemlane
item.description:
Hemlane mixes software with people. Owners and property managers use the platform to list rentals, screen tenants, collect rent, and track maintenance, and they can get help from the Hemlane team when they want it. It covers single-family homes, multi-family buildings, and student housing.

The AI features are limited. The main one is AI-generated listing descriptions. The bigger draw is the setup: rent is paid directly to the owner, and the company highlights that it charges no fees for ACH payments. Real estate agents and tenants have their own sections of the platform.

item.title: HiveTracks
item.description:
Users keep a history for each hive, with guided inspection forms matched to their experience level. The app suggests when to inspect next and offers a bee weather forecast for choosing inspection days. It works on phones with offline use and syncs later.

The core app is free with paid upgrades. Reviews note that mite counts and reports are basic, so serious operations may want extra tools.

Spreadsheets and BeeKeeper-style apps are alternatives. HiveTracks suits hobby and sideline beekeepers.

item.title: Hospitable
item.description:
Hospitable is software for people who run short-term rentals, from a single host to a property management company. It syncs listings and calendars across booking channels, handles guest messaging, assigns tasks to cleaners and co-hosts, and manages owner payouts.

The AI features focus on messages, where hosts spend much of their time. AI Auto Reply answers guest questions on its own, Inbox AI drafts replies for you to approve, and AI Copilot answers questions about your portfolio. An MCP integration lets AI agents work with your Hospitable data. Dynamic pricing is included in the plan rather than sold as an add-on.

item.title: Hostaway
item.description:
Hostaway is a property management system for vacation rentals. It connects to Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com, and Expedia, keeps calendars in sync, builds direct booking websites, and handles guest messaging and day-to-day operations from one dashboard.

Its AI tools include AI CoHost, which looks at live business data to suggest actions and can carry them out, and AI Replies, which drafts or sends responses to guests. Dynamic Pricing adjusts rates automatically. Together they aim to cut the repetitive work that grows with each added property.

item.title: Houdini
item.description:
Instead of editing a model by hand, you build a network of nodes that describes how it is made. Change one input and the whole result updates, which makes it easy to produce variations or redo a shot after a director changes their mind. Its simulation tools for fluids, particles, cloth, and rigid bodies are a main reason studios adopt it.

Film VFX teams, game studios, and motion designers use it, and it connects to engines such as Unreal and Unity through plugins. The learning curve is long, since you need to think in networks rather than in tools.

item.title: IBM Maximo
item.description:
It stores maintenance history for equipment, creates work orders, and tracks inspections. Add-on modules apply AI to predict failures, read inspection images, and monitor condition. Aviation operators use its aviation edition for aircraft maintenance records and task cards.

It is a heavy enterprise system that needs configuration and training. Smaller operations may find lighter tools easier.

SAP, Fiix, and UpKeep cover similar maintenance work. Maximo suits large maintenance organizations.

item.title: ICC Digital Codes
item.description:
Users search codes such as the International Building Code and see local amendments where available. Premium subscriptions add tools like annotations and commentary. A free read-only view is available for many editions.

Local jurisdictions adopt and amend codes, so users should confirm what applies in their area.

UpCodes is an alternative with AI search. ICC Digital Codes suits building inspectors.

item.title: IDEXX
item.description:
In-clinic analyzers and reference labs return results that feed into practice software. AI-assisted image analysis supports radiology review. Practice management products tie records and results together.

Equipment and services are sold to practices with custom pricing.

Antech and Zoetis offer similar services. IDEXX suits veterinarians.

item.title: Imagen AI
item.description:
Photographers upload past edits to build a personal profile. Imagen then edits new shoots and returns adjustments to Lightroom or Photoshop. It also includes culling and cropping tools.

It is billed per photo or by plan.

Aftershoot and Lightroom presets are alternatives. Imagen suits photographers who edit thousands of images.

item.title: IMDbPro
item.description:
Talent agents and managers use it to research who represents whom, check credits, and track projects in development. Box office data and rankings help gauge careers. Users can build lists and get alerts.

It is a subscription service, and listed contact information depends on what companies provide.

Backstage and Casting Networks serve casting needs. IMDbPro suits talent agents researching the industry.

item.title: Intelex
item.description:
Safety teams log incidents, track corrective actions, and schedule inspections. Industrial hygiene modules record exposure monitoring and sampling results. Dashboards show trends across sites.

It is an enterprise product with custom pricing.

Cority and Enablon are alternatives. Intelex suits industrial hygienists and EHS managers.

item.title: Interview Warmup
item.description:
Interview Warmup is a practice tool from Grow with Google. You pick a type of role, and it asks interview questions that employers commonly use. You answer by speaking or typing, and the tool transcribes spoken answers so you can read back what you said.

The feedback is descriptive, not a score. It highlights job-related terms and the words you use most often, and it points out patterns in your answers. You can rerun a question as many times as you like or ask for new ones. When it launched, Google said audio and transcripts were not saved, though you could copy or download a transcript yourself.

item.title: Invaluable
item.description:
Buyers can bid live or online and follow lots from houses worldwide. Subscribers can search price results to see what similar pieces sold for. Auction houses use it for marketing and online bidding.

Fees and premiums vary by auction house.

LiveAuctioneers and WorthPoint are alternatives. Invaluable suits auctioneers, dealers, and collectors.

item.title: Invisalign ClinCheck
item.description:
ClinCheck is the software where Invisalign cases are planned and approved. After a scan, the system proposes a staged plan, and the doctor reviews the 3D animation and requests changes before aligners are made.

Align has added more automation over time, and the platform works with the iTero scanner and a doctor-side suite for diagnostics, patient visuals, and case tracking.

It is tied to Invisalign aligners and requires being an Invisalign provider. Alternatives for other aligner workflows include SoftSmile, uLab Systems, and 3Shape Ortho System. ClinCheck suits orthodontists already treating with Invisalign.

item.title: iZotope Ozone
item.description:
Master Assistant analyzes a track and suggests a starting chain, and users then adjust the modules. It includes a maximizer, imager, and match EQ. Metering shows loudness and spectrum.

Several editions are sold at different prices. Assistant settings are a starting point, not a final master.

LANDR and eMastered offer automated mastering online. Ozone suits sound engineers who master themselves.

item.title: jamovi
item.description:
Users load data, pick analyses such as t-tests or regression from menus, and get results that update live. The R syntax is available for reproducibility. Modules extend it.

It suits teaching and standard analyses, but advanced work usually moves to R.

JASP and SPSS are alternatives. jamovi suits statisticians and students who want a free tool.

item.title: Jellyfish
item.description:
Leaders see how engineering time splits between roadmap work, support, and tech debt, and track delivery. Resource planning and AI impact reports show effects of tools such as coding assistants.

It is an enterprise product with custom pricing.

LinearB and Swarmia are alternatives. Jellyfish suits engineering managers and executives.

item.title: Jungle Scout
item.description:
Jungle Scout is built around Amazon data. Sellers and brands use it to size a category, compare prices, see how competitors advertise, and decide what to launch or stock. It started with tools for finding product ideas and has grown into a set of products for different sizes of business.

The lineup is split by audience. Cobalt gives brands category benchmarking, pricing, and ad-spend insights. Cloud supplies raw data to teams that run their own analytics, Consult offers expert-written reports, and Catalyst is aimed at smaller sellers. Jungle Scout MCP connects approved AI tools to the data, so you can ask questions in plain English and get answers grounded in Amazon figures.

item.title: Kahoot!
item.description:
A host runs a quiz, and players join with a code and answer on phones or laptops. Scores appear after each question. AI features can generate questions from a topic or a document.

A free version covers basic games, and paid plans add reports and larger groups.

Quizizz and Mentimeter are alternatives. Kahoot! suits educators who want energetic review sessions.

item.title: KeyShot
item.description:
Users drag materials onto a model, set up lighting, and see the render update live. It reads files from CAD tools such as SolidWorks and Rhino. KeyShot also includes AI-based features for texture and background creation in newer versions.

It is a paid product with subscription and perpetual options.

Blender Cycles and V-Ray are alternatives. KeyShot suits industrial designers and jewelry designers who need product renders fast.

item.title: Lexicomp
item.description:
Users search a drug and see dosing by age and condition, interaction severity, and patient counseling points. Content is reviewed by pharmacists and updated often. It is available as an app and inside electronic health records.

Subscriptions go to individuals and institutions.

Micromedex and Medscape are alternatives. Lexicomp suits pharmacists and pharmacy technicians.

item.title: LinearB
item.description:
Engineering managers see where work waits, such as in review, and set rules to route pull requests. AI features summarize changes and speed up code review.

Pricing is per developer, with a free tier for small teams. Metrics should be used to support teams, not to rank individuals.

Swarmia and Jellyfish are alternatives. LinearB suits engineering managers.

item.title: Litchi
item.description:
Pilots plan missions on a map with waypoints, altitudes, and camera actions. Orbit and follow-me modes help with filming. Missions can be saved and repeated.

It is a one-time paid app for supported DJI models.

DroneDeploy and Pix4D capture offer survey-focused planning. Litchi suits drone operators who want custom flight paths.

item.title: LiveAuctioneers
item.description:
Auction houses use it to reach bidders worldwide, with catalogs, photos, and bidding tools. Buyers can browse, follow lots, and review past results. Auctioneers also use it to run online-only sales.

Costs include buyer premiums and listing fees set by auction houses and the platform. Results on the site also help dealers see price trends.

Invaluable and eBay are alternatives. LiveAuctioneers suits auctioneers, dealers, and collectors.

item.title: Logic Pro
item.description:
It includes a large library of instruments and loops, plus tools like Session Players, which generate drummer, bass, and keyboard parts. Stem splitter separates tracks from mixed audio. Dolby Atmos mixing is supported.

It is a one-time purchase on Mac and a subscription on iPad.

Ableton Live and FL Studio are alternatives. Logic Pro suits musicians in the Apple ecosystem.

item.title: LTspice
item.description:
Users draw a schematic, run transient, AC, or DC simulations, and plot waveforms. Libraries include models of many Analog Devices parts. It runs on Windows and macOS.

The interface is plain, and some skill with SPICE is needed.

KiCad ngspice and PSpice are alternatives. LTspice suits electrical engineers who design circuits.

item.title: MadCap Flare
item.description:
Writers use topics, snippets, and conditional text to produce several outputs from one project, such as web help and PDF. It handles translation workflows and version control. AI features can help with drafting and editing.

It is a licensed desktop product.

Paligo and Document360 are alternatives. MadCap Flare suits technical writers on large documentation sets.

item.title: Manhattan Associates
item.description:
Its warehouse management system directs picking, packing, and inventory placement. Order management coordinates stores, warehouses, and online orders. AI agents and optimization features help with labor planning and slotting.

It is an enterprise product, and implementations take months.

Blue Yonder and Oracle are alternatives. Manhattan Associates suits warehouse managers at large operations.

item.title: MassageBook
item.description:
Clients book and fill out intake forms online. Therapists record notes after each session and send reminders. A free plan covers basics, and paid plans add marketing tools.

It is built for solo practitioners and small clinics.

Vagaro and Jane are alternatives. MassageBook suits massage therapists.

item.title: MATLAB
item.description:
It has built-in tools for matrices, signal processing, control design, and statistics. Toolboxes add machine learning, computer vision, and domain-specific functions. MATLAB can generate C code for embedded targets, and an AI assistant helps write code in newer releases.

It is standard in aerospace, automotive, and academic engineering. Licenses cost money, though many universities provide them to students, and Octave and Python are free alternatives.

MATLAB suits engineers who need validated toolboxes and a well-documented workflow.

item.title: MatrixGold
item.description:
It has tools for setting stones, building prongs, and sizing rings. Designs export to 3D printers and casting workflows. A rendering module produces product images.

It is a paid product, and training resources are available.

RhinoGold and JewelCAD are alternatives. MatrixGold suits jewelers and jewelry designers.

item.title: Medallia
item.description:
Teams analyze comments with text analytics to find themes and sentiment. Alerts route unhappy customers to staff for follow-up. Dashboards track satisfaction by location, product, or channel.

Enterprise pricing, with implementation help typically needed.

Qualtrics is the main alternative. Medallia suits customer experience managers at large organizations.

item.title: Meez
item.description:
Cooks open recipes on a tablet or phone and follow steps with photos. Costs update with ingredient prices, and recipes scale by yield. Teams share one version so every location uses the same method.

It is a subscription product aimed at restaurants, caterers, and food producers.

MarketMan and Apicbase cover related ground. Meez suits chefs and kitchen managers.

item.title: MegaDetector
item.description:
It runs on large folders of photos and outputs boxes and confidence scores. Researchers then sort detections or pass them to species classifiers. Microsoft AI for Good started the project.

Accuracy varies with camera setup, and some manual review is still expected.

Wildlife Insights offers a web service. MegaDetector suits zoologists and wildlife biologists with large image sets.

item.title: Metasploit
item.description:
