Testers select an exploit, configure a payload, and run it against a target they have permission to test. The framework includes scanners and post-exploitation modules. Rapid7 maintains it.

A free community edition exists, and Metasploit Pro adds features.

Cobalt Strike and Burp Suite serve other test needs. Metasploit suits penetration testers.

item.title: Mindbody
item.description:
Studios set up classes, accept bookings, and manage memberships. Clients book through a branded app or the Mindbody marketplace. Reporting and marketing tools support growth, and AI features help with messaging.

It is a subscription product with tiered pricing.

Vagaro and Zen Planner are alternatives. Mindbody suits yoga instructors who run a studio.

item.title: Mobilize
item.description:
Organizers post events, such as canvassing shifts and phone banks, and manage RSVPs. Reminder texts help turnout. Data syncs to common voter databases and CRMs.

It focuses on volunteer coordination rather than the voter file.

Action Network offers similar event features. Mobilize suits campaign managers coordinating volunteers.

item.title: MoeGo
item.description:
Groomers see appointments by staff and van, store pet profiles, and send reminders. Customers book online and pay by card. AI answers calls and messages in some plans.

It is a subscription product.

Gingr and Pawfinity are alternatives. MoeGo suits pet groomers and small pet service shops.

item.title: Moho
item.description:
Artists draw in vector, build a skeleton of bones, and animate poses instead of redrawing every frame. Smart Bones and physics help with reusable controls and secondary motion. Output goes to video and many game formats.

It is popular with independent animators and small studios because it is cheaper than studio tools. Larger productions often choose Toon Boom Harmony.

Cartoon Animator and Adobe Animate are alternatives. Moho suits animators who want rigging at an accessible price.

item.title: Movebank
item.description:
Researchers upload tracks, annotate them with environmental data, and analyze or share them. A public map displays selected studies. It is run by the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior with partners.

Data access depends on each study’s sharing settings.

Wildlife Insights covers camera traps. Movebank suits wildlife biologists and zoologists who track animals.

item.title: NASA ADS
item.description:
Researchers search by author, object, or topic, and export references to BibTeX and other formats. It shows citations and metrics, and links to the full text where available. Libraries and observatories also use its API.

It is run by the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory with NASA support. Coverage outside its core fields is thinner.

Semantic Scholar and Google Scholar are broader. NASA ADS suits astronomers and astrophysicists.

item.title: Naviance
item.description:
Students explore colleges, build lists, and request transcripts and recommendations. Counselors track deadlines and see how past applicants from the school fared. Career assessments help students explore paths.

Schools and districts buy access, so individuals cannot usually sign up on their own.

Scoir is a close alternative. Naviance suits school-based admissions counselors.

item.title: Nextflow
item.description:
Pipelines are written as processes connected by channels, and run on laptops, clusters, or cloud services. Containers keep software versions consistent. The nf-core community publishes tested pipelines for common analyses.

Seqera, the company behind it, sells hosted tooling. The language has a learning curve for people new to workflows.

Snakemake and Galaxy are alternatives. Nextflow suits bioinformaticians who run pipelines at scale.

item.title: NGP VAN
item.description:
Campaign staff use VAN to cut turf, build call and door lists, and record voter responses from the field. MiniVAN lets canvassers log results on a phone. NGP handles fundraising and reporting for campaigns.

Access depends on party and organization rules, and training matters because data entry quality affects every list.

NationBuilder and Action Network cover parts of the same work. NGP VAN suits campaign managers on progressive campaigns.

item.title: Nmap
item.description:
Users run scans from the command line or a graphical front end such as Zenmap. The scripting engine adds checks for vulnerabilities and service details. Results export to several formats.

Scanning networks without permission is illegal in many places, so use it only on systems you are allowed to test.

Masscan is faster at scale. Nmap suits penetration testers and network engineers.

item.title: Nomad List
item.description:
Users filter cities by budget, weather, and other criteria, and read reports from other nomads. Members get access to chat, meetups, and trip tracking. Visa and tax guides cover many destinations.

Data comes from member reports and may lag.

Teleport and Numbeo are related. Nomad List suits digital nomads choosing where to live.

item.title: Nory
item.description:
Nory connects the parts of restaurant operations that usually live in separate tools. Its forecasting engine predicts demand, and the other modules use that forecast: scheduling sets staffing levels, ordering suggests how much stock to buy, and payroll and invoicing handle the paperwork that follows.

The platform describes its AI as a set of assistants for forecasting, scheduling, ordering, compliance, payroll, invoicing, and customer reviews. The idea is that managers review and approve recommendations instead of building schedules and orders by hand each week. It serves independent brands, franchise groups, multi-location chains, and enterprise operators.

item.title: NovelCrafter
item.description:
NovelCrafter is built around the problem long fiction has: remembering everything. Its Codex works as a story bible that tracks characters, locations, and other details, and the planning views let you lay out a book before and during drafting. Authors writing a series can share a Codex across books so the details stay consistent.

The AI part is optional and you choose the model. NovelCrafter connects to providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic, and to local models, so you decide which one handles brainstorming or prose and what it costs you. The program feeds relevant Codex entries to the model as context, which helps the output stay close to what you have already written. Collaboration tools cover co-writers and editors.

item.title: NVIDIA Isaac Sim
item.description:
Users import robot models, build scenes with physics and sensors, and run tests. It can generate labeled images for training vision models. Integration with ROS lets teams reuse code.

It requires an NVIDIA RTX GPU. The tool is free for individual developers, with enterprise licensing for companies.

Gazebo and Webots are alternatives. Isaac Sim suits robotics engineers who train and test perception.

item.title: NVivo
item.description:
Researchers import text, audio, video, and PDFs, then tag passages with codes and look for themes. Queries, matrices, and visual maps help compare groups and cases. Newer versions include AI-assisted coding and summaries, which researchers should still check.

Social scientists, health researchers, and market researchers use it for projects with many sources. It is expensive for individuals, though universities often hold site licenses.

ATLAS.ti and MAXQDA are close alternatives. NVivo suits researchers who need an organized system for large qualitative projects.

item.title: OBS Studio
item.description:
Users build scenes from cameras, screens, and graphics, and send them to platforms by RTMP or SRT. Plug-ins add NDI, virtual cameras, and more. It runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

It has no built-in AI, but plug-ins add background removal and captions.

vMix and Wirecast are paid alternatives. OBS Studio suits broadcasters and streamers.

item.title: Observable
item.description:
Users write code in notebooks, and charts update as data changes. Observable Plot offers a concise chart API, and Observable Framework builds static data apps. Teams share notebooks and dashboards.

It requires some JavaScript knowledge, which is a barrier for non-coders.

Datawrapper and Flourish are no-code alternatives. Observable suits data visualization specialists who code.

item.title: Omnisend
item.description:
Omnisend is built for ecommerce. It connects to stores on Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, and similar platforms, pulls in customer and order data, and uses it to send email, SMS, and web push messages. Automations such as welcome series, abandoned carts, and win-back flows are the core of how most stores use it.

The AI features sit inside that workflow. It can draft campaign copy, choose send times, build audience segments, generate signup forms from a short description, and answer questions about your performance data in plain language. These save setup time for small teams without a dedicated lifecycle marketer.

item.title: OpenSpace
item.description:
A worker walks the site wearing a camera, and the system builds a navigable record. AI maps images to drawings and tracks progress by area. Teams review conditions remotely and compare changes over time.

It is sold to contractors and owners with custom pricing.

StructionSite and Doxel are alternatives. OpenSpace suits construction managers.

item.title: OpenTable
item.description:
Restaurants manage floor plans, waitlists, and guest notes. Concierges use it to check availability and reserve tables for guests. Reports show covers and no-shows.

Restaurants pay fees by plan or per seated diner.

Resy and Tock are alternatives. OpenTable suits concierge staff and restaurant hosts.

item.title: OpenZeppelin
item.description:
The Contracts library offers tested building blocks such as ERC-20 and ERC-721 tokens. A contracts wizard generates starter code. The company also performs audits and offers monitoring tools.

Using audited libraries lowers risk, but custom code still needs review.

CertiK and Trail of Bits offer audits. OpenZeppelin suits blockchain developers building production contracts.

item.title: Optmyzr
item.description:
Optmyzr is software for people who run paid search and paid social accounts. It connects to Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, Amazon, Meta, and other platforms and gives you tools for automation, monitoring, audits, and reporting, so routine optimization work does not eat the week.

Sidekick is its natural-language copilot, where you can ask questions about an account and get answers. Language-model features also help optimize ad text. Agencies, freelancers, in-house teams, and enterprises use it, and it is built so a PPC specialist stays in control of changes.

item.title: Overleaf
item.description:
Several authors can edit the same document, and it compiles to PDF live. Templates cover many journals and conferences. Paid plans add track changes, comments, and version history, and an AI assistant helps with writing and error explanation.

It removes the need to install LaTeX locally. Many universities offer institutional access.

Local LaTeX with a text editor is the alternative. Overleaf suits scientists, mathematicians, and engineers.

item.title: Passare
item.description:
Directors build arrangements, collect e-signatures, and share planning details with families. Obituary and tribute tools help families write remembrances. Reports track revenue and pre-need contracts.

It is a subscription product for funeral homes.

FrontRunner and Osiris are alternatives. Passare suits funeral directors.

item.title: Peec AI
item.description:
Peec AI covers a gap that traditional SEO tools leave: what AI assistants say about your brand. It runs prompts against AI engines such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini, then reports how often your brand is mentioned, in what position, and with what sentiment.

Source tracking shows which websites the AI cites when it answers, which helps you see where to earn mentions. Reports can be exported, and API and MCP connections let you pull data into other tools. Marketing teams, brands, and agencies use it, and it has separate plans for brands and agencies.

item.title: Petrel
item.description:
Teams combine seismic, well, and production data into 3D models. Tools support geological modeling, simulation setup, and well planning. Cloud versions and AI-assisted interpretation have been added.

It is an enterprise product with custom licensing.

Seequent Leapfrog and Halliburton DecisionSpace are alternatives. Petrel suits oil and gas professionals in exploration and development.

item.title: PhilPapers
item.description:
Users browse by category, search for papers, and set up alerts. Many entries link to open access copies. Categories are curated by volunteer editors.

It is free and community run.

Google Scholar and the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy cover related ground. PhilPapers suits philosophers.

item.title: Photo Mechanic
item.description:
Photographers ingest cards, view previews at high speed, and tag picks. IPTC metadata editing and templates speed up captions. Photos then move to Lightroom or Photoshop for editing.

It is a paid product.

Adobe Bridge and Lightroom handle some of the same tasks. Photo Mechanic suits photo editors working under deadline.

item.title: Physitrack
item.description:
Therapists pick exercises, set sets and reps, and send the program. Patients log completion and pain, and therapists see adherence. Telehealth and outcome measures are included.

Pricing is by therapist seat.

Exercise prescription tools such as Rehab My Patient are alternatives. Physitrack suits physical therapists.

item.title: Pic-Time
item.description:
Clients view and favorite photos in a branded gallery. Photographers set up print stores with lab fulfillment. Automation sends reminders to buy, and AI features help with face search and categories.

A free plan exists, with paid plans for more storage and features.

Pixieset and ShootProof are alternatives. Pic-Time suits wedding photographers who sell prints.

item.title: PictureThis
item.description:
Users take a picture, and the app names the plant and offers information on watering, light, and pests. A diagnosis feature spots disease. Subscriptions unlock unlimited use.

Identification can be wrong for similar species.

PlantNet and iNaturalist are free alternatives. PictureThis suits gardeners.

item.title: Pixieset
item.description:
Photographers upload photos to private galleries with download options and an online store. Studio Manager handles contracts, invoices, and scheduling. Free and paid plans differ in storage.

It suits solo and small studios.

Pic-Time and ShootProof are alternatives. Pixieset suits wedding photographers.

item.title: PixInsight
item.description:
It uses scripts and process modules for tasks like background extraction, noise reduction, and deconvolution. Add-ons use machine learning for noise and star removal. Photographers work in a non-destructive way and save workflows.

The interface is technical, and beginners usually take time to learn it. It is sold as a license.

Siril is a free alternative, and Photoshop is used for finishing. PixInsight suits serious astrophotographers.

item.title: PlanSwift
item.description:
Estimators load PDFs or images, set the scale, and click to measure lengths, areas, and counts. Assemblies connect measurements to material and labor costs. Reports go to spreadsheets or bid forms.

It is a paid license aimed at trade contractors.

Bluebeam and STACK are alternatives. PlanSwift suits estimators who want a focused takeoff tool.

item.title: PlatformIO
item.description:
Engineers set up projects with a configuration file, then build, upload, and debug firmware. It runs as an extension for VS Code. Library management and unit testing are included.

The core is open source, with paid features for teams.

Arduino IDE and Zephyr tooling are alternatives. PlatformIO suits embedded engineers who work across many boards.

item.title: PointClickCare
item.description:
Care staff document daily care, medications, and incidents. Care teams share information with hospitals and families. AI features flag residents at risk and help with documentation.

It is sold to organizations, with custom pricing.

MatrixCare and WellSky are alternatives. PointClickCare suits elder care workers and the facilities that employ them.

item.title: Popmenu
item.description:
Popmenu started as a restaurant website and interactive menu product and now covers much of a restaurant’s online presence. The platform includes website design and hosting, online ordering, digital remarketing, and Google Business Profile management, with dashboards that track marketing, ordering, and website performance.

The AI features are the reason many operators look at it. Popmenu’s AI answering works as a virtual host that picks up calls around the clock, answers routine questions about hours and menu items, and texts guests links for orders or reservations. It reads details from the restaurant’s website and Google Business Profile, so answers match what the restaurant has published. Another feature scans the website and recommends social posts each week.

item.title: Posit
item.description:
Analysts write code in RStudio or Positron, build reports with Quarto, and publish apps and dashboards with Shiny. Posit Connect hosts them for a team. The open-source tools are free, and servers for teams cost money.

Biostatisticians and clinical teams use it widely, often with validated environments for regulated work.

JupyterLab and Hex are alternatives. Posit suits statisticians and R users.

item.title: Praat
item.description:
Users load recordings, view spectrograms, annotate segments, and run scripts for batch analysis. It also supports speech synthesis experiments. The interface is old-fashioned but very capable.

It is open source and runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

ELAN is useful for annotating video and audio. Praat suits linguists studying phonetics.

item.title: Praktika
item.description:
Praktika turns language practice into a conversation with a character. The app has several AI tutors with different personalities, and you talk with them out loud. They correct pronunciation, grammar, and word choice as you speak, and you can steer the conversation toward topics you care about.

A personalized study plan adjusts to your level and goals, so sessions build on one another instead of repeating the same small talk. The app runs on iOS and Android, and the focus is on speaking confidence at your own pace.

item.title: PriceLabs
item.description:
PriceLabs automates the pricing decisions short-term rental hosts used to make by hand. Its algorithm looks at local demand, seasonality, events, and comparable listings, then updates nightly rates on your calendar. You can set minimum and maximum prices and rules for stay lengths, and bulk calendar tools let you edit many listings at once.

Other features support the pricing work. Market dashboards show how your area is performing, portfolio analytics compare properties, Revenue Estimator Pro helps assess a purchase, and Listing Optimizer reviews your listing content. It connects with a large number of property management systems and channels, so prices flow to Airbnb, Vrbo, and others without manual copying.

item.title: Pro Tools
item.description:
It handles multitrack recording, comping, and large session management. Surround and Dolby Atmos mixing are supported. It works with Avid and third-party interfaces and plug-ins, and has added assisted features such as stem separation.

It is sold by subscription or perpetual license, with a free entry version.

Logic Pro and Reaper are alternatives. Pro Tools suits sound engineers in professional studios.

item.title: Procreate
item.description:
It has hundreds of brushes, a custom brush engine, blend modes, and fast canvas handling. Procreate Dreams adds frame-based animation. Files export to PSD and common image formats.

It is a one-time purchase with no subscription. Procreate has said it does not use generative AI, which many artists value.

Adobe Fresco and Clip Studio Paint are alternatives. Procreate suits illustrators and art therapists who want a simple, tactile tool.

item.title: Prolific
item.description:
Researchers set screening criteria, such as age, country, or language, and pay participants for their time. Participants are vetted, and the platform tracks quality. It connects with survey tools like Qualtrics and experiment builders.

Pricing is based on participant payments plus a platform fee. Samples are online volunteers, so results may not represent the general population.

MTurk and CloudResearch are alternatives. Prolific suits behavioral scientists and academic researchers.

item.title: Propared
item.description:
Stage managers build cue sheets, share call times, and send updates to crew. Calendars sync to phones. Documents and rider details stay with each event.

Free and paid plans exist.

Airtable and Notion are general alternatives. Propared suits stage managers and production teams.

item.title: PropStream
item.description:
Investors filter by criteria such as equity, ownership length, or pre-foreclosure status and export lists. Comparable sales and rental estimates help evaluate deals. Marketing tools support direct mail and skip tracing.

Data accuracy varies by county, and investors should verify details before offering.

Reonomy and Zillow serve related needs. PropStream suits residential real estate investors.

item.title: Prospero.ai
item.description:
Prospero.ai aims to give individual investors the kind of signals institutions pay for. Its AI scans market data to produce stock picks, recognize price trends, and gauge sentiment, and it surfaces what large institutional traders are doing so you can see where money is moving.

The app is free to use, and the company describes it as built for retail investors. It works as a research starting point, not an adviser. AI signals can be wrong, so check the underlying filings and your own risk tolerance before acting on any suggestion.

item.title: PTV Vissim
item.description:
Users build a network, add signals and demand, and run simulations to see delays and queues. It tests design changes before they are built. It connects with other PTV tools for planning.

It is a professional license, and models need calibration with local data.

Aimsun and SUMO are alternatives. PTV Vissim suits transportation engineers.

item.title: Publishers Marketplace
item.description:
Literary agents use it to see which editors buy which kinds of books and to post their own deals. Authors use it to research agents. A daily newsletter lists new book deals.

Data is mostly reported by members, so it is not a complete record.

Query Tracker helps authors track submissions. Publishers Marketplace suits literary agents.

item.title: RapidAI
item.description:
RapidAI makes software for time-critical imaging. For suspected stroke, it processes CT or MRI scans, identifies large vessel occlusions and measures tissue at risk, then alerts the team.

Its platform also covers aneurysm and other vascular conditions and helps coordinate transfers between hospitals.

It is sold to hospitals and stroke networks. Results guide care but do not replace clinical judgment. Alternatives include Viz.ai, Aidoc, and Brainomix. RapidAI suits stroke centers and their referring hospitals.

item.title: Read&Write
item.description:
Students use it in browsers, Google Docs, and Word to hear text, highlight, and check spelling. Teachers can create voice notes and study guides. It helps learners with dyslexia and others who struggle with text.

Licenses are sold to schools, with some free features for teachers.

Speechify and NaturalReader are alternatives. Read&Write suits special education teachers.

item.title: Recorded Future
item.description:
Analysts look up indicators like domains and hashes, read risk scores, and see related campaigns. Alerts flag leaked credentials and brand abuse. An AI assistant answers questions about reports and threats.

It is an enterprise product, now part of Mastercard, with custom pricing.

Mandiant and CrowdStrike Falcon Intelligence are alternatives. Recorded Future suits threat intelligence analysts.

item.title: REDCap
item.description:
Researchers build forms, schedule events for longitudinal studies, and capture data with audit trails. It supports surveys, branching logic, and data exports to statistical software. Institutions host it themselves.

It is free to member institutions of the REDCap consortium.

Castor and Medidata Rave are alternatives. REDCap suits clinical researchers and data managers.

item.title: RedTrack
item.description:
RedTrack is a tracker for people who buy traffic and promote affiliate offers. It links traffic sources, affiliate networks, and offers into one view so you can see which campaigns make money. Conversion data goes back to ad platforms so their optimization works from accurate results.

Automation rules can pause or scale campaigns based on performance. Through MCP access, AI agents can read data and take actions using the same controls you set, which allows an assistant to monitor campaigns for you within limits.

item.title: rekordbox
item.description:
It analyzes tracks for beats and key, and sets cue points and playlists. Prepared libraries move to Pioneer DJ players by USB. Newer versions add stem separation and cloud sync.

Basic features are free, and paid plans unlock performance and cloud features.

Serato DJ and Traktor are alternatives. rekordbox suits DJs who play on club standard gear.

item.title: Reonomy
item.description:
Brokers and investors search for properties by criteria, then look up the owner behind an LLC, recent sales, and mortgages. Map search helps find off-market opportunities. Contact data supports outreach.

Subscription pricing is aimed at professionals, and ownership data can lag for recent sales. It is now part of Altus Group.

CoStar and PropStream are alternatives. Reonomy suits real estate developers and investors.

item.title: Rhino
item.description:
Rhino models curves and surfaces with high accuracy. Grasshopper lets designers build parametric definitions with nodes, so changing a number updates a whole design. A large plug-in ecosystem covers rendering, fabrication, and analysis.

It is sold as a perpetual license rather than a subscription. The learning curve is moderate for basic modeling and steeper for Grasshopper.

SketchUp and Revit overlap in some uses. Rhino suits architects and designers who work with complex geometry.

item.title: Roll20
item.description:
Game masters build maps, place tokens, and manage character sheets for systems like Dungeons and Dragons. Dynamic lighting and a built-in marketplace support rich scenes. Players join through a browser.

A free tier is available, and paid tiers add tools.

Foundry VTT and Fantasy Grounds are alternatives. Roll20 suits game masters running remote campaigns.

item.title: ROS
item.description:
Engineers write nodes that communicate over topics and services. Packages cover navigation, perception, and manipulation, and tools like RViz and Gazebo help visualize and simulate. ROS 2 is the current main line.

It is free, and it is a common base for robotics research and products.

Isaac Sim and Gazebo help with simulation. ROS suits robotics engineers.

item.title: SAS Viya
item.description:
Analysts can work in a visual interface or code in SAS, Python, or R. Model management tools track versions and monitor performance. Insurers, banks, and health organizations use it for risk and pricing models.

It is expensive and aimed at enterprises.

DataRobot, Dataiku, and Databricks are alternatives. SAS Viya suits actuaries and analysts in regulated fields.

item.title: Scoir
item.description:
Counselors manage student lists and send transcripts to colleges electronically. Students compare schools and track deadlines. Colleges share information directly with students who show interest.

Schools adopt it, and the student side is free.

Naviance is the main alternative. Scoir suits college admissions counselors.

item.title: Screaming Frog SEO Spider
item.description:
It crawls pages and lists broken links, redirects, duplicate titles, missing metadata, and page depth. It can connect to Google Analytics and Search Console for extra data. Custom extraction and AI integrations help analyze content at scale.

The free version crawls a limited number of URLs, and the paid license removes the cap.

Sitebulb and Ahrefs Site Audit are alternatives. Screaming Frog suits SEO specialists.

item.title: Seeking Alpha
item.description:
Seeking Alpha combines crowd-sourced investment writing with a quantitative rating system. Contributors publish stock analysis, the site covers news and earnings, and its Quant Ratings score stocks on factors such as valuation, growth, and momentum.

The free tier gives limited access to articles and data. Premium adds a stock screener, fuller ratings, and portfolio tools, and some AI-generated stock analysis that draws on the ratings and analyst coverage sits in paid tiers. A separate stock-picking service, Alpha Picks, is sold on its own. Sources disagree on exactly how much of the ratings the free tier includes, so check the plan page.

item.title: Sensor Tower
item.description:
App publishers use it to benchmark competitors, find keywords, and study how top apps present themselves. App store optimization features show how listings rank for search terms. Reports cover categories, regions, and trends.

Figures are estimates, not official numbers, so they are best used for relative comparison. Pricing is custom and aimed at businesses.

AppTweak and AppFollow are alternatives. Sensor Tower suits app marketers and product teams.

item.title: Serato DJ
item.description:
DJs load tracks, loop, set cues, and mix with effects. Stem separation lets them mute vocals or drums in real time. Plans include a free tier for basic use.

Hardware support is wide, though some features need compatible gear.

rekordbox and Traktor are alternatives. Serato DJ suits DJs who want flexible controller support.

item.title: Shopmonkey
item.description:
Technicians and service advisors build estimates from labor guides and parts catalogs, send them to customers for approval, and track the job through completion. Digital vehicle inspections with photos help explain recommended work. Text messaging keeps customers informed.

Shops use it to replace paper tickets and spreadsheets. Parts ordering and accounting integrations vary by plan.

Tekmetric and Shop-Ware are close alternatives. Shopmonkey suits independent repair shops.

item.title: Sketch Engine
item.description:
Users search for words and phrases, see collocations, and compare usage across corpora. A word sketch summarizes grammatical patterns for a word. Users can also build corpora from their own texts.

It is a subscription service, with free access for some academic users.

AntConc is a free desktop alternative. Sketch Engine suits linguists and terminologists.

item.title: SkinVision
item.description:
Users take a photo, and the AI classifies it as lower or higher risk, with a prompt to see a doctor when needed. Some health plans and clinics use it for triage. Clinical studies of accuracy have been published.

It does not replace a dermatologist, and false negatives are possible.

Miiskin and DermEngine are related tools. SkinVision suits dermatologists who want to understand patient-facing skin check apps.

item.title: SoftSmile
item.description:
SoftSmile makes VISION, orthodontic planning software that brings scan segmentation, diagnostics, tooth setup, and case management into one place. The AI proposes a setup and the orthodontist adjusts it.

The software finds collisions, optimizes the plan, and prepares 3D models for production, which helps practices that make their own aligners or send cases to a lab.

SoftSmile is sold to practices and labs. Time-saving figures come from the company, so test it on your own cases. Alternatives include uLab Systems, 3Shape Ortho System, and Invisalign ClinCheck. SoftSmile suits orthodontists who want AI-assisted setups with control over each step.

item.title: SolidWorks
item.description:
Users sketch features, build 3D parts, assemble them, and generate drawings. Add-ons cover simulation, sheet metal, weldments, and product data management. Recent versions add AI-assisted features for tasks like drawing creation.

It is widespread among small and mid-size manufacturers and in engineering education. It runs on Windows, and cloud versions exist.

Autodesk Fusion, Onshape, and Siemens NX are alternatives. SolidWorks suits mechanical engineers and product designers.

item.title: Songscription
item.description:
Songscription converts music you can hear into notation you can read. You give it an audio file, a video link, or a photo of sheet music, and it returns sheet music, MIDI, guitar tabs, or MusicXML. It handles several instruments and can produce piano arrangements and lead sheets.

Transcription is never perfect, so the built-in editor matters. You can fix notes in a piano roll or the score view, and an AI assistant called Annie helps with edits. Musicians use it to learn songs by ear, teachers use it to make arrangements for students, and composers use it to capture ideas quickly.

item.title: Sortly
item.description:
Users add items with photos, tag them with barcodes or QR codes, and scan to update counts. Low-stock alerts prompt reordering. Reports show stock by folder and value.

A free plan covers basic use, and paid plans add more items and users.

inFlow and Zoho Inventory are alternatives. Sortly suits inventory managers at small operations.

item.title: Stark
item.description:
Designers can test text and UI colors against WCAG contrast requirements, preview a layout as people with different vision conditions would see it, and check touch target sizes. Annotation features let designers document focus order and alt text for developers. The browser extension reviews live pages.

Catching problems at the design stage is cheaper than fixing them after launch. Stark gives accessibility specialists a shared place to leave notes for design and engineering teams.

item.title: Stata
item.description:
Users run commands or write scripts, called do-files, which supports reproducibility. It includes tools for panel data, survival analysis, and causal inference. Results export to tables and graphs.

Licenses are paid, with academic pricing.

R and SAS are alternatives. Stata suits economists and researchers who run econometric models.

item.title: StatsBomb
item.description:
Event data records each pass, shot, and defensive action with context, such as pressure and freeze-frame positions. Tools like IQ let analysts compare players and teams. Some data is published openly for research.

Full data is sold to clubs and media on commercial terms. It is part of Hudl.

Opta from Stats Perform is the main alternative. StatsBomb suits sports analysts working in football.

item.title: Stellarium
item.description:
Users pick a location and date to see stars, planets, and satellites, and can control telescopes through plug-ins. It includes sky cultures and deep sky catalogs.

A web version runs in the browser, and desktop apps exist for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Cartes du Ciel is another open-source option. Stellarium suits astronomers and amateur observers.

item.title: Strava
item.description:
Athletes log activities from phones and wearables, compare segments, and follow training. Paid features include route planning and training analysis, and AI-based summaries of activities.

Data privacy settings are important, because routes can reveal where someone lives.

Garmin Connect and TrainingPeaks are alternatives. Strava suits athletes who want a community.

item.title: Streamlabs
item.description:
Streamers use Streamlabs Desktop to build scenes, add overlays, and go live. Alerts show donations and follows. Extra tools help with clips and multistreaming, and an AI assistant can help with clips.

Some features need a paid plan.

OBS Studio is the open-source base. Streamlabs suits streamers who want ready-made overlays.

item.title: StudioBinder
item.description:
Producers build a schedule from a script breakdown and send call sheets to the crew. Shot lists and storyboards help directors plan coverage. A free plan covers basics, and paid plans add team features.

It suits small and mid-size productions more than large studios.

Movie Magic and Celtx are alternatives. StudioBinder suits filmmakers who run their own productions.

item.title: Subtle Medical
item.description:
Subtle Medical builds AI that sits on top of existing scanners. Its tools denoise and enhance images, which lets sites shorten MRI scans or reduce the dose in PET and contrast-enhanced studies.

Imaging centers use it to raise throughput and make exams easier on patients, without replacing their hardware.

It is sold to hospitals and imaging centers. Results depend on scanner and protocol, so sites validate before changing clinical practice. Alternatives include vendor-built reconstruction tools from scanner makers. Subtle suits imaging departments focused on speed and dose.

item.title: Swarmia
item.description:
Managers see cycle time, review speed, and where effort goes between features and maintenance. Teams set working agreements and get Slack nudges. Surveys capture developer experience.

It is a subscription product.

LinearB and Jellyfish are alternatives. Swarmia suits engineering managers who care about team health.

item.title: Tabletop Simulator
item.description:
Users import card images, boards, and custom pieces. Scripting with Lua adds rules and automation. Players join online, so designers can run tests with people in other cities.

It is a one-time purchase, and many community games are available through the Steam Workshop.

Tabletopia is an alternative. Tabletop Simulator suits board game designers who want remote playtests.

item.title: Talkpal
item.description:
Talkpal is built for learners who struggle to find someone to practice speaking with. You have spoken conversations with an AI partner on topics you choose, and it corrects pronunciation and grammar as you go. The app covers a very wide range of languages, including many that larger apps skip.

Conversations can be immersive role-plays, and the app adapts to your level through personalized learning paths. Feedback arrives in real time, so you can fix a mistake while the conversation is still fresh.

item.title: Taranis
item.description:
Images from planes or drones are analyzed to find issues at the leaf level. Reports guide agronomists to problem areas. Insights integrate with farm management tools.

It is a commercial service with custom pricing.

DroneDeploy and Climate FieldView offer related imagery. Taranis suits crop consultants and agronomists.

item.title: Tekla Structures
item.description:
Users create a model that includes connections, rebar, and bolts, then produce drawings and fabrication data. It exports to CNC machines. Collaboration works through IFC and cloud tools.

It is a paid product for specialized users.

Revit and Advance Steel are alternatives. Tekla suits structural engineers and detailers.

item.title: Tekmetric
item.description:
Service advisors write estimates, send digital inspections with photos, and collect approval and payment by text or email. Reports show car count, average repair order, and technician productivity. Integrations connect to parts suppliers and accounting software.

Shops use the data to see what is working and where jobs stall. It is a subscription product with per-shop pricing.

Shopmonkey and Shop-Ware are alternatives. Tekmetric suits independent shop owners and managers.

item.title: Tenable
item.description:
Scanners find missing patches, misconfigurations, and exposed services across servers, cloud accounts, and web apps. Risk scores combine severity with exploit activity and asset importance, and generative AI features summarize attack paths for analysts.

Nessus is widely used for individual scans, while Tenable One targets enterprise programs. Plans and pricing vary.

Qualys and Rapid7 are alternatives. Tenable suits cybersecurity analysts who run vulnerability programs.

item.title: Tenderly
item.description:
Its simulator replays a transaction with changed parameters or code without spending gas. The debugger traces execution step by step. Virtual TestNets fork mainnet state for testing, and alerts watch contracts for events.

It covers major EVM chains, though support depth varies by network. Plans range from free to enterprise.

Hardhat and Foundry tools cover local testing. Tenderly suits blockchain developers who need hosted debugging.

item.title: Terraform
item.description:
Teams write declarative files for servers, networks, and managed services across many cloud providers. Plans show what will change before it happens, and state tracks what exists. A registry offers shared modules.

The community edition is free, and HCP Terraform adds hosted features. OpenTofu is an open-source fork.

Pulumi and AWS CloudFormation are alternatives. Terraform suits cloud architects and platform engineers.

item.title: The Game Crafter
item.description:
Users upload artwork and choose components such as cards, boards, tokens, and boxes. Orders ship as single copies, so there is no minimum run. It also lets designers sell games through its shop.

Unit costs are higher than offset printing at volume, so it suits prototypes and small runs.

Print-on-demand services like Printerstudio are alternatives. The Game Crafter suits independent board game designers.

item.title: TheraPlatform
item.description:
Speech, occupational, and mental health therapists use templates for notes and track treatment plans. Clients book online and pay. A built-in video room supports telehealth sessions.

It is a subscription product priced per clinician.

SimplePractice and TherapyNotes are alternatives. TheraPlatform suits speech therapists in private practice.

item.title: TinEye
item.description:
It finds copies, edits, and earlier versions, and sorts by date. Fact-checkers use it to trace the origin of a photo. A browser extension and API are available.

Coverage is limited to images it has indexed, so a lack of matches is not proof of originality.

Google Lens and Yandex Images are alternatives. TinEye suits fact-checkers verifying images.

item.title: Togal.AI
item.description:
Users upload plans, and the software identifies spaces, walls, and areas in seconds. Estimators review and adjust the results, then export them. It aims to cut hours of manual measuring.

Accuracy depends on drawing quality, so estimators still check outputs.

Bluebeam and PlanSwift are manual alternatives. Togal.AI suits estimators who want automated takeoff.

item.title: Touch Surgery
item.description:
Surgeons and trainees practice steps of a procedure on a phone or tablet. Teams record surgeries and use AI to find phases and generate reports. Hospitals use it for education and quality review.

Content and access vary between free and enterprise tiers.

Osmo and Proximie are related platforms. Touch Surgery suits surgeons and surgical assistants.

item.title: TradingView
item.description:
Traders draw on charts, apply indicators, and write alerts. Pine Script lets users build custom indicators and strategies. A screener finds symbols by criteria, and paid plans increase limits.

It is a charting tool and does not give personal investment advice. Community ideas vary in quality.

Bloomberg Terminal is the professional alternative. TradingView suits stock traders.

item.title: TrainingPeaks
item.description:
It imports data from watches and bike computers and calculates load, fitness, and fatigue. Coaches assign workouts and see compliance. Premium plans add advanced analysis.

It is data heavy, and its value depends on regular logging.

Strava and Intervals.icu are alternatives. TrainingPeaks suits coaches and athletes who follow structured plans.

item.title: TrendSpider
item.description:
TrendSpider is a charting and analysis platform that automates chart work that traders usually do by eye. It detects trendlines, Fibonacci levels, and candlestick patterns across multiple timeframes, so you spend less time drawing and more time deciding.

Beyond charts, it offers scanners to search for setups across markets and backtesting to test a strategy against historical data. Machine learning and language-model features help with building strategies and writing the code behind them. It covers stocks, ETFs, currencies, crypto, futures, and indices.

item.title: Tripleseat
item.description:
Caterers and venue managers track inquiries, build proposals, send contracts, and collect deposits. Banquet event orders pass details to the kitchen and service staff. Reports show lead sources and revenue.

It is a subscription product aimed at venues with regular events.

Cvent and HoneyBook are alternatives with different focus. Tripleseat suits caterers and event venues.

item.title: TrueCoach
item.description:
Coaches assign workouts from an exercise library, and clients log sets in an app. Messaging and progress photos keep communication in one place. Plans are priced by client count.

It focuses on programming and communication, and billing tools are lighter than in all-in-one platforms.

Trainerize and Everfit are alternatives. TrueCoach suits fitness coaches.

item.title: TurboTenant
item.description:
TurboTenant is designed for landlords who manage their own properties. The software covers the main jobs: posting rental listings, screening applicants, creating and signing leases, collecting rent, and handling maintenance requests. Landlords who do not want to be hands-on can hire full-service management for a flat fee.

AI shows up in small, practical places. An AI description generator writes listing copy, and a free Lease Agreement Audit reviews a lease for problems. The company earns money mainly from fees that tenants pay for screening and rent payments, which is how the core landlord tools stay free.

item.title: Twine
item.description:
Writers create passages and link them, and Twine builds a map of the story. Output is an HTML file that runs in a browser. Story formats like Harlowe and SugarCube add variables and logic.

It is free and open source, though advanced features need some scripting.

Ink and Yarn Spinner are alternatives. Twine suits game writers sketching branching narratives.

item.title: Twitch
item.description:
Streamers go live, run chat moderation, and earn through subscriptions, ads, and bits. AutoMod and moderator tools filter chat. Clips capture highlights for sharing.

Income depends on audience size.

YouTube Live and Kick are alternatives. Twitch suits streamers building a live community.

item.title: uLab Systems
item.description:
uLab Systems builds software for planning clear aligner treatment. Its AI proposes tooth movements from a scan, and the clinician edits the plan before approving it.

The company also supports in-office aligner production, so a practice can design and make aligners itself rather than sending every case to an outside lab.

uLab is a paid platform. The in-house approach requires printing and thermoforming equipment and some learning time. Alternatives include SoftSmile, 3Shape Ortho System, and Invisalign ClinCheck. uLab suits practices that want to control aligner design and manufacturing.

item.title: Unity
item.description:
The editor supports 2D and 3D, a large asset store, and C# scripting. Unity includes tools for physics, animation, and multiplayer. AI helpers inside the editor can answer questions and generate assets and code.

A free plan is available for smaller projects, and paid plans apply as revenue grows.

Unreal Engine and Godot are alternatives. Unity suits game developers who ship on many platforms.

item.title: Unreal Engine
item.description:
The engine includes a visual scripting system called Blueprints, so people can build gameplay without writing C++. Lumen handles dynamic lighting and Nanite handles very detailed geometry, which suits cinematic scenes. MetaHuman Creator, which runs with the engine, produces realistic digital characters.

Game studios, film and TV productions, car makers, and architecture firms all use it. The editor is free to download, and Epic takes a royalty on products above a revenue threshold, with separate terms for some non-game uses. Check Epic’s licensing page for current terms.

item.title: Untappd
item.description:
Users log what they drink and discover new beers. Breweries manage their listing and see ratings. Untappd for Business offers digital menus for taprooms and bars.

Ratings reflect a self-selected audience of enthusiasts.

Vivino does the same for wine. Untappd suits brewers and bartenders watching what people drink.

item.title: UpKeep
item.description:
UpKeep helps maintenance teams plan and track their work. The core of the product is work orders, preventive maintenance schedules, asset history, and parts inventory, with a mobile app for technicians. Teams in manufacturing, facilities, food service, fleets, and healthcare use it.

Nova is the AI layer. It can generate work orders, build custom apps, flag problems in your data, and answer questions from technicians in the field by voice. The goal is to cut data entry and make it easier to get answers while standing at a machine or in a mechanical room.

item.title: UpToDate
item.description:
Topics are written and reviewed by physician authors and summarize recommendations with graded evidence. Drug information and calculators sit alongside. Subscriptions are sold to individuals and institutions, and AI search features help find answers.

Content is reviewed by editors, and updates are frequent.

OpenEvidence and DynaMed are alternatives. UpToDate suits doctors who need trusted summaries.

item.title: Upwork
item.description:
Freelancers build profiles, bid on jobs, and get paid through the platform. Clients post jobs and review proposals. AI tools help freelancers write proposals and help clients write job descriptions.

The platform takes fees from freelancers and clients, and competition can be heavy.

Fiverr and Toptal are alternatives. Upwork suits freelancers looking for clients.

item.title: UrbanFootprint
item.description:
Planners test how zoning changes or new development affect housing, jobs, and transportation. Built-in datasets cover parcels, demographics, and mobility. Results can be shared as maps and reports.

It targets professional planning teams and uses custom pricing.

ArcGIS and Carto offer related capabilities. UrbanFootprint suits city planners.

item.title: Vectorworks
item.description:
The Landmark edition adds tools for site modeling, plant libraries, and irrigation. Users can produce drawings, renderings, and schedules from the same model. It works on Windows and macOS.

It is sold by subscription or perpetual license.

AutoCAD and SketchUp are alternatives. Vectorworks suits landscape architects and designers.

item.title: Verkada
item.description:
Staff manage cameras from a browser, search footage by person attributes or events, and get alerts for unusual activity. Access control and visitor management are included. The platform is aimed at schools, offices, and retail.

It is sold with subscriptions to organizations. Privacy and data use rules should be reviewed before deployment.

Rhombus and Avigilon are alternatives. Verkada suits security guards and the teams that manage camera systems.

item.title: VideaHealth
item.description:
VideaHealth is an AI system for dental radiographs. It reviews X-rays as they are taken and highlights suspected decay, bone loss, and other issues on the image.

It is aimed at practices and dental service organizations that want a second read and a shared standard of diagnosis, and the marked images help when explaining treatment to patients.

VideaHealth is sold on subscription. Dentists must confirm every finding. Alternatives include Overjet, Pearl, and Diagnocat. VideaHealth suits practices that want radiograph review built into daily workflow.

item.title: Vidmob
item.description:
Vidmob focuses on the creative side of advertising. Instead of generating ads, it analyzes them. Its models score creative before it runs and break down which elements, such as visuals, messaging, and formats, are linked to better results after launch.

Features include Creative Scoring, Creative Analytics, and a Creative Data API for exporting results into other systems. A separate Influencer Intelligence product applies similar analysis to creator content. The platform uses a large set of proprietary models, and it serves brands, agencies, and in-house creative and media teams.

item.title: Vintrace
item.description:
Winemakers log additions, analyses, and transfers, and see lot histories. Work orders guide cellar staff. Reports support tax and compliance filing.

It is a subscription product for commercial wineries.

Ekos and InnoVint are alternatives. Vintrace suits winemakers who run production at scale.

item.title: VirusTotal
item.description:
Users upload a file or paste a link and see verdicts from dozens of vendors, along with behavior reports and community comments. An API supports automation, and paid plans add search and hunting. AI summaries explain suspicious code.

Uploaded files become visible to others, so sensitive files should not be submitted.

Hybrid Analysis and Any.Run are related tools. VirusTotal suits cybersecurity analysts doing triage.

item.title: Voluum
item.description:
Voluum is an ad tracking platform used by affiliates, agencies, iGaming operators, and in-house marketing teams. It connects with a large number of ad platforms, networks, and tools, and pulls the results into a single place so you can see which traffic sources and offers are profitable.

Its AI features include Traffic Distribution AI, which sends visitors to the offers or landing pages that are performing best, and an MCP connection that lets assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude work with campaign data. Tracking, attribution, and reporting remain the core of the product.

item.title: Weave
item.description:
Front-desk staff see patient information during calls and send appointment reminders by text. The platform can request reviews and collect payments. AI features help with call handling and message drafts.

It is subscription based and integrates with practice management software.

Solutionreach and Modento are alternatives. Weave suits dental hygienists and dentists who manage patient communication.

item.title: WebPT
item.description:
Therapists write notes with templates, track patient progress, and bill insurance from the same system. AI tools help draft documentation. Home exercise programs can be sent to patients.

It is sold by subscription to clinics.

Jane and Raintree are alternatives. WebPT suits physical therapists.

item.title: Wildlife Insights
item.description:
Users upload images, and a model labels species and empty frames, which saves hours of manual sorting. Project teams review and correct results. Aggregated data supports population and range studies.

It is free for conservation use. Accuracy varies by species and region, so reviews are still needed.

Zooniverse and MegaDetector are other options. Wildlife Insights suits conservation biologists.

item.title: Windy
item.description:
Pilots, sailors, paragliders, and outdoor guides use it to see how conditions change by altitude and hour. Layers include radar, satellite, cloud tops, and wave height. The premium plan adds extra data and removes ads.

Forecasts are model output, not guarantees, so users should compare models and check local reports when conditions are marginal.

AccuWeather and Tomorrow.io are alternatives with different focus. Windy suits anyone who needs detailed wind and weather layers.

item.title: Wine-Searcher
item.description:
Users search for a wine and vintage and see listings from retailers and auction houses, with average prices. Ratings from critics appear next to prices. A paid Pro tier adds price history and bulk tools.

Data depends on merchant listings, so rare bottles may have little data.

Vivino and CellarTracker are alternatives. Wine-Searcher suits sommeliers who source and price wine.

item.title: Winnow
item.description:
Winnow targets a specific cost in professional kitchens: food that gets cooked and thrown away. Its Vision product sits above a bin and records each disposal. The camera identifies the food, a scale weighs it, and the system timestamps and photographs the event, so staff do not need to log anything by hand.

That data feeds reports showing which items are wasted, when, and why. A forecasting product, Winnow Foresight, uses the history to suggest how much to produce for each service. Plans range from a simpler tablet-based tracking option to the camera-based Vision system.

item.title: Wireshark
item.description:
It decodes hundreds of protocols and lets users filter packets, follow streams, and view timing. Captures can be saved and shared for later analysis. It runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

It is free and open source. The interface can feel dense, but it is a standard skill for network and security staff.

tcpdump is a command-line option. Wireshark suits cybersecurity analysts and network engineers.

item.title: Wise
item.description:
Users hold balances in many currencies and receive local bank details. Transfers use the mid-market exchange rate with a visible fee. A debit card spends in local currencies.

Fees vary by currency and route, and availability depends on country.

Revolut and PayPal are alternatives. Wise suits digital nomads who move money across borders.

item.title: Wolfram Mathematica
item.description:
Users work in notebooks that combine code, results, and text. The Wolfram Language has built-in functions for a huge range of math and data tasks. It connects with Wolfram Alpha knowledge and, in newer versions, with language model tools.

Licenses are paid, and student editions are cheaper.

MATLAB and SageMath are alternatives. Mathematica suits mathematicians who need symbolic power.

item.title: WorldCat
item.description:
Users search for books, articles, and media, then see which nearby libraries own a copy. Librarians use the underlying records for cataloging and interlibrary loan. OCLC runs the service for member libraries.

Records vary in quality between contributing libraries.

Library of Congress and Google Books are other sources. WorldCat suits librarians and researchers hunting for physical items.

item.title: WorthPoint
item.description:
It collects records from online marketplaces and auction houses, with photos and descriptions of sold items. Image search can help identify an object from a photo. Subscribers use the data to price inventory, decide on consignments, and verify values.

Prices come from sales records, so rare or unusual items may have few comparables. It is a research aid and does not replace a professional appraisal.

LiveAuctioneers and Invaluable show auction results too. WorthPoint suits antique dealers, pickers, and appraisers.

item.title: WP Recipe Maker
item.description:
Bloggers enter ingredients and steps, and the plugin outputs schema markup that search engines can read for rich results. It includes nutrition calculation, unit conversion, and ratings. Premium versions add more features.

It requires a WordPress site.

Tasty Recipes and Create by Mediavine are alternatives. WP Recipe Maker suits food bloggers.

item.title: Xactimate
item.description:
Users sketch a structure, add damage, and select line items with local pricing. The estimate is shared with insurers and contractors. Mobile tools capture photos and measurements.

It is widely used in property claims, and training is available.

Symbility and Cotality tools are alternatives. Xactimate suits property claims adjusters and restoration contractors.

item.title: Yousician
item.description:
Yousician is a music practice app for guitar, bass, piano, ukulele, and singing. Lessons are structured as short exercises and songs, and the app listens to you play through your phone, tablet, or computer microphone. It scores your accuracy and timing as you go, so you get feedback without a teacher in the room.

That listening feature is the main draw for beginners and for experienced players who want a practice routine with measurable progress. Content ranges from first lessons to songs and technique work, and the app tracks your progress over time.

item.title: ZBrush
item.description:
ZBrush works with millions of polygons at once, so artists can push a model from a rough blockout to fine surface detail without switching programs. Its brush system covers everything from broad form changes to small wrinkles and scales. DynaMesh and ZRemesher help keep geometry clean while you sculpt.

Studios use it to make characters, creatures, props, and printable figures. Finished sculpts usually move into Maya, Blender, or a texturing tool for retopology, UVs, and rendering. It has a steep learning curve and an unusual interface, which new users tend to find odd at first.

item.title: Zen Planner
item.description:
Owners set up class schedules and membership plans, and members check in with an app or kiosk. Automated billing reduces missed payments. Reports show attendance and retention.

It is a subscription product.

Mindbody and Kicksite are alternatives. Zen Planner suits martial arts instructors who run a school.

item.title: Zola
item.description:
Couples build a website, manage RSVPs, and collect gifts. Planners and photographers can list services in its vendor directory. AI features help write vows and speeches.

The planning tools are free, and revenue comes from registry and invitations.

The Knot and Joy are alternatives. Zola suits wedding planners who work with couples using the platform.

item.title: Zonos
item.description:
Merchants and brokers use it to classify products into tariff codes, estimate duties and taxes at checkout, and create paperwork. AI helps match product descriptions to HS codes. APIs plug into shops and carriers.

Classification still benefits from review for unusual goods.

Avalara and Flexport offer related services. Zonos suits customs brokers and cross-border sellers.

item.title: 11x
item.description:
11x’s pitch is that AI can do the work of a sales development representative. Alice researches prospects, writes personalized outreach, sends messages across email and LinkedIn, and tries to book meetings. A voice agent, Julian, makes phone calls and follows up. The company presents them as digital workers that run around the clock.

Customers connect their CRM and define the audience and message guidelines, and the agents work through lead lists and hand interested prospects to human salespeople. The approach can raise the volume of outreach well beyond what a small team could do by hand, though response quality depends on targeting and data.

item.title: 360Learning
item.description:
360Learning is based on the idea that the people who know a topic best are usually inside the company, not in a training department. Experts build short courses with the platform’s authoring tool, colleagues give feedback in comments, and learners can ask questions that feed back into the material. It is called collaborative learning.

The platform covers the usual LMS functions: assigning training, tracking completion, compliance, and reporting. Learning paths and skills features help manage development, and integrations connect with HR and communication tools. An AI assistant generates outlines, lessons, and quiz questions from documents, which reduces the time needed to create content.

item.title: AccuWeather
item.description:
AccuWeather provides weather forecasts for locations around the world. Its app and website show current conditions, hourly and 10-day forecasts, radar and satellite maps, and alerts for severe weather. A signature feature is MinuteCast, which predicts when rain or snow will start and stop at your exact location. Longer-range outlooks give a general sense of the weeks ahead, and features such as air quality and pollen cover health-related conditions.

For businesses, AccuWeather sells data and APIs that power weather information in other apps, media, retailers, utilities, and logistics. Meteorologists combine models, observations, and machine learning to produce its forecasts, and the company has developed AI tools for short-term forecasting and for delivering personalized alerts and impact information, such as how weather might affect travel or operations.

item.title: Adobe Captivate
item.description:
Captivate is a long-standing tool for instructional designers. They build courses from slides with interactive elements like quizzes, branching scenarios, drag and drop exercises, and video. A standout feature is software simulation, where the tool records on-screen steps in an application and turns them into demonstrations or practice exercises, which helps train employees on new systems.

Courses are responsive, so they work on desktops and mobile devices, and they publish in formats that learning management systems can track, including SCORM, xAPI, and HTML5. Assets from Adobe’s other tools can be reused. Recent versions add AI help, such as text to speech for narration and automatic generation of some content.

item.title: Adobe Firefly AI Assistant
item.description: Firefly AI Assistant is Adobe’s attempt to bring an agent into its creative apps. Instead of opening each application and applying tools by hand, you describe an outcome, such as adapting a campaign image into several social formats or preparing a video with captions, and the assistant works out the steps. It then carries them out across the right apps in order. The project began under the name Project Moonlight before launching as Firefly AI Assistant.

item.title: Adobe Illustrator
item.description:
Illustrator draws with vectors, meaning shapes are stored as paths and curves instead of pixels, so artwork can be scaled to any size without losing sharpness. That makes it the standard tool for logos, icons, packaging, infographics, and print layouts. Designers build artwork with the Pen tool, shape builders, gradients, and precise typography, and the finished files can go straight to a printer, a website, or a sign shop.

Its AI features aim to speed up the repetitive parts of the job. Text to Vector Graphic generates editable vector shapes from a description. Generative Recolor tries a set of color palettes on an existing design based on a prompt, and Image Trace converts a sketch or photo into vector outlines. Other tools help with selections, pattern creation, and mockups. The output is real vector art on proper layers, so it can be edited like anything else you draw.

item.title: Adobe Photoshop
item.description:
Photoshop is the image editor most photographers, retouchers, and designers learn first. It works on pixels in layers, with masks, selections, adjustment layers, and blend modes that let you change one part of an image without touching the rest. Photo retouching, product shots, poster layouts, and web graphics all fit into that same layer-based workflow, which is why files and techniques carry from one studio to the next.

The AI features sit inside that workflow instead of replacing it. Generative Fill takes a selection and a short text prompt and creates new content that matches the lighting and perspective around it. Generative Expand extends the canvas past the original edges, and the Remove tool erases distractions like power lines or stray people. Select Subject and Neural Filters handle selections, portrait adjustments, and colorization with less manual work. Generated content arrives on its own layer, so you can mask it, blend it, or throw it away.

item.title: Adyen
item.description: Adyen offers a single payments system that covers the entire flow, from the checkout page to the bank. It works as the payment processor and acquirer, which means it connects directly to card networks instead of relying on separate providers, and supports a wide range of payment methods including local options like iDEAL and Alipay. Large retailers, marketplaces, and subscription companies use it to accept payments in many countries with a unified view of the data.

item.title: Affinity
item.description:
Affinity grew from a set of three separate apps: Photo, Designer, and Publisher. These are now combined in a single application, so a designer can retouch an image, draw vector artwork, and lay out a page without switching programs. It’s non-destructive, supports layers and masks, and opens common files including PSD and AI. It became popular as an alternative to Adobe software for people who disliked subscriptions.

Canva acquired the Affinity company and now offers the unified app for free to individuals, with the option to connect to Canva for sharing and collaboration. Organizations that need features like single sign-on can arrange enterprise or education plans. AI tools are optional and tied to a Canva premium plan, so users who prefer to avoid AI can skip them. Integration lets you send designs to Canva and bring them back.

item.title: Airfinity
item.description:
Airfinity provides data and forecasts about health threats and the products to counter them. Its analysts and models track outbreaks, monitor vaccine and drug development pipelines, and estimate supply, demand, and production. The data helps decision makers judge where a disease is heading and which products might reach the market.

The company became widely known for its work during the COVID-19 pandemic, when it tracked vaccine production and distribution around the world, and has since expanded to other diseases and to wider life sciences analysis. Its customers include pharmaceutical companies planning strategy, investors, public health bodies, and policy groups. Machine learning helps process large volumes of data from many sources.

item.title: AliveCor
item.description:
AliveCor makes consumer and clinical ECG tools. The KardiaMobile devices are small sensors that you touch with your fingers while a phone app records a single-lead or multi-lead electrocardiogram. The app uses algorithms cleared by regulators in many regions to say whether the rhythm looks normal, shows atrial fibrillation, or is unclassified.

Records can be saved, shared with a doctor, and compared over time. People with palpitations or a history of arrhythmia use it to capture an episode as it happens, and clinicians use it to monitor patients remotely. The company also offers a subscription that adds more analysis, reports, and access to cardiologist review.

item.title: AlternativeTo
item.description:
AlternativeTo answers a simple question: what else is there like this? You look up an application, such as Photoshop or Slack, and see a list of alternatives, ordered by how many users have liked them, with filters for platform, license, and features. Each entry has a description, screenshots, and user comments, which makes it easy to compare. The site covers software across desktop, mobile, web, and services.

It is useful when you want to avoid a subscription, move to open-source software, find something that runs on Linux, or replace a service that has shut down. Users can propose new applications and vote on alternatives, which keeps the site current. In recent years, it has added extensive coverage of AI tools, with categories for chatbots, image generators, and coding assistants.

item.title: Altium Designer
item.description:
Altium Designer is a professional environment for designing electronics. Engineers draw circuit schematics, lay out the physical board with components and traces, check the design against rules for manufacturing and signal integrity, and generate the files that fabricators need. It supports complex, high-speed, and multi-layer boards used in consumer devices, medical equipment, aerospace, and automotive electronics.

Collaboration and cloud tools extend the desktop product. Altium 365 provides a platform for sharing designs, managing components, and reviewing changes with teammates and manufacturers, and integrations with mechanical CAD allow electrical and mechanical engineers to work together. Component libraries and supply chain data help pick parts that are available. Newer features bring in AI-assisted capabilities, such as automating parts of layout or helping with design checks.

item.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description: AgentCore addresses the infrastructure work of taking an agent from prototype to production. A runtime hosts agents with session isolation so each user’s work is kept separate, and handles scaling. Identity features let agents authenticate to other services on a user’s behalf, a gateway turns existing APIs and services into tools agents can call, and observability traces what agents do. Developers can use it with frameworks such as LangGraph, CrewAI, and the Strands Agents SDK, and with models on Bedrock or from other providers.

item.title: Amazon SageMaker
item.description: SageMaker started as a way to run machine learning on AWS without managing servers. Data scientists use notebooks to prepare data and write code, then train models on managed compute that scales up as needed. Once a model is trained, SageMaker can deploy it behind an endpoint, monitor its performance, and handle versioning, which turns a notebook experiment into a production service. It supports popular frameworks such as PyTorch and TensorFlow.

item.title: Amazon Textract
item.description: Textract turns images of documents into structured data. A developer sends a scanned file or PDF, and the service returns the text it finds along with its layout: it identifies tables and preserves their rows and columns, detects key-value pairs in forms such as a name field and its value, and recognizes handwriting. This is much more useful than plain text recognition, which would return an unordered block of characters.

item.title: Ambience Healthcare
item.description:
Ambience builds AI for the paperwork around medical care. With patient consent, its system captures the conversation between clinician and patient, then generates a structured note in the clinician’s preferred format. The clinician reviews and signs it, which cuts the time spent charting after hours.

Its distinct focus is coding and compliance. From the same conversation and the chart, the tool suggests diagnosis and procedure codes with supporting evidence, which can reduce missed codes and billing errors. Because of that, it targets health systems and large practices rather than single clinicians, and it works with different specialties.

item.title: Anaplan
item.description:
Anaplan lets large organizations plan in a connected way. Instead of separate spreadsheets for finance, sales, and operations, teams build models on a shared platform so a change in one area, such as a drop in demand, flows through to inventory, headcount, and budget. Its modeling engine handles large multidimensional data, and planners can create scenarios to see the effects of different decisions before committing.

AI features aim to lower the barrier to building and using models. An assistant can help create or modify model logic from natural language, forecast with machine learning, and summarize results for decision-makers. The platform integrates with ERP, CRM, and data warehouse systems to pull in actuals, and offers applications for common planning needs, such as sales territory planning and supply chain optimization.

item.title: Animaze
item.description:
Animaze lets people appear as a character instead of themselves. It uses a webcam to track your face and, with some setups, your body and hands, then moves an avatar to match. The result is delivered through a virtual camera, so it shows up in OBS, Zoom, Teams, Discord, and other apps.

Users can pick from a library of avatars, import custom models, or create their own, and add props, backgrounds, and effects. Streamers and VTubers use it to build an on-screen persona, while others use it for presentations, teaching, or just privacy on calls. Support for expressions and triggers allows more lively performances.

item.title: Apify
item.description: Apify turns the web into a source of structured data. A marketplace called Apify Store offers thousands of Actors, which are cloud programs that scrape or automate specific websites and tasks: extracting listings from Google Maps, posts from social networks, product details from e-commerce sites, or contact information from pages. You configure an Actor, run it in the cloud, and receive results as JSON, CSV, or through an API, without managing servers or proxies.

item.title: AppFlowy
item.description:
AppFlowy is positioned as an open-source alternative to Notion. It offers documents, kanban boards, grids, calendars, and linked databases in a single workspace, and the clients are built with Flutter and Rust for desktop and mobile. You can use the cloud service or host your own server, so notes can stay on hardware you control.

Privacy and ownership are the main selling points. Data is stored locally first, the code is open for review, and teams can modify it. The AI assistant can summarize, rewrite, and answer questions about your pages, and it supports local models through tools like Ollama for people who do not want content leaving their machine.

item.title: Apple Vision Pro
item.description:
Vision Pro puts a computer in front of your eyes. High-resolution displays and cameras show the real world with digital windows and objects placed in it, and you interact by looking at things and pinching your fingers, with no controllers needed. It runs visionOS and supports iPad and Apple apps, along with apps made for spatial computing, such as immersive video, 3D design, and games.

Typical uses include watching movies on a giant virtual screen, working with multiple floating windows, viewing and recording spatial photos and videos, and previewing 3D models. Mac Virtual Display mirrors a Mac into the headset, and enterprise users explore training, design review, and remote collaboration. Apple Intelligence features are being added to visionOS, including writing tools and a smarter Siri, and the device’s sensors power features like hand tracking and scene understanding.

item.title: Archistar
item.description:
Archistar addresses the slow, rule-heavy process of getting buildings approved. Its platform reads planning regulations and site data to show what can be built on a lot, such as height, setbacks, and density. Developers and architects can test ideas and see the potential of a site before they invest.

For design checking, the tool compares a proposed building against local codes and flags issues, which reduces the back and forth with planning authorities. Councils use it to review applications faster and with more consistency. Generative design features create massing options that fit the rules, and reports summarize feasibility.

item.title: AudioEye
item.description:
AudioEye is a web accessibility service.
