Its scanner tests pages against the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, finding problems such as missing alt text, poor contrast, unlabeled form fields, and keyboard traps. A script added to the site can then apply fixes automatically for many of these issues, which is quicker than editing every page by hand.

Automation covers only part of the job, so AudioEye also offers expert audits, user testing with people who have disabilities, and managed services. It provides monitoring, reports, and accessibility statements, and integrates with common platforms like Shopify and WordPress. Companies use it to show a good faith effort toward compliance.

item.title: Auth0
item.description: Auth0 saves developers from building login systems themselves, which is a task where mistakes are costly. You add its SDK to an app, and it handles sign-up, login, password reset, social logins like Google or Apple, and passwordless options such as one-time codes and passkeys. It can connect to company identity providers for single sign-on, apply multi-factor and adaptive authentication, and manage roles and permissions. A hosted login page can be customized to match your brand.

item.title: Autodesk Fusion
item.description: Fusion combines the steps of making a physical product in one application. You model parts and assemblies in 3D, run simulations to test stress and heat, and generate toolpaths for CNC machines and 3D printers. It also includes electronics design and drawing tools. Because it runs with cloud-connected data, teams can share designs and collaborate, and it works on both Windows and macOS. Product designers, engineers, machinists, and hobbyists all use it.

item.title: Autodesk Maya
item.description: Maya is among the oldest and most established 3D tools in entertainment. Artists use it to model characters and environments, rig them with skeletons and controls, animate them, simulate cloth, hair, fluids, and effects, and render the result. Its animation tools, including a powerful graph editor and rigging system, are the reason it became the default in animation studios. Plug-ins and scripting in Python and MEL let studios customize it to their pipelines.

item.title: AVEVA
item.description:
AVEVA serves heavy industry with software for designing and running plants. Engineering tools support the design of facilities such as refineries and power stations in 3D, process simulation helps engineers model how plants will behave, and operations software monitors and controls equipment in real time. The PI System, which it acquired through OSIsoft, collects and stores time-series data from industrial sensors across thousands of sites.

AI and analytics sit on top of this data. Predictive analytics monitor equipment for early signs of failure, and optimization tools help reduce energy use and improve throughput. Industrial AI assistants help operators and engineers search documents and data, and digital twin capabilities connect engineering models with live operations. The company’s AVEVA Connect cloud platform brings these tools together.

item.title: Azure AI Document Intelligence
item.description: Azure AI Document Intelligence reads documents so applications can use the data. Its layout model finds text, tables, headings, and selection marks, and prebuilt models recognize common document types such as invoices, receipts, business cards, identity documents, and many tax and mortgage forms, returning fields like totals, dates, and names with confidence scores. You can train custom models with a small number of examples to extract the fields in your own forms.

item.title: Azure AI Foundry
item.description: Foundry is where Microsoft brings together its AI development tools for businesses. A catalog lists models from OpenAI, Microsoft, Meta, Mistral, DeepSeek, and others, which you can test side by side and deploy through one set of APIs. Everything runs under Azure’s identity, networking, and compliance controls, which is what many regulated companies need before they can use generative AI. The service has gone through several names, including Azure AI Studio, so older tutorials may use different labels.

item.title: Azure AI Speech
item.description:
Azure AI Speech brings Microsoft’s speech technology into applications. Speech-to-text transcribes audio in real time or from recordings in many languages, with options for custom vocabulary and speaker separation. Text-to-speech offers a large library of neural voices in many languages and styles, with control over tone, speed, and emotion using SSML. Real-time speech translation converts spoken language into another language for captions or voice.

Additional features serve specialized needs. Custom Neural Voice lets approved customers build a branded voice from recorded samples, subject to a restricted-access process to prevent misuse. Voice live and conversational features support building voice agents, and avatar capabilities create talking presenters from text. Container deployments allow running models on premises or at the edge, and the service integrates with Azure OpenAI and other Azure AI tools.

item.title: Azure AI Vision
item.description:
Azure AI Vision gives developers pretrained image analysis. The Image Analysis service can describe an image in a sentence, tag objects and scenes, detect people and objects with locations, and extract printed and handwritten text through OCR. Additional capabilities include background removal, smart cropping, and searching images by meaning, using models that understand both text and images.

Video and spatial analysis features can analyze camera feeds to count people and measure how they move through physical spaces, useful in retail and building management. Face-related features exist but are limited by a responsible AI approval process, since facial recognition has privacy and fairness concerns. Customers can also train custom models for their own image categories, and containers allow running some features on the edge.

item.title: BabyAGI
item.description:
BabyAGI arrived early in the wave of autonomous agent experiments. The original script was only a few dozen lines: given an objective, a language model creates a task list, executes the first task, stores the result in a vector database, then generates and reprioritizes new tasks based on what it learned. That simple loop was widely copied and adapted.

The project mattered because it made the idea of an AI agent easy to understand and try. It sparked many descendants and discussion about what autonomous systems could do, and developers learned from its limits, such as loops, drift, and cost. Later versions were reworked into a framework for building self-improving agents with functions stored in a database.

item.title: Baidu ERNIE
item.description:
ERNIE, which stands for Enhanced Representation through Knowledge Integration, is Baidu’s answer to ChatGPT. The consumer chatbot answers questions, writes and edits text, generates images, and handles tasks in Chinese and other languages, and it is built into Baidu’s search engine and apps. It benefits from Baidu’s knowledge graph and search data, and is a major option for Chinese-language users.

For developers and companies, Baidu offers ERNIE models through its Qianfan cloud platform, with APIs, fine-tuning, and tools for building AI applications. The company has released versions of its models with open weights, which lets developers run them independently. The models support multimodal inputs and reasoning, and are used in enterprise products, cloud services, and Baidu’s autonomous driving and other businesses.

item.title: Bardeen
item.description:
Bardeen automates repetitive work that happens on web pages. A user installs the extension, then runs playbooks that click through sites, extract data, and send it elsewhere. Typical uses include scraping lists of people from LinkedIn into Google Sheets, saving a company’s details to a CRM, or sending a meeting summary to Slack.

A natural language builder lets users describe what they want, and the AI assembles the steps, which can be edited. Triggers run automations on a schedule or when something happens, and integrations cover hundreds of apps. Sales and recruiting teams, who spend time moving data between tabs, are heavy users.

item.title: Basecamp
item.description:
Basecamp takes a different approach from most project tools. Each project is a self-contained workspace with sections for to-dos, a message board for announcements and discussions, a shared schedule, documents and files, and a group chat called Campfire. Instead of dozens of views and customization options, it offers a fixed, simple structure that’s easy to learn, and encourages asynchronous communication over constant meetings.

The company that makes it, 37signals, is outspoken about its philosophy: calm, focused work and fewer meetings. Features like automatic check-ins replace status meetings, Hill Charts show progress visually, and notifications are designed to be quiet by default. Clients can be invited into projects, which makes it popular with agencies and small businesses.

item.title: Baserow
item.description:
Baserow gives teams an easy way to build databases. It looks like a spreadsheet, but tables can link to each other, store different field types, and show data as a grid, gallery, kanban board, calendar, or form. People without coding skills build trackers, inventories, and small internal tools with it.

It is open source, so companies can run it on their own servers, which appeals to those with data residency or privacy needs. The platform has a REST API and webhooks, an application builder for interfaces, and automations that run on triggers. An AI assistant can create tables from a prompt, and AI fields can generate or classify values for each row.

item.title: Ben's Bites
item.description:
Ben’s Bites began as a daily email in which Ben Tossell shared what he found interesting in AI. It became popular because he wrote like a person rather than a press release, picking tools worth trying and giving short reactions. Readers range from founders and developers to curious non-technical people who want to keep up.

Over time, it expanded beyond a single email. A community of subscribers shares tips and projects, and there are resources such as prompt collections and a list of tools. Some content is for paying members, while the main newsletter remains free. Sponsorships support the free edition and are labeled.

item.title: Better Stack
item.description:
Better Stack started with uptime monitoring, checking websites and APIs and alerting the team when something fails. It has since added more of the operations toolkit. Telemetry covers logs and metrics, with fast search over large volumes, and incident management handles on-call schedules and escalation, with calls, texts, and chat alerts.

Public and private status pages let companies tell customers what is going on during an outage. The pieces work together: a failed check can open an incident, notify the person on call, and update the status page. The pitch is lower cost and less setup than assembling Datadog, PagerDuty, and Statuspage.

item.title: BigQuery
item.description: BigQuery lets teams analyze huge amounts of data without managing servers. You load data from files, databases, streams, or other Google services, write SQL, and BigQuery spreads the work across many machines and returns results quickly, whether the table holds millions or trillions of rows. Because storage and compute are separated and managed, there is no cluster to size or tune, which is a big reason analytics teams like it.

item.title: Blackbaud
item.description:
Blackbaud is one of the largest vendors serving the social good sector. Its Raiser’s Edge NXT is a widely used fundraising and donor management system that tracks supporters, gifts, campaigns, and relationships, with tools for prospect research and online giving. Other products handle accounting, grants management, school administration, volunteer management, and corporate giving programs.

AI has been added across the line. Blackbaud Intelligence helps predict donors who are likely to give more, recommends who to contact, and drafts fundraising messages, and assistants help staff query data and build reports. Integrations connect with email, payment, and analytics tools. As a major data holder, Blackbaud has had to handle security responsibilities, including responding to a ransomware incident that affected customers.

item.title: Bland AI
item.description:
Bland provides voice agents that talk on real phone calls. Companies use them to answer inbound calls, call leads, confirm appointments, and run surveys, replacing or supplementing call center staff. The agents speak naturally, handle interruptions, and can work around the clock.

Developers control behavior through a system of Conversational Pathways, which define the steps and branches of a call, along with tools to call APIs, look up records, and update systems. The platform supports many languages and voices, call analytics, and handoff to human agents. It offers APIs for scaling to large volumes of calls.

item.title: Blender
item.description:
Blender is a complete 3D program that costs nothing. It handles modeling and sculpting, rigging and animation, physics simulation, rendering, compositing, and basic video editing in one application. It is used for animated films, game assets, product visualization, architectural renders, and motion graphics. The software is released under the GPL and developed in public by the Blender Foundation and a worldwide community, with funding from donations and corporate sponsors.

Two features define the current Blender. Cycles is a path-tracing renderer that produces photorealistic images, and EEVEE is a real-time engine for quick previews and stylized work. Geometry Nodes lets you build procedural models and effects by connecting nodes rather than editing meshes by hand, which has become popular for environments and motion design. The Grease Pencil tool allows 2D drawing and animation inside the 3D space.

item.title: Bloomberg Terminal
item.description: The Bloomberg Terminal is the main workstation for traders, portfolio managers, analysts, and bankers. It delivers real-time and historical prices across stocks, bonds, currencies, and commodities, together with news, research, company data, and analytics. A command-based interface lets users call up functions with short codes, which is why people who use it daily rarely touch menus. Its messaging system, Bloomberg Chat, is also where much of the market does its dealing.

item.title: Boomi
item.description:
Boomi was one of the first cloud integration platforms. Its visual builder lets teams connect applications and move data between them, with a large catalog of connectors, API management, data integration, and workflow automation in one platform. Companies use it to sync records between sales, finance, HR, and operations systems without extensive custom code.

The company has leaned into AI agents. Boomi lets teams build agents that use connected systems as tools, and offers an agent catalog and controls to track what agents are allowed to do, which matters as companies deploy many of them. Data management and master data tools help keep records consistent across systems.

item.title: Box AI
item.description:
Box is a content management platform, and Box AI brings intelligence to the files stored there. Users can ask questions about a document, compare several files, summarize a long report, or generate text based on content in a folder. The answers come from the files themselves, so they can be traced back to a source.

For businesses, a strong feature is structured data extraction. Box AI can pull fields from invoices, contracts, and forms, such as dates, parties, and amounts, and put them in metadata that others can search and filter. Box AI Agents can be configured for particular workflows, and the platform lets admins choose among models from various providers.

item.title: Brainly
item.description:
Brainly grew from a Q&A site for students. A learner posts a question, other users and moderators answer it, and the best responses are verified. Over time, it has built a large library of questions and answers across math, science, languages, and history, with versions for many countries that follow local curricula.

The product now blends community with AI. An AI tutor gives step-by-step explanations, can solve problems from a photo, and helps with writing and study guides. A paid plan removes ads and unlocks more AI help and expert-verified answers. Some features are free with limits.

item.title: Bria
item.description:
Bria builds visual generative AI around licensing. Its models are trained on licensed data from content partners rather than scraped web images, and contributors share in revenue, which gives companies a clearer position on copyright than many alternatives. The company also offers indemnification to enterprise customers.

The product is delivered as APIs and tools for businesses. Capabilities include generating images from prompts, editing and background removal, creating product shots, and controls for brand consistency. Enterprises in advertising, e-commerce, and media can embed these features in their apps, with options for fine-tuning on their own assets.

item.title: BrightEdge
item.description:
BrightEdge targets big websites where SEO is a team effort. Its platform tracks rankings across many keywords and markets, ties organic traffic to revenue, and shows which pages are doing well. Content recommendations point to topics worth writing about and pages to improve, using data on search demand and competitor performance.

AI plays two roles. Inside the platform, machine learning finds patterns and generates recommendations. Outside it, the company tracks how brands appear in AI-generated search results and answer engines, a newer measurement area for marketers. Reporting suits agencies and enterprise teams that must show results to executives.

item.title: Browzwear
item.description:
Browzwear helps clothing companies design digitally. In VStitcher, designers and pattern makers import 2D patterns, stitch them together virtually, and see the garment on an avatar with accurate fabric behavior. Changes to patterns or materials show immediately, and the 3D model can be checked for fit across sizes and body shapes.

The goal is to reduce physical samples, which are slow and costly. Teams can review a design with buyers using realistic renderings, adjust it, and send tech packs to factories, and the same files can feed marketing images. Browzwear also offers tools for fabric scanning and connections to product lifecycle management systems.

item.title: Bruno
item.description:
Bruno is part of the group of tools for sending API requests, alongside Postman and Insomnia. Its approach is different: collections are saved in a plain text markup language as files in a folder, not in a vendor’s cloud. Teams commit them to git, review changes in pull requests, and keep API tests next to the code they test.

You can build requests with variables, scripts, and assertions, run collections for testing, and use it from a command line interface in CI pipelines. It supports REST, GraphQL, and other protocols. Because it works offline and does not require an account, it appeals to developers who dislike mandatory sign-ins and cloud syncing after changes in other tools.

item.title: Builder.io
item.description:
Builder.io bridges developers and non-developers. Engineers integrate it into a website built with React, Vue, Next.js, or other frameworks, registering their components, and marketers and designers then assemble and edit pages visually using those components without waiting for a code release. That reduces bottlenecks for landing pages, campaigns, and content, while code stays under developers’ control.

AI has become central. Visual Copilot converts Figma designs into code in a chosen framework and styling approach, using the team’s own components where possible, which cuts down on the tedious work of translating designs. Newer offerings let teams describe features and have an AI agent build and update applications. A headless CMS manages structured content, and personalization and A/B testing features help optimize pages.

item.title: Buildium
item.description:
Buildium is designed for landlords and property managers who run a few dozen to a few thousand units. A manager can list vacancies, screen applicants, sign leases online, collect rent through a resident portal, and track maintenance requests with vendors. Owners can receive statements and reports, and community associations have their own tools.

Accounting is built in, with trust accounting, bank reconciliation, and tax reports that property managers need. Mobile apps let staff handle requests in the field. Some AI features help with tasks such as drafting messages and summarizing information, and integrations connect with listing sites, screening services, and other software.

item.title: Bumble
item.description:
Bumble set itself apart by changing who starts the conversation. When a man and a woman match, the woman has to send the first message within a time limit, which the company says reduces unwanted messages and gives women more control. In same-sex matches, either person can begin. The app uses the swipe format, and offers filters for interests, intentions, and distance.

Beyond dating, Bumble has modes to meet friends and to network professionally, though these have been less central to its success. Safety features include photo verification, a feature that detects and blurs unwanted nude images, and tools for reporting and blocking. AI is used to detect fake profiles, spam, and scams, and to flag harassing messages, which are persistent problems for dating apps.

item.title: BuzzSumo
item.description:
BuzzSumo helps content marketers learn what already works. You enter a topic or domain and see the pieces that earned the most engagement on social networks, along with backlinks, so you can see what resonates before writing. Filters narrow by date, format, and language, which makes it easy to find trending ideas.

Other features cover outreach and monitoring. The influencer search finds people who regularly share and write about a topic, alerts notify you when a keyword or competitor is mentioned, and question tools show what people ask about a subject. AI helps generate ideas and outlines from the findings, and reports can be exported for clients.

item.title: Capture One
item.description:
Capture One began as software for tethered shooting, where a camera connects to a computer and photos appear on screen immediately, and it’s still a leader there. Studio and commercial photographers like its fast, reliable tethering, strong RAW processing, and color tools, including detailed color editing, skin tone adjustment, and support for many camera profiles. It offers a catalog system and sessions for organizing shoots.

Editing features include layers and masks, advanced color grading, and tools for sharpening and noise reduction. AI is used for masking, such as selecting subjects and backgrounds, and for other tasks that speed up workflow. A mobile app and live collaboration features let clients and teams review images during a shoot, and it works across Mac and Windows.

item.title: CARTO
item.description:
CARTO focuses on location data at scale. Instead of copying data to a separate tool, it works where the data already lives, using the warehouse’s compute. Analysts can run spatial operations such as joins, clustering, and routing, and build interactive maps that stay connected to live data.

The platform has three common uses. Analysts build maps and dashboards to explore patterns, data teams construct workflows with a visual editor for spatial processing, and developers embed maps and analytics into applications through APIs. Datasets for demographics, points of interest, and mobility are available to enrich internal data. AI agents let users ask spatial questions in natural language.

item.title: Cartoon Animator
item.description:
Cartoon Animator is built to make 2D animation approachable. You can bring in artwork, a photo, or one of the included characters, add a bone rig, and animate the character. Face tracking from a webcam drives expressions, motion templates provide walks and gestures, and audio can generate lip movement automatically.

The software includes tools for composing scenes, with backgrounds, props, and cameras, and it can export videos, image sequences, and assets for editors. It also links to Reallusion’s other products. Users can bring in layered files from Photoshop and Clip Studio, which helps artists who draw their own characters.

item.title: Cavalry
item.description:
Cavalry offers a different way to make motion graphics. Instead of placing keyframes for each property, you build systems: duplicate a shape in a grid, add a noise behavior, connect values with expressions, and see the animation emerge. Changing one parameter updates the whole piece, which makes iteration quick for design-heavy work such as logo animations, generative patterns, and loops.

It combines 2D vector design, animation, and rendering. Features include a timeline, a node-based graph for connections, text and font tools, and the ability to import vector and bitmap assets. It exports video, sequences, and Lottie, and has tools for creating assets for social media and games. Scripting allows custom behaviors for technical artists.

item.title: CertiK
item.description:
CertiK works on security for blockchain projects. Its core service is the audit, in which engineers and automated tools review a project’s smart contract code to find bugs, logic mistakes, and vulnerabilities before funds are at risk. Audit reports are often published, and projects display them to build trust with users.

Beyond audits, CertiK offers monitoring and scoring. Its Skynet platform tracks security signals and rates projects, and it provides alerts, wallet and transaction analysis, and tools for investigating hacks. Bug bounty programs and penetration testing add other layers, and it also offers formal verification for high-assurance contracts.

item.title: Chainalysis
item.description:
Chainalysis makes sense of public blockchains. Cryptocurrency transactions are visible but pseudonymous, which makes it hard to know who is behind an address. Chainalysis clusters addresses, identifies services such as exchanges and mixers, and links activity to known entities using a large body of data and heuristics. Investigators can follow funds through a chain of transfers, and compliance teams can check whether a transaction touches risky or sanctioned counterparties.

Its products serve distinct users. Reactor is an investigation tool used by law enforcement and security teams, KYT (Know Your Transaction) monitors transactions for exchanges and financial institutions, and other tools support risk scoring, sanctions screening, and reporting. The company publishes research on crypto crime trends, which is widely cited. Machine learning helps detect patterns of illicit behavior and attribute clusters of activity.

item.title: Cinema 4D
item.description:
Cinema 4D is a mainstay of motion graphics. Artists use it to model objects, animate them, and render images and video for title sequences, product visuals, broadcast graphics, and advertising. It’s valued for being easier to learn than many 3D programs, with a logical interface, strong procedural tools, and reliable performance, which has made it popular with designers who need 3D without a long learning curve.

Its tools include MoGraph, a system for creating complex animations from clones and effectors, scene nodes for procedural building, simulation tools for cloth and particles, and a built-in physical renderer plus Redshift for fast, high-quality GPU rendering. It exchanges data smoothly with Adobe After Effects, Photoshop, and Illustrator, and works with game engines and other 3D programs. Maxon bundles it with other products in its Maxon One subscription.

item.title: Claude Cowork
item.description: Cowork takes the agent approach behind Claude Code and puts it in an ordinary app window. Instead of typing commands, you describe a job such as sorting a folder of receipts, turning notes into a report, or building a spreadsheet from several PDFs. Claude breaks the request into steps, makes a plan, works on the files you have shared with it, and reports back when it finishes. Files it reads or creates appear in a panel so you can open them.

item.title: Claude Design
item.description: Claude Design lets you make visual material by talking to Claude. Instead of dragging shapes in an editor, you ask for what you need, such as a slide deck for a product update, a landing page mockup, or a clickable prototype, and Claude builds a first version. You refine it with follow-up messages, like asking for a calmer color palette, a different layout, or an extra section, and the design updates.

item.title: ClickCease
item.description:
ClickCease deals with click fraud in pay-per-click advertising. When advertisers pay for each click on Google or Facebook ads, bots, competitors, and repeated clicks can drain budgets. The tool watches traffic, flags suspicious patterns such as repeated clicks from the same device or location, and adds the offending sources to block lists automatically.

A dashboard shows blocked clicks, estimated savings, and details about where bad traffic came from. Reports can be used to request refunds from ad platforms in some cases. Extras include tracking of invalid traffic on other channels and tools for monitoring ad campaigns and landing pages.

item.title: Clio
item.description:
Clio is a practice management system for small and mid-sized law firms. It keeps matters, contacts, documents, calendars, and communications in one place, tracks billable time, produces invoices, and takes payments through trust accounting and online billing. Client intake tools capture new inquiries and conflict checks, and a client portal lets clients view documents and messages securely. For many firms, it replaces a patchwork of spreadsheets and separate apps.

The AI assistant, Clio Duo, helps with the paperwork. It can summarize a matter’s documents and emails, answer questions about a case, draft correspondence, and suggest time entries. Clio has also moved into legal research and drafting by acquiring a legal research company, adding tools to find authorities and prepare documents inside the same environment. These tools aim to reduce the time lawyers spend on administrative work and first drafts.

item.title: Clipchamp
item.description:
Clipchamp is designed for people who need a video without learning professional software. The editor has a drag and drop timeline, trimming and filters, text, transitions, and a library of templates for social posts, ads, and presentations. It records your screen and webcam, so it handles tutorials and quick explainers.

AI features speed up common tasks. Auto Compose builds a draft video from clips and photos, captions are generated automatically, text to speech adds narration, and silence removal tightens recordings. Microsoft folded the tool into its ecosystem, so it integrates with OneDrive and Microsoft 365, and a version of the editor ships with Windows.

item.title: CoachHub
item.description:
CoachHub is a digital coaching platform sold to employers. Employees are matched with certified coaches for one-on-one sessions on topics such as leadership, communication, and career growth. Sessions take place by video, and the company offers coaches across many countries and languages.

Between sessions, an AI coach named AIMY supports employees. It is available for quick conversations, helps rehearse difficult discussions, and supports goal setting, extending coaching beyond what a limited number of human sessions can cover. The platform reports on usage and progress to the sponsoring company.

item.title: Codacy
item.description:
Codacy connects to repositories on GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket and analyzes code as it changes. It runs static analysis across many languages, checks for style problems, bugs, security issues, and complexity, and posts results as comments on pull requests. Teams can set quality gates that block merges when code does not meet agreed standards.

Dashboards show trends over time, including code coverage, duplication, and issue counts per repository, which helps engineering leads see whether quality is improving. Security features scan dependencies and secrets, and recent AI features suggest fixes and help review code produced by AI assistants. It integrates with CI systems and IDEs.

item.title: Constant Contact
item.description:
Constant Contact has been a staple of small business email marketing for a long time. Users build mailing lists, design emails from templates with a drag-and-drop editor, schedule campaigns, and track opens and clicks. It emphasizes ease of use and customer support, including phone and chat help, which appeals to owners who are not marketing specialists.

The product extends beyond email. Tools include SMS marketing, social media posting, landing pages, online surveys, and event registration, with automation for welcome series and follow-ups. AI features generate email copy and subject lines, suggest content ideas, and help build campaigns from a short brief, and an AI-driven website builder is part of the suite.

item.title: Coolors
item.description:
Coolors makes picking colors quick and fun. You open the generator, press the spacebar, and it produces a harmonious five-color palette. You can lock the colors you like and keep generating until the rest fit, adjust hue, saturation, and brightness, and see names and codes for each color. It is used by web designers, brand designers, illustrators, and anyone choosing colors for a project.

Several tools extend the generator. You can extract a palette from a photo, check color contrast for accessibility, preview palettes on mockups, explore thousands of palettes shared by the community, and export in many formats including CSS, SVG, and code for design tools. Plugins connect to Figma, Adobe apps, and browsers. AI features can generate palettes from a text description or mood.

item.title: Cornerstone OnDemand
item.description:
Cornerstone OnDemand is one of the established vendors of learning management systems. Large employers use it to host training, assign compliance courses, track completion, and manage development plans. The platform covers learning, performance reviews, succession planning, and a content library from outside providers.

Its newer direction centers on skills. AI infers the skills employees have from their roles and activity, compares them to what jobs require, and recommends courses and career paths. Generative AI helps create content, summarize learning, and give managers guidance. The aim is to move from course catalogs to skill growth.

item.title: Course Hero
item.description:
Course Hero started as a library of materials uploaded by students from their classes. Learners search for notes, practice problems, and study guides tied to specific courses and schools, and unlock documents by uploading their own or paying for a subscription. Tutors answer questions on a range of subjects.

An AI assistant now sits alongside the library. It explains concepts, helps with study guides and flashcards, and answers questions about uploaded materials. This makes the site more of a general study tool than a document repository, though the document library remains the main draw for many users.

item.title: Creatopy
item.description:
Creatopy is built for ad production. Designers or marketers create a layout in an editor, and the tool adapts it to dozens of banner sizes and social formats, saving the manual resizing that normally eats hours. Animation tools turn static ads into HTML5 banners, and brand kits keep colors, fonts, and logos consistent.

Teams can scale campaigns with a feature that fills templates from a spreadsheet or product feed, producing many variations of an ad automatically. Approval workflows let clients comment and sign off, and integrations push ads directly to ad networks, so there is less downloading and uploading. AI helps with copy, images, and layout suggestions.

item.title: Cresta
item.description:
Cresta works with customer service and sales teams. During a live call or chat, it analyzes the conversation and gives an agent real-time guidance, such as the next best response, a reminder to cover a compliance point, or a prompt to offer a relevant product. New agents ramp faster, and experienced ones get support on tough conversations.

After calls, Cresta scores interactions automatically against quality criteria, replacing the small samples that supervisors normally review. Managers see which behaviors drive better outcomes and can coach agents using real examples. Analytics surface trends in why customers call and where processes break down.

item.title: Crusoe
item.description:
Crusoe started with a particular idea: use natural gas that would otherwise be burned off at oil wells to power computers. That energy-first approach became a business in cloud computing and then in AI infrastructure, as demand for GPUs rose. Today it builds and operates data centers designed for high-density AI workloads.

Its cloud offers GPU instances, managed Kubernetes and Slurm, and managed inference services for running models, aimed at AI labs and companies that need large amounts of compute. The company emphasizes cleaner energy sources and large campuses for training clusters, working with chip makers and partners to deploy the latest hardware.

item.title: Cvent
item.description:
Cvent is one of the most widely used enterprise event management suites. Planners create event websites and registration forms, collect payments, manage agendas and speakers, and communicate with attendees. A venue sourcing marketplace helps find hotels and meeting spaces and request proposals, which is a central part of corporate meeting planning, and tools handle housing blocks and travel for attendees.

On site and after the event, it provides engagement and measurement. Mobile apps, check-in, and badge printing run the day, while surveys and analytics measure attendance and satisfaction. AI features help generate event content, match attendees for networking, and assist with planning tasks, and integrations connect with CRMs and marketing automation to link events to pipeline. It supports in-person, virtual, and hybrid formats.

item.title: Databricks Agent Bricks
item.description: Agent Bricks is aimed at companies that want agents grounded in their own data. Rather than writing everything by hand, a team describes the task, such as answering questions over internal documents, extracting information from forms, or coordinating several agents, and the platform helps build it. It generates synthetic test data, evaluates quality with judges, and tunes the agent by trying different models and settings to improve accuracy and cost.

item.title: DataCamp
item.description:
DataCamp is built around learning by doing. Each lesson combines a few minutes of video with exercises you complete in an in-browser editor, so you write real code with immediate feedback and no setup. Courses cover Python, R, SQL, Excel, Power BI, statistics, machine learning, and more recently AI and large language models, taught by instructors from industry and academia.

Structured paths help learners progress. Career tracks, such as data analyst or data scientist, string together courses and projects, skill assessments show strengths and gaps, and certifications validate skills for employers. An AI assistant gives hints and explains errors, and a workspace allows practice in notebooks. Teams can buy it for corporate training with reporting.

item.title: DaVinci Resolve
item.description: DaVinci Resolve started as a color grading system used on Hollywood films and grew into a complete post-production suite. It combines a video editor, the Color page for grading, Fusion for visual effects and motion graphics, Fairlight for audio mixing, and a delivery page for exporting. Because all of these are in one application, a project can move from edit to color to sound without being exported or relinked. It runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

item.title: Daytona
item.description:
Daytona offers sandboxes for running code safely. AI agents that write and execute code need a place where mistakes or malicious instructions cannot harm real systems, and Daytona spins up an isolated environment on demand, runs the code, returns the results, and discards the sandbox. Fast startup keeps agent loops responsive.

The company started with standardized development environments that teams could create from a repository in one step. It turned toward infrastructure for AI agents, offering SDKs to create sandboxes, run commands, work with files, and snapshot state. The open-source core can be self-hosted, and a managed cloud is available.

item.title: Decagon
item.description:
Decagon builds AI agents for customer service. Companies connect it to their help center, policies, and internal systems, and the agent answers questions, looks up orders, processes refunds, and handles account changes. It aims to resolve the issue instead of only deflecting people to articles.

A key idea is that support teams control the agent without engineers. They write instructions in natural language, called Agent Operating Procedures, that define how to handle scenarios, which keeps the behavior consistent and reviewable. Testing and monitoring tools show how the agent performs, and analytics highlight why customers contact support.

item.title: Deepnote
item.description:
Deepnote reimagines the Jupyter notebook for teams. Several people can edit a notebook at once, comment on cells, and run code on managed cloud machines without setup. It connects to data sources such as Snowflake, BigQuery, and Postgres, and supports SQL blocks alongside Python, so analysts can mix queries and analysis.

Results are easy to share. Notebooks can be published as interactive apps or dashboards with inputs, charts can be built without code, and scheduled runs keep outputs fresh. Version history and permissions help with team workflows, and it works with common libraries and Jupyter files.

item.title: DeepScribe
item.description:
DeepScribe is an ambient scribe for doctors. With the patient’s consent, the system listens during the visit, separates the conversation from small talk, and produces a structured note in the format a specialty expects. The clinician edits and signs it in the electronic health record.

The company started with oncology, where notes are long and complex, and has expanded to other outpatient fields. Beyond notes, it helps capture details needed for coding and quality reporting, and works with major record systems so notes appear where doctors expect them. The goal is to give clinicians their evenings back.

item.title: Deputy
item.description:
Deputy is workforce management software for businesses with shift workers. Managers create schedules in a drag and drop calendar, publish them to staff, and employees see shifts in a mobile app where they can swap, pick up open shifts, or declare availability. Time clocks record when people arrive, and the data feeds payroll.

Compliance and cost control are big parts of the pitch. Deputy flags overtime and break rule violations based on local labor laws, forecasts labor needs against sales, and helps keep spending on target. Communication tools allow announcements and tasks, and integrations connect to payroll and point of sale systems.

item.title: Dia
item.description:
Dia puts an AI assistant at the center of web browsing. The address bar accepts both web addresses and questions, so you can search, ask about the page you are viewing, or have the assistant work across several open tabs, such as comparing products or summarizing a set of articles. It can draft writing in context and pull from what you have open.

The browser keeps familiar elements such as tabs and extensions, but adds features that use browsing history and open pages as context, with options for custom skills that package repeated prompts. It focuses on helping with everyday tasks like research, email drafts, and shopping comparisons.

item.title: Digital Diagnostics
item.description:
Digital Diagnostics offers autonomous AI for eye screening. A clinic staff member takes photos of a patient’s retina with a compatible camera, the software analyzes the images, and within minutes the clinic gets a result: either the screening is negative, or the patient should see an eye specialist. No ophthalmologist needs to read the images.

That matters because many people with diabetes skip yearly eye exams, and early detection of retinopathy prevents vision loss. Putting screening in a primary care office makes it easier to catch disease. The company also develops AI for other conditions and works with health systems on implementation and billing.

item.title: DISCO
item.description:
DISCO helps legal teams handle the huge volumes of documents produced in lawsuits and investigations. Teams upload email, files, and chats, search and tag them, and decide what is relevant and privileged. The platform runs in the cloud, so reviewers can work together without managing servers.

AI features reduce manual review. Models rank documents by likely relevance, so reviewers see the important ones first, and generative tools summarize documents, answer questions about a set, and help build timelines. Law firms and corporate legal departments use it to cut review costs and speed up cases.

item.title: Dotmatics
item.description:
Dotmatics sells a connected software platform for laboratories. Scientists record experiments in electronic notebooks, manage samples and compounds, analyze results, and search data across projects. The aim is to link research data that would otherwise be spread across spreadsheets and separate instruments, so teams can find and reuse it.

The company has assembled a portfolio of well-known science tools. SnapGene supports molecular biology, GraphPad Prism is a standard for statistical analysis and graphs, Geneious handles sequence analysis, and other products cover chemistry, biology, and lab informatics. Machine learning and analytics features help with tasks such as modeling and data search.

item.title: Dropbox Sign
item.description:
Dropbox Sign lets people sign documents without printing them. You upload a file, mark where each signer needs to sign or fill in fields, and send it by email. Signers open it on any device, sign, and the finished copy is stored with an audit trail that shows who signed and when. Templates make repeat documents such as contracts and NDAs quick to send.

The product started as HelloSign and was acquired by Dropbox, which renamed it. It connects with Dropbox storage, Google Drive, Gmail, Microsoft tools, and CRM systems, so documents can be sent from where they already live. A developer API lets software companies embed signing flows inside their own products, and Dropbox has added AI features in its wider document tools.

item.title: DxO PhotoLab
item.description:
DxO PhotoLab builds on years of lab testing of cameras and lenses. When you open a RAW file, it automatically applies corrections specific to your camera and lens combination for distortion, vignetting, and sharpness, which gives a solid starting point. The editor then provides tools for exposure, color, tone, and detail, with local adjustments using masks and control points inherited from the Nik Collection, which DxO owns.

Its noise reduction is its best-known feature. DeepPRIME XD uses AI to remove noise and recover detail from high-ISO images, and many photographers rate it among the best available, especially for low-light work. Other tools include ClearView for contrast, color rendering profiles, and lens sharpness adjustments. It works as a standalone editor and as a plugin with Lightroom or Photoshop, and DxO also sells PureRAW for batch processing.

item.title: Dynatrace
item.description:
Dynatrace is one of the established names in monitoring large, complex IT environments. A single agent, OneAgent, installs on servers, containers, and cloud services and automatically discovers applications and their dependencies, then collects metrics, traces, logs, and user experience data without much manual setup. A model of how components relate, kept up to date automatically, lets the platform see how a slowdown in one service affects others.

Its distinguishing feature is Davis AI. Instead of only alerting when thresholds are crossed, Davis uses causal analysis to identify the likely root cause of a problem and the business impact, reducing the pile of alerts into a smaller number of actionable issues. Newer generative AI features let users ask questions in natural language, and the platform adds automation that can trigger remediation. Dynatrace also covers security, application vulnerabilities, and monitoring of AI workloads.

item.title: Easy With AI
item.description:
Easy With AI is a simple catalog. Visitors browse categories such as writing, image generation, and productivity, read a short description, and follow a link to the tool.

Small directories provide another view of the market, though coverage and updates vary. Details such as pricing change often and should be checked on the product’s site.

The site is free. Similar resources include Futurepedia, There’s An AI For That, Future Tools, Aixploria, and Best of AI. Easy With AI suits people browsing for tools.

item.title: Elasticsearch
item.description: Elasticsearch stores documents as JSON and indexes them so searches come back in milliseconds, even across billions of records. It began as a full-text search engine for things like product catalogs and website search, and it is also used heavily for logs, metrics, and security data. It is the core of the Elastic Stack, which adds Kibana for dashboards, and ingestion tools for getting data in. Companies use it wherever they need to search or aggregate a large volume of text-heavy data quickly.

item.title: eMastered
item.description:
eMastered applies automatic mastering to a mixed track. A musician uploads the song, the service analyzes it, and an algorithm processes it for balance, loudness, and clarity so it sounds polished on streaming platforms. Users can adjust settings such as intensity, EQ, and reference tracks before downloading.

It is designed for independent artists and producers who cannot afford a mastering engineer for every release. The process takes minutes and costs less than hiring a professional, and a subscription can cover unlimited masters on some plans.

item.title: Envision
item.description:
Envision uses AI to help blind and low-vision people with everyday visual tasks. Users point a phone or wearable camera at printed text, a product, or a scene and hear it read or described aloud. It can read documents, scan barcodes, recognize faces of saved contacts, and identify colors and objects.

The glasses offer hands-free use, with a camera worn at head level and spoken output, which suits tasks like reading mail or navigating a new place. An assistant lets users ask follow-up questions about what the camera sees, and a calling feature reaches sighted helpers when AI is not enough.

item.title: Excalidraw
item.description: Excalidraw has a distinct look: lines and shapes appear as if drawn by hand, which lowers the pressure to make diagrams perfect and encourages quick sketching. It runs in the browser without an account. You draw boxes, arrows, and text, drop in shapes from libraries, and share a link so others can edit with you in real time. It’s popular with developers for architecture sketches and with teachers and designers for brainstorming.

item.title: FactSet
item.description:
FactSet is one of the main data providers for banks, asset managers, and hedge funds. It aggregates information from many sources into a single platform: company financials, earnings estimates, ownership, supply chain relationships, news, transcripts, and market prices. Analysts use it to screen companies, build models, check ownership, and prepare reports, and portfolio managers use its analytics to measure risk and performance.

Delivery options range from the FactSet Workstation, an interface with analytics and charting, to data feeds and APIs that supply data to a firm’s own systems, and add-ins for Excel. Generative AI features let users search and summarize documents such as earnings calls and filings in natural language, and the company offers tools to connect its data to AI applications and agents. It also provides content for wealth managers and corporate users.

item.title: FamilySearch
item.description:
FamilySearch lets anyone explore their family history without paying. Users search a vast collection of historical records, including census, birth, marriage, death, immigration, and military records, from many countries, and many are digitized images. A collaborative family tree combines contributions from millions of people, so you can often find relatives and connect with branches others have researched.

Technology plays a large role in making records searchable. Handwriting recognition and machine learning transcribe and index scanned documents at scale, which has opened up collections that would take volunteers years to index by hand. Tools suggest possible record matches for people in your tree, and photo and story features preserve family memories. The service also operates local centers and online help.

item.title: Figma Weave
item.description: Weave brings generative image workflows into Figma. Instead of exporting an image to another tool, a designer can run a prebuilt workflow on a selected layer, for example swapping the background of a product shot, applying an artistic style to an image, or creating variations. More than twenty such workflows cover common creative tasks, and the results land back in the design file, ready to be used in a layout.

item.title: Filevine
item.description:
Filevine began in personal injury practice and has expanded to many types of law. It gives a firm a single place to track each matter: documents, notes, deadlines, tasks, communications, and billing. Workflows can be customized so that each case type follows the steps a firm wants, with automations that assign tasks and send reminders.

AI features help with the paper-heavy parts of legal work. They can summarize medical records and long case files, draft demand letters and other documents from case data, and help respond to clients. A document review tool extracts key facts and organizes them, which saves paralegals hours on cases with large volumes of material. Client-facing portals and text messaging keep people informed.

item.title: Final Cut Pro
item.description: Final Cut Pro is Apple’s answer to Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve, built to take advantage of Apple hardware. Its magnetic timeline keeps clips connected so that moving or deleting one does not leave gaps or throw other clips out of sync, which many editors find faster than a traditional track-based layout. It is well known for smooth performance with high-resolution footage on Mac, support for professional formats, and tight integration with Motion for graphics and Compressor for output.

item.title: Finastra
item.description:
Finastra supplies the systems that sit behind a bank’s services. Its portfolio includes core banking platforms, commercial and retail lending, payments, trade finance, and treasury and capital markets tools. Banks of different sizes use it, from community institutions to global groups, and often run Finastra systems for decades.

The company has been moving customers toward the cloud and open banking. Its FusionFabric.cloud platform lets banks and third-party developers build apps and connect to Finastra’s services through APIs, and it has been adding AI features for tasks such as credit analysis, document processing, and customer service. Partnerships with large cloud providers support hosting.

item.title: Find an AI Tools
item.description:
Find an AI Tools is a simple list of AI products organized by category. Users browse to see what exists in areas like writing, design, and coding, then click through to the tool.

As with other directories, coverage depends on submissions, and descriptions can lag behind product changes. It is best treated as a starting point.

The site is free. Always check pricing and privacy on the tool’s website. Similar resources include Futurepedia, There’s An AI For That, Easy With AI, Aixploria, and Best of AI. Find an AI Tools suits people scanning for AI tools.

item.title: Firebase
item.description:
Firebase lets developers build apps without running their own servers. Its core services are Cloud Firestore and Realtime Database for storing and syncing data, Authentication for sign-in with email, phone, or social accounts, Cloud Storage for files, Hosting for websites, and Cloud Functions for server-side code. Analytics, Crashlytics, and Cloud Messaging for push notifications round out the app lifecycle tools, and SDKs support iOS, Android, web, Flutter, and Unity.

AI has become part of the platform. Gemini in Firebase helps developers write code, debug, and understand their projects, and Firebase AI Logic gives apps a secure way to call Gemini and other models directly from the client. Genkit is an open-source framework for building AI features and agents, and Firebase Studio provides a browser-based environment for prototyping apps with AI assistance.

item.title: Flourish
item.description:
Flourish makes data storytelling accessible. Users upload a spreadsheet, pick a template such as a bar chart race, scatter plot, hierarchy, map, or scrolling story, and customize colors, labels, and animations. The result is an interactive graphic that can be embedded in a website or article, or exported as an image or video.

Its biggest draw is the library of templates, including formats that are hard to build by hand, like animated race charts and data-driven stories that change as the reader scrolls. Teams can set up brand themes, collaborate on projects, and update charts when data changes. Newsrooms and organizations use it to publish clear graphics quickly.

item.title: Foxglove
item.description:
Foxglove helps robotics teams understand what their machines did. Robots generate streams from cameras, lidar, GPS, motors, and logs, and debugging requires looking at them together on a timeline. Foxglove’s viewer shows images, point clouds, plots, maps, and 3D scenes in customizable panels that stay synchronized, and it works with ROS and other frameworks.

The platform adds data management. Teams upload recordings to the cloud, search across them by metadata and events, share links to specific moments, and collaborate on issues. The company also created MCAP, an open container format for multimodal robotics data that is now used widely, including as the default recording format in ROS 2.

item.title: Freightos
item.description:
Freightos brings quoting and booking for international freight online. Shippers and forwarders enter details about a shipment and receive rates from carriers and forwarders, then book and manage the shipment on the platform. This replaces emailing multiple providers for quotes.

WebCargo is the air cargo side, used by forwarders to get rates and book space with airlines. Freightos also publishes the Freightos Baltic Index, a benchmark for container spot rates that is often cited in news about shipping costs. Its data helps businesses understand market conditions.

item.title: FullStory
item.description:
FullStory lets teams see how real people use their websites and apps. It captures sessions, which can be replayed like a video of the user’s screen, and detects signals such as rage clicks, dead clicks, and error clicks that suggest frustration. Searching across sessions helps teams find all users affected by a particular bug or those who abandoned a checkout step, instead of guessing from numbers alone.

Beyond replays, it offers analytics such as funnels, heatmaps, and journey maps, and tools for tying issues to revenue impact. AI features summarize sessions and surface patterns, so teams don’t have to watch hundreds of recordings, and help prioritize the problems that matter most. Privacy controls mask sensitive information, and integrations send findings to engineering and support tools like Jira and Slack.

item.title: FutureHouse
item.description:
FutureHouse works on automating scientific research. The lab builds language-model agents that read and reason over the research literature, and makes some available to scientists on a platform. Crow answers questions with cited sources from papers, Falcon performs deeper literature reviews, and Owl helps check whether a topic has been studied.

A more ambitious project, Robin, links agents into a multi-step workflow. Agents suggest hypotheses, plan experiments, and analyze results, and the lab used the system to propose a candidate treatment, which was then tested experimentally. The goal is to speed up discovery by letting agents handle parts of the loop.

item.title: Garmin Pilot
item.description:
Garmin Pilot covers the same ground as other flight apps. Pilots plan routes, get weather and notices to air missions, file flight plans, and carry charts and approach procedures on a tablet. In flight, it displays a moving map, traffic, and weather from compatible receivers.

Its advantage is integration with Garmin hardware. The app connects to Garmin avionics and portable devices, so flight plans can be sent to the aircraft’s navigator and data flows both ways. Features such as terrain awareness and flight data logging round out the toolset.

item.title: Gemini CLI
item.description: Gemini CLI brings Gemini into the terminal as a coding and automation agent. In a project directory, you describe a task in plain language, such as explaining a codebase, fixing a failing test, or building a feature, and the agent reads files, proposes changes, runs shell commands, and iterates. It can search the web, use a context file to learn project conventions, and work with long contexts thanks to Gemini’s large context window.

item.title: Gemini Code Assist
item.description:
Gemini Code Assist brings Google’s models into the developer’s editor. In VS Code and JetBrains IDEs, it suggests code as you type, answers questions in chat, explains and refactors code, generates tests, and helps fix errors. It can take a larger task and make coordinated changes across files in agent mode. Google also offers a command-line version, Gemini CLI, which many developers use directly in the terminal.

For organizations, enterprise editions add code customization, which lets the assistant take into account a company’s private repositories so its suggestions follow internal libraries and styles, as well as security and compliance features, indemnification, and admin controls. It works with Google Cloud tools such as Cloud Shell, Firebase, and BigQuery, and it can review pull requests on GitHub through a companion app.

item.title: Gemini Spark
item.description:
Spark is Google’s move toward an always-on assistant. You give it jobs, such as pulling together information from your inbox and documents, preparing for a trip, or following up on a task over several days, and it works in the background on dedicated virtual machines in Google’s cloud. Because it runs there, it keeps going even when your phone or laptop is off, and it reports back with results.

Control is part of the design. Spark asks for permission before taking significant actions such as sending messages or making purchases, and users can set skills and schedules to automate recurring work. It starts with Gmail, Docs, and other Google services, and connects to outside tools through the Model Context Protocol and integrations. On Android, a running agent’s progress is meant to be visible at the top of the screen.

item.title: GIMP
item.description: GIMP, the GNU Image Manipulation Program, has been a mainstay of free software for decades. It handles photo retouching, compositing, and digital painting with layers, masks, curves, selection tools, brushes, and a large set of filters. It reads and writes many file formats, including PSD files to a degree, and supports scripting in Python and Script-Fu for automation. The latest major version brought improvements such as non-destructive editing and better color management.

item.title: GitHub Agent HQ
item.description: Agent HQ is GitHub’s way of treating coding agents as a team you manage instead of a single assistant. Rather than choosing one AI vendor, a developer can assign work to agents from different providers, such as OpenAI’s Codex and Anthropic’s Claude Code, from the same place where code, issues, and pull requests already live. Each agent works on its task and returns changes for review in the usual pull request flow.

item.title: GitLab Duo
item.description:
GitLab Duo integrates AI into the places where developers already work in GitLab. In the editor, it suggests code and generates tests, in merge requests it summarizes changes and helps with code review, and a chat assistant answers questions about code, issues, and GitLab itself. For DevSecOps, it can explain security vulnerabilities and propose fixes, and help find the root cause when a CI/CD pipeline fails.

The company has also introduced agent capabilities that can take on tasks across the software lifecycle, such as planning, coding, and review, with human oversight. Because it works within GitLab, it has access to context from repositories, issues, and pipelines, which general assistants lack. Self-managed customers can use it with their own deployment, and organizations control which models and features are available.

item.title: Google Cloud Text-to-Speech
item.description:
Google Cloud Text-to-Speech gives developers speech synthesis built on the technology behind Google’s assistants. A request with text returns audio in formats like MP3 or WAV, with a choice of voices and languages. The newer voice families, such as WaveNet and the Chirp generation, sound much more natural than traditional synthetic voices, and there are many accents and genders to choose from.

Developers can fine-tune delivery with SSML, adding pauses, emphasis, pronunciation, and speed. The service supports long audio synthesis for audiobooks and narration, and streaming for real-time applications such as voice assistants and interactive voice response systems. Customers can request a custom voice trained on their own recordings, with strict requirements, and the service integrates with other Google Cloud tools.

item.title: Google Cloud Vision
item.description:
Google Cloud Vision is a set of pretrained image analysis features available through an API. Send an image, and it can return labels describing what it contains, detect objects and their locations, read printed and handwritten text, identify landmarks and logos, detect faces and emotions without identifying individuals, and flag explicit content with SafeSearch. It processes single images and batches, including scanned documents.

Typical uses include indexing photo libraries, extracting text from receipts and signs, moderating uploaded images, and powering search by image. Google offers related products for more specialized needs, such as Document AI for forms and Vertex AI for custom models and newer multimodal Gemini models that can describe and reason about images in more detail. Product search features help retailers match photos to catalogs.

item.title: Google Document AI
item.description:
Document AI turns paper and PDF documents into structured data. Prebuilt processors read common document types: invoices with their line items, expense receipts, bank statements, government IDs, and forms. An OCR processor extracts text with layout information, and a layout parser prepares documents for use with language models by splitting them into meaningful chunks.

Customization is a strength. A custom extractor, based on Google’s Gemini models, can be set up with a few examples to pull specific fields from a company’s own documents, even if they vary in layout. A workbench lets teams train and evaluate processors, and a human-in-the-loop option sends uncertain results to reviewers. The output integrates with BigQuery, Cloud Storage, and workflow tools, which helps feed data to analytics and AI systems.

item.title: Google Stitch
item.description:
Stitch is designed to get from an idea to an interface quickly. You describe an app screen or a website, upload a sketch or screenshot, and Stitch generates a designed layout with components, colors, and text, which you can modify through further prompts or by editing directly. It can produce multiple variations, so you can explore directions before settling on one.

Output is meant to be practical. Designs can be pasted into Figma for further work by designers, or exported as front-end code, such as HTML and CSS, to give developers a starting point. The tool incorporates technology from Galileo AI, which Google acquired, and runs on Gemini models, with experimental features that improve over time.

item.title: GPT4All
item.description:
GPT4All brings language models to personal computers. After installing the app on Windows, macOS, or Linux, you choose a model from a built-in list, download it, and chat without an internet connection. Everything runs on your own CPU or GPU, so your prompts and files do not go to a remote server.

A feature called LocalDocs lets you point the app at folders of your files so the model can answer questions about them using retrieval, which makes it useful as a private research or note assistant. The project is open source and also provides libraries and bindings for developers who want to integrate local models into their own software.

item.title: Gradio
item.description: Gradio makes it easy to show a model to other people. With a few lines of Python, you wrap a function, such as one that takes an image and returns a caption, and Gradio produces a web interface with the right input and output components: text boxes, image uploaders, audio recorders, sliders, and more. Running the script gives you a local web app, and a share option creates a temporary public link, which is handy for demos and feedback.

item.title: Grafana
item.description: Grafana is the dashboard tool many engineering teams reach for first. It connects to data sources such as Prometheus, Loki, Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL, and cloud monitoring services, and lets you build panels and dashboards that visualize time-series data, with alerts that notify teams when something goes wrong. Because it does not store data itself, it can sit on top of whatever you already collect, which is a major reason it is so widely adopted.

item.title: Graphite
item.description:
Graphite is built around a workflow in which large changes are split into small, dependent pull requests. This stacked approach, popular at big tech companies, lets engineers keep working on the next piece without waiting for the previous one to be reviewed and merged. Graphite provides a command line tool and a web interface that make managing stacks simple, which plain GitHub handles awkwardly.

It adds features around review. A merge queue keeps the main branch healthy by testing and merging changes in order, an inbox helps reviewers see what needs attention, and insights show how long reviews take. An AI reviewer comments on pull requests to catch bugs and style problems, which matters as more code is written by AI assistants.

item.title: Greptile
item.description:
Greptile is an AI code reviewer with a focus on codebase context. Instead of reading only the diff, it builds an understanding of the whole repository, including how functions and modules relate, so comments can point to impacts in files the pull request did not touch.

It posts review comments and summaries on GitHub and GitLab pull requests. Teams can set rules in plain language, and the system learns from thumbs up and down on its comments to reduce noise. An API allows developers to ask questions about the codebase.

item.title: H&R Block
item.description:
H&R Block is one of the largest tax preparation brands in the United States. Customers can file themselves with online software, which asks questions, imports tax documents, and calculates returns, or go to one of thousands of offices where a tax professional prepares the return. A middle option connects people with an expert online who can answer questions or complete the return for them.

AI shows up as an assistant that answers tax questions in plain language, helps find deductions and credits, and explains forms, working within the tax software and drawing on the company’s tax knowledge. Other features include importing prior-year returns, audit support, and refund tracking. The company also provides services such as small business tax and bookkeeping.

item.title: Headway
item.description:
Headway offers book summaries you can read or listen to in minutes. Each summary covers the main ideas of a nonfiction title, such as business, psychology, or self-improvement, so users can sample many books quickly. Audio versions suit commutes and workouts.

The app leans on habit building. Users set daily goals, track streaks, and get reminders, and collections organize summaries by theme and goal. Quizzes and flashcards help retain what was read, and AI features personalize recommendations.

item.title: Heap
item.description:
Heap approaches analytics with automatic capture. Once its snippet is on a site or app, it records user interactions without developers adding tracking code for each event. Product managers can then define what counts as a signup or a purchase later and look back at historical data, which avoids the gaps that come from forgetting to instrument something.

Analysis tools include funnels, retention, user paths, and session replay, and a feature that surfaces friction points and drop-offs. It supports building segments of users and comparing their behavior, and it can send data to a warehouse. Heap was acquired by Contentsquare, which combines its quantitative analytics with Contentsquare’s digital experience tools.

item.title: Help Scout
item.description:
Help Scout is for teams that want customer support without a heavy ticketing feel. Messages arrive in shared inboxes, where agents can assign conversations, leave private notes, and collaborate, while customers get replies that look like ordinary emails. That personal feel is a selling point for businesses that value relationships.

The product includes a knowledge base called Docs, a chat and messaging widget called Beacon, and reports on response times and satisfaction. Workflows automate routing and tagging. AI features draft replies from past conversations and help articles, summarize long threads, and adjust tone, and an AI answers questions for customers using the knowledge base.

item.title: Heroku
item.description:
Heroku popularized the idea that deploying an app should be easy. A developer pushes code to a Git repository, and Heroku builds it, runs it in lightweight containers called dynos, and handles routing, scaling, and logs. Add-ons provide databases, caching, monitoring, and other services with a few clicks, so a small team can run a production app without managing servers. Many Ruby, Python, Node, and Java apps started there.

Heroku has been adding AI capabilities for developers. Managed inference lets apps call hosted models through the platform, and agent features help build and run AI-powered applications alongside the regular app and database, with the aim of keeping the developer experience simple. Heroku Postgres remains a central product, with pgvector support for embeddings.

item.title: HomeGauge
item.description:
HomeGauge is software for the home inspection trade. Inspectors collect findings on-site, add photos, and generate reports with standard language, ratings, and summaries for buyers and agents. Repair estimate features give clients an idea of costs.

The product has been around for years and has a loyal user base, along with scheduling and business tools. Newer rivals emphasize modern interfaces and automation, and AI features that draft report language.

HomeGauge is sold by subscription or license. Inspectors remain responsible for accuracy and compliance with standards of practice. Alternatives include Spectora, ISN, Horizon, Palmetto, and ITB. HomeGauge suits home inspectors.

item.title: HoneyBook
item.description:
HoneyBook is designed for people who sell services, such as photographers, designers, coaches, and consultants. A client inquiry arrives through a form, the owner sends a proposal with a contract and an invoice, and the client signs and pays online, all within a single flow. This replaces a patchwork of documents, email threads, and payment apps.

Other features support day-to-day work. Automations send reminders and follow-ups, a scheduler lets clients book meetings, and a client portal keeps messages, files, and payments in one timeline. Templates for proposals and questionnaires make repeat work faster, and AI helps draft emails and project descriptions. Reports show income and pipeline.

item.title: Housecall Pro
item.description:
Housecall Pro helps small service companies run their operations. Office staff schedule jobs and dispatch technicians on a calendar and map, customers receive confirmations and arrival notifications, and technicians use a mobile app to see their jobs, send estimates, collect signatures, and take payments on site. Invoices and payments flow into accounting.

The platform includes marketing and sales tools. Review requests, email campaigns, and a customer database help a business grow repeat work, and a booking widget lets homeowners schedule online. Some AI features answer calls and messages, help with scheduling and follow-ups, and summarize job details so owners can stay on top of the business.

item.title: IBM Bob
item.description:
Bob is IBM’s agentic assistant for software development. Instead of only autocompleting code, it takes part in the full lifecycle: understanding a codebase, planning changes, writing and reviewing code, generating tests, and helping with deployment. Different agents take on roles, such as architect or reviewer, and work inside the developer’s editor.

Enterprise use is the focus. IBM emphasizes security and governance, with protection against sensitive data leaks, policy enforcement, and testing of the AI for vulnerabilities. It routes tasks among several language models, including IBM’s own Granite family and models from other providers, and is positioned for modernization work such as moving older Java or COBOL applications.

item.title: Icertis
item.description:
Icertis helps big companies manage a very large volume of contracts. Its platform stores contracts in a central repository, supports authoring from templates and clause libraries, routes agreements for approval, and tracks obligations after signing, so deadlines and commitments are not missed.
