Customers use it for sales, procurement, partner, and employment agreements across many countries.

AI is a core part of the pitch. The Icertis Contract Intelligence platform reads agreements to extract key terms, flags risky or nonstandard language, and compares contracts against playbooks. Generative AI features answer questions about a contract portfolio, summarize agreements, and assist with drafting, and the company has expanded its capabilities through acquisitions. It integrates with enterprise systems such as Salesforce, SAP, and Microsoft.

item.title: ImageTrend
item.description:
ImageTrend makes software for first responders. Paramedics and EMTs record patient information, treatments, and outcomes on a tablet or computer, producing the report used for handoff to hospitals, billing, and quality review. The data also feeds state and national registries.

The company also provides tools for state EMS offices, trauma and stroke registries, and hospital data collection, as well as analytics for system performance. Newer tools use AI to help reduce documentation time and check data quality.

item.title: Infura
item.description:
Infura gives developers a dependable way to talk to blockchains. Running a node means maintaining servers, storage, and synchronization, so many projects prefer to use an API instead. Infura offers JSON-RPC and WebSocket endpoints for Ethereum, layer 2 networks, and other chains, letting apps read data, send transactions, and subscribe to events through a single key.

The service includes extras. Support for IPFS provides decentralized file storage, and features such as gas estimation and network monitoring help developers. Because Infura is part of Consensys, which also makes MetaMask, it is deeply integrated into much of the Ethereum ecosystem, and a lot of wallets and applications depend on it.

item.title: Inkscape
item.description:
Inkscape is a capable vector editor that costs nothing. Users draw with pens, shapes, and text, and the results are stored as scalable vector graphics, which remain sharp at any size. It includes tools for paths, boolean operations, gradients, patterns, and a trace feature that converts bitmaps to vectors. Designers use it for logos, icons, illustrations, laser cutting files, and web graphics.

As an open-source project, it has a community that builds extensions and shares resources. Its SVG-centered design makes it a good fit for web work, and it can export to PNG, PDF, and other formats, and import many common file types. The interface has improved significantly in recent versions, and it runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. AI features are not built into the core, though plugins and external tools add some.

item.title: Insight Timer
item.description:
Insight Timer is known for its sheer size and its free offering. The app hosts a huge collection of guided meditations on topics such as stress, sleep, anxiety, and focus, along with music tracks, talks, and live events with teachers worldwide. A simple timer with bells is at the heart of the app, from which it takes its name, and it supports daily streaks and a community of users.

The free library covers most needs, which sets it apart from subscription-first apps like Calm and Headspace. A paid membership unlocks structured courses, offline downloads, advanced filters, and other features, and teachers can earn money from their content. Search and recommendations help sort through the volume of content, and some AI features support discovery and personalization.

item.title: Invoke
item.description:
Invoke is built for people who want control over AI images. Beyond typing a prompt, the layered canvas lets users paint, mask, and inpaint specific areas, combine generated elements, and iterate on a composition like in an image editor. Control features guide pose, depth, and structure.

It works with Stable Diffusion and other open models, and users can add their own checkpoints and fine-tunes. The open-source release runs on a local machine with a capable GPU, which keeps images private, and the company provides a hosted version for teams with management features.

item.title: IQVIA
item.description:
IQVIA sits at the center of the pharmaceutical industry’s information flow. It collects and sells data on prescriptions, healthcare utilization, and patient activity from a large number of sources, which companies use to understand markets, size opportunities, and plan commercial strategy. The company is also a major contract research organization that runs clinical trials, recruiting patients, managing sites, and handling data on behalf of drug developers.

Technology and AI are applied to both lines of business. Analytics platforms combine data sets to deliver insights to sales and marketing teams, and AI helps identify suitable trial sites and patients, predict enrollment, and automate documentation and safety reporting. IQVIA has been building AI agents for tasks such as data analysis and trial operations, often in partnership with large technology companies.

item.title: iRhythm
item.description:
iRhythm provides a way to monitor heart rhythm over a longer time than a short office test. A doctor prescribes the Zio patch, which is a small adhesive device placed on the chest. It records every heartbeat for up to two weeks while the patient goes about normal life, then is mailed back for analysis.

The company’s software uses deep learning to analyze the recording and flag events such as atrial fibrillation, pauses, and other arrhythmias. Certified technicians and clinicians then review the findings and create a report for the physician. This approach catches intermittent problems that a brief ECG would miss, and helps guide treatment decisions.

item.title: Justworks
item.description:
Justworks is aimed at small companies that don’t want to run HR in house. The platform handles payroll, tax filings, benefits enrollment, time off, onboarding, and compliance in a single system, with a mobile app for employees. Its HR support team helps with questions about employment rules.

The distinct feature is the co-employment model. Justworks operates as a professional employer organization, which means it becomes a co-employer for tax and insurance purposes, pooling its customers to buy group health insurance and workers compensation at rates a small firm could not get alone. The business keeps day-to-day control over its staff and hiring.

item.title: Kaggle
item.description:
Kaggle is where many data scientists learn and prove their skills. Companies and researchers post competitions with real problems, such as predicting outcomes from data or classifying images, and participants submit models to a leaderboard. Winning solutions are often published, and the discussion forums are a rich source of techniques. Rankings and medals help build a public track record.

The platform offers more than contests. Public datasets cover topics from health to sports, free notebooks run Python and R in the browser with access to GPUs and TPUs within limits, and a models hub shares pretrained models. Kaggle Learn provides short, practical courses on Python, pandas, machine learning, and more. Benchmarks and community challenges around large language models have been added, and the site integrates with Google Cloud.

item.title: KAYAK
item.description:
KAYAK doesn’t sell travel itself. Instead, it searches airlines, online travel agencies, and hotel sites at once and shows the options in one place, with filters for price, stops, airlines, and times. When you pick an option, it sends you to the provider to book. This saves time compared with checking many sites individually, and the interface offers flexible date grids and nearby airport searches to find cheaper alternatives.

Several tools help with timing and decisions. Price alerts notify you when a fare changes, and forecasts indicate whether prices are likely to rise or fall, so you can choose between booking now or waiting. KAYAK also offers trip planning, a Trips organizer for itineraries, and filters for things like total cost including bag fees. Conversational AI search lets you describe a trip in plain language and get suggestions.

item.title: Keap
item.description:
Keap targets small service businesses and solo operators. It keeps contacts and conversations in one place, tracks deals through a pipeline, and uses an automation builder to send follow-ups based on what people do, such as filling in a form, opening an email, or paying an invoice. The goal is to keep leads moving without manual chasing.

It also handles the money side. Businesses can send quotes and invoices, take payments, set up recurring billing, and book appointments, which makes it common among coaches, consultants, and home service companies. AI helps draft emails and texts, and templates provide ready-made campaigns.

item.title: KiCad
item.description:
KiCad is the most popular open-source tool for designing printed circuit boards. Engineers draw schematics, assign components, lay out the board with traces and layers, and generate the files that manufacturers need, such as Gerbers and drill files. A 3D viewer shows how the finished board will look, and checks for design rules help catch errors before fabrication. It handles professional designs with many layers and high-speed signals.

The project has strong community and institutional backing. It is developed by volunteers and professionals, with support from organizations like CERN, and has a large library of symbols, footprints, and 3D models. Plugins and scripting in Python extend it, and manufacturers such as PCB fabricators provide direct support. Recent releases have improved the interface, simulation, and collaboration.

item.title: Kinexon
item.description:
Kinexon is a real-time location system. Small sensors worn by athletes or attached to a ball or a piece of equipment communicate with fixed anchors around a venue, and the system calculates positions many times per second. Teams use the data to measure distance, speed, accelerations, and tactical positioning.

In sports, coaches and sports scientists monitor workload to manage fatigue and reduce injury risk, and analysts study movement patterns. The company has been used in leagues for handball, basketball, hockey, football, and others. Broadcasters use the tracking data for graphics.

item.title: Klue
item.description:
Klue is a competitive enablement platform. Product marketing teams gather information on rivals from news, websites, reviews, and internal sales feedback, and organize it into battlecards with talking points, strengths, weaknesses, and objection handling. Sales reps access these cards in their CRM or Slack during deals.

AI helps keep the content fresh. It scans for changes, summarizes updates, and helps draft battlecard sections. Win/loss analysis tools collect feedback from deals and reveal patterns. Reports show which competitive content is used and how it relates to outcomes.

item.title: Kore.ai
item.description:
Kore.ai helps large organizations deploy virtual assistants. Companies design conversations and workflows in a low-code environment, connect them to back-end systems, and publish them on websites, mobile apps, messaging platforms, and voice lines. The assistants can answer questions and complete tasks such as resetting a password or checking a balance.

The platform has moved from rule-based dialogue to generative AI and agents. It supports large language models from several providers, retrieval over company content, and tools for building multi-agent systems, with governance features for testing and monitoring. Prebuilt solutions for banking, healthcare, retail, and HR speed up projects, and agent assist tools support human staff on live calls.

item.title: Label Studio
item.description:
Label Studio is a flexible annotation platform. Teams use it to label data for machine learning, such as drawing boxes on images, tagging entities in text, transcribing audio, and rating language model outputs. Its configuration system lets users define custom labeling interfaces with simple markup, so one tool can serve a wide range of projects, and it runs locally or on a server.

Model-assisted labeling speeds up work. A machine learning backend can pre-label data for humans to correct, and active learning helps prioritize the most informative examples. The platform supports evaluating language models, with templates for tasks like ranking responses and checking for factual errors, which has become a common use as teams build AI applications. An API and SDK connect it with training pipelines.

item.title: LangGraph
item.description:
LangGraph models an agent as a graph. Each node is a step, such as calling a model, running a tool, or checking a condition, and edges define the flow between steps, including loops and branches. A shared state object passes information along. This explicit structure gives developers control over what the agent does and when, which makes complex agents easier to reason about than a free-running loop.

Features aimed at production use set it apart. Checkpointing saves state so a run can pause and resume, or recover from failure. Human-in-the-loop steps let an agent wait for approval before taking an action, and time-travel debugging lets developers replay and edit earlier steps. It supports streaming of intermediate results, long-term memory, and multi-agent designs, in Python and JavaScript.

item.title: LegalOn
item.description:
LegalOn helps legal teams review contracts faster. A lawyer opens a draft in Word, and the tool checks it against a review checklist, highlighting risky or missing clauses and suggesting alternative wording. The checklists are built by lawyers, which the company says makes the guidance reliable.

Beyond review, the platform offers features for contract creation and management, and AI that answers questions about legal matters and compares language across documents. It started in Japan under the name LegalForce, where it grew quickly, and has expanded into North America and Europe.

item.title: LegalZoom
item.description:
LegalZoom helps people handle common legal tasks without a law firm. Users answer questions online, and the service prepares and files documents for things like forming an LLC or corporation, creating wills and trusts, registering trademarks and copyrights, and handling name changes. Registered agent services, compliance filings, and business licenses are available for new companies.

Human help is available at higher levels. Plans can include attorney consultations, document review, and legal advice subscriptions, and some tasks are reviewed by staff before filing. The company has added AI tools to guide users through forms, answer questions, and speed up document preparation, though legal advice itself comes from licensed professionals.

item.title: Legora
item.description:
Legora is a legal AI company from Sweden that has expanded globally. Lawyers use its assistant for tasks such as reviewing contracts and extracting key terms across many documents, researching legal questions, summarizing materials, and drafting and revising documents. A Word add-in brings these abilities into the editor where lawyers already work, so suggestions appear as tracked changes.

The platform emphasizes collaboration and structure. Features such as tabular review let teams compare many documents side by side in a grid, workflows capture a firm’s preferred processes, and shared workspaces allow lawyers and clients to work together. Firms can customize the system with their own playbooks and precedents, and security features aim to meet the confidentiality needs of legal practice.

item.title: lemlist
item.description:
lemlist helps sales teams and agencies reach prospects at scale. Users build sequences that combine email, LinkedIn steps, and phone tasks, and personalize messages with variables such as name and company. The brand made its name with personalized images and videos that change for each recipient, a way to stand out in crowded inboxes.

Deliverability is a major part of the product. Inbox warm-up gradually builds sender reputation, and tools check domains and monitor placement so emails land in primary inboxes, not spam. A lead database lets users find contacts and verify emails, and AI helps write openers and suggest follow-ups.

item.title: LexisNexis Protégé
item.description:
Protégé is the AI layer of LexisNexis’s legal research platform. Lawyers can ask research questions in plain language and receive answers that cite cases, statutes, and secondary sources from the LexisNexis collection, with links to the underlying authorities. It can summarize documents, compare them, extract key terms, and draft memos and clauses, and it connects with the Shepard’s citation service to help check whether authorities are still good law.

Newer versions emphasize agentic work and the lawyer’s workflow. Protégé can break a task into steps, such as gathering documents, researching issues, and producing a draft, and works in Microsoft Word so suggestions appear in the document being edited. Firms can customize it with their own documents and playbooks, and security terms are designed for confidential client information.

item.title: Libsyn
item.description:
Libsyn, short for Liberated Syndication, has hosted podcasts since the early days of the medium. Creators upload audio, and Libsyn produces the RSS feed that podcast apps use, so a show appears across Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and many other directories. It also offers an embeddable player and a basic website.

Pricing has historically been based on the amount of storage you upload each month, which differs from plans tied to downloads. Statistics show downloads by episode and location, and the platform has monetization options, including dynamic ad insertion and sponsorship marketplaces, plus tools for video podcasts and premium subscriptions.

item.title: LiveKit
item.description:
LiveKit started as an open-source WebRTC platform that handles the hard parts of real-time communication: routing audio and video between many participants, scaling to large rooms, and working across web and mobile. Developers use its SDKs to build video conferencing, livestreaming, telehealth, and interactive broadcast features, and can run it on their own servers or use the hosted LiveKit Cloud.

The company became prominent in voice AI. The Agents framework lets developers build agents that listen, think with a language model, and speak back, with low latency, handling details such as turn-taking and interruptions. It supports telephony so agents can answer phone calls, plus plugins for speech recognition, language, and voice providers. LiveKit powers voice features in well-known AI products, which helped establish it as a standard for real-time AI.

item.title: LivePerson
item.description:
LivePerson began with live chat and developed into a conversational platform. Brands use it to let customers message them on the channels they already use, with a mix of human agents and automated assistants. The platform manages the conversations, routes them to the right team, and records the data.

AI is central. Bots handle common requests, such as order status or billing questions, and hand off to agents when needed, and agent assist tools suggest responses. The company offers tools for building and managing assistants powered by large language models, with guardrails and analytics to check quality and compliance. Customers include banks, telecoms, and retailers.

item.title: LMArena
item.description: LMArena began as the LMSYS Chatbot Arena, a research project from UC Berkeley researchers. You enter a prompt, get answers from two anonymous models, and vote for the one you prefer, and only then are the model names revealed. Votes from a very large number of people are converted into ratings, using a statistical method similar to chess Elo scores, which produces a ranking that reflects real preferences instead of fixed test questions.

item.title: Lumen5
item.description:
Lumen5 is built for people who have words but no video. You paste in a link or text, and the tool breaks it into scenes, picks suggested footage and images from its library, and adds captions and music. You then edit the storyboard, swap clips, and adjust colors, fonts, and timing in a simple editor.

The service suits content marketing teams, publishers, and small businesses that want to turn articles into social clips quickly. Brand settings keep logos and colors consistent, and templates provide formats for different platforms and aspect ratios. AI can summarize text into short scene copy and suggest visuals.

item.title: MagicSchool
item.description:
MagicSchool was built for educators. Teachers choose a tool, such as a lesson plan generator, rubric builder, quiz maker, IEP helper, or email writer, fill in a short form, and receive a draft they can edit. More than eighty tools cover planning, assessment, communication, and support for students with different needs, which saves time on routine paperwork.

Student-facing features let teachers create safe AI chat rooms for classes, where they set the topic, rules, and level of help, and see the conversations. The platform emphasizes privacy and compliance for schools, with settings designed to protect students, and districts can adopt it with administrative controls. Integrations connect with Google Classroom and other learning tools.

item.title: Magnet Forensics
item.description:
Magnet Forensics serves police, government agencies, and corporate investigators. Its flagship product, Magnet AXIOM, gathers data from devices and online accounts and organizes it so examiners can search messages, photos, browsing history, and app data. Timelines and artifacts help reconstruct what happened and produce reports for legal use.

The company has grown through combination. It merged with Grayshift, which makes tools for accessing locked mobile devices, and offers related products for acquiring evidence, triaging devices at a scene, and reviewing cases collaboratively. AI features help classify images, detect relevant content, and speed up the review of large volumes of data.

item.title: Maltego
item.description:
Maltego is known for visual link analysis. An investigator starts with an entity such as a domain name, email address, or company, then runs transforms that pull related data from sources like DNS records, social media, breach databases, and corporate registries. The results appear as a graph that shows how things connect, which makes patterns easier to see than in a list.

The tool is widely used in cybersecurity and open-source intelligence work. Threat analysts trace infrastructure behind attacks, fraud teams look for networks of related accounts, and journalists and researchers map ownership and connections. A marketplace of data integrations extends what the graph can query, and collaboration features let teams share findings.

item.title: Mangools
item.description:
Mangools packages the basic SEO jobs in friendly tools. KWFinder finds keywords and shows search volume and difficulty, SERPChecker analyzes the pages ranking for a term, SERPWatcher tracks your rankings over time, LinkMiner shows backlinks, and SiteProfiler gives an overview of a domain. Each is easy to use without deep SEO knowledge.

The strength is simplicity. Color-coded difficulty scores and clean layouts mean beginners can find a keyword worth targeting, and small agencies can report progress to clients. The tools share a login and subscription, and the company offers learning material on SEO basics.

item.title: MasterControl
item.description:
MasterControl serves regulated manufacturers, such as pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device companies. Its quality management system handles documents, training, change control, deviations, and corrective actions in a way that satisfies FDA and international rules. Electronic records and signatures provide the audit trail regulators expect.

The platform extends to manufacturing. Electronic batch records and production tools capture how products are made, connecting quality data to the shop floor. AI features help review documents, find trends in quality events, and speed up routine tasks.

item.title: Matillion
item.description:
Matillion is a data integration platform. Data teams use a visual designer to extract data from sources, load it into a cloud warehouse, and transform it there using the warehouse’s own compute. This ELT approach scales with the warehouse and keeps data in the company’s environment.

AI has become part of the product through Maia, a set of agents that act as virtual data engineers. A user describes what they need, and Maia can create pipelines, suggest fixes when something fails, and write documentation. Humans stay in the loop and can review the generated work. The platform also supports orchestration, scheduling, and version control with Git.

item.title: Meilisearch
item.description:
Meilisearch focuses on delivering relevant results quickly with little configuration. Developers send their documents to it through a simple API, and it returns ranked results as the user types, with typo tolerance, synonyms, filtering, and sorting working out of the box. That makes it popular for adding search to a store or a knowledge base.

Newer features address AI. Hybrid search combines keyword matching with vector similarity, so a query can find results by meaning as well as exact words, and it can connect to embedding models. Teams can host Meilisearch themselves, since it is open source, or use the company’s managed cloud.

item.title: Meltano
item.description:
Meltano treats data integration like software development. A project defines extractors and loaders in a configuration file, and Meltano runs them to move data from sources into a warehouse. Because everything is code, pipelines live in Git, run in CI, and can be reviewed like other changes.

It builds on the Singer standard, which has hundreds of community connectors, and integrates with dbt for transformations and Airflow for orchestration. Teams can write custom connectors with a software development kit, which is handy for sources that commercial tools do not cover.

item.title: Memrise
item.description:
Memrise built its approach on memory science. Learners review words and phrases at spaced intervals, so the items they find hardest come back more often. Short videos of real people speaking in everyday situations expose learners to natural accents and pace, which differs from the robotic audio common in older courses.

Newer features add conversation. AI chat partners let users practice dialogues, ask for corrections, and role play situations like ordering food or booking a room. The app offers many languages, with courses created by the company and, in earlier years, by community members, plus a mobile experience designed for short daily sessions.

item.title: Mendeley
item.description:
Mendeley helps researchers organize the papers they read. Users import PDFs, and the software extracts details such as the title and authors, stores them in a library, and lets them highlight and annotate. A Word plugin inserts citations and builds a reference list in thousands of styles, which saves hours when writing papers and theses.

It has social and discovery elements, including groups for sharing libraries and a catalog of research papers. Syncing across the desktop, web, and mobile keeps a library available wherever you work. Elsevier acquired the company, which led some researchers to prefer open alternatives because of concerns about data and lock-in.

item.title: Mentimeter
item.description:
Mentimeter makes presentations interactive. You build slides with questions such as multiple choice polls, word clouds, rating scales, rankings, and open-ended questions, share a join code or QR code, and the audience responds from their phones. Results appear live on the screen, which turns a one-way talk into a conversation and gives quiet participants an easy way to contribute.

It suits a range of settings. Teachers use it to check understanding, trainers to energize workshops, and companies to run all-hands meetings and collect anonymous feedback. Features include quizzes with leaderboards, Q&A with upvoting, and templates, and you can import existing slides from PowerPoint or Google Slides. AI helps generate a presentation from a prompt, suggest questions, and summarize responses.

item.title: Merlin Bird ID
item.description:
Merlin makes bird identification easy for beginners and experts. You can answer a few questions about where and when you saw a bird, its size, colors, and behavior, and Merlin suggests species. Photo ID uses image recognition to name a bird from a picture, and Sound ID listens to birdsong through your phone’s microphone in real time and shows which species are singing, which many users find astonishing.

The app is built on data from eBird, a huge citizen science project where birdwatchers log sightings, and machine learning trained on millions of photos and recordings. Downloadable regional packs let you identify birds without cell service, which helps in the field. Each species has photos, sounds, maps, and information, and a life list lets you track birds you have seen.

item.title: MetaHuman
item.description:
MetaHuman made high-quality digital humans available to everyone. In MetaHuman Creator, you start from presets and adjust facial features, skin, hair, eyes, teeth, and clothing, and get a fully rigged character with realistic details that works with Unreal Engine. Instead of weeks of sculpting and rigging, a studio or hobbyist can have a believable character in a short time.

Other tools expand what you can create. Mesh to MetaHuman converts a scan or custom model into a MetaHuman, MetaHuman Animator turns an iPhone or head-mounted camera recording of an actor’s performance into detailed facial animation, and characters can be used in games, films, virtual production, and training. Epic has expanded where MetaHumans can be used, including in other 3D tools and engines under its license terms, and Epic’s Fab marketplace sells related assets.

item.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot
item.description: Microsoft 365 Copilot is the business version of Microsoft’s AI, and its main advantage is context. It can see your files, emails, calendar, chats, and meetings through Microsoft Graph, within the permissions you already have. In Word it drafts and rewrites documents based on other files, in Outlook it summarizes long threads and drafts replies, and in Teams it recaps meetings, lists decisions, and answers questions about what was discussed. PowerPoint can build a deck from a document, and Excel can explain formulas and analyze data with plain-language prompts.

item.title: Microsoft Clarity
item.description:
Clarity shows how people really use a website. A snippet of code installed on the site captures sessions, which can be replayed like a video, along with heatmaps that show where visitors click and how far they scroll. It automatically flags signs of frustration, including rage clicks, dead clicks, excessive scrolling, and JavaScript errors, so teams can focus on pages where users struggle.

AI features add convenience. Copilot summarizes many sessions to surface common issues and gives answers to questions about user behavior, and filters let you segment by device, country, and traffic source. Clarity also offers insights on how AI chatbots and search drive traffic to a site. It integrates with Google Analytics, Microsoft Advertising, and platforms such as Shopify and WordPress.

item.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio
item.description:
Copilot Studio lets organizations create their own AI agents without heavy coding. In a visual editor, makers describe an agent’s purpose, connect knowledge sources such as SharePoint sites and websites, add topics and actions, and test it in a chat window. The finished agent can be published to Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot, websites, and messaging channels, and can answer questions, complete tasks, or hand off to people.

Its strength is connection to business systems. Hundreds of connectors reach tools like Salesforce, ServiceNow, SAP, and Dynamics 365, and agents can use Power Automate flows to run processes. Autonomous agents can respond to triggers such as a new email or record, not only a chat message, and the platform supports the Model Context Protocol to reach more tools. Administrators manage governance, data loss prevention, and access through Microsoft’s admin centers.

item.title: Microsoft Dynamics 365
item.description:
Dynamics 365 combines CRM and ERP in a modular set of cloud applications. The sales and customer service apps manage leads, opportunities, cases, and customer communications, while finance, supply chain, and Business Central handle accounting, inventory, purchasing, and operations. Because the modules share a data platform, a company can start with one and add others over time, and they connect closely with Microsoft 365, Teams, and Power BI.

Copilot is built throughout. In sales, it summarizes accounts and meetings, drafts emails, and suggests next steps. In service, it helps agents find answers and summarize cases, and in finance and supply chain, it supports tasks like reconciliations, collections, and spotting disruptions. AI agents take on routine tasks, such as qualifying leads or processing orders, and Copilot Studio lets companies build their own.

item.title: Microsoft Entra ID
item.description:
Entra ID is the identity system behind most Microsoft cloud accounts. When someone signs in to Microsoft 365, Teams, or Azure, Entra ID checks who they are and what they may access. It provides single sign-on to thousands of third-party apps, manages users and groups, and supports multi-factor authentication, passwordless sign-in with passkeys and authenticator apps, and device registration.

The security features are a key reason companies use it. Conditional Access policies decide when to allow, block, or challenge sign-ins based on conditions such as location, device health, and risk level. Identity Protection uses machine learning to detect risky sign-ins and compromised accounts, and governance tools handle access reviews, entitlement management, and privileged access. It extends to customers and partners through external identity features, and increasingly to non-human identities such as apps and AI agents.

item.title: Microsoft Power Apps
item.description:
Power Apps lets people without a programming background build apps for their organization. Makers choose canvas apps, where you design screens by dragging controls, or model-driven apps that are generated from a data model. Typical uses include inspection forms, approval workflows, inventory trackers, and internal portals that replace spreadsheets and email chains. Apps run on web and mobile and integrate with Microsoft 365 and Teams.

It connects to a large range of data through connectors, including SharePoint, SQL Server, Salesforce, and Dataverse, Microsoft’s data platform. Power Automate adds workflow logic, and Power BI provides reporting. Copilot can create an app or a table from a plain-language description and help with formulas, and newer features allow building apps by chatting with an agent. Governance tools let IT manage environments and data policies.

item.title: Microsoft Security Copilot
item.description:
Security Copilot aims to relieve the pressure on overstretched security operations teams. An analyst can ask in plain language what happened in an incident, and Copilot gathers signals from Microsoft’s security products, summarizes the attack path, explains the alerts, and suggests next steps. It can write queries in languages like KQL, analyze suspicious scripts and files, and produce incident reports, saving time on routine tasks.

The product has moved toward agents. Purpose-built agents handle jobs such as triaging phishing alerts, assessing vulnerabilities, and prioritizing conditions that need attention, working with human oversight. It is embedded in the portals analysts already use, and plugins connect to non-Microsoft tools, so it can use data from other systems. Controls govern what it can access and do.

item.title: Mighty Networks
item.description:
Mighty Networks is a platform for building a membership community. A creator sets up a space with feeds, groups, live events, and online courses, and members join by paying a subscription or one-time fee. The pitch is an experience that feels like your own app, with mobile apps that can carry your brand.

Monetization is built in. Creators can charge for memberships, courses, and events, offer tiered access, and run bundles. The AI assistant helps with tasks such as naming a community, drafting posts and course outlines, and suggesting engagement ideas. Analytics show member activity, which helps community managers improve retention.

item.title: Mindtickle
item.description:
Mindtickle is a sales readiness platform. New hires follow structured learning paths with lessons and quizzes, and practice pitches by recording videos or role-playing with AI, receiving feedback. Managers review the practice and see how reps compare on skills.

The platform links training to results. It tracks which skills correlate with success, identifies gaps across a team, and connects with CRM data to see how readiness affects performance. AI features generate content, score practice sessions, and recommend coaching.

item.title: Mistral Vibe
item.description:
Vibe is Mistral’s agent for software work. The command-line version runs in a project directory, reads and writes files, searches code, runs shell commands, and tracks tasks, using Mistral’s coding models to carry out requests such as fixing bugs, adding features, and explaining code. It is open source under the Apache 2.0 license, written in Python, and integrates with editors such as Zed and with other tools.

The broader Vibe offering extends agent capabilities to office tasks and teams. It builds on Mistral’s Devstral coding models and its large general models, which are available through Mistral’s API and, for some, as open weights that organizations can run on their own servers. This flexibility is a selling point for companies and governments that want agents without relying on US cloud providers.

item.title: Mixpanel
item.description:
Mixpanel helps product teams understand behavior. You send events from your product, such as sign-ups, searches, and purchases, along with properties about users, and Mixpanel turns them into reports. Funnels show where people drop off, retention charts show who comes back, flows map the paths people take, and cohorts group users by behavior. Self-serve reports let product managers and marketers answer questions without writing SQL.

The platform includes more than charts. Session replay shows what users actually did, feature flags and experiments test changes, and lexicon tools manage the data schema. AI features let people ask questions in plain language and generate reports, summarize findings, and surface anomalies. Data can be connected from warehouses, and Mixpanel integrates with tools for marketing, support, and customer data pipelines.

item.title: Moderne
item.description:
Moderne makes large-scale code change practical. OpenRewrite is an open-source refactoring engine that applies automated recipes to code, such as upgrading Java versions or replacing a deprecated API. Moderne indexes an organization’s repositories and runs recipes across all of them, producing pull requests.

That addresses the problem of maintaining hundreds of services. Instead of each team doing the same migration by hand, a platform team can run a recipe once and review the results. Search and analysis tools find where patterns occur, and AI assists in creating recipes and handling changes that rules cannot.

item.title: MoEngage
item.description:
MoEngage is built for brands with mobile apps and large user bases. It collects behavior data such as app opens, purchases, and browsing, then lets marketers segment users and design campaigns across channels. Journeys can be built visually, so a user who abandons a cart gets a push notification, then an email if they don’t respond.

Analytics show how campaigns perform and how users move through funnels. AI features predict who is likely to churn or buy, choose the best time to send each message, and suggest content, and a generative assistant helps write copy. The platform integrates with data warehouses and other tools, and operates worldwide, with a strong presence in Asia.

item.title: MongoDB Atlas
item.description:
MongoDB stores data as flexible JSON-like documents instead of rows and columns, which suits applications whose data shape changes often. Atlas runs it as a managed service: it handles provisioning, backups, scaling, and security, and works across the major clouds. Developers connect with drivers for most languages, and features like replication and sharding support high availability and large datasets. A free tier allows small projects and learning.

For AI, Atlas offers vector search alongside the regular database, so applications can store embeddings and run similarity queries without moving data to a separate vector database. This supports retrieval-augmented generation, recommendations, and semantic search. MongoDB has also acquired a company that builds embedding and reranking models, and integrates with common AI frameworks such as LangChain and LlamaIndex. Full-text search, time-series, and analytics features sit in the same platform.

item.title: Morgen
item.description:
Morgen is a calendar and planner. Users connect Google, Outlook, iCloud, and other calendars to see everything in one view, and bring in tasks from tools like Notion, Todoist, and Linear. Tasks can be dragged onto the calendar to block time for them.

The planner feature suggests where tasks fit in the day, taking events, deadlines, and durations into account, and rearranges when plans change. Scheduling links let others book time, with rules for availability and buffers. Frames let users reserve time for certain types of work.

item.title: Motive
item.description:
Motive started as KeepTruckin with electronic logging devices that record drivers’ hours, which US regulations require for many commercial trucks. It expanded into a fleet platform with GPS tracking, vehicle diagnostics, and tools for compliance, dispatching, and maintenance, serving trucking companies, construction firms, and other businesses with vehicles on the road.

AI dashcams are a major product. A camera facing the road and the driver uses computer vision to detect events such as distracted driving, phone use, following too closely, and rolling stops, and alerts drivers in real time while sending clips to managers for coaching. Safety scoring, reports, and exoneration video after accidents help reduce incidents and insurance costs. The company also offers a fleet card and spend controls.

item.title: MURAL
item.description:
MURAL gives distributed teams a shared canvas. Participants add sticky notes, diagrams, images, and text to a large board at the same time, and facilitators run sessions with tools such as timers, private mode for individual thinking, voting, and guided agendas. A big library of templates covers retros, roadmaps, design sprints, and strategy exercises.

AI assists with the messy part of workshops, which is making sense of dozens of notes. It can group sticky notes by theme, summarize a board, and generate ideas to get a session started. Integrations with Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Jira, and Slack connect boards to the tools where work gets done.

item.title: MX
item.description:
MX is a financial data platform. It gathers account and transaction data from thousands of institutions, enriches it by cleaning merchant names and categorizing spending, and delivers it to banks, credit unions, and fintech apps that want to offer money management features.

Its products include account aggregation, a digital banking experience that institutions can embed, insights and budgeting tools, and data for lending decisions. AI improves categorization and personalization, and connections increasingly use direct bank APIs instead of screen scraping.

item.title: MyTherapy
item.description:
MyTherapy is a free medication reminder app. Users enter their drugs and schedule, receive alerts at the right times, and confirm each dose. The app also tracks health values such as blood pressure and weight, and records symptoms and mood, which builds a picture of how treatment is going.

Reports summarize adherence and measurements, giving doctors useful data at appointments. Family members can be set up to follow along, which helps those who care for relatives. The app supports many languages.

item.title: Nansen
item.description:
Nansen turns raw blockchain data into readable information. Every wallet on a public chain is an anonymous string of characters, so Nansen builds a database of labels, tagging wallets that belong to exchanges, funds, protocols, and traders with a track record. Seeing that a labeled fund bought a token is more informative than seeing an unknown address.

Dashboards track token flows, new token launches, NFT activity, and the holdings of tagged wallets. Alerts notify users when watched wallets move funds, and analytical tools help researchers study a project’s holders and trading patterns. An AI assistant answers questions about on-chain data in plain language, and it supports many chains.

item.title: NemoClaw
item.description:
OpenClaw is an open-source agent project that can carry out tasks on a user’s computer and accounts, which made it popular and also raised security worries. NemoClaw is NVIDIA’s response for organizations: it installs OpenClaw inside an isolated runtime, called OpenShell, with strict default permissions, so the agent can only touch what administrators allow. A privacy router helps decide which requests can use outside models and which stay local.

NVIDIA pairs the platform with its Nemotron models and with its NeMo software for building and managing agents, but says NemoClaw works on different hardware and with other models. It was announced with a group of enterprise partners and early integrations with agent frameworks, positioning NVIDIA to offer software as well as chips for the agent era.

item.title: NeuronWriter
item.description:
NeuronWriter is a content optimization tool. A user enters a keyword, the tool analyzes the pages that rank, and it produces a list of recommended terms, questions, and headings, along with a target length. As the writer drafts in its editor, a score shows how well the content covers the topic.

It includes an AI writing assistant for outlines and drafts, internal linking suggestions, and a way to plan content around topics. Competitor analysis shows what top pages do well. Agencies use it for client content because of its pricing.

item.title: NocoDB
item.description:
NocoDB turns a database into something that feels like Airtable. Connect it to an existing SQL database or create a new one, and users see tables as spreadsheets they can filter, sort, and edit, with views as kanban boards, galleries, calendars, and forms. Non-technical colleagues get access to data without learning SQL.

It generates REST and GraphQL APIs for tables, supports permissions and webhooks, and offers automation and an AI assistant to help with fields and queries. Because it is open source, teams can host it themselves and keep data on their own servers.

item.title: Nomi
item.description:
Nomi lets users build a personal AI companion. You choose a name, appearance, personality traits, and backstory, then chat by text or voice. The app emphasizes memory, so the character recalls details you shared in earlier conversations and builds a continuing relationship, which is what many users value about it.

Relationship type is configurable, and group chats and shared experiences add variety. Users can see the companion’s interests and send images, and the creators have promoted the idea of an emotionally rich AI that grows with the user. The app runs on mobile and web.

item.title: Notable
item.description:
Notable automates administrative work in healthcare. Its agents reach out to patients by text, phone, or app to schedule visits, collect forms, confirm insurance, and manage referrals, and they write the results into the health record. The goal is to free staff from repetitive tasks and improve patient access.

Integration is the key difference: agents work inside systems like Epic and others, performing steps in the same workflows staff use. Health systems deploy them for areas such as pre-visit intake, care gap outreach, and prior authorization support.

item.title: Notion Custom Agents
item.description: Custom Agents extend Notion AI from something you chat with into something that works on its own. A team sets up an agent with instructions and the content it can access, then chooses what should trigger it: a schedule, a comment on a page, a change to a database, an @mention, or messages in a public Slack channel. The agent then does the job, such as triaging incoming requests, compiling a weekly report, updating a tracker, or answering questions in a channel.

item.title: NVIDIA CUDA
item.description: CUDA is the software layer that lets programmers use an NVIDIA graphics processor for things other than graphics. You write functions called kernels, usually in C++ or Python, that run across thousands of GPU threads at once, which suits workloads built from large amounts of parallel math. Scientific simulation, video processing, and above all neural networks fit that description, so CUDA became the foundation for modern AI training and inference.

item.title: o9 Solutions
item.description:
o9 targets the planning process in big supply chains. Instead of separate systems for forecasting, inventory, production, and finance, it builds one connected model of the business, called the Enterprise Knowledge Graph, so a change in demand updates the supply plan and the financial outlook. Planners can run what-if scenarios to compare options before choosing.

Machine learning forecasts demand using sales history, promotions, weather, and other signals, and the platform recommends actions such as shifting inventory or changing production. Generative AI features let planners ask questions in natural language and summarize risks. Customers include consumer goods, retail, and manufacturing companies with complex networks.

item.title: OpenSolar
item.description:
OpenSolar helps solar installers and sales teams win jobs. A user enters an address, and the software pulls satellite imagery and builds a 3D model of the roof, where panels can be placed and shading analyzed. It estimates energy production and savings, then generates a proposal customers can view online and sign.

The platform includes tools for the whole sales process. A customer relationship manager tracks leads, a pricing engine builds quotes, and integrated financing lets homeowners compare loan or lease options. AI features automate roof detection and layout, which speeds up design for each prospect, and electrical design tools help with permit packages.

item.title: OpenTools
item.description:
OpenTools is a catalog for finding AI products. Visitors search or filter by what they want to do, see short descriptions and pricing information, and follow links to the tools. Beyond products, the site lists models and Model Context Protocol servers, which are useful to developers building agents.

Guides and news help readers understand what is new and how to use tools well. Builders can submit their products for listing, which is how most directories grow.

item.title: Optimizely
item.description:
Optimizely began as an A/B testing tool and grew into a suite for digital experiences. Teams use web experimentation to compare versions of pages, feature experimentation to test changes in apps behind feature flags, and personalization to show different content to different audiences. Statistical engines determine which variations win, and rollouts can be controlled to reduce risk.

The platform also includes content management and commerce. A CMS lets marketers create and manage web content, and commerce products support B2B and B2C stores, so a company can build, publish, test, and optimize in a single environment. AI features, under the Opal brand, help generate content, suggest experiment ideas, and run agents that automate steps in marketing workflows.

item.title: Oracle NetSuite
item.description:
NetSuite was one of the first cloud ERP systems and is widely used by growing companies. A single system runs financials, inventory, procurement, order management, billing, and customer relationship management, so departments work from the same data instead of reconciling spreadsheets. Industry editions adapt it for areas like wholesale distribution, manufacturing, retail, and software, and it supports multiple subsidiaries, currencies, and tax rules, which suits companies expanding internationally.

AI features sit across the suite. Generative tools can summarize records, draft emails and descriptions, and answer questions about data in plain language, while machine learning supports forecasting, anomaly detection, and automation of accounting tasks like matching invoices. Reporting and analytics tools let finance teams build dashboards, and SuiteScript and workflows allow customization.

item.title: OrcaSlicer
item.description:
OrcaSlicer prepares 3D models for printing. It loads a model, lets you orient it and add supports, then generates the toolpaths that tell the printer what to do. It grew out of Bambu Studio and Slic3r-family projects and has become popular because it offers many settings alongside sensible defaults.

Calibration is a standout feature. Built-in tests help tune flow rate, pressure advance, temperature, and retraction for each filament, which improves quality and consistency. It supports many printers through profiles, manages multiple materials and colors, and can send jobs to printers over a network.

item.title: Oura Ring
item.description:
Oura packs sensors into a ring that is comfortable to wear day and night. It tracks sleep stages, resting heart rate, heart rate variability, body temperature, and movement, then gives scores for sleep and readiness that suggest how hard to push each day. Many people choose it for sleep tracking, since a ring is less obtrusive than a watch in bed, and battery life lasts several days.

The app presents trends and offers guidance. Features cover cycle and fertility insights, stress and recovery information, activity goals, and workouts. An AI advisor lets users ask questions about their data in plain language and receive personalized suggestions. Oura works with Apple Health, Google Health Connect, and other apps, and it has partnered with companies in areas like glucose monitoring.

item.title: Paychex
item.description:
Paychex is one of the largest payroll providers in the United States. Businesses use it to pay employees, file payroll taxes, manage time and attendance, administer retirement and health benefits, and handle HR tasks such as onboarding and compliance. A defining feature is access to human specialists, which suits owners who do not want to figure out payroll rules on their own.

The Paychex Flex platform pulls these services into one system with mobile apps for employees and managers. AI features assist with answering HR questions, flagging payroll errors, and analyzing workforce data. The company also offers professional employer organization services, in which it co-employs workers and takes on benefits and compliance responsibilities. It acquired Paycor, a provider of HR and payroll software, to move further into mid-sized businesses.

item.title: Paycom
item.description:
Paycom is an HR and payroll platform built on one database for all functions. Employers manage hiring, onboarding, time and attendance, payroll, benefits, performance, and learning in a unified system, so data entered once appears everywhere. This design is meant to reduce errors from syncing separate tools.

Its best-known idea is Beti, which stands for Better Employee Transaction Interface. Employees review and approve their own timecards, expenses, and paid time off before payroll is run, which pushes corrections to the person who knows the data best and reduces payroll mistakes. Paycom has also added AI assistants for HR questions and tasks.

item.title: Paylocity
item.description:
Paylocity provides cloud HR and payroll software, primarily for mid-sized companies. Employers run payroll, manage benefits enrollment, track time and scheduling, handle onboarding and performance, and report on workforce data, all within one platform. A mobile app lets employees see pay stubs, request time off, and update details.

The company emphasizes employee experience and community features, such as company feeds, recognition, and surveys, in addition to core payroll. An AI assistant answers employee questions about pay, benefits, and company policy using the employer’s data, and helps managers and HR with drafting and analysis, which reduces the number of routine tickets.

item.title: Pendo
item.description:
Pendo helps product teams understand and improve their software. After adding a snippet to an application, Pendo records usage automatically: which pages and features people use, where they drop off, and how behavior varies by customer or segment. Product managers use dashboards, funnels, and retention reports to decide what to build and what to fix.

The platform lets teams act on insights without waiting for developers. In-app guides, tooltips, announcements, and checklists guide users through features, surveys and NPS collect feedback, and a roadmap tool captures feature requests. Session replay shows what people did, and AI features summarize feedback, suggest improvements, and analyze conversations with AI features inside products, which is a growing need as software adds assistants.

item.title: Percy
item.description:
Percy automates visual testing. Developers add it to their test suite, and on each code change it captures screenshots of pages and components across browsers and screen sizes. It compares them with an approved baseline and highlights the pixels that differ, so a reviewer can accept intended changes or catch accidental ones before they reach users.

Visual bugs, such as overlapping text, broken layouts, or missing images, often slip past functional tests, which only check behavior. Percy fills this gap and integrates with pull requests, so design and engineering can review changes together. AI helps ignore noise like anti-aliasing differences or dynamic content, which keeps the review list short.

item.title: Perplexity Computer
item.description: Perplexity Computer extends Perplexity from answering questions to doing work. You give it a goal, such as researching a market and building a report, tracking a set of sources, or assembling a presentation, and it plans the job, splits it into parts, and runs them, sometimes in parallel. Different steps are sent to different AI models depending on what they are good at, which is the central idea of the product.

item.title: Persefoni
item.description:
Persefoni helps companies calculate and report their greenhouse gas emissions. It collects data from energy bills, travel, procurement, and suppliers, applies emission factors, and calculates totals for direct emissions, purchased energy, and value chain emissions. The system keeps an audit trail so figures can be verified.

Reporting is a main use. The platform produces disclosures aligned with frameworks such as the GHG Protocol, CDP, and regional regulations, and helps set and track reduction targets. An AI assistant answers questions about methodology and data, and supports tasks like mapping spend data to emission categories.

item.title: Photomath
item.description:
Photomath makes it easy to get unstuck on math. You point your phone’s camera at a printed or handwritten problem, and the app recognizes it and shows the answer along with steps for solving it. It covers arithmetic, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, and calculus, and explains the reasoning for each step, so students can learn the method instead of copying an answer.

Further features support learning. Animated tutorials illustrate how steps work, multiple solution methods are available for some problems, and a graphing tool shows functions. Recent versions add AI-powered explanations that answer follow-up questions, and the app works in many languages. Teachers and parents use it to check work and see how a problem can be approached.

item.title: Physical Intelligence
item.description:
Physical Intelligence works on foundation models for robots. Most robots are programmed for one job, but the company aims to train a general model that can control many kinds of robots to do many tasks, such as folding laundry, clearing tables, and packing items, by learning from large amounts of robot data.

It has released research and open models, including the pi-zero family of vision-language-action models, along with code that lets other researchers try them. These models take camera images and instructions in natural language and output actions for the robot. The company collaborates with robot makers and collects data across different hardware.

item.title: Pigment
item.description:
Pigment is a modern take on planning software. Finance teams build models of their company, including headcount, revenue, and spend, in an environment that feels familiar to spreadsheet users but works with large data volumes and multiple dimensions. Plans link across departments, so a hiring plan updates the budget automatically.

It supports scenario planning, which lets teams test the impact of different assumptions side by side, and produces dashboards and reports for executives. AI agents help analyze variances, generate commentary, and build parts of models from prompts. Integrations bring in data from ERP and CRM systems and data warehouses.

item.title: Planhat
item.description:
Planhat is a customer platform built for subscription businesses. It connects to a company’s tools and data, builds a profile for each account, and shows health, usage trends, revenue, and conversations in one place. Teams use it to prepare for renewals and spot upsell opportunities.

Automation and workflows trigger tasks and outreach when something changes, such as a drop in usage or an upcoming renewal. Dashboards and reports show retention and growth, and AI summarizes accounts and suggests actions.

item.title: Plausible
item.description:
Plausible keeps analytics simple. A tiny script collects page views, visitors, referrers, devices, and locations without using cookies or storing personal data, so most sites do not need a consent banner for it. The dashboard fits on a single page, which makes it quick to read for people who don’t want to learn a complex tool.

It supports goals and events, so site owners can track signups or purchases, and funnels for conversion steps. Features like UTM tracking and a stats API round out the basics. The code is open source, and users can self-host a free community edition or pay for the hosted service, which is run from European servers.

item.title: Poised
item.description:
Poised is a communication coach for online meetings. During a call, the app runs privately on the user’s device, tracks how they speak, and shows real-time prompts such as slowing down or reducing filler words. After the call, it provides a summary and trends over time.

Practice features let users rehearse presentations or interviews and get analysis. It is designed for professionals, students, and non-native English speakers who want to improve how they come across.

item.title: Postscript
item.description:
Postscript focuses on text message marketing for online stores. It connects to Shopify, collects subscribers through popups and checkout opt-ins, and lets merchants send campaigns about sales and product launches. Automated flows trigger messages for events like abandoned carts, browse behavior, and order updates, which tend to produce strong results.

Segmentation uses shopping data, such as purchase history and product interest, to tailor messages. Two-way conversations let customers reply and get help from a team member, and an AI assistant helps draft messages and suggests offers. Analytics tie texts to revenue so merchants can see what pays off.

item.title: Prezi
item.description:
Prezi stands out for its zooming interface. Instead of a linear deck, you lay out ideas spatially on a big canvas and the presentation moves among them with motion, which gives viewers a sense of how topics relate and can make a talk feel more dynamic. The approach suits overview-and-detail stories and keeps attention better for some audiences than traditional slides.

The product line has expanded. Prezi Video overlays presentation content next to the speaker on video calls and recordings, Prezi Design creates interactive visual content, and the AI assistant generates presentations from a prompt, rewrites text, and builds structure. Templates, brand kits, and analytics help teams use it for sales, teaching, and training.

item.title: Product Hunt
item.description:
Product Hunt started as a simple list of cool new products and became a standard place for startups to debut. Makers submit a product with a tagline, description, images, and a link, and the community upvotes and comments throughout the day. Top-ranked products earn visibility, and a launch can bring early users, feedback, and press attention. The site covers apps, developer tools, hardware, and books.

For readers, it’s a way to see what is new. You can browse by day, week, or month, follow topics such as artificial intelligence, productivity, or design, and read discussions that often include makers answering questions. Collections and newsletters curate products, and a leaderboard highlights trending launches. Makers can also post updates and use the site’s tools to share a launch checklist and gather reviews.

item.title: QGIS
item.description:
QGIS gives anyone access to professional-level mapping and spatial analysis at no cost. Users load vector and raster data from files, databases, and web services, style maps, edit geometries, and run analyses such as buffers, overlays, terrain analysis, and routing. A processing toolbox bundles hundreds of algorithms, and it integrates with GRASS and SAGA for specialized tasks. It handles many formats and projections, and print layouts produce publication-quality maps.

The plugin ecosystem is a major strength. Community-developed plugins add functions for data download, cartography, hydrology, field data collection, and more, and Python scripting supports automation. In AI-related work, plugins bring in machine learning for tasks like classifying land cover, detecting objects in imagery, and using models such as Segment Anything for segmentation. Users run QGIS Server to publish maps and QField to collect data on mobile devices.

item.title: Qlik
item.description: Qlik is known for its associative engine, which treats all the data in an app as connected. When you click a value in a chart, everything else updates to show related data, and values that are unrelated are shown as excluded, which helps users discover connections they did not think to query. This differs from tools that require predefined queries and has been a selling point for business users exploring data.

item.title: Qualio
item.description:
Qualio is designed for regulated life sciences companies that need a quality system but not a heavy enterprise one. Teams write and approve controlled documents, assign and track training, manage change requests and corrective actions, and keep the records auditors expect, all in a cloud app with electronic signatures.

The product is aimed at smaller and growth-stage companies. Pre-built templates and workflows speed up setup, and the platform adds modules for events, risk, and supplier qualification. AI features help draft and review documents and answer questions about the quality system.

item.title: Questel
item.description:
Questel serves people who work with patents and trademarks. Its search tools let users query large databases of patents from many countries, apply classifications, and find prior art for patentability and infringement questions. Analytics show landscapes of who is filing in a field and trends over time.

The company also offers portfolio management, with docketing, renewals, and workflow tools for tracking deadlines across jurisdictions, along with services for filing and annuity payments. AI features assist with semantic search, summarization, and drafting, helping professionals review large numbers of documents faster. Its products come from combining several IP software companies.

item.title: QuickBooks
item.description: QuickBooks is the accounting software most small businesses and their accountants know. QuickBooks Online runs in a browser and on phones, connects to bank accounts to import transactions, sends invoices, tracks bills and expenses, and produces profit and loss statements, balance sheets, and cash flow reports. It also supports sales tax tracking, inventory in higher tiers, and multi-user access for bookkeepers and accountants. A desktop edition remains for businesses that prefer installed software.

item.title: QuickNode
item.description:
QuickNode offers blockchain infrastructure as a service. Running a node for a blockchain takes hardware, storage, and maintenance, so QuickNode hosts them and gives developers endpoints they connect to over standard protocols. Apps use these endpoints to fetch balances, read smart contract data, and submit transactions.

Beyond basic access, the platform includes tools for data and automation. Add-ons offer token and NFT APIs, streaming of on-chain events, and workflows that move blockchain data into databases. It supports many networks, including Ethereum, Solana, and layer 2 chains, with dashboards for usage and performance monitoring.

item.title: Qure.ai
item.description:
Qure.ai makes AI tools for radiology. Its software reads medical images and highlights suspected abnormalities, such as signs of tuberculosis or pneumonia on a chest X-ray, or a hemorrhage on a head CT. The software returns an annotated image and a short summary, so radiologists and clinicians can prioritize urgent cases.

The company is known for working in settings with few radiologists. Screening programs for tuberculosis use its tools to triage chest X-rays quickly, and hospitals use it to speed up emergency reads. It has regulatory clearances in several markets and integrates with PACS systems, the software that stores and displays medical images.

item.title: Rasa
item.description:
Rasa is a toolkit for developers who build conversational assistants. It started with machine learning components for understanding user messages and managing dialogue, and has evolved to combine language models with structured business logic. Teams define flows for tasks such as updating an address or booking an appointment, and the model handles the language.

Control is its main appeal. Companies can host Rasa themselves, keeping conversations and customer data within their own environment, and decide exactly what the assistant is allowed to do. That suits banks, telecoms, and healthcare organizations with strict privacy and compliance needs, and it reduces the risk of a language model improvising.

item.title: Rask AI
item.description:
Rask AI makes video localization simpler. You upload a video or provide a link, and the tool transcribes the speech, translates it into one of many languages, and produces a new audio track with a synthetic voice. Editing tools let you correct the transcript and translation before generating the final version.

Additional features improve the result. Voice cloning keeps the speaker’s voice character in the new language, and lip sync adjusts the mouth movements to match the dubbed audio. It also handles multiple speakers, subtitles, and exports, and offers an API for teams that localize at scale.

item.title: ReadMe
item.description:
ReadMe helps companies document their APIs. Teams upload an OpenAPI specification, and the platform generates an interactive reference with code samples in several languages and a try-it console that makes real requests with the reader’s own key. Guides and changelogs sit alongside, forming a single developer hub.

It is also a source of insight. API owners see which endpoints developers use, where requests fail, and which pages cause confusion, so documentation can improve based on evidence. Personalized docs show a logged-in developer their own API keys and data, which makes onboarding faster. An AI assistant answers questions from the documentation.

item.title: Redis
item.description: Redis stores data in memory, which makes reading and writing it extremely fast. Developers use it as a cache that sits in front of a slower database, as a session store for logged-in users, as a message queue, and for leaderboards, rate limiting, and counters. Its data types, such as lists, sets, sorted sets, hashes, and streams, make these patterns easy to build with simple commands. It’s one of the most widely deployed pieces of infrastructure on the web.

item.title: Remote
item.description:
Remote is a global employment platform. A company that wants to hire someone in another country normally needs a legal entity there, which is slow and costly. With Remote as the employer of record, the worker is legally employed by Remote locally, while the company directs their daily work. Remote handles contracts, payroll, taxes, benefits, and statutory requirements.

The platform also supports contractors, offers tools for onboarding, expenses, and equipment, and provides local compliance knowledge across many countries. A global payroll product helps companies that already have entities coordinate payments, and AI features assist HR teams with questions and workflows. The company has built its own entities in many countries rather than relying on partners.

item.title: Replit Agent 4
item.description: Replit Agent 4 continues the idea that you can describe software and have an agent build it. In the Replit workspace, you explain what you want, and the agent writes the code, sets up the environment and database, tests the result, and deploys it. You review progress, give feedback in plain language, and ask for changes. Replit says this version is substantially faster than its predecessor, which matters because building an app involves many steps.

item.title: Retell AI
item.description:
Retell provides the infrastructure for voice agents. A developer defines an agent’s prompt and tools, connects a phone number, and the platform handles speech recognition, the language model, speech synthesis, and call control with natural turn-taking and interruption handling.

Use cases include answering customer calls, scheduling appointments, qualifying leads, and following up with customers. Integrations with calendars and CRMs let agents take actions, and analytics show call outcomes. Handoff to humans is supported.

item.title: Rocket Lawyer
item.description:
Rocket Lawyer is aimed at people who need legal help without a full law firm engagement. Members answer questions in an interview format and the service generates documents such as lease agreements, NDAs, wills, and operating agreements. Documents can be signed electronically and stored, and templates are tailored to the user’s state.

Beyond documents, membership gives access to attorneys through ask-a-lawyer services and, for some matters, discounted consultations. Small businesses use it for formation, contracts, and compliance support. AI tools help explain legal terms and draft documents, and are positioned as a way to get started before consulting a professional.

item.title: RoseTTAFold
item.description:
RoseTTAFold predicts how a chain of amino acids folds into a three-dimensional protein. Knowing a protein’s shape helps scientists understand what it does and how to target it with drugs. The model was developed at the Institute for Protein Design and the University of Washington, around the same time as AlphaFold, and offered a comparable approach with a three-track neural network.

The work has grown into a family. RoseTTAFold All-Atom models complexes that include small molecules, DNA, and other components, and RFdiffusion generates new protein backbones for design tasks such as binders and enzymes. Together these tools support a shift from predicting existing proteins to creating new ones, with applications in medicine and materials.

item.title: Salesforce Agentforce
item.description: Agentforce lets companies deploy AI agents that work inside Salesforce. An agent might answer customer questions, qualify inbound leads, schedule meetings, or update records, using the company’s own data and rules. Builders define an agent’s role, topics, and the actions it may take, connect it to knowledge and data, and test it before release. A reasoning engine decides how to handle each request, and guardrails limit what the agent may do.

item.title: SAP Concur
item.description:
Concur is a staple of corporate finance. Employees book travel, capture receipts with a phone, and submit expense reports, which flow through approvals and into accounting systems. Policies are applied automatically, flagging out-of-policy spending, and credit card feeds reduce manual entry. Finance teams use it to control costs, reimburse employees, and meet audit requirements.

The platform has grown to include invoice and travel management, with integrations to airlines, hotels, and payment providers. AI supports automatic receipt reading, categorization, audit of expenses to detect errors or fraud, and assistance through SAP’s Joule for answering questions and completing tasks. Reporting provides visibility into travel and spending trends.

item.title: SAP Joule
item.description:
Joule is the assistant inside SAP’s software. Instead of navigating menus in an ERP, finance, or HR system, users ask questions such as which invoices are overdue or what the status of an order is, and Joule retrieves the answer from live business data. It respects the user’s permissions, so it only shows what that person is allowed to see.

It has grown from a question-and-answer helper into a platform for agents. Prebuilt Joule agents handle tasks like processing invoices or supporting recruiters, and Joule Studio lets customers and partners build their own agents and skills that work across SAP and non-SAP systems. SAP presents this as part of a broader business AI platform that connects data and models.

item.title: SAP Signavio
item.description:
Signavio helps companies understand how their processes really work. Teams model processes in a visual notation so everyone can see the intended steps, owners, and rules, and store them in a shared repository. This makes it easier to document, improve, and standardize work across departments.
