Process mining adds evidence. By reading event logs from systems like SAP ERP, it reconstructs what happened in practice, revealing delays, rework, and variants that differ from the designed flow. Analysts can then quantify the impact and decide what to fix. Collaboration and journey modeling tools help teams plan transformations such as moving to a new ERP.

item.title: Sardine
item.description:
Sardine is a fraud and compliance platform for financial services. It collects signals about the device and the way a user interacts, such as typing patterns and whether a session looks automated, and combines them with transaction data to score the risk of an account opening, a payment, or a login. Decisions happen in milliseconds, so legitimate customers face little friction.

The platform covers a range of risk. It addresses account takeover, payment fraud, scams, and identity fraud, and integrates with know your customer and anti-money laundering workflows. AI agents help compliance teams by gathering evidence, reviewing alerts, and drafting case notes, which reduces the manual work behind investigations.

item.title: SavvyCal
item.description:
SavvyCal tries to make scheduling feel less like a chore. Instead of a one-sided grid of available times, the invitee can overlay their own calendar, which helps them see conflicts and pick a time that works for both sides. The host can also mark preferred slots, so the invitee sees which options are ideal.

Other features cover business needs. Teams can use round robin and collective scheduling, polls help find a time for groups, and links can be personalized for different meetings. Integrations connect to calendars, video tools, and CRMs, and payments can be collected for paid sessions. Branding options keep the experience consistent.

item.title: Scopus
item.description:
Scopus indexes scholarly journals, books, and conference papers across science, technology, medicine, social sciences, and the arts and humanities, and tracks citations among them. Researchers use it to search literature, follow citation trails, and find related work. It’s curated: content must meet quality criteria to be included, which gives the database a reputation for reliability.

Institutions rely on Scopus for research evaluation. It provides author profiles with h-index and other metrics, journal rankings such as CiteScore, and tools for analyzing the output of departments and universities. Funders and universities use these numbers in assessments, rankings, and hiring, which makes the database influential, and sometimes controversial because of the weight put on metrics.

item.title: Secureframe
item.description:
Secureframe automates compliance work. It integrates with cloud providers, code repositories, identity systems, and HR tools to check that required controls are in place, gather evidence for auditors, and alert teams when something drifts out of compliance.

The platform also manages policies, employee training, vendor risk, and a trust page for customers. AI drafts policies, maps controls across frameworks, and fills in security questionnaires from a company’s own answers, saving time during sales cycles.

item.title: Securiti
item.description:
Securiti addresses the problem that companies often do not know where their sensitive data lives. It scans cloud storage, databases, SaaS apps, and data pipelines, classifies personal and confidential information, and builds a map of where it sits and who can access it. This approach is known as data security posture management.

On top of that, it automates privacy and governance tasks. Teams respond to data subject requests, manage consent, run privacy assessments, and enforce policies that block risky access. For AI, Securiti helps discover models and data feeding them, apply guardrails, and meet emerging regulations, which has become a priority as companies adopt generative AI.

item.title: Seeing AI
item.description:
Seeing AI turns a smartphone into a talking camera. Point it at printed text and it reads aloud, short text instantly or whole documents with guidance for framing the page. It recognizes products by scanning barcodes, identifies currency notes, describes colors, and detects light levels, helping with everyday tasks like finding the right can in a pantry.

More advanced channels describe scenes and people. The app can give a description of a photo or surroundings, recognize friends who have been added with consent, and describe their apparent expressions. Handwriting reading and image exploration by touch are available on supported devices, and newer versions use generative AI to give more detailed descriptions and answer follow-up questions.

item.title: SemiLaunch
item.description:
SemiLaunch gives small makers a place to announce a product. Makers submit their project, which appears in a weekly cohort, and visitors browse, vote, and comment. Top products are highlighted, helping early-stage founders gain attention and feedback.

The weekly format differs from daily launch sites, giving products more time to collect votes. Listings also serve as backlinks and discovery for new tools in directories.

Visibility depends on community size. SemiLaunch has a free tier and paid promotion options. Alternatives include Product Hunt, Peerlist, BetaList, Indie Hackers, and Dang.ai. SemiLaunch suits indie makers looking for launch exposure.

item.title: SentinelOne
item.description:
SentinelOne is a cybersecurity company known for autonomous endpoint protection. Its agent runs on computers and servers, uses machine learning to detect malicious behavior on the device, and can respond automatically by isolating a machine, killing a process, or rolling back changes made by ransomware. That local decision-making works even when a device is offline.

The Singularity platform extends this across the environment. It brings together endpoint detection and response with cloud workload security, identity threat detection, vulnerability management, and a data lake that collects logs from many sources for threat hunting. Purple AI is a generative assistant that lets analysts ask questions in natural language, such as whether a suspicious file appeared elsewhere, and turns them into queries, summarizes findings, and suggests next steps.

item.title: ServiceNow Otto
item.description:
Otto is ServiceNow’s way of unifying its AI products into a single assistant. It combines the conversational search that came from Moveworks, the workflow skills of Now Assist, and an agentic interface on the Now Platform. An employee can ask for help in plain language, and Otto finds an answer or starts the workflow that does the job, such as requesting access or opening an IT ticket.

The point is action across systems. ServiceNow positions it as an assistant that works with the enterprise tools a person already uses, not just answering from a knowledge base. Governance is a major theme: AI Control Tower tracks the agents, logs interactions, and enforces policies, which matters when many agents are acting at once.

item.title: Shortform
item.description:
Shortform sits between a short summary and the book itself. Each guide covers a book’s ideas in depth, adds analysis comparing it with other books, and includes exercises that help readers apply the lessons. Readers can use them to decide what to read in full or to review a book they have finished.

The library spans business, psychology, history, and self-help, and includes guides to classic works and some articles and fiction. AI features offer a chat assistant for asking questions about a guide.

item.title: Sierra
item.description:
Sierra focuses on replacing scripted chatbots with agents that can actually resolve customer issues. Companies such as consumer brands and subscription services deploy Sierra agents to answer questions, process returns, change plans, schedule appointments, and handle other tasks by connecting to back-end systems. The agent follows the company’s policies and tone, and hands off to a human when needed.

Several elements distinguish its approach. An Agent OS provides the tools for building, testing, and monitoring agents, with simulation and evaluation to catch problems before customers see them, and supports voice and messaging channels. The company often uses outcome-based pricing, where customers pay for resolved conversations instead of seats, which aligns cost with value. It combines multiple language models to improve reliability.

item.title: Skool
item.description:
Skool is a simple platform for running a community. Members post in a feed, take courses in a classroom section, attend events from a shared calendar, and earn points for participating, which unlock levels on a leaderboard. The gamification is meant to keep people engaged without a lot of setup.

The pricing and design are deliberately simple. Skool charges a flat fee for community owners and offers few customization options, so creators spend time on content and members, not on configuring a site. Communities can charge a monthly or annual fee, and a built-in discovery page, plus members’ direct messages, helps people find groups.

item.title: Slackbot
item.description:
Slackbot used to be a simple helper that answered canned questions. It has been rebuilt as an agent that works across a Slack workspace. You can ask it to find a decision made in a channel, summarize a thread, draft a message or a document, schedule a meeting from calendar availability, or pull together information from several conversations, and it answers using content you already have permission to see.

Beyond answering, it can take actions. Slackbot can post, set reminders, update records through connected apps, and delegate longer tasks to agents built with Salesforce’s Agentforce, tying Slack more closely to the rest of Salesforce’s platform. Slack has used models from partners to power it, and the assistant adapts to the user’s context and role within the workspace.

item.title: Smartlead
item.description:
Smartlead is built for outbound email at scale. Users connect many mailboxes, and the platform spreads sends across them, adjusts volume, and warms up new accounts so messages reach inboxes. Sequences, follow-ups, and reply management handle campaign logic.

Agencies value its multi-client workspaces, unified inbox, and analytics. AI helps personalize openers and classify replies. Integrations connect with lead databases and CRMs.

Smartlead is paid, with plans by active leads and emails. Cold email is regulated, and sending at scale damages domains if done badly. Alternatives include Instantly, lemlist, Apollo, Reply.io, and Woodpecker. Smartlead suits agencies and outbound teams.

item.title: SnapGene
item.description:
SnapGene gives molecular biologists a visual, reliable way to plan DNA work. Researchers open or create plasmid and DNA sequences, see features such as genes and promoters automatically annotated, and simulate cloning steps like restriction digests, ligations, Gibson assembly, and Gateway cloning before going to the bench. The tool shows resulting maps and sequences, helping avoid costly mistakes.

It has a large library of standard vectors and features, tools for designing primers, and a viewer that lets collaborators open files without a license. Sequence comparison, alignments, and the ability to import from databases support daily lab tasks. Files are shared in a format that is widely used across the field. A server version supports team libraries.

item.title: Snorkel AI
item.description:
Snorkel started as an academic project that asked whether people could label data programmatically. Instead of tagging thousands of examples one by one, a domain expert writes labeling functions, which are rules, patterns, or model calls that vote on a label. Snorkel combines their noisy outputs into training labels, a technique called weak supervision.

The company has moved toward the needs of generative AI. Its platform helps enterprises curate data for fine-tuning and evaluating language models, with experts reviewing samples and defining what good answers look like. A network of expert annotators supplies specialized data in areas like law, medicine, and finance, and tools measure how models perform on custom benchmarks.

item.title: SonarQube
item.description:
SonarQube analyzes source code without running it. It checks for bugs, security vulnerabilities, hardcoded secrets, code smells, duplication, and test coverage, and reports issues in a dashboard and in pull requests. Teams define quality gates, such as no new critical bugs, which can block a merge when code does not meet the standard, so problems are caught early in development.

It integrates with CI/CD systems like GitHub Actions, GitLab, Jenkins, and Azure DevOps, and with IDEs through SonarLint, which highlights issues as you type. AI features include CodeFix, which suggests changes for issues it finds, and capabilities designed to check AI-generated code, an area of growing concern as more code is written by assistants. It supports a large number of languages and frameworks.

item.title: Speak
item.description:
Speak puts spoken practice first. Instead of tapping through vocabulary drills, you speak aloud in lessons that simulate real situations such as ordering food, introducing yourself, or having a job interview. The app listens, corrects pronunciation and grammar, and prompts you to try again, so you gain confidence speaking, which many apps neglect.

An AI tutor handles open-ended conversation. You can discuss topics you choose, practice roleplays, and ask the tutor to explain mistakes, with the system adapting to your level. The app began with a focus on English for Korean speakers and has expanded to teach other languages, with courses designed for particular native languages. It was developed with backing from OpenAI’s startup fund.

item.title: Splunk
item.description:
Splunk made machine data searchable. It ingests logs, metrics, and events from servers, applications, networks, and cloud services, indexes them, and lets users search and visualize with its Search Processing Language. Companies use it to troubleshoot outages, monitor performance, and investigate security incidents, and it has been a mainstay of security operations centers for many years.

The product line includes Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Cloud for core analytics, Enterprise Security as a SIEM for threat detection, and observability tools for infrastructure and application monitoring. AI features include an assistant that helps write searches from plain language and summarizes findings, and machine learning for anomaly detection. Cisco acquired Splunk and is integrating it with its networking and security products.

item.title: SpyFu
item.description:
SpyFu is a competitor research tool. Enter a domain and it reveals the keywords that site ranks for in organic search, the keywords it buys on Google Ads, and how those change over time. The ad history is a distinctive feature, since you can see which ad copy a competitor has tested and kept running.

That data helps marketers decide where to compete. Keyword research shows search volume and difficulty, backlink tools find link opportunities, and rank tracking monitors progress. Agencies use the reports to pitch clients, and PPC managers use the ad history to find ideas and gaps in their own campaigns.

item.title: Squarespace
item.description:
Squarespace appeals to people who want an attractive site without a developer. You choose a template, change the content with a visual editor, and publish with hosting, security, and a domain included. Its designs are known for clean layouts and good typography, which makes it popular with creatives, small businesses, restaurants, and portfolio sites.

The platform goes beyond static pages. Built-in commerce handles products, subscriptions, and checkout, email campaigns support marketing, and Acuity Scheduling covers appointments. AI features include a site builder that generates a starting design and content from answers to a few questions, text-writing assistance, and tools for improving search visibility. Analytics show traffic and sales.

item.title: Squibler
item.description:
Squibler is a writing platform for longer projects. Authors plan a book with outlines and a corkboard, write in a distraction-free editor, and track characters, settings, and plot threads. An AI assistant generates outlines, suggests plot developments, and drafts text on request.

It targets novelists, nonfiction authors, and scriptwriters, with templates for different forms and export to formats ready for self-publishing. Collaboration features let editors comment.

Squibler has a free trial and paid plans. AI-drafted text should be edited heavily, and publishing platforms ask authors to disclose AI-generated content. Alternatives include Scrivener, Sudowrite, Atticus, Novelcrafter, and Google Docs. Squibler suits authors organizing long manuscripts.

item.title: Storylane
item.description:
Storylane is an interactive demo platform. A user records their product with a browser extension that captures screenshots or the underlying page, then adds hotspots, tooltips, and callouts to guide viewers through a story. The result is a demo that prospects can click through on their own, without needing a sandbox or a live call.

Teams use it across the sales cycle. Marketing embeds demos on landing pages, sales sends personalized versions in outreach emails, and customer success uses them for onboarding. AI features add voiceovers, translations into other languages, and personalization of names and logos for each prospect. Analytics show who viewed a demo and where they dropped off.

item.title: Storytel
item.description:
Storytel gives readers and listeners unlimited access to a library through a monthly subscription. The company began in Sweden and is a major audiobook service across the Nordics, with strong local-language catalogs in many markets, including Spanish, Polish, and Indian languages. Listeners use the mobile app to stream or download books and can adjust speed and set sleep timers.

The service has experimented with AI. VoiceSwitcher lets a listener change between the original human narrator and a synthetic voice for the same book, which helps with books that would not otherwise be recorded. Storytel also uses AI voices to expand its catalog and to translate books, an approach that has drawn debate about the role of human narrators.

item.title: Streamlit
item.description: Streamlit is built for data scientists who want to share work without learning web development. You write a Python script and add calls like text input, sliders, charts, and buttons, and Streamlit produces an interactive web app that reruns the script when the user changes something. This model is simple enough that people can make an app in minutes, and it has become a standard for internal tools and demos.

item.title: Stripe Agentic Commerce Suite
item.description:
As AI agents begin to shop and pay on behalf of people, merchants and payment systems need a way to handle it. Stripe’s suite helps businesses become discoverable to agents: a merchant uploads a product catalog, chooses which agent platforms to sell through, and Stripe handles discovery, checkout, and payments.

It builds on open protocols. The Agentic Commerce Protocol, developed with OpenAI, defines how an agent and a merchant negotiate a checkout. The Machine Payments Protocol, written with Tempo, lets agents and services coordinate payments in code, including small recurring transactions. Stripe also supports an agent wallet and stablecoin payments over the x402 protocol, and it issues limited-use tokens so an agent can spend within set limits.

item.title: Substack
item.description: Substack makes it simple to start a paid newsletter. A writer creates a publication, writes posts in an editor, and sends them to subscribers by email and on the web. The platform handles hosting, email delivery, and payments, so there is no technical setup. Writers can offer free and paid tiers, and subscribers pay monthly or annually, with Substack taking a percentage of paid subscriptions, in addition to payment processing fees.

item.title: Sumsub
item.description:
Sumsub provides identity verification for online services that must know who their customers are. A user photographs an ID document and takes a selfie, and Sumsub checks that the document is real, matches the person, and that a live person is present, which helps block stolen identities and deepfakes. Results come back in seconds or minutes.

Beyond onboarding, the platform covers compliance. It screens users against sanctions and politically exposed persons lists, monitors transactions for suspicious behavior, and supports business verification for companies. Fraud prevention features detect fake documents, duplicate accounts, and bots, and a case management dashboard lets compliance staff review flagged applicants.

item.title: SuperAGI
item.description:
SuperAGI appeared during the first wave of autonomous agent interest. It offered a framework and dashboard for creating agents that use tools, with features for running several agents at once, managing resources, and viewing performance.

The company later built applications on top of the framework for sales and marketing automation. Many agent frameworks have emerged since, and the field has moved toward different designs and commercial platforms.

SuperAGI is open source, with paid products. Check its repository for current activity. Alternatives include LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK, and Dify. SuperAGI suits developers who want to explore an open agent platform.

item.title: Superwhisper
item.description:
Superwhisper is a dictation tool. You press a shortcut, speak, and the text appears wherever your cursor is, in an email, a document, or a code editor. Because it can run speech recognition models on your own machine, nothing has to be sent to the cloud, which matters for privacy and works without an internet connection.

Modes make it more than plain transcription. A mode can clean up filler words, format the text as an email or meeting notes, translate it, or follow a custom prompt that uses a language model to rewrite what you said. It also understands context from the app you are in, and supports many languages and voice models, including cloud options for higher accuracy.

item.title: Surge AI
item.description:
Surge AI supplies the human judgment that goes into modern language models. Labs need people to compare answers, write ideal responses, and grade quality, and these ratings train models through techniques like RLHF. Surge recruits and manages annotators with specialized skills, such as coding, writing, and expertise in science, law, or medicine.

Its pitch is quality over crowd volume. Careful screening, training, and quality checks aim to produce data that is more accurate than what general crowd platforms deliver. Services include building evaluation sets, adversarial testing to find model weaknesses, and custom datasets for specific tasks. The company works with large AI developers and publishes research on data quality.

item.title: SurveyMonkey
item.description:
SurveyMonkey is one of the best-known survey tools. Users create surveys with a drag-and-drop builder, choose from templates for customer satisfaction, employee engagement, market research, and events, and share them by link, email, or embedding. Question logic, branching, and randomization allow more sophisticated designs, and responses appear in real time with charts and filters.

AI features aim to make surveys better and analysis quicker. The assistant can build a survey from a description, suggest improved wording to avoid bias, and analyze open-ended responses by identifying themes and sentiment. A panel service lets researchers purchase responses from target audiences, and integrations connect results to tools like Salesforce, Slack, and Tableau.

item.title: Synthesizer V
item.description:
Synthesizer V is a singing voice synthesizer. A musician enters notes in a piano roll, types lyrics under each note, and the software sings them in a chosen voice. Parameters control pitch, vibrato, breathiness, and timing, so a producer can shape the performance rather than accept a flat robotic output.

The AI voice databases are the main attraction. They are trained on real singers and sound more natural than older concatenative systems, and some support several languages with a single voice. Vocal modes change the style, such as a softer or more intense delivery. Synthesizer V runs as a standalone editor or as a plugin in digital audio workstations, and a free version offers limited features.

item.title: Synthflow
item.description:
Synthflow is a no-code voice agent platform. A user designs the call flow in a visual editor, picks a voice, connects a phone number, and the agent handles calls, such as answering questions, booking appointments, and qualifying leads. Integrations connect calendars and CRMs.

Agencies resell the platform with white-label options, building agents for dental offices, home services, and similar businesses. Analytics show call outcomes and transcripts.

Synthflow is paid, with plans by minutes. Voice agents need testing for accuracy and disclosure of AI use. Alternatives include Retell AI, Vapi, Bland AI, Air AI, and PolyAI. Synthflow suits agencies and small businesses deploying voice agents.

item.title: Syte
item.description:
Syte brings visual search to e-commerce. A shopper uploads a photo or taps on an image, and the system finds similar items in the store’s catalog. Computer vision also tags products with detailed attributes, which improves search, filters, and recommendations.

Retailers use it for shop-the-look features, similar item suggestions, and personalization. Integrations work with common e-commerce platforms, and generative AI supports conversational shopping assistants.

Syte is sold to retailers on subscription. Alternatives include Algolia, Bloomreach, Vue.ai, Klevu, and Google Lens integrations. Syte suits fashion and home retailers with large catalogs.

item.title: Talkspace
item.description:
Talkspace lets people get mental health care remotely. Users complete an assessment, are matched with a licensed therapist, and can communicate through messaging, live video, or audio sessions, which makes treatment convenient and sometimes more affordable than in-person visits. Psychiatry services provide evaluations and medication management where appropriate.

A major difference from some competitors is insurance coverage: many users can pay with commercial insurance or Medicare plans through Talkspace, and employers and health plans offer it as a benefit. The company has added AI tools for matching, documentation, and safety monitoring, and is exploring ways AI can support providers while keeping therapy human. It publishes research on outcomes.

item.title: Tavus
item.description:
Tavus builds AI humans. A person records a short sample, and the platform creates a digital replica that can speak a script, so one recording can become thousands of personalized videos with each viewer’s name and details. This suits sales outreach and customer communications.

The company also provides conversational video agents, which see and hear a user and respond in real time with a face and voice, through an API. Use cases include interviews, coaching, and customer service.

item.title: Teachable
item.description:
Teachable is a platform for people who want to sell what they know. A creator uploads video lessons, text, and quizzes, organizes them into a course, sets a price, and publishes it on a branded school site. Students enroll, pay, and track their progress, and the creator gets sales and engagement data.

The platform handles the business side. It processes payments in many currencies, supports subscriptions, bundles, and coupons, and offers tools for affiliate programs and email marketing. Coaching products and downloadable files can be sold alongside courses, and certificates reward completion. AI features help draft course outlines and descriptions.

item.title: Temporal
item.description:
Temporal addresses a hard part of building reliable software: making long-running, multi-step processes survive failures. Developers write workflows in an ordinary programming language such as Go, Java, Python, or TypeScript, and Temporal records each step and its state, so if a server crashes or a network call fails, the workflow continues from where it stopped without losing progress. Retries, timeouts, and timers are built in.

That makes it suitable for processes that take minutes to months, such as payment flows, order fulfillment, customer onboarding, infrastructure provisioning, and data processing. Increasingly, teams use it to orchestrate AI agents, where tasks call models and tools over long durations and need reliability and observability. Temporal Cloud provides a managed service, and the open-source server can be self-hosted.

item.title: The Batch
item.description: The Batch is a free weekly newsletter for people who follow AI. Each issue begins with a letter from Andrew Ng, a leading AI researcher and educator, sharing his perspective on a current topic, such as how teams should build with AI or what trends matter. That is followed by several concise news items on research, products, policy, and industry developments, each with a clear explanation and links to sources.

item.title: Thinkific
item.description:
Thinkific is an online course platform. Creators build courses from video, audio, text, and quizzes, organize them into chapters, and host them on a site with their own branding and domain. Students log in to learn, and the platform tracks completion and issues certificates.

Features extend beyond courses. Memberships and communities keep learners engaged, bundles and subscriptions provide pricing options, and integrations connect with email tools, payment processors, and Zapier. Businesses also use Thinkific to train customers, partners, and employees, and AI tools help generate course outlines and quiz questions.

item.title: Thunkable
item.description:
Thunkable lets people build mobile apps without writing code. The designer places buttons, lists, maps, and other components on a screen, and a visual blocks editor, similar to Scratch, defines the logic. A live test app on your phone shows changes as you make them, which makes learning fast.

Apps are native, not just web wrappers, and can use device features like the camera, location, and notifications. Connections to databases, APIs, and services like Firebase and Airtable allow real functionality. Schools use Thunkable to teach app creation, and small businesses and entrepreneurs use it to build prototypes and simple tools.

item.title: Tinder
item.description: Tinder popularized the swipe. You see a profile with photos and a short bio, swipe right to like or left to pass, and if the other person also likes you, you match and can message. The format is fast and casual, which fits its large, young user base across many countries. People use it for dating, relationships, and meeting new people, and settings let you filter by distance, age, and gender preferences.

item.title: TLDR AI
item.description:
TLDR AI is a quick daily read for people who work with or follow AI. Each issue lists a handful of top stories, such as model releases, research papers, tools, and industry news, with a two- or three-sentence summary and a link to the full source. The format is meant to be read in a few minutes, so subscribers can stay current without sifting through feeds.

It belongs to a family of TLDR newsletters covering tech, startups, and other fields. The AI edition includes sections for headlines, research, engineering and open-source projects, and miscellaneous items, with reading times shown so readers can choose what to open. It is supported by sponsorships, which are labeled.

item.title: Toon Boom Harmony
item.description:
Harmony is the industry standard for 2D animation production. Studios use it for traditional hand-drawn animation, cut-out animation with rigged characters, and hybrids of the two. It offers drawing and painting tools, a timeline and X-sheet familiar to animators, deformers and bone rigging that let characters move naturally, and effects and compositing in one package.

It scales from individual artists to big productions. Versions range from Essentials for beginners to Premium for studios, with pipeline tools, scripting, and integrations with 3D and game engines. Many well-known animated series have been made with Harmony. It supports exporting to video, game engines, and other formats.

item.title: Tractive
item.description:
Tractive helps owners keep track of their pets. A small GPS device attached to a collar sends the animal’s location to a phone app via cellular networks, so you can see where your dog or cat is in real time, view recent routes, and set virtual fences that trigger alerts if the pet leaves a defined area. A light and sound function helps find a pet at night.

Beyond location, the devices monitor activity, sleep, and behavior, and some models track signs of health changes such as excessive scratching or licking. Data shows trends and can help owners share information with veterinarians. Features such as a lost-pet mode, sharing access with family, and integration with pet services support everyday use.

item.title: Trados Studio
item.description:
Trados is one of the best-known tools among professional translators. When translators work on a document, Trados breaks it into segments and checks a translation memory for matches from previous projects, offering exact and fuzzy matches so work is reused and terminology stays consistent. That improves speed and quality, especially on repetitive technical content, and lowers costs for clients who pay by new words.

The product has evolved with the technology. It integrates machine translation engines, including adaptive and neural options, and supports AI-assisted features for suggestions and quality checks. Trados Enterprise is a cloud version for teams and organizations, supporting collaboration, project management, and workflows with vendors, while the desktop Studio remains popular among freelancers and agencies.

item.title: Trello
item.description: Trello organizes work on a board. Lists represent stages like To Do, Doing, and Done, and each task is a card that you drag from list to list. Cards can hold descriptions, checklists, due dates, attachments, comments, and assigned members. The simplicity is the point: most people learn it in minutes, which makes it popular for small teams, personal projects, content calendars, and simple workflows like hiring or event planning.

item.title: Trimble Construction
item.description:
Trimble is a major technology supplier to the construction industry. Its portfolio includes software for estimating costs, scheduling, managing projects and finances, coordinating building models, and running equipment. SketchUp and Tekla, used for design and structural detailing, are part of the group, and Trimble Connect provides a collaboration space for project data.

Its hardware is a distinctive strength. Survey instruments, GPS and GNSS receivers, and machine control systems guide excavators and other equipment based on a 3D model, linking digital plans to work on the ground. Integrating these systems with software lets data flow from the model to the field and back as built information. AI features assist with planning, quantity takeoff, and analyzing project data.

item.title: TubeBuddy
item.description:
TubeBuddy is a browser extension and mobile app for YouTube creators. It adds tools to the YouTube interface, including a keyword explorer that estimates how competitive a search term is, tag suggestions, and a score that shows how well a video is optimized. These help creators choose topics and fill in titles and descriptions with search in mind.

Other features save time. Bulk tools update many videos at once, thumbnail A/B testing compares designs for click rates, and scheduling and reminders organize publishing. Analytics show how a channel performs and how it compares to others. AI tools suggest titles, descriptions, and ideas based on a video’s topic.

item.title: Twilio ConversationRelay
item.description:
ConversationRelay connects phone calls to AI. When a call arrives on a Twilio number, the service converts the caller’s speech to text in real time and streams it over a WebSocket to the developer’s server. The server sends text back, which Twilio converts into speech, so the caller hears a natural response. This lets teams plug in any large language model and their own business logic.

Twilio manages the hard parts of voice. It handles interruptions when a caller speaks over the agent, supports multiple languages and voice providers, and can transfer the call to a human with the transcript. It also offers a no-code Studio widget for simpler flows, plus compliance support for regulated industries, including options for HIPAA and PCI. A reporting feature gives insight into latency and where agents struggle.

item.title: Typesense
item.description:
Typesense is built for instant search experiences, like the results that appear as a user types in a store or documentation site. It keeps its index in memory for speed, handles typos by default, and supports filtering, faceting, sorting, and grouping. Its API is simple, and client libraries exist for popular languages.

It also supports modern retrieval needs. Vector search lets applications find results by meaning using embeddings, and hybrid search combines that with keyword matching. Built-in features can generate embeddings, and a conversational search mode answers questions using retrieved documents. Developers can run Typesense on their own servers or use Typesense Cloud.

item.title: UKG
item.description:
UKG is a major provider of human capital management software. Employers use it to run payroll, track time and attendance, schedule shifts for hourly workers, manage benefits, hire, and develop employees. It is especially strong in industries with large hourly workforces such as retail, healthcare, and manufacturing, where scheduling and labor compliance are complex.

AI is woven into the products. Its assistant helps managers and employees answer questions and complete tasks, analytics predict turnover and scheduling needs, and tools suggest schedules that balance demand, cost, and employee preferences. The company has multiple product lines, including UKG Pro for larger organizations and UKG Ready for mid-sized companies.

item.title: Upstart
item.description:
Upstart set out to improve how lenders decide who gets credit. Its models use many variables, including education, job history, and credit data, to predict the likelihood a borrower will repay, with the aim of approving more people at lower rates than traditional scores alone would. Borrowers apply online, often receive decisions quickly, and loans are funded by partner banks and credit unions.

The platform serves lenders as software and as a marketplace. Banks use Upstart to originate personal loans, auto loans, and home equity products, with automation that speeds approvals and reduces manual review. The company regularly tests its models for disparate impact, and has worked with regulators on fair lending, which remains a major concern for AI in credit.

item.title: UserWay
item.description:
UserWay is a web accessibility service. Its widget gives visitors controls to adjust text size, contrast, spacing, and animations, and it applies automated fixes such as adding missing labels. A scanner checks pages against the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines and reports issues, so site owners can see problems and prioritize them.

For deeper work, UserWay offers managed services with human experts who audit and fix content, plus tools for documents and PDFs. Reports and accessibility statements help show good faith efforts toward compliance. The product works with common platforms such as WordPress, Shopify, and Wix.

item.title: Veeva Systems
item.description:
Veeva is the dominant software vendor for pharmaceutical companies. Its CRM supports sales and medical teams that engage with physicians, Vault is a cloud platform for managing documents and processes in areas such as clinical operations, regulatory submissions, quality, and safety, and data products supply information about healthcare providers and markets. Companies use these tools to run regulated, document-heavy processes.

The company has been adding AI across its applications. Veeva AI agents help users search content, prepare documents, and automate steps such as drafting summaries or checking submissions, built into Vault and its CRM and operating under the industry’s compliance requirements. It has also moved its CRM off the Salesforce platform onto its own technology.

item.title: Vertex
item.description:
Vertex helps businesses get sales and use tax, VAT, and similar indirect taxes right. When a company sells a product, the right tax depends on the buyer’s location, the product type, and applicable rules, which change often. Vertex maintains a large database of rates and rules, and its engine calculates the correct tax inside systems like SAP, Oracle, and Microsoft Dynamics.

The company also covers filing and reporting. Tools prepare returns, manage exemption certificates, and support e-invoicing mandates that countries are introducing. AI features help classify products to the right tax codes and speed up compliance work. Customers are mostly large enterprises with complex tax footprints across many jurisdictions.

item.title: Vidyard
item.description:
Vidyard is a video platform for business teams. Salespeople record quick webcam or screen videos for prospects, send them by email or link, and see who watched and for how long. Marketers host videos on their websites with branded players and gated forms.

AI features speed up production. Script suggestions help with what to say, avatars let a rep send a personalized video without recording each one, and transcripts, summaries, and chapters make longer videos easier to use. Integrations with Salesforce and HubSpot put engagement data in the CRM.

item.title: Vimeo
item.description:
Vimeo started as a community for filmmakers and grew into a professional video platform. Businesses use it to host and share video without ads, embed customizable players on their websites, control who can watch, and see analytics on viewing. Features such as review tools, live streaming, and webinars support marketing, training, and internal communications.

AI features have been added to speed up work. Tools can generate scripts, create video from text or slides, produce captions and translations, and edit footage by removing filler words or creating highlights, and an AI assistant helps with chapters and summaries. Vimeo’s editing tools and recording app allow teams to produce video without separate software.

item.title: Virtual Staging AI
item.description:
Virtual Staging AI is built for property listings. An agent uploads a photo of an empty room, selects a room type and style, and the AI places furniture and decor that fits the space. Results arrive in minutes, so listings can show potential before a sale.

Staged photos tend to attract more interest, and virtual staging costs far less than renting furniture. Many markets and listing services require disclosure that images are digitally staged, and the room must not be misrepresented.

item.title: Visual Studio Code
item.description: Visual Studio Code, usually called VS Code, is the most widely used code editor among developers. It is light enough to open quickly yet has what most people need: syntax highlighting, a debugger, integrated terminal, Git support, and a huge extension marketplace that adds languages, linters, themes, and tools. The core is open source, and it runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. It also has a browser version, and remote development features let you work inside containers, over SSH, or in cloud environments.

item.title: Vuforia
item.description:
Vuforia is one of the longest-running AR toolkits. Developers use its engine to make an app recognize a printed image, a 3D object, or a physical space, and then anchor digital content to it. A technician could point a tablet at a machine and see step-by-step instructions overlaid on the right parts.

PTC has focused it on industry. Vuforia products include tools for creating work instructions, remote expert assistance with live video and annotations, and authoring tools that turn CAD models into AR experiences without much coding. It supports phones, tablets, and headsets, and connects to PTC’s engineering software.

item.title: Waze
item.description:
Waze built its reputation on live information from drivers. Users report traffic jams, accidents, speed traps, road hazards, and closed roads as they happen, and others see the alerts immediately. The app uses that crowd-sourced data, together with anonymous speed information from devices, to route around slowdowns and update arrival times, often finding shortcuts that other apps miss.

The app is free and has features suited to everyday driving. It shows fuel prices, offers voice navigation with customizable voices, lets you plan drives to leave at a set time, and supports carpool matching in some areas. It integrates with Android Auto and Apple CarPlay and connects to music and calendar apps. Local communities of volunteer editors help keep maps accurate.

item.title: Web of Science
item.description:
Web of Science is one of the oldest and most influential indexes of scholarly literature. It covers curated sets of journals, conference proceedings, and books and records which works cite which, making it possible to follow ideas forward and backward through the literature. Researchers use it to find relevant papers, track citations, and analyze trends in a field.

Institutions also use its data for research evaluation. Clarivate publishes the Journal Citation Reports, which includes the impact factor, one of the most discussed metrics in academia, and Web of Science supports measures of authors, journals, and institutions. A Research Assistant adds AI-driven features such as natural language search and summaries of results. The selectivity of coverage is a selling point and also a criticism, as it favors certain journals and languages.

item.title: Webex
item.description:
Webex is one of the older names in video conferencing, and Cisco has kept it competitive by adding hardware, calling, and collaboration tools. Companies use it for meetings, webinars, team messaging, a phone system, and conference room devices, with security and compliance controls that suit regulated industries and government.

The AI Assistant adds help across these pieces. It writes meeting summaries and action items, answers questions about what was discussed, catches up people who join late, and summarizes long message threads. Audio features remove background noise and can isolate a speaker’s voice in a loud room, and real-time translation and captions help international teams. Cisco also sells AI agents for contact centers.

item.title: Winston AI
item.description:
Winston AI is a detection tool for written content. A user pastes text or uploads a document, and the service returns a score estimating how likely it is that AI wrote it, with sentence-level highlighting. A plagiarism checker compares text against web sources, and reports can be shared as evidence.

Publishers use it to screen submissions, teachers to review student work, and agencies to check freelancers. Additional features include detection of AI-generated images and tools aimed at checking whether text has been paraphrased to evade detection. Browser extensions and an API support workflows.

item.title: Wisdom Panel
item.description:
Wisdom Panel offers genetic testing for dogs and cats. An owner swabs the pet’s cheek, mails the sample, and receives a report on breed ancestry, family tree, and traits. The report also screens for genetic health conditions the pet may carry or be at risk for, which can inform decisions with a veterinarian.

The company draws on a large database of breed samples and research, and sells tests through retailers, directly to owners, and through veterinary clinics. Health screening results are meant to start conversations with a vet, and some conditions come with guidance on diet or monitoring. The brand belongs to Mars Petcare, which also owns other pet care businesses.

item.title: WordPress
item.description:
WordPress is the software behind a large share of the web. You install it on a web host or sign up with a hosted service, and manage pages, posts, media, and users from a dashboard. A block editor lets you build layouts visually, and thousands of themes control how a site looks. Plugins extend it for SEO, contact forms, memberships, caching, analytics, and online stores through WooCommerce.

It comes in two forms that are easy to confuse. WordPress.org is the free software you host yourself, which gives full control and requires handling hosting, updates, and security. WordPress.com is a hosted service from Automattic with plans that handle those chores. AI arrives mostly through add-ons: Jetpack and other plugins offer writing help, image generation, and chat assistants, and AI site builders can generate a first draft of a site from a prompt. The core project is also adding building blocks for AI features.

item.title: Wrike
item.description:
Wrike is used by teams that coordinate lots of work. Projects can be viewed as lists, boards, Gantt charts, or calendars, and tasks carry dependencies, owners, due dates, and custom fields. Request forms and approvals let outside teams submit work in a structured way, which helps marketing, creative, and operations groups manage intake.

AI features reduce routine effort. Wrike’s tools can summarize long comment threads, create tasks from text, draft project descriptions, and predict which projects are at risk of missing deadlines. Dashboards show workloads and progress across portfolios, and integrations connect to Slack, Salesforce, Microsoft 365, and Adobe tools. Proofing helps creative teams review assets.

item.title: Xero
item.description:
Xero is an online accounting platform used widely in the UK, Australia, New Zealand, and increasingly elsewhere. Business owners and bookkeepers connect their bank accounts so transactions flow in automatically, then match them to invoices and bills in a reconciliation process that Xero makes quick with suggested matches. It generates invoices, tracks expenses and cash flow, and produces reports such as profit and loss and balance sheets.

An accountant-friendly design is part of its appeal. Unlimited users on most plans let owners, bookkeepers, and accountants work in the same file, and a large marketplace of integrations connects Xero to payment providers, payroll, inventory, and point-of-sale systems. AI features include suggested coding of transactions, predictive cash flow tools, and an assistant for asking questions about the business and automating tasks like drafting invoice reminders.

item.title: Yardi
item.description:
Yardi is one of the largest suppliers of software to the real estate industry. Property managers use it to market units, screen applicants, sign leases, collect rent, track maintenance, and run accounting. Different products fit different segments: Voyager serves larger portfolios, Breeze suits smaller operators, and other tools cover commercial space, senior living, and investment management.

AI features are collected under Virtuoso, which Yardi uses for tasks like answering resident questions, drafting leasing responses, handling invoices and documents, and analyzing performance. The goal is to take routine work off property staff and to provide insights from data that the company already holds in its accounting and leasing systems.

item.title: YNAB
item.description:
YNAB is as much a method as an app. Users assign each dollar of income to a category, such as rent, groceries, or savings, and update the plan as real spending happens. When money moves between categories, the app shows the tradeoff. The idea is to work from money you already have, not money you expect, which many people find reduces financial stress.

Features support that approach. Bank syncing imports transactions, goals track bills and savings targets, reports show spending trends, and shared budgets let partners manage money together. The company offers workshops and guides that teach the approach, which is a big part of why users stick with it. There is a mobile app and a web version.

item.title: Zapier MCP
item.description:
Zapier MCP turns Zapier’s app library into tools an AI can use. You create an MCP server, choose the apps and actions you want to allow, such as sending a Slack message, adding a row in Google Sheets, or creating a CRM contact, and connect that server to a compatible client. The assistant can then call those actions during a conversation.

This avoids writing custom integrations. Zapier already handles authentication and the quirks of each app’s API, so connecting an assistant to a new service is a matter of adding an action and authorizing your account. You control the scope, and each call uses your connected account, which helps limit what the AI can touch.

item.title: Zencastr
item.description:
Zencastr was built for remote podcast interviews. Instead of recording a call, it captures each participant’s microphone on their own device and uploads the separate tracks, which produces cleaner audio than the compressed stream you hear during a call. Guests join through a link in their browser, with no account needed.

Beyond recording, it offers tools for finishing a show. Automatic post-production levels audio and removes silence, an editor allows basic cuts, and AI features generate transcripts, summaries, and show notes. Video recording and a hosting option cover more of the workflow, and exports go to editing programs.

item.title: beacon.sh
item.description:
beacon.sh addresses a limit of coding agents: they start each session knowing little about the project. Beacon watches what the agent does, such as commands that work, mistakes it makes, and conventions it discovers, and stores them as notes the agent can use next time.

It works with popular coding agents and keeps the memory in files and a local store the developer can inspect and edit. Over time, that cuts repeated explanations and failed attempts.

item.title: Cedric
item.description:
Cedric acts as a stand-in for meetings. A user gives it slides, notes, and background documents, and it attends a call, presents, and responds to questions using that material. When it does not know something, it can note the question for follow-up.

The idea appeals to people with a heavy meeting load, such as founders or sales teams running repeated demos. It raises etiquette and trust questions: others in the meeting should know they are talking to an AI agent.

item.title: ClawsGO Science
item.description:
ClawsGO Science goes beyond literature review. The agent can plan an analysis, write and run code in a cloud environment, process datasets, and report results with the steps shown. It is built for scientific work such as data analysis and computational experiments.

Doing the work, not only describing it, can speed up exploratory research. Results still need scrutiny, since an agent can make statistical or coding mistakes, and reproducibility depends on seeing exactly what was run.

item.title: Testifly
item.description:
Testifly uses AI agents to test web applications. A team gives it a URL and login details, and the system explores the app, plans test cases, generates tests, and runs them, then heals tests when the UI changes. The aim is coverage without writing and maintaining scripts.

Autonomous testing can find regressions that no one thought to cover, and reduces the upkeep that makes automated tests brittle. Results still need review, since passing tests do not prove the right behavior is checked.

item.title: UnleashX
item.description:
UnleashX provides voice and workflow automation. Teams configure AI agents that handle phone conversations and carry out actions across systems, such as calling leads, qualifying them, updating records, and sending follow-ups. Rules define what the worker may do.

The platform presents these as digital employees for roles like sales development and support. Outbound calling needs consent and compliance with telemarketing rules, and AI voice agents should disclose themselves.

UnleashX is paid, and independent information is limited, so run a pilot first. Alternatives include Bland AI, Retell AI, Vapi, Synthflow, and 11x. UnleashX suits small teams automating calls and follow-ups.

item.title: DeepSeek Super-Agent
item.description:
Super-Agent explores what a team-facing coding agent could look like. Built on DeepSeek’s Harness runtime, it is tied to one GitHub repository and listens for requests from approved colleagues in Feishu, a workplace chat app. A teammate can ask it to investigate or change something, and it works on the code and reports back.

The prototype shows how a lab thinks about agents inside everyday collaboration tools instead of only in a developer’s terminal. Because it is a prototype, it focuses on demonstrating the design, not on a polished product with broad integrations, and it requires technical setup.

item.title: Herdr
item.description:
Herdr manages the growing pile of agent sessions developers run. Instead of many terminal windows, it presents agents in one tabbed interface and shows whether each is working, finished, or waiting for input, when the agent reports status. It supports any agent that runs in a terminal.

The key design choice is the herdr-core runtime, a small server on your machine that runs the sessions. The app is only a front end, so quitting or updating it does not stop agents. A terminal version of Herdr, the original, still exists as a separate program with its own server.

item.title: Google Genie
item.description: Genie is a different kind of generative model. Instead of producing a fixed image or video, it creates a world you can explore: describe a scene, and the model generates an environment that responds as you move through it, frame by frame, with the scene staying consistent as you turn around. DeepMind frames world models as a step toward AI that understands how environments behave, with possible uses in games, robotics training, and simulation.

item.title: Kimi Code
item.description:
Kimi Code is a command line agent in the same family as Claude Code and Codex CLI. You start it in a project folder, describe a task, and it reads files, edits code, runs commands, and checks results, deciding what to do next based on what happens. Permissions let you approve risky actions.

It defaults to Moonshot AI’s Kimi models, which are known for strong coding and long context, and can also connect to other compatible providers. Features include built-in subagents for coding, exploring, and planning, support for the Model Context Protocol to connect tools, lifecycle hooks for automation and safety checks, and an ACP mode so editors like Zed and JetBrains can drive it.

item.title: Claude Duet
item.description: Duet is built on the idea that an assistant should not wait for you to ask. Each morning it sends a brief on what matters across your connected apps, and it checks those accounts every few hours for new items that need attention. You can hand it tasks, and it works on its own virtual machine with a browser, so your laptop or phone does not need to stay on. It keeps working while you are away and tells you when something is done or needs a decision.

item.title: AI Directory
item.description:
AI Directory is one of many catalogs that try to keep up with the flood of AI products. Visitors can browse tools by category or search for a use case, such as writing, image generation, coding, or video, and see short descriptions with links to each tool’s own site.

Directories help with discovery. New tools appear constantly, and a list organized by task is easier to scan than a search engine. Makers can submit their products for listing, which is how most such sites grow, so coverage depends on who submits and how closely entries are reviewed.

item.title: Conduyt
item.description:
Conduyt takes an approach to CRM pricing that departs from the per-seat model. A team pays a single price no matter how many people use the product, which suits small sales teams and agencies that would otherwise pay for every added user.

The basics are familiar: a contact database, deal pipelines, and activity tracking, with AI features that draft follow-up messages, summarize interactions, and reduce routine data entry. Positioned as AI-native, it aims to have the software do the admin work that salespeople dislike.

item.title: Milan Voice AI
item.description:
Milan Voice AI generates speech for creators and developers. Users type text and choose or create a voice, with options to clone a voice from a short sample or describe a new one. Multi-speaker mode takes a script with several characters and produces a dialogue, useful for podcasts, audiobooks, and videos.

Typical uses include narration, character voices, and prototypes of voice features. An API supports integration into apps. Voice cloning requires permission from the person whose voice is copied, and synthetic audio should be disclosed where appropriate.

item.title: Taromi
item.description:
Taromi pairs the practice of tarot with AI interpretation. A user poses a question, draws cards from a virtual deck, and receives a written reading that explains the cards in context. Many users treat it as a prompt for reflection more than a prediction.

The format is easy to use daily, with options for different spreads and for saving past readings. Like horoscopes, tarot has no proven ability to foretell events, and readings generated by AI are creative text, not guidance backed by evidence.

item.title: TattooJinn
item.description:
TattooJinn narrows image generation to tattoo art. A user types an idea and picks a style, such as traditional, fine line, or blackwork, and the tool creates design concepts. Variations help someone test placement and look before committing.

The designs work as inspiration for conversations with a tattoo artist, who adapts them to a body and a technique. AI images may include details that do not translate well to skin or may resemble existing artists’ work, so an artist should redraw or approve anything permanent.

item.title: Ancestry
item.description:
Ancestry is a genealogy service. Users build a family tree and the site suggests matching records, such as birth certificates, census pages, immigration lists, and military files, from its collection. Hints appear as you add relatives, which helps trace lines back through generations.

Technology helps both records and relatives. Handwriting recognition and machine learning transcribe old documents so they become searchable, and the DNA test connects users with genetic relatives and estimates ethnic origins. Members can share trees and message distant cousins, which often breaks through research dead ends.

item.title: AppFolio
item.description:
AppFolio runs the daily operations of a property management business. Staff list vacancies on rental sites, screen applicants, sign leases, collect rent online, and track maintenance requests and vendors. Owners receive statements and reports, and residents use a portal and app to pay and submit requests.

AI features take over routine communication. An assistant answers common tenant questions by text at any hour, qualifies leads, schedules showings, and flags maintenance requests that need attention. Analytics help managers see trends in occupancy, delinquency, and costs, and accounting tools are designed for property trust accounting.

item.title: Aquant
item.description:
Aquant is a service intelligence platform. Equipment makers and service organizations hold years of repair history, manuals, and technician notes, which are hard to search in the moment. Aquant uses AI to learn from that data and recommend probable causes and fixes for a given symptom.

For a technician on a job, this works like an expert on call. They describe the problem or enter an error code, and the system suggests what to check, which parts are likely needed, and what has worked on similar cases. Service managers use the same data to see recurring failures and to reduce repeat visits and unnecessary parts.

item.title: AspenTech
item.description:
AspenTech sells engineering software to process industries. Chemical engineers use Aspen Plus and Aspen HYSYS to model how reactions, separations, and heat flows behave across a plant, which lets them design and test processes on screen before building them, and tune existing plants for efficiency, safety, and emissions.

The company also sells operations software. Optimization tools help plants decide how to run units to hit targets for cost and throughput, and asset performance products use machine learning on sensor data to predict equipment failures before they cause downtime. Digital twins of plant units connect design models to real operating data.

item.title: Blend
item.description:
Blend builds software for lenders. Instead of paper forms and email, borrowers apply on a digital platform that collects information, connects to bank accounts and payroll sources to verify income and assets, and tracks the status of the application. Loan officers and processors see the file in a shared workflow.

Automation cuts the manual work in underwriting preparation. The platform pulls data from verified sources, checks documents, and flags missing or inconsistent items so staff can fix problems early. It covers mortgages, home equity, and consumer lending products, and integrates with loan origination systems and credit providers.

item.title: Bluebeam
item.description:
Bluebeam Revu is a PDF tool built for construction. Teams review plans on screen, add markups such as clouds, callouts, and stamps, and measure lengths, areas, and counts directly on drawings to prepare quantity takeoffs for estimates. Custom tool sets store commonly used markups.

Collaboration is a big part. Studio Sessions let many people mark up the same document at the same time, and Studio Projects store drawing sets in the cloud. Overlay and comparison features show what changed between revisions, with AI helping to line up sheets and highlight differences, which reduces missed updates.

item.title: BlueDot
item.description:
BlueDot is an epidemic intelligence company. Its system scans huge volumes of text and data, including news in many languages, animal disease reports, and travel patterns, looking for signs of unusual outbreaks. Epidemiologists review the signals and issue alerts with analysis.

The company drew attention when it flagged the cluster of pneumonia cases that became COVID-19 before many official announcements. Flight data helps estimate where infected travelers might go, which supports early warnings to governments, airlines, and health organizations.

item.title: Boundless
item.description:
Boundless helps people navigate US immigration paperwork. Users answer questions in a guided flow, and the software builds the forms needed for a case, such as a marriage-based green card or naturalization. Checks flag missing information and inconsistencies that often cause delays.

Human experts remain part of the process. Plans include review by immigration attorneys or specialists, and customers can get help with responding to requests from authorities. Tracking tools show deadlines and the status of the case, and educational material explains steps and timelines.

item.title: BoxBrownie
item.description:
BoxBrownie serves real estate marketing. Agents and photographers upload listing photos, and editors, supported by AI, enhance the images by fixing exposure, correcting color, replacing dull skies, and removing clutter or distractions. Turnaround is typically quick, which suits fast-moving listings.

Virtual staging is a major product. The service places digital furniture and decor into photos of empty rooms so buyers can imagine the space, which costs far less than physical staging. Other services include twilight conversions, lawn improvements, and floor plans.

item.title: Buildertrend
item.description:
Buildertrend focuses on residential construction. Builders manage a project from estimate to completion in a single system: schedules, selections, budgets, purchase orders, daily logs, photos, and documents. Clients can log in to approve choices, view progress, and see invoices, which cuts down on phone calls.

Financial tools track costs against budgets, handle change orders, and send bills and payments. Subcontractors get access to their schedules and tasks, and mobile apps let teams update from the job site. AI features assist with tasks like summarizing communication and extracting data from documents.

item.title: Canary Technologies
item.description:
Canary builds software for hotels. Guests can check in online before arrival, sign registration forms, verify identity, and pay deposits, which shortens lines at the front desk. After arrival, messaging lets them ask for towels, late checkout, or recommendations through text instead of calling.

An AI layer answers common questions and handles requests, routing issues to staff when needed. Upsell tools offer room upgrades and add-ons at the right moment, which brings extra revenue. Other products cover contactless payments, digital tipping, and a guest-facing digital tablet in rooms.

item.title: Cardiologs
item.description:
Cardiologs applies AI to heart rhythm recordings. Technicians and cardiologists traditionally spend hours reviewing long ECG tracings, such as 24-hour or multi-day Holter recordings. The software analyzes the signal, classifies heartbeats and rhythms, and highlights segments that need attention so reviewers can concentrate on them.

Reports summarize findings, including atrial fibrillation burden, pauses, and other events, in a form the physician can verify and edit. The tool works with data from different monitoring devices and integrates into clinical workflows. Philips acquired the company to add ECG analysis to its cardiac monitoring portfolio.

item.title: CAST AI
item.description:
CAST AI is an automation layer for Kubernetes. After connecting to a cluster on AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure, it analyzes workloads, chooses the best-priced instance types, scales nodes up and down, and replaces expensive capacity with spot instances when workloads can tolerate interruptions.

The platform also covers related needs. Savings reports show the effect, workload autoscaling adjusts resource requests, and security scanning finds misconfigurations. More recently it added tools for running GPU workloads and AI inference more efficiently. Customers keep their own cloud accounts.

item.title: Celonis
item.description:
Celonis is the best-known process mining platform. Every action in business systems, such as creating an order or approving an invoice, leaves a record with a time stamp. Celonis reads these logs and rebuilds the real process, showing the paths that cases take, where they wait, and how often they deviate from the intended flow.

With that picture, teams find delays, rework, and costly exceptions. The platform quantifies the impact, suggests improvements, and can trigger automated actions or alerts. AI features answer questions about process data and recommend where to focus. Common uses include order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, and supply chain work.

item.title: Circle
item.description:
Circle gives communities a home of their own. A creator sets up spaces for topics, posts content, hosts live events, runs courses, and lets members message each other, all under a custom domain and brand. It aims to feel more focused than a social network and less cluttered than a forum.

Monetization is built in. Communities can charge for memberships, offer paid tiers, and sell courses and events, with workflows to onboard new members. AI features draft welcome messages, summarize conversations, and help members find information, while analytics show engagement and which members are most active. Mobile apps and integrations with tools like Zapier extend reach.

item.title: Cognite
item.description:
Cognite addresses data silos in industry. A plant produces time series from sensors, maintenance records, engineering diagrams, and 3D models that live in different systems. Cognite Data Fusion links them into a graph in which a pump, its sensor readings, its work orders, and its drawings are connected, so people and applications can find everything about an asset.

That foundation supports applications. Teams build digital twins, predictive maintenance models, and dashboards, and an AI assistant helps users ask questions about assets and operations in natural language. The platform is used in oil and gas, power, and manufacturing, where downtime is costly.

item.title: Collov AI
item.description:
Collov AI helps people imagine a space. A user uploads a photo of a room, picks a style such as modern, farmhouse, or minimalist, and the tool produces a redesigned image with furniture and decor. It can also virtually stage an empty room for real estate listings.

Interior designers use it to show clients options early, and real estate agents use it to make listings more appealing. Homeowners use it for ideas before buying furniture. The renders are visualizations and do not reflect exact measurements or the availability of products.

item.title: ComplyAdvantage
item.description:
ComplyAdvantage provides financial crime tools for banks, fintechs, and other regulated firms. At onboarding, it checks whether a customer or company appears on sanctions lists, politically exposed person lists, or negative news, and continues to monitor them over time. Transaction monitoring flags unusual activity that may signal money laundering.

Its data comes from a large collection of sources that is structured and updated continuously, and machine learning ranks matches to cut down on false alarms that compliance staff would otherwise review by hand. Case management tools help analysts document decisions for regulators, and risk assessment features support a risk-based approach.

item.title: Daloopa
item.description:
Daloopa serves the finance professionals who build models from public company reports. Instead of typing numbers from filings into Excel, an analyst gets a database of financial line items pulled from documents like quarterly reports and presentations, with each number linked back to its source in the original file.

Updates arrive soon after companies report, so models stay current. An Excel add-in lets analysts pull data into their own templates, and an API and integrations with AI assistants allow data to flow into other workflows. The company has focused on accuracy and traceability, since errors in financial data are costly.

item.title: Datarock
item.description:
Datarock works in mineral exploration. Geologists take photos of drill core samples and log what they see, which is slow and subjective. Datarock’s models analyze the images to identify rock types, measure fractures, and capture structural features, producing consistent digital logs.

The faster, more objective data helps exploration teams make decisions about where to drill next and supports resource modeling. Results integrate with geological software, and the company has expanded to other imagery such as hyperspectral scans and borehole images.

item.title: Deel
item.description:
Deel is a global hiring and payments platform. A company that wants to employ someone in another country can use Deel as the employer of record, which means Deel holds the legal employment relationship locally and handles contracts, payroll, benefits, and taxes. It also manages contractors, with agreements and payments in many currencies.

Beyond employment, Deel has built an HR suite covering global payroll for companies with their own entities, benefits, equipment, time tracking, and immigration support. AI features review and generate contracts against local rules, answer compliance questions, and automate workflows, which reduces the research that cross-border hiring requires.

item.title: Dental Monitoring
item.description:
Dental Monitoring lets orthodontists check on patients remotely. A patient attaches a small cheek retractor to a phone, scans their teeth on a schedule, and uploads the images. The software compares scans to the treatment plan and measures how teeth are moving.

AI flags problems such as aligners that do not fit, lost attachments, hygiene concerns, or progress that is behind schedule. The orthodontist reviews alerts and decides whether to adjust the plan, send the next aligners earlier, or schedule a visit. This can reduce in-person appointments and catch issues sooner.

item.title: DhiWise
item.description:
DhiWise sits between design and development. A designer prepares screens in Figma, and DhiWise generates app code, including navigation, state management, and connections to APIs defined by a specification. The output follows common project structure, so developers can continue in their own tools.

It speaks to teams that build many similar screens and want consistency. Developers use it to produce the first version of the user interface and wiring, then refine business logic by hand. AI features add the ability to generate code from prompts and to adapt designs.

item.title: Docketwise
item.description:
Docketwise is built specifically for immigration law. Attorneys collect information from clients with online questionnaires, and the software places answers on the correct government forms, which saves repeated typing. Because forms change, the platform keeps them updated.

It manages the rest of a case. Deadlines and receipts are tracked, status updates can be pulled from government sources, and client portals let people upload documents and see progress. Billing and email integrations support daily practice, and AI features help with drafting and summarizing.

item.title: DocumentCloud
item.description:
DocumentCloud is a platform built for newsrooms. Reporters upload documents such as court filings, government reports, and leaked files, and the system makes them searchable through optical character recognition. They can annotate passages, add notes, and publish documents so readers can see the original source behind a story.

For large collections, the tool helps with analysis. Entity extraction finds people, places, and organizations mentioned, and search across projects lets teams collaborate on investigations. Add-ons extend the system with automated tasks, including redaction, translation, and data extraction.

item.title: Duve
item.description:
Duve is a guest experience platform. Before arrival, guests receive a digital check-in flow, can upload documents, and see offers for upgrades and extras. During the stay, a messaging assistant answers questions about the property and the area, and requests are routed to staff when a person is needed.
