It differed from general chatbots by using carefully written, clinically reviewed content instead of free-form generation, and the company ran studies to evaluate it. It aimed to make support more accessible and affordable than traditional therapy, and was used by individuals, employers, and health systems. It was always described as a supplement to, not a replacement for, professional care.

item.title: Wysa
item.description: Wysa is a conversational app for stress, low mood, and anxiety. Users chat with a friendly penguin character that asks about how they feel and offers exercises, such as reframing negative thoughts, breathing techniques, sleep tools, and guided meditations. The responses draw on structured therapeutic content written and reviewed by clinicians instead of unconstrained text generation, which is meant to make it safer and more predictable than a general chatbot.

item.title: XMind
item.description:
XMind is a long-standing mind mapping tool known for its range of layouts. Start with a central idea and branch outward, or switch to another structure such as a logic chart, fishbone diagram, matrix, tree chart, or timeline to fit the problem. It has a polished interface, attractive themes, and features such as markers, stickers, notes, and attachments, and it works offline.

Special modes help with presentation and organization. Brainstorming mode captures ideas quickly, outline view turns a map into a list, and Zen mode removes distractions. A presentation feature plays the map as a slideshow, and exports cover PDF, images, Word, and Markdown. AI features can generate a map from a topic, expand a branch with suggestions, and summarize content into a structure.

item.title: Zebra Medical Vision
item.description:
Zebra Medical Vision developed AI that reads medical scans and flags findings. Its algorithms examined chest X-rays, CT scans, and mammograms for conditions such as lung nodules, bone density loss, fatty liver, coronary calcium, and signs of fractures, often picking up incidental findings that a radiologist focused on another question might not report. The company had several algorithms cleared by regulators in the United States and Europe.

A distinctive aspect was population health analysis: by screening scans that were already taken for other purposes, hospitals could identify patients at risk of conditions such as osteoporosis or cardiovascular disease and follow up. Zebra Medical Vision offered its tools through a cloud platform that integrated with radiology workflows.

item.title: 10Web
item.description:
10Web combines site generation with hosting. You describe a business or enter the address of an existing website, and the AI builds a WordPress site with layout, text, and images, which you can then edit with a visual builder based on Elementor. The result is a standard WordPress site, so it can use the plugin and theme ecosystem and can be moved elsewhere.

Hosting and optimization are part of the package. Sites run on managed WordPress hosting with a focus on speed, including automatic optimization of images and code to improve page speed scores, and tools for backups and security. AI features generate copy, images, and SEO suggestions, and an assistant can edit pages based on instructions. Agencies can white-label the platform and manage client sites, and there is an API for builders who want to embed it.

item.title: 15Five
item.description:
15Five helps organizations manage how people work and develop. Employees submit short weekly check-ins about priorities, progress, and morale, and managers review them and respond, which keeps a regular rhythm of communication. The platform includes performance reviews, goal and OKR tracking, one-on-one meeting agendas, recognition features, and engagement surveys to measure how employees feel.

AI is used to support managers. The system can summarize check-in responses and survey results, suggest coaching tips, help write review feedback, and flag potential issues like declining engagement or flight risk. Its Best-Self Management framework offers training for managers on developing teams. Reports give HR leaders a view of trends across teams.

item.title: 6sense
item.description:
6sense helps B2B teams find buyers who are not yet raising their hands. It collects signals from many sources, such as web visits, content consumption, and third-party research activity, identifies the companies behind the anonymous traffic, and uses machine learning to predict which accounts are in the market and at what stage of the buying journey. Teams see lists of target accounts ranked by readiness to buy.

The platform acts on those insights. Marketing can run advertising aimed at accounts showing interest, sales gets alerts when key accounts spike in activity, and workflows enroll contacts in email sequences. AI agents help with outreach and qualification, and integrations with CRMs and marketing automation tools keep data in sync. Predictions rely on data from many sources, so they are probabilistic.

item.title: 7shifts
item.description:
7shifts is built for the quirks of restaurant staffing. Managers create schedules based on forecast sales, availability, and labor targets, and publish them to a staff app where employees can see shifts, request swaps, and pick up open shifts. The goal is to keep enough people on the floor without overspending on wages.

The platform adds operations tools. A time clock tracks hours, compliance features flag overtime and break rules by location, tip pooling and distribution help with fair payouts, and team chat replaces scattered text threads. Integrations with point of sale systems provide sales data that feeds labor forecasts, and payroll exports reduce manual work.

item.title: Abridge
item.description: Abridge targets one of healthcare’s biggest burdens: the time doctors spend writing notes. With patient consent, the app records the conversation during a visit, and AI turns it into a structured clinical note in the format the clinician needs, ready for review and insertion into the electronic health record. After the visit, a patient-friendly summary can also be produced. The aim is to let doctors focus on the patient instead of the screen.

item.title: ActiveCampaign AI
item.description:
ActiveCampaign is built around automation. You design customer journeys that react to behavior: someone joins a list, visits a page, abandons a cart, or opens an email, and the system sends the right follow-up at the right time. Segmentation, split testing, site tracking, and a built-in CRM let small and mid-sized businesses personalize campaigns without a large marketing team. It is common in e-commerce, services, and B2B companies.

Its AI tools help build and manage those journeys. Active Intelligence can audit an account, draft campaigns and automations from a short description, flag automations that are broken or underperforming, and answer questions about results in plain language. Predictive features estimate the best time to send, how likely a contact is to buy, and which deals are most likely to close. A content assistant writes subject lines and email copy.

item.title: Acuity Scheduling
item.description:
Acuity Scheduling lets people book time with you through a branded page that you can link to or embed on a website. It syncs with Google, Outlook, and iCloud calendars so you never get double-booked, and clients pick from available slots in their own time zone. It is used by coaches, therapists, tutors, salons, consultants, and other service providers who sell appointments or classes.

Beyond booking, it handles the admin around an appointment. Clients can fill out custom intake forms, pay deposits or full fees, buy packages and gift certificates, and use coupons. Automatic email and text reminders reduce no-shows, and clients can reschedule themselves. Group classes, multiple staff calendars, and multiple locations are supported on higher plans. Integrations connect to Zoom, Stripe, PayPal, QuickBooks, and Zapier.

item.title: Ada
item.description: Ada helps companies handle customer support questions without adding staff. Its AI agent answers inquiries on websites, in apps, and over messaging channels by drawing on a company’s knowledge base and systems, and it can take actions such as checking an order, changing an address, or processing a return by connecting to back-end tools. When a request is too complex or sensitive, it hands the conversation to a human agent with context.

item.title: Ada Health
item.description:
Ada guides users through a structured conversation about their symptoms. It asks about what you feel, when it started, your medical history, and related factors, adapting each question based on earlier answers, and then shows possible conditions with likelihoods and recommendations such as self-care, seeing a doctor, or seeking urgent help. The app was developed with doctors and is available in several languages.

The consumer app is free to use, and Ada also licenses its technology to health systems and insurers, who embed it in their own services for triage and navigation. The aim is to help people understand their symptoms, avoid unnecessary visits, and know when something needs prompt attention. Users can share a summary with their clinician.

item.title: Adalo
item.description:
Adalo lets people without programming skills build mobile apps. You design screens with a drag-and-drop editor, add components such as lists, forms, and buttons, set up a database for your data, and define what happens when users interact. It handles user accounts, payments, and push notifications, and produces apps that can be published to the Apple App Store and Google Play, as well as web apps.

AI features speed up the first draft: you can describe an app and have the builder generate screens and data structures, then refine them manually. A marketplace of components and integrations extends functionality, and connections to external databases and APIs allow more complex apps. Typical projects include community directories, booking apps, marketplaces, internal tools, and simple social apps.

item.title: AdCreative.ai
item.description:
AdCreative.ai is aimed at marketers who need many ad variations quickly. You enter your brand colors, logo, and product details, and it produces sets of banners and social ads in different sizes, along with headlines and body text. Instead of starting from a blank canvas, you choose from designs and tweak them. That volume is useful for testing, since ad performance often depends on trying many variations.

What sets it apart is scoring. A creative score estimates how well each design is likely to perform, based on models trained on ad performance data, and insights tools suggest what to change. If you connect your ad accounts, the system can learn which visuals and copy work for your audience, and competitor insights show what rivals are running. Newer features add product photoshoots and user-generated-style videos made by AI.

item.title: Adobe After Effects
item.description: After Effects works on a timeline of layers that you animate, composite, and apply effects to. It is used for broadcast graphics, title sequences, explainer videos, social animations, and visual effects shots. Keyframes, expressions, and a huge plugin ecosystem give it flexibility, and it connects closely with Premiere Pro, Photoshop, Illustrator, and Cinema 4D, so assets move between apps easily. Many motion designers spend most of their working day in it.

item.title: Adobe Enhance Speech
item.description: Enhance Speech is a simple tool with a dramatic effect. You upload a recording of a voice, such as an interview, podcast, voiceover, or video narration, and the AI processes it to remove noise, reverb, and room echo, and rebalances the voice. In moments, a recording made on a phone in a kitchen can sound much closer to something recorded in a studio. It has become popular among creators who record in imperfect spaces.

item.title: Adobe Firefly
item.description: Firefly is Adobe’s generative AI platform. The Firefly web app generates images from a text description, extends or edits existing ones, creates short video clips, and produces audio and vector artwork. Adobe trained its own models on licensed content such as Adobe Stock and public-domain material, and it markets them as safer for commercial use than models trained on scraped images. Outputs carry content credentials that note they were made with AI.

item.title: Adobe Lightroom AI
item.description:
Lightroom is built for photographers who handle many images. It organizes a library, lets you rate and filter, and edits photos non-destructively with sliders for exposure, color, tone, and detail. Edits can be copied across a whole shoot, which saves hours after a wedding or event. Lightroom syncs between desktop, phone, and the web, while Lightroom Classic is the desktop-only version with a more traditional file-based workflow.

AI has changed the way people edit in it. Masking tools select the subject, sky, background, or people with a click, so you can adjust one part of a photo without painting a selection. Denoise cleans up high-ISO images while preserving detail, Generative Remove deletes distractions, and Lens Blur adds realistic background blur. Adaptive presets adjust to the content of each photo, and auto-edit settings give a starting point.

item.title: Adobe Podcast
item.description:
Adobe Podcast started with one very useful trick: you upload a voice recording made in a noisy room, and it comes back sounding like it was recorded in a studio. Enhance Speech removes hiss, echo, and background noise and evens out the voice. People use it to rescue interview audio, remote recordings, and phone-quality clips, and it works well on single speakers talking clearly.

The wider product is a browser-based recording and editing studio. You can record yourself or a remote guest, then edit by deleting words in the transcript, much like editing a text document. Features that clean up speech, adjust volume, and add music or sound effects sit alongside it. A mic check tool tests how your setup sounds before you start. Because everything runs in the browser, there is nothing to install, and files can be exported for use in other editors.

item.title: Adobe Premiere Pro AI
item.description: Premiere Pro is a timeline-based video editor used for everything from YouTube videos and corporate content to broadcast and feature work. It handles most camera formats, supports proxy workflows for heavy footage, and connects directly to After Effects, Audition, and other Adobe apps. That connection is a large part of why editing teams keep using it: a project can pass between an editor, a colorist, and a motion designer without leaving the Adobe ecosystem.

item.title: Adobe Sensei
item.description: Sensei is not an app you open. It is the label Adobe uses for the AI and machine learning that runs inside its products, from Photoshop and Premiere Pro to Lightroom, Acrobat, and the Experience Cloud marketing tools. When Photoshop selects a subject in one click, Premiere reframes a video for vertical, or Lightroom masks a sky automatically, that is Sensei doing the work. Many of these features arrived before generative AI became popular, and they handle analysis and automation more than image creation.

item.title: ADP
item.description:
ADP is one of the best-known payroll companies in the world. It pays employees, files payroll taxes, and manages benefits administration, time and attendance, hiring, and HR records. Products range from simple small-business payroll to large, multi-country platforms for enterprises, and many companies outsource payroll entirely to ADP to ensure accuracy and compliance with changing tax rules.

Technology is increasingly part of the offering. ADP uses AI for assistants that answer HR and payroll questions, flag errors before payroll runs, and give managers insight into workforce trends, using its large dataset of payroll information to benchmark pay and turnover. The platform integrates with accounting and HR systems, and mobile apps let employees see pay stubs and request time off.

item.title: Agent GPT
item.description: AgentGPT was one of the first tools that made autonomous agents easy to try. You open a web page, name an agent, describe a goal like planning a trip or researching a market, and click deploy. The agent then writes its own list of tasks, executes them one by one using a language model, and revises the list as it learns. Watching it reason through a goal in real time was a vivid demonstration of the idea behind agents.

item.title: Agno
item.description:
Agno, formerly called Phidata, aims to make agent building straightforward and fast. A developer defines an agent in a few lines: choose a model, give it instructions and tools, and optionally attach memory and a knowledge base. Agents can search the web, query databases, call APIs, and work with text, images, and audio. Multiple agents can be combined into teams that collaborate on complex tasks.

The framework emphasizes performance and production use. It is designed to start agents quickly and use little memory, which helps when many run at once, and it includes features such as session storage, retrieval from vector databases, structured outputs, and reasoning steps. AgentOS, a runtime layer, lets teams serve agents through an API with a control interface, and monitoring tools show runs and performance.

item.title: Ahrefs
item.description: Ahrefs is best known for its backlink data. Its crawler maps links across the web, so you can look at any site and see who links to it, which pages draw the most traffic, and what keywords bring visitors. Site Explorer is the tool most people open first, and it is often used to study a competitor’s strategy. Keywords Explorer suggests search terms and estimates how hard each one would be to rank for.

item.title: AI Dungeon
item.description:
AI Dungeon pioneered AI storytelling games. You choose a setting, such as fantasy, mystery, or survival, or create your own, and then type what your character does. The AI responds with what happens next, with no fixed script, so you can attempt anything and the story adapts. The result is a different kind of game from traditional adventures, with open-ended possibilities and sometimes surprising turns.

Creative tools are part of the platform. Players can build custom scenarios with their own characters and rules, share them with the community, and play adventures others have made. Story features let you edit and redo the AI’s output to steer the narrative, and memory settings help it keep track of characters and plot. Multiplayer modes let friends play together in one story.

item.title: AI For Developer
item.description:
AI For Developer is a niche directory focused on the developer audience. Instead of listing every AI product, it gathers tools that matter to people who write software: coding assistants, AI-powered editors, model APIs, testing and documentation tools, and infrastructure for building AI features. Listings give a short description, links, and categories, which makes it easy to browse by use case.

Directories like this serve as a starting point for discovery. They help developers learn what exists, compare similar tools, and keep up with the rapid pace of new launches. A curated approach aims to reduce the noise of general AI directories that include thousands of products across every field, by focusing on relevance to engineering.

item.title: AI-Writer
item.description:
AI-Writer takes a different approach from many article generators. You provide a headline and optional keywords, and it creates a full-length article that pulls in information from sources it finds and cites them, so the draft includes references you can check. This responds to a common complaint about AI writing, which is that it makes claims without support.

Additional features support content marketing. It offers SEO analysis to guide the article toward relevant terms, a built-in indicator that shows how much of the text is verifiable against its sources, and tools for creating outlines, rewriting, and summarizing. The tool is aimed at bloggers, affiliate marketers, and agencies that publish many articles.

item.title: AI21 Labs
item.description: AI21 Labs was founded by AI researchers in Tel Aviv and has been building language models since before ChatGPT made them mainstream. Its best-known models are the Jamba family, which blend a state-space architecture called Mamba with transformer layers. The aim is a model that handles very long documents with less memory and faster output than a standard transformer of similar size. Several Jamba versions have been released with open weights.

item.title: AIDir.wiki
item.description:
AIDir.wiki collects information about AI products in a wiki format. Each entry describes a tool or model, notes what it is for, lists key features and pricing information, and links to the official site. Because it is community-maintained, contributors can add new tools and update existing entries as products change, which is meant to keep information fresher than a static list.

The wiki structure encourages cross-linking, so related tools, alternatives, and categories connect. Visitors can browse by category or search for a specific product, and use it as a reference when comparing options. It joins a broad field of AI directories, from curated lists to large databases, and positions itself as an open, collaborative resource.

item.title: Aidoc
item.description:
Aidoc builds AI for radiology workflows. When a scan such as a head CT or chest CT is taken, Aidoc’s algorithms analyze it in the background and, if they detect a suspected critical finding, move the study to the top of the radiologist’s worklist and notify the relevant team. This shortens the time to review urgent cases like intracranial hemorrhage, pulmonary embolism, and aortic dissection, where minutes matter.

The company has grown from single-finding triage into a broader platform. It offers an operating system for deploying many algorithms, including those from other developers, and coordinates care for conditions that need multidisciplinary response. Recent work includes foundation models for imaging and tools that combine imaging with clinical data, and a growing number of FDA clearances.

item.title: Airbyte
item.description: Airbyte solves the data movement problem. Data teams use it to pull information from applications, databases, and APIs, such as Salesforce, Postgres, Stripe, and Google Ads, and load it into destinations such as Snowflake, BigQuery, and Databricks, on a schedule. Hundreds of pre-built connectors cover common sources, and a low-code builder, with AI assistance, lets teams create connectors for others. Because it is open source, the connector catalog grows with community contributions.

item.title: Airtable
item.description: Airtable looks like a spreadsheet but behaves like a database. Records live in tables with typed fields such as dates, attachments, checkboxes, and links to records in other tables, which allows relationships that spreadsheets cannot handle. The same data can be shown as a grid, kanban board, calendar, gallery, or timeline, and filters and groups tailor each view. It’s used for content calendars, product roadmaps, CRM, event planning, and operations.

item.title: AIVA
item.description: AIVA, short for Artificial Intelligence Virtual Artist, was built to compose music, with an early emphasis on classical and cinematic styles. You pick a style from a library of hundreds, set the length and key, and it generates a track. You can also upload an audio or MIDI file as an influence, or define your own chord progression. Video creators, game developers, podcasters, and advertisers use it to get background music without hiring a composer.

item.title: AIVE
item.description:
AIVE was described as a video enhancement service that used deep-learning super-resolution to sharpen detail, reduce noise, and raise the resolution of existing footage. That kind of tool takes low-resolution or damaged video, such as old family tapes, archival film, or compressed web clips, and reconstructs a clearer version. The idea is sound, and a number of products do it well.

The domain listed for AIVE no longer hosts a video enhancement tool. It now shows an unrelated media site, and searches turn up no active product of this name with the features described. A separate company called Aive makes a platform for automating video post-production for brands, which is a different kind of product. Because the original service cannot be confirmed, this entry should not be used as a recommendation.

item.title: Ajelix
item.description:
Ajelix is built for people who struggle with spreadsheet formulas. You describe what you want, such as the sum of sales in a region for a given month, and it produces the formula along with an explanation, so you can learn as you go. In reverse, you can paste a complicated formula and get a step-by-step explanation in plain language, which is useful when inheriting someone else’s workbook.

It also covers related tasks. Generators can write Google Apps Script and VBA macros from descriptions, convert formulas between Excel and Google Sheets, and assist with SQL queries. An analysis feature lets you upload a file and ask questions to create charts and summaries. The tools are available on the web and as add-ons for spreadsheet apps.

item.title: AlphaFold
item.description: AlphaFold tackled a problem that biologists worked on for fifty years: predicting how a chain of amino acids folds into a three-dimensional protein. Shape determines function, so knowing the structure helps researchers understand diseases, design drugs, and engineer enzymes. Before AlphaFold, determining a structure took expensive experiments such as X-ray crystallography that could take months or years. AlphaFold predicts many structures with accuracy that is often close to experimental results.

item.title: AlphaSense
item.description: AlphaSense is a search engine for business information. Analysts, investors, and strategy teams use it to find what companies and experts are saying across a large body of documents: earnings call transcripts, SEC filings, broker and industry research, press releases, news, and expert call transcripts. Its search understands financial language, so a query for supply chain risk or pricing pressure returns relevant passages instead of just keyword matches, with highlights and context.

item.title: Altered AI
item.description:
Altered focuses on voice conversion, sometimes called speech-to-speech. You record a performance, and the system re-voices it in another voice from its library while keeping the timing, emotion, and delivery of the original. That differs from text-to-speech, where the machine invents the performance. For productions, it means one actor can voice several characters, or a performance can be changed to match a different character without a second recording session.

The tools are designed for professionals. Altered Studio provides a way to process recordings and fine-tune results, and the platform includes text-to-speech and voice cloning options for productions that need them. Typical customers are game studios, audiobook makers, animation and film teams, and agencies that localize content. Licensed voices matter in this field, since using someone’s voice without permission raises legal and ethical issues.

item.title: Altern
item.description:
Altern is a browsable directory of AI products. Visitors can search by task or browse categories, such as writing, design, coding, and video, and see short descriptions, pricing, links, and user ratings. Rankings and filters aim to surface popular and well-regarded tools so people do not have to sift through thousands of options alone.

Tool makers can submit their products to be listed, and users can leave ratings and reviews. The directory also offers comparisons and alternatives for specific products, which is useful when you already know one tool and want to see similar ones. Like other discovery sites, it covers a wide range from established products to new launches.

item.title: Amazon Bedrock
item.description: Bedrock is how many companies on AWS use large language models without running any model infrastructure. Instead of signing separate contracts with each AI lab, you pick from a catalog of models from providers such as Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, and Amazon itself, and call them through one API. The data stays inside your AWS account, which matters to teams with security, privacy, and compliance requirements, and it works with the IAM, networking, and logging tools they already use.

item.title: Amazon CodeWhisperer
item.description:
CodeWhisperer was Amazon’s first coding assistant, a counterpart to GitHub Copilot that suggested lines and whole functions as you typed in editors such as VS Code and the JetBrains IDEs. It was trained with a special focus on AWS APIs, so it was particularly good at code that called S3, Lambda, DynamoDB, and other AWS services. It also supported many popular programming languages.

Two features set it apart from early rivals. A reference tracker flagged suggestions that resembled open-source code and showed the license, and a security scan checked your code for vulnerabilities such as exposed credentials and injection flaws. An individual tier was free, and a professional tier added admin controls and higher limits.

item.title: Amplenote
item.description:
Amplenote treats notes and tasks as part of the same system. You write notes with a Markdown-like editor, link them together, and embed tasks that appear both in the note and in a central task list and calendar. Daily jots capture quick thoughts, and the calendar shows tasks and events alongside notes, so planning the day and recording information happen in one place.

Its task score is an unusual feature: each task gets a number based on its importance, urgency, and effort, and the app highlights the highest-scoring tasks so you know where to begin. A plugin system lets users extend the app with scripts, including features that connect to outside tools. The built-in AI assistant can summarize notes, brainstorm, rewrite text, and use the contents of your notes as context, and it works on web, mobile, and desktop.

item.title: Amplitude AI
item.description: Amplitude helps product teams see what users actually do. You instrument your app or website to send events, such as signing up, clicking a button, or finishing a purchase, and Amplitude turns them into funnels, retention curves, user paths, and cohorts. These views answer questions like where new users drop off and which features bring people back. It is used by product managers, designers, and data analysts at companies from startups to large enterprises.

item.title: Andi
item.description:
Andi is a search engine for people who find link lists cluttered. You ask a question, and it returns a short answer with cited sources, plus links you can open. The idea is to combine the answering ability of a language model with the freshness of the web.

Privacy and design are part of the pitch. Andi has said it does not rely on advertising or sell user data, and the interface is clean, with options to refine a query and explore related questions. It is one of several startups, along with Perplexity, You.com, and Phind, that took on the conventional search model.

item.title: Anima
item.description:
Anima sits between designers and developers. A designer working in Figma, Sketch, or Adobe XD installs the plugin, and the tool turns the design into code that uses real layout rules, so pages respond to different screen sizes. Developers receive a starting point for components in frameworks like React and Vue.

It also helps with prototypes. Designers can add interactions and publish a clickable prototype for user testing, and Anima’s AI features generate designs and code from text prompts or from existing screens. Teams use it to cut the time between an approved design and a working front end.

item.title: Animaker
item.description:
Animaker lets people without animation skills make animated videos. You choose a template or start from scratch, add characters, props, backgrounds, and text, and arrange them on a timeline. A character builder customizes avatars with facial expressions and actions, and ready-made assets cover business, education, and storytelling scenes. It also supports whiteboard-style videos, infographic videos, and live-action editing, with exports up to 4K.

AI tools shorten the production steps. Text-to-animation turns a script into a rough animated scene, voiceover tools generate narration in many voices and languages, and translation and auto-subtitle features help localize videos. Teams use it for training videos, product explainers, school lessons, social media clips, and internal communications, where hiring an animation studio would be too costly.

item.title: AnythingLLM
item.description:
AnythingLLM gives you a private place to talk to your files. You add documents, web pages, or other content to a workspace, and the app indexes them in a vector database. When you ask a question, it retrieves relevant passages and sends them to a language model, which answers with references.

Flexibility is the main draw. You can choose a local model through Ollama or LM Studio, or a cloud model from providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic, and swap them without rebuilding your workspace. It has agents that can browse the web or run tools, supports multiple users and permissions in the server version, and offers an API and embeddable chat widget.

item.title: Anytype
item.description:
Anytype is a workspace for notes and structured information built around privacy. Data is stored locally and encrypted, and syncs between devices peer to peer or through backup nodes, so you keep ownership of your content rather than leaving it on a company server. The app is open source.

Its model uses objects and types. Everything is an object, such as a page, a person, a book, or a task, and each type has fields. Objects link to each other and appear in sets and collections, which function like databases. This lets users create a personal wiki or a custom organizer without code. Optional AI features can summarize and help write.

item.title: Anyword
item.description:
Anyword’s distinguishing feature is its performance prediction. When you ask for ad copy or an email subject line, the platform generates several versions and gives each a predicted score, based on models trained on large amounts of marketing performance data, along with an estimate for different audiences. The idea is to help marketers choose which copy to test or publish instead of guessing.

It works across typical marketing needs: ad copy for social and search, email campaigns, landing pages, blog content, and product descriptions. Brand voice settings and a knowledge base keep outputs consistent with a company’s tone and facts. Teams can integrate it with ad platforms and other tools, and an analytics layer connects the predictions with actual results. Targeting options adapt copy to specific audience segments.

item.title: Apollo
item.description:
Apollo gives sales teams a place to find and contact prospects. Users search a database of people and companies by title, industry, size, and technology used, then add leads to email sequences, calling lists, and LinkedIn tasks. A browser extension finds contact details as you browse the web.

The platform includes tools for the whole outbound workflow: email verification, scheduling, a dialer, meeting booking, analytics, and integrations with CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot. AI features help write messages, score leads, and automate steps, and workflows can enrich existing records to keep a CRM current.

item.title: Apollo
item.description: Apollo is one of the most used tools for outbound sales. At its core is a searchable database of business contacts and companies, which you can filter by job title, industry, company size, location, technology used, and more. You export the matches or push them into sequences, and Apollo supplies emails and phone numbers. Startups and small sales teams like that it bundles data and outreach in one affordable product.

item.title: Apple Maps
item.description: Apple Maps comes installed on every Apple device and has improved a great deal since its rocky start. It provides turn-by-turn driving directions, walking, cycling, and public transit routes, plus lane guidance and speed limit information. Features such as Look Around give a street-level view of many cities, detailed maps show buildings and landmarks in 3D, and downloadable offline maps work without a connection. Guides collect recommended places in a city, and you can share your arrival time with friends.

item.title: AppSheet
item.description:
AppSheet lets people create business apps without programming. You point it at data in Google Sheets, Excel, a database, or another source, and AppSheet generates an app with views, forms, and actions. Typical uses include field service, inspections, inventory tracking, approvals, and data collection, where workers need to capture information on a phone, with photos, barcodes, GPS, and signatures.

AI helps create apps. Gemini can build an app from a plain-language description, and an assistant can suggest improvements and write expressions. Automation features, called bots, trigger actions such as sending emails, updating records, or creating documents when data changes, and integrations connect with Google Workspace, Apps Script, and other services. Governance features cover access control and deployment for organizations.

item.title: Arc Browser
item.description: Arc reimagined the browser. Instead of a row of tabs across the top, it uses a vertical sidebar where tabs are grouped into spaces, such as work and personal, each with its own pinned items and theme. Tabs that you do not use are archived automatically, and features like split view, boosts for customizing websites, and easels for collecting ideas made it a favorite of power users and designers. It is built on Chromium, so most Chrome extensions work.

item.title: Artbreeder
item.description: Artbreeder began with an unusual idea: instead of typing a prompt, you start with existing images and breed them together, like mixing genes. Each image has sliders for traits, such as age, expression, or lighting for a portrait, so you can nudge it in a direction and save the results. Children of images can be crossed again, which lets a visual idea evolve step by step. The community shares images that others can remix.

item.title: Article Forge
item.description:
Article Forge is one of the older AI article generators. You enter a keyword and optionally subtopics, and it produces a long article with headings, sections, and optionally images and videos, in a few minutes. It was designed for people who publish a lot of content, such as affiliate sites, small business blogs, and agencies that manage many clients.

Further tools support publishing. A built-in scheduler can post articles to WordPress automatically, an uniqueness check helps avoid duplicate content, and options control article length, language, and tone. A rewriting function can adjust text, and API access lets developers integrate generation into other systems.

item.title: Asana
item.description:
Asana helps teams keep track of who is doing what by when. Work is organized into projects and tasks, viewable as lists, boards, timelines, or calendars, with dependencies, owners, due dates, and custom fields. Goals connect daily tasks to company objectives, and portfolios give leaders an overview of many projects.

AI features reduce the overhead of managing work. They can generate project plans from a description, summarize updates and conversations, answer questions about project status, and spot risks to deadlines. Asana has also introduced AI teammates that can be assigned work and operate inside projects, with controls to keep humans in charge. Automations handle routing and reminders.

item.title: Asana
item.description: Asana organizes work as tasks inside projects. Each task has an owner, a due date, and a place in a larger plan, and the same project can be viewed as a list, a kanban board, a timeline, or a calendar. Teams use it for campaign planning, product launches, client work, and operations requests, anywhere several people need to see who is doing what and by when. Portfolios and Goals roll individual projects up into a view managers can read without opening every one.

item.title: Attention Insight
item.description: Attention Insight offers an inexpensive shortcut to a classic design question: will anyone notice this? Upload a screenshot, ad, packaging mockup, or video, and its AI produces a heatmap of the areas likely to draw the eye in the first few seconds. The model is trained on eye-tracking data, so the predictions approximate what real viewers would do. It returns results in seconds, which makes it practical to compare several versions of a design.

item.title: Attentive
item.description:
Attentive helps brands market over text message. Shoppers opt in through signup forms and popups, and the brand sends campaigns, product alerts, and automated messages such as abandoned cart reminders and back-in-stock notices. Messages can include images and links, and customers can reply to start a conversation.

AI plays a part in targeting and content. The platform chooses send times, predicts which offers each subscriber might respond to, and helps write messages in a brand’s voice. Integrations with Shopify, Klaviyo, and other tools bring in purchase data, and analytics tie messages to revenue. A service team often helps brands set up programs.

item.title: Auphonic
item.description:
Auphonic automates the finishing steps of audio production. You upload a recording, such as a podcast episode or interview, and it applies adaptive leveling to even out volume differences between speakers, normalizes loudness to the standards used by streaming and broadcast, reduces background noise and hum, and applies filtering to improve clarity. The result is consistent, professional sounding audio with little manual work.

It supports multitrack recordings, where each person is recorded separately, and balances them automatically. Additional features include speech recognition to create transcripts, chapter marks, and exports to podcast hosts and cloud storage, and an API allows batch processing. Presets and a web interface make it approachable for non-engineers, and it’s used by independent podcasters, radio stations, and educators.

item.title: AutoCrit
item.description:
AutoCrit is an editing tool for novelists. A writer pastes in a chapter or uploads a manuscript, and the software reports on things editors look for: repeated words and phrases, adverbs, filter words, clichés, sentence variety, and dialogue. Reports highlight the text so you can see where to revise.

Its distinctive feature is comparison with published fiction. It measures a manuscript against patterns from successful books in the same genre, such as pacing and the balance of dialogue and description, so a writer can see how their draft differs. Generative features offer suggestions on revision and brainstorming, and a library of guides helps with craft.

item.title: AutoGen
item.description:
AutoGen made multi-agent applications approachable. Developers define agents with roles, such as a coder, a reviewer, and a user proxy, and let them converse to solve a problem. Agents can write and run code, call tools, and ask humans for input, and the framework manages the message passing between them.

The project began at Microsoft Research and attracted a large community. A visual tool, AutoGen Studio, let people prototype agent teams without code. Over time, Microsoft consolidated its efforts, pointing new projects to the Microsoft Agent Framework, which combines ideas from AutoGen and Semantic Kernel, and describing AutoGen as being in maintenance mode.

item.title: AutoGPT
item.description: AutoGPT went viral as an early demonstration of autonomous agents. You gave it a goal, and it would break the goal into steps, use tools such as web search and file access, and keep going without further instructions. It showed what was possible with language models and what was not, since those early agents often looped or got stuck. The project became one of the most starred repositories on GitHub.

item.title: Avoma
item.description: Avoma joins sales, customer success, and recruiting meetings on Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams, then records and transcribes them and produces notes organized by meeting type. Instead of a generic summary, it uses templates suited to the call, such as a discovery call or a customer check-in, and pulls out action items, objections, and next steps. Notes and key fields can be pushed into CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot, which saves reps from doing data entry after every call.

item.title: AWS GovCloud
item.description: AWS GovCloud is a separate set of AWS regions built for workloads that carry strict regulatory requirements. US government agencies, contractors, and other organizations handling controlled data use it to host systems that must comply with standards such as FedRAMP High, the Department of Defense Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide, ITAR, CJIS, and HIPAA. The regions are physically and logically isolated from the standard AWS regions, and access is restricted to vetted US citizens.

item.title: Azure OpenAI Service
item.description:
Azure OpenAI is OpenAI’s model lineup delivered through Microsoft’s cloud. Companies use it to get the same families of language, reasoning, image, and audio models, but under Azure’s terms, billing, and security controls. For regulated industries and large enterprises, that matters: the data is processed inside Azure, can be isolated on a private network, and is covered by Microsoft’s compliance certifications and service-level agreement.

Development happens in Microsoft Foundry, where you deploy a model, test it in a playground, and connect it to your own data and tools. Available features include fine-tuning, content filtering, tool and function calling, retrieval over company documents, and tracing. Deployments come in several types, such as standard pay-as-you-go, batch, and provisioned throughput, which reserves capacity for steady workloads with predictable latency. Foundry also offers non-OpenAI models, so teams can compare options in one place.

item.title: Babbel
item.description: Babbel focuses on getting learners to speak useful phrases quickly. Lessons last around ten to fifteen minutes and follow real-life topics such as ordering food, travel, work, and introductions. Content is written by teams of linguists and teachers, and each course is designed for a speaker of a specific native language, so explanations address the mistakes people with that background typically make. It covers more than a dozen languages, including Spanish, French, German, Italian, and Portuguese.

item.title: Babylon Health
item.description:
Babylon Health set out to make primary care available through a smartphone. Its app offered an AI-powered symptom checker and chatbot, video consultations with doctors, prescriptions, and health tracking. It partnered with the UK’s National Health Service, ran digital GP services, and expanded to countries including Rwanda and the United States, attracting large investment and a public listing.

The company faced criticism over the safety claims made for its AI, the quality of its services, and its finances. Doctors and researchers questioned how well the chatbot performed in comparison to human clinicians, and contracts with public health systems brought scrutiny. It then ran into financial trouble, and the business went into administration, with parts sold, including its UK operations.

item.title: Balto
item.description:
Balto sits beside an agent during a call. The software listens to the conversation, recognizes where it is in a script or process, and shows prompts on the agent’s screen: a question to ask, a compliance statement to read, a way to answer an objection. The aim is consistent performance across a team and less reliance on memory.

Supervisors benefit as well. Balto scores calls automatically, shows which behaviors lead to better outcomes, and reduces the number of calls reviewers must listen to by hand. New agents can ramp faster because the software coaches them in real time. Industries with strict rules, such as insurance and financial services, use it for compliance.

item.title: BambooHR
item.description:
BambooHR is built for companies without a large HR department. It keeps employee information in one place, tracks time off, handles onboarding checklists and documents, and offers an employee self-service portal. Applicant tracking helps with hiring, performance tools support reviews and goals, and payroll and benefits administration are available for U.S. customers. Reporting shows headcount, turnover, and other metrics.

The product is known for being easy to use, with a friendly interface and quick setup. AI features help HR teams with tasks such as drafting job descriptions and performance review language, summarizing feedback, and answering employee questions using company policies. Integrations connect with accounting, benefits, and productivity tools, and an app marketplace extends the platform.

item.title: Beatoven.ai
item.description: Beatoven.ai is aimed at video makers, podcasters, and game developers who need background music without searching a stock library. You describe the track you want, such as a calm acoustic piece for a travel vlog, or choose a genre, mood, and duration, and the AI composes an original piece. You can change the emotion of different sections along the timeline, which is helpful when a video moves from a tense moment to a resolved one.

item.title: Beautiful.ai
item.description:
Beautiful.ai tackles a common complaint about PowerPoint: you spend more time fiddling with alignment than thinking about content. Its slides are built from smart templates that rearrange themselves when you add or remove text, images, or chart elements, so the design stays clean. Rules keep spacing, fonts, and colors consistent, and a library of layouts covers timelines, comparisons, charts, team slides, and more.

AI features help create the first draft. You can describe a presentation, or paste in notes, and it generates an outline and slides in the app’s format, which you then edit. Teams can store brand colors, fonts, and logos in a shared theme, share slide libraries, and collaborate on decks with comments. Presentations can be exported to PowerPoint or PDF, or shared by link with view analytics.

item.title: BeFunky
item.description:
BeFunky is a browser-based editor for people who want quick results without learning Photoshop. The photo editor has sliders for exposure and color, crop and resize tools, and a large set of filters and effects. A collage maker arranges photos into layouts, and the graphic designer tool offers templates for social media posts, flyers, and cards. Everything runs in a web page, with mobile access too.

AI tools handle common edits. An enhancer sharpens and improves photos, a background remover cuts out subjects, and retouching tools smooth skin and remove blemishes. Artistic effects turn photos into paintings or cartoons, and an upscaler increases resolution. Newer features add AI image generation and a way to remove objects. Many of these are one-click operations, which is the main appeal.

item.title: BenevolentAI
item.description:
BenevolentAI built a platform that gathers large amounts of biomedical information, including scientific literature, clinical data, and experimental results, into a knowledge graph that connects diseases, genes, proteins, and drugs. Machine learning explores the graph to suggest which biological targets might be worth pursuing for a given disease and which molecules might act on them, aiming to speed up the early stages of drug discovery.

The company gained attention when its system flagged baricitinib, an existing drug, as a possible treatment for COVID-19, which was later supported by clinical trials. It has formed partnerships with large pharmaceutical firms and developed its own programs. The platform combines AI with scientists who validate predictions in the lab.

item.title: Betterworks
item.description:
Betterworks supports how companies manage performance throughout the year. Employees set goals or OKRs that link to company priorities, managers hold regular check-ins, and feedback and recognition are captured along the way. Review cycles then draw on this record, so evaluations rely less on recent memory.

AI features help with the writing and analysis. An assistant can improve goal statements, summarize a year of feedback into review drafts, and suggest coaching points, while analytics show goal progress and engagement across teams. Integrations connect with HR systems like Workday and collaboration tools such as Slack and Microsoft Teams.

item.title: BigCommerce
item.description:
BigCommerce provides the pieces needed to sell online. A merchant sets up a storefront with themes, manages products and inventory, accepts payments, calculates shipping and tax, and sells across channels such as Amazon, eBay, Google, social platforms, and marketplaces. Many features that other platforms handle through apps, such as product variants, reviews, and discounts, are built in, which keeps costs more predictable.

It stands out in two areas. It supports B2B commerce with features like customer-specific pricing, quotes, and bulk ordering, and it’s designed for headless setups in which the storefront is built separately and connected through APIs, which suits brands wanting a custom front end. AI tools help generate product descriptions, support merchandising, and optimize search, and an ecosystem of apps and partners extends the platform.

item.title: BILL AI
item.description:
BILL helps businesses handle bills and payments without paper and manual entry. Vendors’ invoices arrive by email or upload, the system extracts the details, routes them for approval, and schedules payment by ACH, check, or card. On the receivables side, it sends invoices to customers and collects payments.

AI takes on the data entry. It reads invoice fields, suggests accounting categories, matches invoices to purchase orders and receipts, and flags duplicates or unusual items. Integrations with QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, and other accounting systems keep the books in sync, and spend management tools add corporate cards and expense tracking.

item.title: Bing Chat
item.description: Bing Chat was Microsoft’s first big move into AI-assisted search. It put a conversational assistant next to the Bing search box, so you could ask a question and get a written answer with links to sources instead of scanning a page of results. Microsoft later renamed and expanded it as Copilot, and the assistant now works across the web, in the Edge browser, in Windows, and in standalone mobile and desktop apps.

item.title: Biteable
item.description:
Biteable makes video creation approachable for non-editors. Users pick a template for something like a company announcement, training clip, or social promo, and replace text, images, and footage scene by scene. Brand settings keep colors, fonts, and logos consistent across a team.

AI features accelerate the first draft. A script or prompt can generate a sequence of scenes with suggested visuals, text can be turned into narration, and videos can be resized for formats such as vertical social posts and widescreen. Collaboration features let teammates review and edit, and analytics show how videos perform.

item.title: Bito AI
item.description:
Bito started as a chat and code-completion assistant inside VS Code and JetBrains IDEs and as a command-line tool. You could ask it to explain a function, write unit tests, find bugs, or generate documentation, and it used a model of your choice for the answers. Its early appeal was practical convenience: reusable prompts for common tasks and support for working with context from your project.

The product has increasingly centered on code review. The AI Code Review Agent examines pull requests on GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket, leaves comments on issues such as bugs, security problems, and style violations, and summarizes the change for reviewers. It builds a model of the codebase so its feedback accounts for how the changed code fits with the rest, which helps reduce noisy comments. Teams use it to speed up reviews and catch issues earlier.

item.title: Blackbox AI
item.description: Blackbox AI was built for programmers. It offers code completion, a chat interface for coding questions, code search, and the ability to turn a screenshot or image into code. A VS Code extension and a web app made it easy to try, and the free tier helped it reach a large number of developers. Users ask it to explain unfamiliar code, convert code between languages, write functions, and fix errors.

item.title: Blue Yonder
item.description: Blue Yonder helps companies plan and run their supply chains. Demand forecasting predicts what customers will buy, inventory planning decides how much stock to hold and where, and transportation and warehouse systems manage how goods move. Retailers, manufacturers, and logistics providers use it to balance supply and demand, reduce stockouts and excess inventory, and respond to disruptions. The company grew from JDA Software and acquired an AI startup that gave it its name.

item.title: Boomerang
item.description: Boomerang adds time management to Gmail and Outlook. You can write an email and schedule it to send later, set a message to return to your inbox if nobody replies by a certain date, or hide an email until the moment you want to deal with it. Recurring messages, read receipts, and a pause feature that holds incoming mail until you choose to see it help people manage busy inboxes.

item.title: Boomy
item.description: Boomy is one of the easiest ways to generate music. You pick a style such as lo-fi, electronic, rap beats, or cinematic, and the system composes a track in moments. You can then adjust it by changing the arrangement, adding vocals or effects, and recording your own voice over the music. It requires no musical knowledge, which is why it appeals to casual creators and people who want custom background tracks.

item.title: Botkeeper
item.description:
Botkeeper offered accounting firms a way to scale bookkeeping with automation. Its software connected to clients’ accounting systems, categorized transactions with machine learning, reconciled accounts, and prepared financial statements, with human reviewers checking the work. The aim was to let firms serve more clients with the same staff and to reduce routine data entry.

The company raised substantial funding, but it shut down after losing a large share of its revenue when major customers were acquired and changed their arrangements. It then sold its Infinite AI platform to Xendoo, a bookkeeping firm, which said it would keep the platform active and supported as its own division. The long-term roadmap is less clear, and customers had to decide whether to move.

item.title: Brandmark
item.description:
Brandmark makes logo design accessible to people without a designer. You type a name and tagline, choose keywords, colors, and styles you like, and its algorithms generate many logo concepts that combine icons, fonts, and layouts. You can edit the colors, fonts, and arrangement, and see how the logo looks on mockups such as business cards and websites.

Rather than a subscription, Brandmark sells one-time packages. The basic package includes a logo in standard file formats, and higher tiers add vector files, social media graphics, a brand style guide, business card templates, and the right to use the design commercially. The vector files can be edited in design software, and the packages focus on getting a usable identity quickly.

item.title: Brandwatch
item.description:
Brandwatch is used by marketing, communications, and research teams to understand what people say online. It collects posts and mentions from social networks, news sites, forums, blogs, and reviews, and lets analysts build searches to track a brand, a competitor, a campaign, or a topic. Dashboards show volume over time, sentiment, demographics, top influencers, and emerging themes, which helps with campaign measurement, crisis monitoring, and product feedback.

AI plays a role in making sense of the data. Language models classify sentiment and topics, group conversations into themes, summarize large sets of posts, and answer questions about the findings in natural language. Image recognition finds logos in pictures posted without any text. Alerts warn teams when mentions spike, and the social management side supports publishing and responding to messages from one place.

item.title: Brave Leo
item.description: Leo sits in the browser’s sidebar and works with whatever page you are viewing. You can ask it to summarize an article or a long video transcript, explain a technical passage, extract key points from a PDF, or answer questions about the content, without copying text into a separate chatbot. It can also help write or rewrite text, translate, brainstorm, and answer general questions, with the option of using the web for current information.

item.title: Brevo AI
item.description:
Brevo started as an email marketing service called Sendinblue and has expanded into a broader customer engagement suite. It covers email and SMS campaigns, WhatsApp messaging, transactional email for apps, landing pages, forms, live chat, and a CRM for sales pipelines. Automation workflows send messages based on behavior, such as a signup or abandoned cart, and segmentation lets marketers target the right audience.

AI features support content and timing. A writing assistant drafts subject lines and email copy, generates images, and adjusts tone, while send-time optimization picks the best time to reach each contact. Predictive tools estimate engagement, and AI chat features help with customer conversations. The product is positioned for small and mid-sized businesses that want many channels in one tool at a reasonable price.

item.title: Brilliant
item.description:
Brilliant teaches by making you work through problems. Instead of watching a lecture, you manipulate diagrams, solve puzzles, and answer questions that build up from basic ideas, with immediate feedback. Lessons are short, so it fits into a daily routine. Courses cover topics such as logic, algebra, calculus, probability, statistics, physics, computer science, programming, and, more recently, AI and machine learning concepts.

The learning path is designed to develop intuition before formal rules. It breaks big topics into small steps, uses visuals heavily, and reviews earlier material to help it stick. Adaptive features adjust difficulty based on how you do, and AI features offer hints and explanations when you get stuck. Courses are written by educators and professionals, and they are polished in a way that appeals to curious adults as well as students.

item.title: Bubble
item.description:
Bubble lets people build real web apps without programming. The editor works by placing elements on a page, defining a database, and setting up workflows that say what happens when a user clicks or a condition occurs. Apps can include logins, payments, and integrations with other services.

It is used for marketplaces, internal tools, SaaS products, and prototypes, and some companies run substantial businesses on it. AI features can generate a starting app or page layout from a description, and plugins extend functionality. Bubble hosts the app, so there is no server to manage.

item.title: Bubble
item.description: Bubble lets people build real software without writing code. You design pages by dragging elements onto a canvas, define what happens when users click or submit with visual workflows, and store data in a built-in database. That is enough to build marketplaces, internal tools, customer portals, and SaaS products. Because the logic is visual but still detailed, Bubble apps can be quite complex, which is why it has been popular with founders who want to test an idea before hiring developers.

item.title: Buffer
item.description: Buffer is built for people who want to run their social accounts without living in each app. You connect your profiles, write a post once, adjust it per platform, and schedule it into a queue that publishes at set times. A calendar view shows what is planned, and an idea library keeps drafts and inspiration in one place. The interface is deliberately plain, which is a big part of why freelancers, creators, and small businesses like it.

item.title: Buoy Health
item.description: Buoy Health helps people decide what to do when they feel unwell. It asks a series of questions in a conversational flow, adapts based on the answers, and then provides possible explanations and a recommendation on the right level of care, such as self-care, a primary care visit, urgent care, or the emergency room. The aim is to reduce confusion and avoid unnecessary visits as well as delays in seeking urgent care.

item.title: Busuu
item.description:
Busuu offers courses in several popular languages, organized by the levels of the Common European Framework, from beginner to upper-intermediate. Lessons teach vocabulary, grammar, listening, reading, and speaking in short sessions, and a review system revisits words to help you remember them. Learners can set a goal, such as being ready for travel or a certain level, and the study plan adjusts to fit.

The feature that sets it apart is community feedback. You can write or record a short answer and have it corrected by native speakers who use the app, which gives real human feedback on your output. AI tools add conversation practice, personalized review, and explanations of mistakes. Some plans offer certificates and exam preparation for recognized language tests.

item.title: Buzzsprout
item.description:
Buzzsprout focuses on being the easiest way to get a podcast online. You upload an audio file, add show notes, and publish, and it distributes the episode to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other directories through an RSS feed it manages. It provides an embeddable player for your website, detailed download statistics, and tools for promoting episodes on social media.

Additional features help creators improve and grow. Magic Mastering automatically cleans up and balances audio loudness, an AI transcription service creates transcripts, and tools can generate chapters, episode titles, and descriptions. Dynamic content features and a way to import an existing podcast make switching easy. Monetization options include support from listeners and ads in some plans.

item.title: Calendly
item.description:
Calendly removes the back-and-forth of finding a meeting time. You connect your calendar, set the hours you are available and the types of meetings you offer, and share a link. Invitees choose a slot in their own time zone, and the event appears on both calendars with a video link added automatically. Buffers, meeting limits, and minimum notice settings keep the schedule manageable.

Teams use more advanced features. Round-robin scheduling spreads meetings across several people, collective events find times when everyone is free, and routing forms send prospects to the right person based on their answers. Workflows send reminders and follow-ups, payments can be collected through Stripe or PayPal, and integrations connect with Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Salesforce, HubSpot, and Slack. Newer AI features help with note-taking and scheduling assistance.

item.title: Canva
item.description: For infographics, Canva works as a template-first editor. You choose a layout for a process, timeline, comparison, statistic, or report, then replace the placeholder text and swap in your own colors and fonts. The element library supplies icons, illustrations, shapes, and photos, and chart tools let you paste or upload numbers to draw bar charts, pie charts, and other graphs that update when the data changes. Because it is a drag-and-drop tool, people without design training can produce something tidy in under an hour.

item.title: Canva
item.description: Canva is a design tool for people who are not designers. You start from a template, swap in your own text and photos, and export the result, which cuts out most of the layout decisions that make design software hard to learn. It covers social media posts, presentations, flyers, resumes, posters, short videos, whiteboards, and simple websites in one editor. A built-in library of photos, graphics, fonts, and music means most projects can be finished without leaving the app.

item.title: Capacity
item.description:
Capacity aims to be a single assistant across several support functions. It connects to a company’s knowledge sources and systems, then answers questions from employees about IT, HR, and policies, and from customers about products and orders. Automated workflows can complete actions such as resetting a password or opening a ticket.

The pitch is reducing the volume of tickets that require a person. By resolving common requests automatically and escalating the rest with context, it can free staff for harder issues. Analytics show which questions come up most and where documentation is lacking.

item.title: Captions AI
item.description: Captions is built for creators who film themselves speaking. You record or upload a video, and it transcribes the speech and adds stylish animated captions, which is important because many people watch social video with the sound off. It can remove filler words and silences, cut the video into a tighter version, and add zooms and effects that keep viewers watching. It works well on a phone, which suits creators who edit as they go.

item.title: Carbon Trust
item.description:
The Carbon Trust began as a UK organization set up to help businesses and the public sector cut emissions, and it now works internationally. It advises companies on how to measure their greenhouse gas emissions across operations and supply chains, set reduction targets, and plan the changes needed to meet them. Its work spans corporate carbon footprinting, product footprints, net zero strategy, and support with climate disclosure requirements.

A well-known part of its business is certification and standards. The Carbon Trust Standard recognizes organizations that measure and reduce their footprint, and other programs verify claims about products and supply chains. Software and data tools support these services, and AI is used to process large amounts of supplier and energy data, estimate emissions where measured data is missing, and identify the best reduction opportunities.

item.title: Carnegie Learning
item.description: Carnegie Learning grew out of research at Carnegie Mellon University on how people learn math. Its flagship product, MATHia, is an intelligent tutoring system that watches how a student solves each step of a problem, estimates which skills the student has mastered, and adjusts the next problem and hints accordingly. The aim is to give every student something like a personal tutor, with feedback at the moment a mistake occurs.

item.title: Cartesia
item.description:
Cartesia focuses on speed in voice AI. Its Sonic models, built on state-space model architectures instead of only transformers, generate natural-sounding speech with very low latency, so a voice agent can start speaking almost as soon as a response is ready. That matters for phone calls and live assistants, where delays feel awkward. The company also offers voice cloning and control over emotion and speaking rate.

The platform has grown into a set of real-time voice building blocks. Sonic handles text-to-speech, Ink handles speech-to-text, and tools for managed voice agents help companies deploy agents that answer phone calls. Developers connect through APIs and SDKs, and Cartesia works with common voice agent frameworks and telephony providers. Multilingual support lets one system serve customers in different languages.

item.title: Casetext
item.description: Casetext began as a community site where lawyers annotated and shared case law, then grew into a legal research service with tools such as a brief-checking feature called Parallel Search, which found relevant cases using natural language. It was among the first legal technology companies to build on large language models, and its CoCounsel assistant could review documents, summarize depositions, draft research memos, and help prepare contract analyses with citations to sources.

item.title: Causal
item.description:
Causal was created for finance teams that outgrew spreadsheets. Users build models from blocks that represent revenue, headcount, and costs, link them to data from accounting and CRM systems, and see results as charts and dashboards. The structure makes models easier to follow and share than a sprawling workbook.

Scenario planning is a core strength. Teams can change assumptions, such as hiring plans or pricing, and compare outcomes side by side, then present the results to executives and investors. AI features help create models from descriptions and explain changes in numbers.

item.title: CB Insights
item.description:
CB Insights tracks the innovation economy. Its database covers private companies, funding rounds, investors, acquisitions, patents, and news, and analysts and algorithms turn that into research on market trends. Corporate strategy teams, investors, and consultants use it to understand which sectors are growing and who the major players are.

Features include company profiles, market maps, forecasts of company outcomes, and an AI assistant that answers questions from the platform’s data and research. Alerts and newsletters keep subscribers up to date, and tools support building lists of companies matching specific criteria.

item.title: Cerebras
item.description:
Cerebras took an unusual approach to AI hardware. Instead of cutting a silicon wafer into many small chips, it builds a single enormous chip from the whole wafer, which holds an enormous amount of compute and on-chip memory. That design reduces the data movement between chips that slows down large models, and lets it generate tokens at very high speeds.

The company sells its systems and operates a cloud inference service where developers call open models through an API, with fast responses that suit agents, coding tools, and real-time applications. It has partnerships with AI labs and cloud providers, and supports training as well as inference. Developers can try the API with a free tier and then pay by usage, often at competitive per-token rates.

item.title: Charisma.ai
item.description:
Charisma.ai helps creators combine writing with generative AI. Instead of leaving a character entirely to a language model, creators design a story with scenes, goals, and character personalities, and the platform lets characters respond flexibly to what players say while steering the conversation along the intended narrative. This approach aims to keep stories coherent and on message, which is a common problem with free-form AI dialogue.

Tools include a visual story editor, character memory and emotion systems, voice and animation integration, and SDKs for Unity, Unreal, and web apps. The platform has been used for games, interactive entertainment, branded experiences, and training simulations where conversation practice is valuable. Writers can control tone and limits while still giving players freedom.

item.title: CharlieHR
item.description:
CharlieHR is designed for companies without a dedicated HR team. It keeps employee records, tracks time off, runs onboarding checklists, stores contracts, and supports regular reviews and one-on-ones. The interface is simple, so small teams can adopt it without lengthy setup.

An AI assistant helps with everyday HR questions about policies and employment topics, and supports tasks such as drafting job descriptions or other documents. Integrations connect with payroll providers, so data does not need to be entered twice. Reports give founders a view of headcount and absence.

item.title: Chatbase
item.description: Chatbase started as a simple way to create a chatbot from your own data. You upload files, point it to a website, or connect sources such as Notion, and it builds an agent that answers questions using that information. You embed the chat widget on your site with a snippet of code and you have support available around the clock. The simplicity made it popular with small businesses and startups that wanted a support bot without engineering work.

item.title: ChatGPT
item.description: ChatGPT is a chat interface to OpenAI’s language models. You type or speak a request and it answers in plain language, whether that means drafting an email, explaining a concept, debugging a function, or summarizing a long PDF. It can take images and files as input and generate images in return. For many people it is the first AI tool they ever used, and that familiarity is a big part of why it remains the default comparison for every other assistant.

item.title: ChatGPT Canvas
item.description:
Canvas changes how you work with ChatGPT on longer projects. When a request involves writing a document or code, ChatGPT can open a separate pane next to the conversation, where the text or code appears as an editable file. You can edit it directly, highlight a passage and ask ChatGPT to change just that part, and see changes without the whole response being regenerated.

For writing, shortcuts adjust the length, reading level, and tone, add polish or emojis, and suggest edits inline like a collaborator leaving comments. For coding, Canvas helps review code, add comments and logs, fix bugs, and port a project to another language, and it can run some code, such as Python, within the interface. Version history lets you go back to earlier drafts.

item.title: Chegg AI
item.description:
Chegg began by renting textbooks and grew into a subscription service for homework help. Students could search a library of solved textbook problems, ask experts questions, and get tutoring. The model worked well until general-purpose chatbots arrived, at which point many students began asking ChatGPT instead. Chegg’s traffic and subscriber numbers fell sharply, and the company has cut staff more than once and rethought its strategy.

CheggMate is the company’s response, an AI study assistant that combines large language models with Chegg’s own content. It aims to explain problems step by step, help with concepts, and generate practice questions, drawing on the study material the company has built over the years. The goal is to be more reliable for coursework than a generic chatbot because it grounds answers in verified content.

item.title: Chibi AI
item.description:
Chibi AI aims to support writers who produce longer pieces.
