Because the data lives in a familiar place, small business owners and operations teams can create apps for inventory, field reports, event check-ins, and customer portals without writing code.

The platform has added more advanced features over time. Users can set up roles and permissions, run workflows that send emails or update records, and connect to services through integrations. AI features can generate apps from a description, extract data from images and documents, and add AI-powered actions such as summarizing or categorizing. Glide’s own database supports larger datasets than a typical spreadsheet.

item.title: Gong
item.description:
Gong captures sales conversations and turns them into insight. It records calls and meetings, transcribes them, and pulls in emails and CRM data, then analyzes what is happening across the pipeline: which topics come up in deals that close, how often competitors are mentioned, how much reps talk compared with customers, and where deals are stalling. Managers can search a library of calls instead of relying on reps’ summaries.

The AI features save time at several levels. Calls are summarized with key points and next steps, which are written back to the CRM. Deal boards highlight risks, such as no recent contact with a decision-maker, and forecasting tools estimate which deals will close. Coaching tools find moments to review and compare behavior across reps, and newer AI agents help with tasks such as preparing for meetings, researching accounts, and drafting follow-ups.

item.title: Google AI Studio
item.description: Google AI Studio is where developers go to try Google’s models without setting anything up. You sign in with a Google account, pick a Gemini model, and start prompting in a playground that lets you adjust settings like temperature, add system instructions, and attach images, audio, video, or documents. Once a prompt works, one click gives you the code to run it through the Gemini API in Python, JavaScript, and other languages.

item.title: Google Assistant
item.description: Google Assistant is the voice assistant that ships on Android phones, Nest speakers and displays, Android Auto, Wear OS watches, and many third-party smart home devices. You wake it with a phrase or a button, then ask it to set a timer, add a calendar event, send a message, play music, or turn off the lights. It works well for short, concrete commands, and a large ecosystem of smart home brands supports it, which made it one of the more capable options for controlling a connected home.

item.title: Google Jules
item.description:
Jules is designed for the delegating style of AI-assisted coding. You link a GitHub repository, describe a task, and Jules makes a plan, works in a secure cloud virtual machine, and proposes changes while you do something else. It clones the repository, installs dependencies, writes code, runs tests, and presents the plan and results for your review. When you approve, it opens a pull request.

It handles routine, well-defined jobs such as bug fixes, adding tests, upgrading dependencies, updating documentation, and implementing small features. You can run several tasks in parallel, review the plan before it starts, and give feedback while it is working. It is powered by Google’s Gemini models and integrates with GitHub issues and the command line.

item.title: Google Maps
item.description: Google Maps is the default map for much of the world. It provides turn-by-turn navigation with live traffic and rerouting, public transit schedules, walking and cycling directions, and detailed maps with business hours, photos, reviews, and popular times. Street View lets you look at places at ground level, Live View uses your phone’s camera to show directions as arrows in the real world, and offline maps work without a connection.

item.title: Google Translate
item.description: Google Translate is the translation tool most people try first. You type or paste text and get a translation in a second, with the language detected automatically. The mobile app adds the features travelers rely on: a camera mode that replaces text on signs and menus, a conversation mode that translates both sides of a spoken exchange, handwriting input, and offline language packs that work without a connection. Chrome can translate whole web pages, and you can upload documents and get a translated copy.

item.title: Gorgias
item.description:
Gorgias is a helpdesk made for online stores. Messages from email, live chat, social media, SMS, and phone arrive in one inbox, with the customer’s order history, shipping status, and account details shown next to the conversation. Agents can refund an order, edit an address, or cancel a shipment without leaving the ticket, which speeds up the most common support tasks in retail.

Automation takes care of a lot of the repetitive work. Rules route and tag tickets, macros fill in standard replies with order data, and self-service flows let shoppers track orders or request returns. An AI agent answers questions about shipping, returns, and products using the store’s policies and catalog, and can complete actions in the store before passing complex issues to people. Gorgias can also support sales conversations and product recommendations.

item.title: GPT Engineer
item.description:
GPT Engineer was among the first projects to show that a language model could generate a whole working program from a prompt. A user wrote a specification, the tool asked clarifying questions, and then it produced files and code. The open-source command line version attracted a large community of developers.

The founders built a hosted product, gptengineer.app, that let non-programmers describe a web app and see it built. That product was renamed Lovable, which grew into one of the best-known AI app builders. The original open-source repository remains available as a way to experiment with prompt-to-code workflows.

item.title: GPTZero
item.description: GPTZero was created by a Princeton student soon after ChatGPT appeared and became one of the most used AI detectors. You paste text or upload a document, and it returns the probability that the writing is human or AI, with sentences highlighted by likelihood. It looks at features such as perplexity and burstiness, which describe how predictable and varied the writing is, and uses trained models for classification. Teachers, editors, and publishers use it to flag content for a closer look.

item.title: Grain
item.description:
Grain records meetings on Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and other platforms and turns them into transcripts, summaries, and short clips. Its clip feature is a distinguishing idea: instead of sharing a whole recording, you highlight a moment, such as a customer’s feedback or a question about pricing, and share just that clip with colleagues. This makes customer insights easier to spread across product, marketing, and leadership.

AI features produce structured notes from each meeting using templates, such as discovery calls or customer interviews, and answer questions across a library of recordings. Integrations send notes and fields to Salesforce, HubSpot, Notion, and Slack, which cuts manual updates. A desktop capture option can record meetings without a visible bot joining the call, which some teams prefer for external meetings.

item.title: Grammarly
item.description:
Grammarly started as a grammar checker and became the writing helper people keep installed everywhere. A browser extension, desktop app, mobile keyboard, and plugins for Word and Google Docs underline mistakes in emails, messages, and documents as you type. It catches typos and grammar errors, flags wordy or unclear sentences, and suggests a different tone, such as more confident or more friendly. A free version covers the basics.

Generative AI is built into the same flow. You can ask it to rewrite a paragraph, shorten a message, draft a reply to an email, or brainstorm ideas from a prompt. AI agents focus on particular jobs, such as giving feedback on a student paper, predicting how a reader might respond, or checking citations. Paid tiers add full-sentence rewrites, tone detection, plagiarism checking, and an AI detector, and business plans add style guides, brand tone, and analytics for teams.

item.title: Granular
item.description:
Granular was built to help large farm operations plan and track their business. Its software covered field activity and agronomy, inventory, labor, equipment, and financial reporting, and tried to give farm managers a view of costs and profitability for each crop and field. Corteva Agriscience acquired it, and for several years it was marketed to commercial growers who wanted enterprise-level tools.

The product line has since been restructured. Corteva discontinued Granular Agronomy, the field-level software, and sold the financial and business-management side to a company called Traction Ag. The pieces now go by different names and are maintained by different companies, which makes it important to confirm what is currently offered under the Granular name.

item.title: Greenhouse
item.description: Greenhouse is an applicant tracking system for companies that want hiring to be systematic instead of ad hoc. Each job has a defined process: a posting, a set of stages, interview kits with questions, and scorecards that interviewers fill out against the same criteria. The aim is to reduce bias and gut-feel decisions by making every candidate go through the same structured steps. Recruiters, hiring managers, and interviewers each get a view suited to their part of the work.

item.title: Groq
item.description: Groq is known for speed. Its chips, called Language Processing Units, were designed from scratch for running AI models rather than adapted from graphics hardware, and they produce text far faster than typical GPU-based services. That makes a difference for chat that feels instant, voice assistants that cannot afford to wait, and agents that make many model calls in a row. The company is not a model lab; it hosts models made by others.

item.title: GrowthBar
item.description:
GrowthBar tries to simplify SEO for people who are not specialists. You enter a keyword, and the tool shows search volume and difficulty, related keywords, and what the top-ranking pages cover, including their headings and word counts. A Chrome extension displays similar data directly in search results, which helps when researching competitors.

The AI content features turn that research into drafts. GrowthBar can generate outlines, blog posts, and meta descriptions, and tools for rewriting and expanding text help refine them. It also includes rank tracking and backlink data, and an AI assistant to help brainstorm topics. The target users are small business owners, freelancers, and agencies that publish content regularly.

item.title: H2O.ai
item.description:
H2O.ai built its reputation on open-source machine learning. H2O-3 is a widely used library for training models on large datasets, with an AutoML feature that tries many algorithms and picks the best. The company’s commercial Driverless AI automated feature engineering and model building for business users, and its tools have been used in finance, insurance, and healthcare.

More recently, H2O.ai has focused on generative AI. H2O LLM Studio lets teams fine-tune language models without much code, h2oGPT is an open-source project for chatting with documents, and its enterprise platform lets companies deploy private assistants and agents, including on-premises or in air-gapped environments. It has also released small language models designed to run efficiently.

item.title: Happy Scribe
item.description:
Happy Scribe converts speech into text. You upload an audio or video file, or connect a source like Zoom or YouTube, and receive a transcript in minutes with speaker labels and timestamps. It supports many languages and dialects, which suits journalists, researchers, podcasters, and companies that work in several markets. A browser editor lets you listen while you correct the text.

Subtitling is a major use. The service can generate subtitles and captions for videos, translate them into other languages, and export in standard formats for YouTube, Vimeo, and video editors. For cases where accuracy matters more, such as legal or broadcast work, you can order human-made transcripts and subtitles, which cost more and take longer. An API and integrations connect it to workflows.

item.title: Harvey
item.description:
Harvey was built for lawyers and has become one of the best-known legal AI companies. Attorneys use its assistant to ask legal questions, draft and revise contracts and memos, summarize documents, and analyze large sets of files, such as the documents in a due diligence review. It runs on leading language models adapted for legal work and is designed to provide citations so lawyers can verify the answers.

Beyond a chat assistant, Harvey offers structured features. Vault stores and analyzes large document collections, workflows automate multi-step tasks such as contract review against a playbook, and integrations connect with tools law firms already use, including document management and legal research providers. Firms can customize the system with their own templates and precedents, and security controls support the confidentiality requirements of legal practice.

item.title: Height
item.description: Height set out to make project management less manual. It was a task and project tracker with a clean interface, and its main idea was that AI should do routine upkeep: sorting incoming requests, writing and updating subtasks, assigning work, and keeping descriptions consistent. Teams used it as a lighter alternative to Jira with more automation, and the product drew fans among startups for its design and its early AI features.

item.title: Helpshift
item.description:
Helpshift places support inside the app. Users reach help from a screen in a game or mobile product, without leaving to email, and conversations carry context about the device, account, and recent activity. Agents see this information and respond in the same thread.

AI reduces the load. Intent detection reads messages, classifies the issue, and routes it to the right team, while chatbots answer common questions and collect details before a human steps in. A knowledge base and automation tools support self-service, and analytics track satisfaction and resolution times.

item.title: Heptabase
item.description: Heptabase treats notes as cards that you place on whiteboards, group, and connect. Instead of a long document or a folder tree, you build up an understanding of a topic visually: a card for each idea, laid out next to related ones, with arrows and sections that show structure. It suits people who learn and plan by seeing the relationships among ideas, such as researchers, students, writers, and product thinkers.

item.title: HeyGen
item.description: HeyGen lets you make a talking-head video without filming. You choose an avatar or create your own from a short recording, paste or write a script, and HeyGen generates a video with natural speech and lip movement. It supports dozens of languages, and one of its popular uses is video translation: upload a video of yourself, and it produces a version in another language with your voice and matching lip movements. Marketers, trainers, and sales teams use it to produce content quickly.

item.title: HiBob
item.description:
HiBob is built for companies that want a modern HR system for distributed teams. It stores employee records, handles onboarding and time off, supports performance reviews, and manages compensation and benefits. The interface is designed for employees as well as HR, with a social feel and company-wide features.

Analytics and AI help leaders. Compensation benchmarking compares pay with market data, workforce planning tools model headcount, and an assistant answers HR questions and drafts documents. Payroll integrations and a marketplace of apps connect Bob with finance and IT systems.

item.title: Homestyler
item.description:
Homestyler makes home design accessible. You draw a floor plan or start from a template, add walls, doors, and windows, and then furnish rooms from a catalog of real products and styles. A 3D view lets you walk through the space, and realistic renderings show how finishes and lighting would look. Homeowners use it to plan renovations and arrange furniture, and designers use it to present ideas to clients.

AI features speed up design. Tools can generate interior styles from a photo of a room, suggest layouts, and produce renderings from a simple description, and some features let you scan or upload a room as a starting point. Community galleries share designs for inspiration, and links to retailers make it easier to buy items you have selected.

item.title: Hootsuite
item.description:
Hootsuite is one of the oldest social media management tools. Teams connect accounts for networks such as Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, and YouTube, plan content on a calendar, schedule posts, and respond to comments and messages in a shared inbox. Approval workflows suit larger organizations.

Listening and analytics tools track brand mentions and compare performance across channels. OwlyWriter, the AI assistant, helps write captions, suggest ideas, and repurpose content. Advertising management and employee advocacy products extend the suite for enterprises.

item.title: Hotjar AI
item.description:
Hotjar helps teams see what visitors actually do on a site. Heatmaps show where people click, move, and scroll, session recordings replay individual visits, and on-page surveys and feedback widgets ask visitors what they think. Together they reveal confusing layouts, broken elements, and places where people give up, which complements numbers from analytics tools that show what happened but not why.

AI cuts down the time it takes to find insights. Instead of watching hundreds of recordings, teams can get automatic summaries of sessions, highlights of common frustrations, and analysis of open-ended survey responses grouped into themes. This helps designers, product managers, and marketers decide what to fix first. Funnels and trends let you see where users drop out, and integrations send findings to tools like Slack, Jira, and HubSpot.

item.title: Houzz
item.description:
Houzz started as a place to browse home photos and save ideas. Users look through millions of images of kitchens, bathrooms, gardens, and living rooms, save them to idea books, and find the products and professionals behind them. A directory lists architects, designers, and contractors with reviews and portfolios, so homeowners can contact people who match their taste and budget.

The platform includes a marketplace for furniture, lighting, and home goods, with augmented reality features that show how an item might look in your room. For professionals, Houzz Pro is software for managing leads, estimates, invoices, projects, and client communication, with tools to showcase their work. AI features help with design suggestions, image search, and automating parts of the business workflow.

item.title: HubSpot
item.description: HubSpot started as a marketing software company and grew into a full platform for managing the customer relationship from first visit to renewal. It is organized into hubs: Marketing Hub for email, forms, ads, and landing pages, Sales Hub for pipelines and sequences, Service Hub for tickets and help desk, Content Hub for websites and blogs, and Operations Hub for data syncing and automation. All of them read from the same CRM, so a marketer, a sales rep, and a support agent are looking at one record of the customer.

item.title: HubSpot
item.description: HubSpot began as an inbound marketing tool, and Marketing Hub is still the center of its original idea: attract visitors with useful content, capture them as contacts, and nurture them toward a purchase. It includes email marketing, landing pages, forms, blogging, social publishing, ad tracking, and SEO recommendations, all tied to a CRM that records every interaction with a contact. That shared data is what lets a marketer see which campaigns produce actual customers, not only clicks.

item.title: HubSpot CRM
item.description: HubSpot CRM is the shared database underneath every HubSpot product, and it can also be used on its own at no cost. It stores contacts, companies, deals, and tickets, logs emails and calls against each record, and shows a pipeline of deals by stage. Connecting Gmail or Outlook means sent and received messages are attached to the right contact automatically, so people spend less time on manual data entry. For a small business that has been running on spreadsheets, it is an easy first step into a real CRM.

item.title: Hugging Face
item.description: Hugging Face is often described as the GitHub of machine learning. Researchers and companies upload models and datasets to its Hub, where anyone can browse them, read the documentation, and download them. If an open model is released, whether a language model, an image generator, or a speech system, it almost always appears there first. Each model page has a card describing what it does, how it was trained, and how to use it, along with community discussions.

item.title: Hume AI
item.description: Hume AI started from research on human emotion. Its models analyze the way people speak and show emotion, including tone, pace, and inflection, and its Empathic Voice Interface (EVI) uses that understanding in a conversational voice assistant. EVI listens to the user’s voice, picks up on cues like frustration or excitement, and adjusts its responses and speaking style accordingly, so a voice agent can feel more natural than one that only transcribes words.

item.title: Hunter
item.description: Hunter is a tool for finding contact details for business outreach. A Domain Search shows the email addresses associated with a company along with the sources where they were found, and the email pattern the company uses. An Email Finder takes a person’s name and company and returns the most likely address with a confidence score. Email Verifier checks whether an address is valid and likely to deliver, which reduces bounces.

item.title: Hypotenuse AI
item.description:
Hypotenuse AI is built for online stores with large catalogs. You upload a spreadsheet of products with attributes, and it writes descriptions for each one, in a consistent tone and optimized for search, saving the effort of writing hundreds or thousands of descriptions by hand. It can also produce category pages, meta descriptions, blog posts, and ad copy.

Features support brand and workflow. A brand voice setting keeps text aligned with a company’s style, a plagiarism check helps ensure uniqueness, and integrations connect with Shopify and other platforms to publish content directly. The product also offers AI image tools for creating and editing product images and backgrounds, which makes it a toolkit for content across a catalog.

item.title: IBM Watson Government
item.description:
IBM Watson Government packages IBM’s AI offerings for the public sector. Agencies use them for tasks such as analyzing large volumes of text, extracting information from documents, supporting citizen service chatbots, and detecting fraud or anomalies in data. The emphasis is on meeting security and compliance standards that governments require.

The services run on IBM’s cloud and in hybrid environments, with options for on-premises deployment. Newer watsonx products add generative AI and governance tools for tracking models and risks, which agencies need under rules for responsible AI.

item.title: Imgflip
item.description:
Imgflip makes memes easy. Users pick from a large library of templates, add text, and download or share the result. Other tools on the site include GIF makers, a meme gallery, and custom template uploads, and the community creates and votes on content.

The AI meme generator speeds up the creative step. A user describes a topic or mood, and the tool chooses a template and writes captions, which can then be edited. People use it for social media, group chats, and marketing that leans on humor.

item.title: iNaturalist
item.description:
iNaturalist is a citizen science project and app. Users upload photos or sounds of organisms they find, a computer vision model suggests what species it is, and other observers weigh in. When enough people agree, the observation reaches research grade, and the data is shared with scientific databases.

The result is one of the largest collections of biodiversity observations. Researchers use it to track species ranges, detect invasive species, and study changes over time. Projects and bioblitz events organize community efforts, and schools use it for nature education.

item.title: Inciteful
item.description:
Inciteful takes a paper or a list of papers and builds a network of the research that surrounds them. Using citation data, it identifies the papers that are most connected, which tend to be foundational works, review articles, and recent developments. You enter a DOI, title, or several seed papers, and the tool shows a ranked list of papers, authors, and journals, with visual graphs of how they connect.

It is most useful early in a literature review. Starting from a few papers you know, you can discover similar and influential work you might have missed, track the most cited authors in the area, and spot new papers that cite your seeds. A Paper Discovery view finds the most important papers connected to your starting point, and a Literature Connector finds papers that link two different topics. Results can be exported to reference managers.

item.title: Indeed
item.description:
Indeed started as a search engine for job listings, pulling postings from company career pages and other boards into one place. Job seekers search by title and location, set alerts, upload a resume, and apply directly, often in a few clicks. The site also provides salary estimates, company information, and reviews, and Indeed is now closely tied to Glassdoor, which is part of the same company.

For employers, it is a major source of applicants. Companies post jobs for free or pay to sponsor them for more visibility, and tools help with screening questions, scheduling interviews, and messaging candidates. AI features match job seekers to relevant roles and recommend candidates to employers, summarize job requirements, and increasingly assist with resume improvement and hiring workflows. Recruiters search a resume database, with paid access to some functions.

item.title: Infermedica
item.description:
Infermedica builds medical decision support for patient-facing use. A person answers questions about symptoms in an adaptive interview, and the system estimates likely conditions and recommends a level of care, such as self-care, a doctor visit, or emergency services. Organizations embed this in their apps and websites.

The engine rests on a medical knowledge base maintained by physicians, combined with probabilistic reasoning and language models for understanding free text. Use cases include directing patients to the right service, preparing clinicians with an intake summary, and reducing unnecessary visits.

item.title: Infogram
item.description:
Infogram helps turn numbers into visual stories. You choose a template for an infographic, report, chart, or dashboard, import data from a spreadsheet or connect to a live source, and customize the design with your brand colors and fonts. The tool produces polished charts and maps, many of them interactive, that can be embedded on websites or shared as links.

Several features support data communication. Over thirty chart types, including maps and tables, handle different kinds of data, and live data connections update visuals when the source changes. Teams can collaborate on projects, keep brand templates, and publish with analytics. Downloads include images and PDFs, and AI features help generate visuals and suggest ways to present data.

item.title: INK Editor
item.description:
INK combines an editor with optimization guidance. As you write an article, the tool analyzes the search results for your target keyword and gives a score that reflects how well you cover the topic, which terms to include, and how readable the piece is. Suggestions appear in the sidebar, so you can improve the draft while writing instead of editing afterward.

AI features generate text and help overcome writer’s block. You can ask for outlines, introductions, and rewritten paragraphs, and use a plagiarism checker and content shield tools to monitor originality. The product works in a web editor and has extensions for common platforms, and teams can collaborate on content.

item.title: Insilico Medicine
item.description:
Insilico Medicine applies generative AI across the drug discovery process. PandaOmics analyzes biological data and literature to suggest disease targets, Chemistry42 designs novel molecules that bind to those targets, and other tools predict clinical trial outcomes and automate parts of the process. The idea is to cut the time and cost needed to move from an idea to a candidate drug.

The company has taken its approach into the clinic, with its own pipeline of drug candidates in areas such as fibrosis, cancer, and age-related diseases. One of its candidates, designed with the platform for a lung disease, advanced into human trials, which is regarded as an important test of whether AI-designed drugs can succeed. It also partners with pharmaceutical firms and sells software and services.

item.title: Intercom
item.description:
Intercom began as a live chat widget for websites and now covers the full range of customer communication. It combines a messenger on your site or app, a shared inbox for support teams, a searchable help center, email, and product tours. Companies use it to answer questions, onboard new users, and keep conversations in one thread across channels. It is common among software and subscription businesses.

Fin is the AI agent at the center of the current product. It reads your help articles and past conversations, then answers customer questions directly in chat and email, including follow-ups. When it cannot solve a problem or the customer asks for a person, it hands the conversation to a human with context attached. Fin can also take actions in other systems, like checking an order or updating an account, if you connect it. A copilot for human agents drafts replies and summarizes long threads.

item.title: InVideo
item.description:
InVideo targets creators and marketers who need many videos fast. In InVideo AI, you describe the video you want, such as a product explainer, a faceless YouTube video, or a social ad, and it writes a script, selects stock clips, adds a voiceover and music, and assembles it. You can then give plain-language instructions to change scenes, tone, or length, which makes iteration quick for people without editing skills.

The traditional editor remains for more control. It provides templates, a timeline, text and effects, and a large stock library, and it can turn blog posts and scripts into videos. Voice features include text-to-speech in many languages and voice cloning, and recent versions have added AI-generated video clips and avatars alongside stock footage. Exports are available in formats for different social platforms.

item.title: InVision
item.description:
InVision was one of the leading prototyping and design collaboration tools of the 2010s. Designers uploaded static screens, linked them into clickable prototypes, and shared them with stakeholders for feedback. It also offered a design system manager and, later, Freehand, a collaborative whiteboard.

As Figma and other tools took over design work, InVision’s usage declined, and the company announced it would close its products. Teams moved their work to other platforms, and exports were offered for a period before shutdown.

item.title: Inworld AI
item.description:
Inworld AI began by giving non-player characters in games personality, memory, and the ability to converse. Developers define a character’s background, goals, and knowledge, and the platform handles dialogue, emotion, and behavior using language models, so players can talk to characters freely instead of choosing from scripted options. Integrations with Unity and Unreal Engine make it easy to add to games.

The company has evolved toward infrastructure for real-time AI applications. Its runtime helps developers build and scale voice and conversational experiences with low latency, and it offers text-to-speech models and tools for combining speech recognition, language models, and voice into agents. Use cases extend from games to training simulations, companions, and consumer apps with talking characters.

item.title: Ironclad
item.description:
Ironclad serves legal and business teams that handle many contracts. Requests start from templates through a workflow, drafts are negotiated with counterparties inside the platform, and approvals and e-signatures finish the process. Executed contracts become structured data in a repository.

AI features are central. They read incoming contracts, flag deviations from company positions, suggest edits, and extract key terms such as renewal dates and liability caps. A repository search lets teams answer questions about their agreements, and reports show where contracts get stuck.

item.title: IXL
item.description:
IXL provides practice at scale. Students work through skills organized by grade level, and the questions get easier or harder based on their answers. Instant feedback explains mistakes, and a real-time diagnostic estimates the level at which a student is working across subjects.

Teachers and parents get reports showing progress, strengths, and gaps, and suggested next skills. The platform aligns with state standards, which helps classroom use. AI features offer personalized recommendations and help with tutoring, and the company offers add-ons such as a writing coach.

item.title: iZotope RX
item.description:
RX is the tool engineers reach for when audio is flawed. Its spectral display shows sound as an image, making it possible to see and remove specific problems, such as a cough, a phone buzz, or a chair squeak, without affecting the rest. Modules cover denoising, de-clicking, de-hum, de-reverb, de-clipping, and other repair tasks, and are used by post-production teams, podcast producers, forensic analysts, and musicians.

Machine learning powers its newer tools. Dialogue Isolate separates speech from background sounds, Music Rebalance lets you adjust the levels of vocals, bass, and drums in a finished mix, and Spectral Recovery restores high frequencies lost in low-quality files. Dialogue Contour and other features help produce consistent speech. It works as a standalone editor and as plugins in digital audio workstations and video editors.

item.title: Jan
item.description:
Jan lets you use language models without sending data anywhere. After installing the app, you browse a model hub, download models such as Llama, Mistral, or Qwen in a size your hardware can handle, and chat with them offline. Everything runs on your machine, which is attractive to people concerned about privacy or working without internet access, and it avoids per-use fees.

It is more than a chat window. Jan can connect to remote services like OpenAI and Anthropic with your own API keys, so you can switch between local and cloud models in one interface. A local server exposes an OpenAI-compatible API, so other tools can use your models, and support for the Model Context Protocol lets assistants use tools. The project also develops its own small models tuned for tasks.

item.title: Jasper
item.description:
For copywriting, Jasper offers more structure than a general chatbot. Marketers choose a format such as a Facebook ad, a product description, a landing page section, or an email sequence, supply the details, and get multiple options in their brand’s voice. The Brand Voice feature learns tone and style from examples, and a company knowledge base provides facts about products and audiences so the copy uses accurate claims.

Collaboration features suit teams. Shared templates and style guides keep writers consistent, and campaigns can be planned in one place with copy, images, and variations for different channels. An editor helps refine text, change tone, and check for plagiarism. Newer agent features help automate common marketing tasks, such as producing a set of assets from a brief.

item.title: Jasper
item.description:
As a marketing platform, Jasper aims to speed up the full path from a brief to a finished campaign. Marketers define their brand voice, audience, and product information once, then generate blog posts, social posts, ads, emails, and landing pages that follow those guidelines. Campaign tools help plan content around a launch, adapt messages for each channel, and keep versions organized.

The latest versions emphasize agents and workflows. Specialized agents handle tasks such as researching a topic, creating a content calendar, repurposing a webinar into several assets, and optimizing copy for search. Integrations connect with tools such as Google Docs, Webflow, and HubSpot, and analytics features tie content to performance. Controls let enterprises govern who can use what and ensure compliance with brand rules.

item.title: Jasper
item.description: Jasper was one of the first dedicated AI writing products and has focused on marketing teams that need a lot of on-brand content. You describe what you need, such as a product launch email or a set of ad variations, and it drafts the copy using your guidelines. Brand Voice learns your tone from sample content, and a knowledge base stores product details, audiences, and approved messaging, so output needs fewer corrections.

item.title: Jenni AI
item.description:
Jenni AI is designed around the way academics write. In its editor, you start a document and Jenni suggests how to continue sentences, offers to expand or rephrase text, and helps structure arguments. It can generate an outline from a topic and help draft sections, with the writer keeping control and deciding what to accept.

Research features distinguish it from general writing tools. You can search for academic sources, insert citations in styles such as APA and MLA, and manage a bibliography. A feature lets you upload PDFs and ask questions about them, so you can use sources more efficiently. The tool also supports different citation formats and exports to common document formats.

item.title: John Deere Operations Center
item.description:
The Operations Center connects Deere equipment to farm management. Tractors, planters, sprayers, and combines send data about where they worked, what they applied, and how crops yielded, and farmers see this on field maps. Records of planting, spraying, and harvest are kept in one place and can be shared with advisors.

From that data, the platform helps plan the next season. Prescriptions vary seed or fertilizer rates across a field, and analytics compare performance between fields and years. Integrations with other agronomy software and equipment from other makers extend its reach, and AI is used for tasks such as image-based crop and weed detection on machines.

item.title: Juro
item.description:
Juro puts the contract workflow in a browser editor. Sales and business teams generate contracts from approved templates, negotiate with counterparties in the same document, collect signatures, and store the result in a searchable repository. Legal sets the rules and approvals, so routine deals move without a lawyer.

AI is part of the product. It can draft clauses from a plain-English description, review third-party paper against a company’s positions, summarize agreements, and answer questions about the contract portfolio. Integrations with CRMs and messaging tools keep the process connected to sales.

item.title: K Health
item.description:
K Health begins with a conversation. In the app, you describe your symptoms and answer questions, and the AI compares your information with a large database of anonymized patient records to suggest what similar patients turned out to have, along with possible next steps. The symptom checker is free and meant to help you decide what to do.

If you need care, you can move to a visit with a clinician through messaging or video, often within minutes, for common issues such as colds, infections, and prescriptions, and for ongoing care with a primary care provider. The company works with health systems and insurers in some places, and it offers programs for conditions like mental health and weight management. AI helps summarize information for doctors and speeds up triage.

item.title: Kaedim
item.description:
Kaedim addresses a slow stage in game and digital content production: turning concept art into 3D assets. You upload an image of a character, prop, or environment piece, and Kaedim produces a 3D model that matches it. The aim is to give artists a solid starting point they can refine, which cuts down the days of modeling work needed for each asset.

The service has been known for mixing machine learning with human review. Models go through checks by 3D artists who clean up errors before they are delivered, which improves reliability compared with fully automatic generators, but may slow turnaround. Output can be downloaded in common formats and used in engines like Unity and Unreal or imported into Blender and Maya for editing. Teams use it for game props, virtual production, and prototyping product ideas.

item.title: Kagi
item.description:
Kagi takes a different business model from other search engines: users pay a subscription, and in return there are no ads, no tracking-based profiles, and no incentive to favor advertisers. Results are meant to be clean and relevant, and the company says it does not sell data. The service uses several sources, including its own index of smaller sites, and puts effort into reducing low-quality content and SEO spam.

Control is a defining feature. Users can raise, lower, or block domains, so a site that is always useless for you disappears, and lenses restrict a search to a set of sources, such as forums or academic sites. AI tools include summaries of pages and videos, answers with citations, and an assistant that gives access to multiple language models. Kagi has also launched Orion, a privacy-focused browser, and other products around the search experience.

item.title: Kapwing
item.description:
Kapwing is an online editor aimed at creators and teams who need fast, polished content. You upload video or start from a template, trim, add captions, music, and effects, and export in formats suited to platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube. Because it runs in the browser, there is nothing to install, and collaborators can work in the same project and leave comments.

AI features are at the center of the workflow. Auto subtitles transcribe speech and add stylized captions in many languages, background removal works without a green screen, and tools can remove silences and filler words, translate and dub videos, and clean up audio. A repurposing tool cuts long videos into short clips for social media, and text-to-video and script features help generate drafts. Brand kits keep fonts and colors consistent.

item.title: Kasisto
item.description:
Kasisto builds AI assistants for banks. Its KAI technology understands banking questions and can carry out actions, such as showing recent transactions, transferring funds, or explaining a fee, in a chat within a bank’s mobile app or website. The language models are tuned to the vocabulary and rules of finance.

A newer product, KAI Answers, uses generative AI to answer questions from a bank’s own policies and documents, with citations so staff and customers can see the source. Banks use it to cut call volumes and improve self-service, and the company has worked with institutions around the world.

item.title: Kensho
item.description:
Kensho began as a startup applying machine learning to financial markets and was acquired by S&P Global, where it operates as the company’s AI innovation hub. Its products address practical data problems in finance. Kensho Link matches records between data sets, such as linking company names across different sources, Kensho Classify tags documents by category, and Kensho Extract pulls data out of PDFs and filings.

More recent work connects financial data to generative AI. Kensho develops tools that allow AI assistants and agents to access S&P Global’s data reliably, with grounding that provides sources for answers, plus language models and benchmarks for finance. Its technology supports S&P products and is available to clients who want to build their own applications.

item.title: Khan Academy
item.description:
Khan Academy provides free education to anyone with an internet connection. Its library of short videos, articles, and interactive exercises covers school subjects from basic arithmetic through calculus, biology, chemistry, grammar, history, and test preparation such as the SAT. Learners can follow structured courses, and the mastery system encourages students to practice until they have a skill before moving ahead.

For teachers and schools, it offers tools to assign work, track progress, and see which students need help. District partnerships connect it with curricula, and Khan Academy Kids offers content for young children in a separate app. The nonprofit is funded by donations and philanthropic support rather than by charging learners, which sets it apart from commercial education companies.

item.title: Khanmigo
item.description:
Khanmigo is designed around a tutoring philosophy. Instead of handing students the answer, it asks guiding questions, offers hints, and checks understanding, much like a good human tutor. It works with Khan Academy’s exercises and videos, so it can step in when a student gets stuck on a particular problem. It also offers activities such as practicing a debate, writing with feedback, and exploring historical figures through role-play.

Teachers have a version with tools that save planning time. It can help create lesson plans, quizzes, rubrics, and examples, suggest ways to explain a concept, and differentiate material for different levels. Teachers can see how students interact with it, which provides insight into where they struggle. Safeguards are built in, such as moderation and notifying adults if conversations raise concerns, because the users are children.

item.title: Kickresume
item.description:
Kickresume helps people create resumes quickly. You choose a template, enter your experience, and the builder arranges everything in a clean layout. A library of professionally designed templates covers different industries and styles, and the exports are designed to be readable by applicant tracking systems, which scan resumes before a human sees them. It also builds cover letters, personal websites, and portfolios.

AI assists with the writing. The AI resume writer can generate summaries and bullet points from your role and achievements, tailor a resume for a specific job description, and write a cover letter. A resume checker evaluates structure, keywords, and clarity and suggests improvements, and extra tools help with interview practice and job tracking. The AI features speed up drafting but can produce generic language.

item.title: Kimi
item.description:
Kimi first gained attention for handling very long documents. Users can upload large PDFs, books, or collections of files and ask questions, and the assistant keeps track of the whole text, which suited tasks like summarizing reports and analyzing contracts. It also searches the web, writes and reasons about code, and has agent features that carry out multi-step tasks.

Moonshot AI releases powerful models, including open-weight versions of its Kimi K2 family, which are among the larger open models and strong at coding and agentic tasks. Developers use them through Moonshot’s API or run them through third-party providers, and they are often used inside coding tools. The company competes with other Chinese labs such as DeepSeek, Alibaba, and Zhipu.

item.title: Kira Systems
item.description:
Kira was one of the first widely adopted machine learning tools in legal work. It reads contracts and identifies provisions such as change of control, termination rights, assignment, and indemnification, then extracts the relevant text into a structured summary. Lawyers use it in mergers and acquisitions due diligence, where hundreds or thousands of agreements must be reviewed quickly, and in lease, finance, and compliance reviews.

Litera acquired Kira Systems and continues to develop it. The newer version adds generative AI to the original extraction models, with features like rapid clause analysis that organizes clauses across many documents. Users can start from built-in models for common provisions, train their own for specific needs, and review results in a side-by-side view that links back to the source text. Integration with Litera’s other tools connects review to drafting and transaction workflows.

item.title: Klaviyo AI
item.description:
Klaviyo is built on the idea that a store’s own customer data is the best basis for marketing. It connects to platforms like Shopify, BigCommerce, and WooCommerce, pulling in orders, browsing behavior, and product information. Marketers build segments, such as customers who bought twice in the last 60 days, and send targeted email and SMS campaigns and automated flows, like abandoned cart reminders, welcome series, and post-purchase follow-ups.

AI adds prediction and automation. Klaviyo estimates a customer’s likelihood to buy again, expected lifetime value, and probable next order date, and uses those signals for segmentation. Product recommendations personalize emails, send-time optimization chooses delivery times, and generative tools write subject lines and campaign copy and build flows from a description. A customer hub, reviews, and a CDP add other parts of the retention workflow.

item.title: Koala AI
item.description: Koala focuses on creating articles that are designed to rank. You enter a keyword, and the tool analyzes current search results, collects information from the web, and writes a structured article with headings, optional images, and links. It supports one-click generation of long pieces, and special modes for product reviews, listicles, and how-to guides. Real-time data is meant to keep information fresh compared with models that only use training data.

item.title: Krisp
item.description: Krisp installs as a virtual microphone and speaker, so it sits between your hardware and whatever calling app you use. It removes noise before it reaches the other person: barking dogs, keyboard clatter, traffic, and other voices in the room. It can also clean incoming audio, so a participant on a bad connection or in a loud space sounds clearer to you. Because it works with Zoom, Teams, Meet, Slack, and nearly any other app, one setup covers all of them.

item.title: Kustomer AI
item.description:
Kustomer takes a CRM-style approach to support. Instead of treating each ticket as an isolated item, it builds a timeline for each customer that includes every conversation, order, and interaction across channels. Agents see the full history in one view, which reduces the need to ask customers to repeat themselves. Channels include email, chat, SMS, social messaging, and voice, and workflow rules automate routing and tagging.

AI features have grown in importance. AI agents can answer common questions, check order status, and complete simple actions, escalating complex cases to humans with context. Tools for human agents summarize long histories, suggest replies, and classify issues, and insights analyze conversation patterns to find problems in products or processes. The system connects with e-commerce and business platforms to bring in order and account data.

item.title: Lambda Labs
item.description:
Lambda started by selling deep learning workstations and servers to researchers and grew into a GPU cloud. Developers rent instances with NVIDIA GPUs, from single machines to large clusters, pre-configured with the Lambda Stack of machine learning software, so they can start training or running models quickly. Its focus on AI workloads and straightforward pricing has made it a favorite among startups, universities, and AI labs.

The company offers several ways to buy compute. On-demand instances are billed by the hour, reserved capacity provides discounted access for longer commitments, and 1-Click clusters let teams spin up multi-node setups for large training runs. Lambda also sells hardware for on-premises use, including workstations and servers, and offers inference services for deploying models.

item.title: LANDR
item.description:
LANDR started with automated mastering. An artist uploads a mixed song, the system analyzes it, and an algorithm applies equalization, compression, and loudness adjustments, producing a master in minutes at a price below hiring an engineer. Style and loudness options guide the result.

The company now offers a wider set of services for independent musicians: distribution to streaming platforms, a marketplace of samples, plugins, a collaboration network, and tools for mixing and creating. A subscription bundles many of these.

item.title: LangChain
item.description: LangChain gave developers a common toolkit when language models first became available through APIs. It supplies building blocks for the typical parts of an AI application: calling a model, formatting prompts, parsing outputs, connecting to tools and data sources, and keeping memory of a conversation. Because it supports many model providers and vector stores behind consistent interfaces, you can swap one for another with little code change. Python and JavaScript versions are available.

item.title: Langflow
item.description:
Langflow makes it possible to design an AI application by connecting blocks on a canvas. Components represent language models, prompts, memory, document loaders, vector stores, and tools, and you wire them together to define how data flows. An integrated playground lets you chat with the flow, inspect each step, and adjust it, which is useful for experimenting with retrieval and agent behavior without writing a full application.

Flows can be exported and run as API endpoints or embedded in apps, and you can write custom components in Python when the built-in ones are not enough. It works with many model providers and vector databases, and supports multi-agent setups and Model Context Protocol servers. Teams use it for prototypes, internal assistants, and RAG pipelines before moving to code.

item.title: LanguageTool
item.description:
LanguageTool checks writing for spelling, grammar, punctuation, and style, and is notable for its broad language support, including English, German, French, Spanish, Dutch, Portuguese, and many more. It runs as browser extensions, add-ins for Microsoft Word and Google Docs, a desktop app, and an API, so it can check text wherever you write. Many people use it for writing in a second language or switching between languages.

The core engine is open source and can be self-hosted, which appeals to organizations with privacy requirements and to developers who want to integrate a checker. The premium tier adds more advanced style suggestions, tone and clarity feedback, and AI-powered rephrasing, along with higher character limits. Teams can set custom dictionaries and style rules.

item.title: Later
item.description:
Later started as a way to plan Instagram feeds visually. Users drag photos and videos onto a calendar, see how the grid will look, write captions, and schedule posts to go out automatically. It has since expanded to other networks, including TikTok, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Facebook, and X, with tools to manage a content library, collaborate with teammates, and track results.

Other features support social growth. A link-in-bio page lets creators send followers to multiple destinations, analytics show which posts perform best and when audiences are most active, and AI helps write captions, suggest hashtags, and repurpose content. The company also owns an influencer marketing platform, which helps brands find creators and manage campaigns.

item.title: Lattice AI
item.description:
Lattice helps companies run performance and development programs. Managers and employees complete reviews and give continuous feedback, set goals and OKRs, hold one-on-ones with shared agendas, and track growth plans. Engagement surveys measure how employees feel, and compensation tools support pay reviews and planning, while an HR information system keeps employee records.

AI is added to reduce busywork. It can help managers draft feedback and review summaries, analyze survey comments for themes, and suggest talking points for one-on-ones. Insights flag possible retention risks or teams with low engagement, and an AI assistant answers questions about company data. The company has also launched products for managing AI agents as part of the workforce, a controversial idea.

item.title: LawGeex
item.description:
LawGeex addresses the high volume of routine contracts that reach legal departments, such as NDAs and standard vendor agreements. Legal teams define a playbook that states what is acceptable in each type of clause, and LawGeex’s AI reads incoming contracts and checks them against it. Contracts that conform can be approved quickly, and those that deviate are flagged with the problem and suggested edits.

The idea is to let lawyers focus on contracts that really need judgment. Business users can submit documents for review through integrations and workflows, and reviewers see a clear summary of what matched, what did not, and where to look. The system learns from corrections, and reporting shows how many contracts were reviewed and how long approvals take. It supports a range of commercial agreements.

item.title: Le Chat
item.description:
Le Chat is Mistral’s answer to ChatGPT and Claude. The French company designed the app for general use: answering questions, writing and editing, summarizing documents, analyzing images, generating images, and running code. Fast response modes make it quick for everyday queries, and a canvas supports working on documents and code beside the chat.

Further features address more advanced needs. Deep research compiles longer reports from web sources, connectors link to services like Gmail, Google Drive, and Notion, and custom agents let users set up specialized assistants. Memory can retain preferences between chats, and mobile apps bring it to phones. The assistant uses Mistral’s own models, some of which are open-weight, and emphasizes European hosting and privacy options.

item.title: Leapsome
item.description:
Leapsome gathers people processes in one product. HR teams run review cycles, set goals and OKRs, send engagement surveys, deliver learning content, and manage compensation planning, with the data connected so decisions draw on the full picture. It is used by mid-sized, often distributed companies.

AI helps with the heaviest reading and writing. It summarizes feedback, analyzes comments from surveys for sentiment and themes, helps managers draft reviews, and suggests development actions. Dashboards show trends by team.

item.title: Lens.org
item.description:
The Lens aims to make innovation data open. It combines a very large database of patents from patent offices worldwide with scholarly works from sources like Crossref, PubMed, and others. Users can search by keywords, inventors, institutions, or classifications, and the results show patent families, legal status, citations, and links to the full text where available. The free access sets it apart from commercial patent databases.

The key feature is the connection between patents and papers. It tracks which scholarly works are cited in patents, which lets researchers and technology transfer offices see how academic research is used in inventions, and lets innovators find prior art. Collections let you save and share sets of results, and analytics and dashboards visualize trends, such as top applicants or fast-growing technology areas. Sequence search supports biotechnology patents.

item.title: Lensa AI
item.description:
Lensa is a mobile photo editor best known for a single viral feature. Magic Avatars let users upload a set of selfies and receive a collection of stylized portraits in the style of fantasy art, anime, or illustration. The effect spread quickly on social media, driving downloads and making many people aware of AI image generation. The avatars are created with a model fine-tuned on each user’s photos.

The core of the app is a selfie and portrait editor. It offers retouching for skin and eyes, background replacement, blur and sharpening, and a range of filters and effects. Subscribers get access to the full tool set, and Magic Avatars can be purchased as packs. Prisma Labs, the developer, also makes other photo and AI apps.

item.title: Lex
item.description:
Lex is a document editor with AI woven in. The interface is clean and focused on writing, and the AI helps in small ways: continuing a thought when you are stuck, offering alternative phrasings, and giving feedback on drafts. Users keep control, and the tool tries not to replace their voice.

Features include a way to ask for critique, suggestions for headlines and next paragraphs, and the ability to have the AI respond to your own text in a side conversation. Writers use it for essays, newsletters, and notes where they want a thinking partner rather than automatic content.

item.title: Lexion
item.description:
Lexion helped legal teams make sense of their contracts. It read agreements, pulled out terms like parties, dates, renewal windows, and liability caps, and stored them in a searchable repository. Alerts warned teams about upcoming renewals and obligations, and workflows routed new requests.

AI answered questions across the portfolio, such as which contracts have auto-renewal or a particular clause. The company was built for fast-growing technology companies that wanted contract management without a heavy implementation.

item.title: Linear
item.description: Linear is a project management tool aimed at product and engineering teams. Its pitch is that the tool should get out of your way: pages load instantly, nearly everything can be done from the keyboard, and the data model is opinionated about how software gets built. Work is tracked as issues, grouped into cycles (time-boxed sprints), projects, and initiatives, with roadmaps on top for the longer view. Many teams switch to it from Jira because there is far less configuration to maintain.

item.title: Liner
item.description:
Liner started as a tool for highlighting text on web pages and saving it. Users mark passages in articles and PDFs, which are collected and organized, so they can find them later. A browser extension and app make highlighting part of normal browsing.

AI features add search and summaries. An AI search engine returns answers with sources and surfaces relevant parts of highlighted content, and tools summarize pages and documents. A chat assistant answers questions about what a user is reading. It is popular with students and researchers, particularly in Korea where the company began.

item.title: LinkedIn
item.description:
LinkedIn is the main place for professional identity online. Members create profiles that work as living resumes, connect with colleagues and contacts, follow companies, and share posts and articles. It is also a major channel for hiring and job hunting, with job listings, recruiter messaging, and tools that show how you compare with other applicants. Companies maintain pages and advertise to professional audiences.

AI features run through the product. Job search can be done in plain language, writing assistance helps draft posts and profile sections, and an AI hiring assistant helps recruiters find and screen candidates. Premium subscriptions add insights, more messages, and learning courses through LinkedIn Learning. Skills assessments, recommendations, and endorsements are used to signal ability. The feed is ranked by algorithms that favor engagement.

item.title: LinkedIn Sales Navigator
item.description:
Sales Navigator gives salespeople deeper access to LinkedIn’s network. It provides advanced filters for finding people and companies, such as by seniority, function, company size, industry, and recent job changes. Users save leads and accounts into lists, and the system sends alerts when something relevant happens, like a prospect changing jobs or a company hiring in a certain department, which can prompt a timely message.

Further features support outreach. InMail messages reach people outside your network, TeamLink shows how colleagues are connected to a prospect for warm introductions, and integrations sync with CRMs such as Salesforce and HubSpot to keep records current. AI tools recommend leads, summarize accounts, and suggest ways to start a conversation, using the profile and activity data on the platform.

item.title: Llamasoft
item.description:
Llamasoft helped companies answer strategic supply chain questions. Where should factories and warehouses be placed? How would costs change if a port closes or demand shifts? Its software builds a digital model of a supply network, then uses optimization and simulation to test alternatives and recommend the best configuration, balancing cost, service levels, and risk. Large manufacturers, retailers, and consumer goods companies used it for network design and planning.

Coupa acquired Llamasoft and folded it into its business spend management platform, so customers can connect supply chain decisions with procurement and spend data. The technology continues under Coupa branding, with capabilities such as network optimization, inventory and sourcing analysis, and demand sensing, supported by machine learning and a digital twin of the supply chain.

item.title: LM Studio
item.description:
LM Studio makes running models on your own computer approachable. You open the app, search a catalog of models from Hugging Face, download one that fits your hardware, and start chatting, with no command line needed. Everything runs locally, so conversations stay on your machine, you can work offline, and there are no per-token fees. It supports popular open models such as Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and gpt-oss.

For developers, LM Studio can start a local server that mimics the OpenAI API, so existing tools and scripts can point at your own model. It supports multiple model formats, including GGUF and Apple’s MLX for efficient performance on Mac, lets you tune settings such as context length and GPU offloading, and works with the Model Context Protocol to connect tools. A command-line version and SDKs support automation.

item.title: Locofy.ai
item.description:
Locofy bridges design and development. A designer prepares screens in Figma, a developer or designer tags elements as buttons, inputs, or lists, and Locofy generates component-based code with responsive layouts. The output can be previewed and exported to a project.

It supports frameworks including React, Next.js, Gatsby, Vue, and React Native, and can connect to GitHub for syncing. AI features detect components and responsive behavior automatically, and a Builder lets users edit and add logic before export.

item.title: LogoAI
item.description:
LogoAI creates logo options from a short brief. A user enters a name, picks an industry and styles they like, and the tool generates a set of designs. They can customize colors, fonts, and layouts, and download vector files and brand assets.

Small businesses and startups use it for a fast start on branding. Packages include business cards, social media graphics, and brand guidelines. The vector output can be used in print and on the web.

item.title: Lokalise AI
item.description:
Lokalise helps teams ship products in multiple languages. Developers and designers connect their code repositories and design files, and Lokalise collects the text that needs translating, lets translators and reviewers work on it in an editor with context, and sends finished translations back. Integrations with GitHub, GitLab, Figma, and content systems keep localization in step with development rather than delaying releases.

AI sits at the center of recent versions. It can translate new strings with models that take glossaries, tone, and context into account, flag likely errors, and score translation quality so humans focus on the content that needs attention. Translation memory reuses approved translations for consistency and cost savings, and workflows route content to in-house teams or translation vendors. Reporting shows progress by language.

item.title: LongShot AI
item.description:
LongShot AI is aimed at publishers and marketers who want blog posts with fewer unsupported claims. You provide a topic or keyword, and the tool researches the web and writes a structured article, with options to cite sources and run fact checks against search results. It can generate outlines, intros, and full drafts, and has a workspace for editing.

Additional features help with the content workflow. An SEO assistant suggests keywords and optimization steps, a rewrite tool paraphrases and adjusts tone, and a calendar helps plan publishing. Teams can collaborate in the editor, and templates cover common formats such as product reviews, how-to articles, and listicles. Users range from solo bloggers to small agencies.

item.title: Looka
item.description:
Looka makes logo design approachable. You answer a few questions about your business, choose styles and colors you like, and Looka generates many logo concepts using different icons, fonts, and layouts. You can customize any option in an editor, then see how it looks on mockups such as business cards, signs, and social media profiles.

It offers two ways to pay. A one-time purchase of a logo package provides high-resolution and vector files, and a subscription Brand Kit adds a library of templates, a style guide, and tools for marketing materials, business cards, and social posts in your brand colors. It also includes a simple website builder, so a new business can establish a basic presence in one place.

item.title: Loom
item.description:
Loom replaces many meetings and long emails with a short video. You click record, show your screen while talking, and Loom uploads the video instantly and gives you a link to share. Viewers can watch at their own pace, react with emojis, comment at specific timestamps, and get an automatic transcript. It’s widely used for product walkthroughs, bug reports, onboarding, feedback, and updates to distributed teams.

AI features cut the work around videos. Loom creates titles and summaries, chapters for easy navigation, and action items, and can remove filler words and silences or turn a recording into a written document or ticket. Integrations connect with Slack, Jira, Notion, and Gmail, and since Atlassian acquired Loom, it fits more closely with tools like Jira and Confluence.

item.title: Lottie
item.description: Lottie is an animation format created at Airbnb that exports motion from After Effects as small JSON files. The files are vector-based, so they scale to any size without blur, and they are far lighter than GIFs or videos. App and web developers use them for loading spinners, onboarding screens, icons, and illustrations. A Lottie animation can be changed in code, colors can be swapped, and playback controlled, which makes it interactive.

item.title: Loudly
item.description:
Loudly offers music for people who need soundtracks without composing. Users can create tracks by choosing a genre, mood, and tempo, or by describing what they want in a prompt, and then download the result. A library of ready-made AI tracks lets you browse by genre and use case. It is intended for video creators, podcasters, streamers, game developers, and businesses that need background music.

Several features support practical use. A personalization option adjusts elements like instruments and structure, stems can be downloaded for editing, and an API allows developers to embed music generation in their own products, such as apps that need adaptive soundtracks. The company positions its music as safe for commercial use, with licenses that cover content on social platforms.

item.title: Lovo AI
item.description:
Lovo makes synthetic speech for creators and businesses. Users type or paste a script, choose a voice, and adjust tone, speed, and emphasis to generate narration. Genny, the editor, lets them place speech alongside video, images, and music in one timeline.

Voice cloning and a marketplace of voices expand the options, and the platform supports many languages. Typical uses are explainer videos, e-learning, ads, and audiobooks. An API provides access for developers.

item.title: Lucidchart AI
item.description:
Lucidchart is a mature online diagramming tool from Lucid Software. Users create flowcharts, process maps, org charts, wireframes, network diagrams, and technical drawings with a large library of shapes and templates, and collaborate in real time with comments and version history. Because it runs in the browser and integrates with the tools that teams already use, it’s popular in business and IT.

Several features go beyond drawing. Data linking can generate org charts or network diagrams from spreadsheets and cloud accounts, so diagrams stay current, and a presentation mode turns diagrams into slides. AI features generate diagrams from a text description, suggest improvements, and summarize complex drawings. Lucidchart is part of the Lucid suite, which also includes Lucidspark for whiteboarding and Lucidscale for cloud diagrams.

item.title: Ludo.ai
item.description:
Ludo.ai aims to speed up the early stages of game development. Designers can brainstorm game concepts and mechanics, get suggestions based on trends in app stores, and generate descriptions and feature lists. A market research tool analyzes top-performing games to show what genres and themes are popular, which helps indie studios and publishers decide what to build.

The platform includes asset generation. It can produce concept art and character designs, sprites and sprite sheets, short animations, UI elements, and sound effects and music from prompts, and convert images into basic 3D models in some plans. Outputs are intended for prototypes and mockups to test ideas quickly, and can be exported for use in engines like Unity.

item.title: Luma AI
item.description:
Luma began in 3D. Its first app let anyone capture an object or space with a phone camera and turn it into a photorealistic 3D scene using neural radiance fields and, later, Gaussian splatting. People used it to scan products, rooms, and sculptures, and share them in a browser or export them to 3D tools. It also released Genie, a text-to-3D model that creates 3D assets from a description.

The company has since shifted its attention to video and multimodal generation. Its Ray video models create clips from text or images, and tools for editing existing footage, keyframes, and reframing give creators control. These models are available through the Dream Machine app and an API. Luma has also introduced agents that plan and carry out creative work across text, images, video, and audio, and it works with studios on production workflows.

item.title: Luminance
item.description:
Luminance is built for lawyers who deal with large volumes of agreements. Teams upload contracts, and the platform identifies key terms, highlights unusual or risky clauses, and compares documents against company standards. Its origins lie in machine learning developed at the University of Cambridge.

Beyond review, Luminance supports negotiation and drafting. An AI assistant can propose edits in Word, summarize positions, and handle routine agreements with limited human involvement, escalating exceptions to lawyers. In due diligence, it speeds through thousands of documents to find issues across a deal’s data room.

item.title: Lunit
item.description:
Lunit applies deep learning to medical images. Insight CXR reads chest X-rays and flags abnormalities such as nodules and signs of tuberculosis, while Insight MMG reviews mammograms to help radiologists detect breast cancer. Radiologists see marked regions and probability scores to support their reading.

The company also works in oncology pathology. Its SCOPE tools analyze tissue slides to characterize the tumor environment, which helps predict how patients may respond to treatments such as immunotherapy. This feeds into drug development and personalized care.

item.title: Mage.space
item.description:
Mage.space gives people a simple front end for open-source image models. You choose from a catalog of checkpoints, write a prompt, adjust settings like style, size, and number of images, and generate. It supports image-to-image transformations, inpainting, and control features that guide composition, and results can be upscaled. Because it hosts the models, users do not need a powerful computer or a local installation.

The platform appeals to people who want flexibility in styles, from realistic photos to anime and fantasy art, and who want to experiment with community-trained models. It has a gallery of public creations, and a text-to-video tool has been added to some plans. Content rules are looser than on some mainstream services, though it still prohibits illegal material.

item.title: Magento
item.description:
Magento was created as an open-source e-commerce framework and became one of the most customizable platforms for online stores. Merchants with complex needs use it to manage large catalogs, multiple storefronts and currencies, custom pricing and checkout, and integrations with ERP and other systems. A huge ecosystem of extensions, agencies, and developers supports it.

Adobe acquired Magento and sells a commercial version, Adobe Commerce, with additional features for B2B selling, merchandising, and cloud hosting and support, plus integration with Adobe’s marketing and analytics products. Adobe Sensei AI powers features such as product recommendations and search. The free Magento Open Source edition continues for those who want to host and manage their own stores.

item.title: Make
item.description: Make, formerly called Integromat, lets you automate work between apps by drawing it. You place modules on a canvas for each app, such as Gmail, Google Sheets, Slack, or a CRM, and connect them with lines that show how data flows. You can add routers that split the flow into branches, filters that decide which items continue, iterators that handle lists, and functions that change data on the way. This visual layout makes complicated logic easier to follow than a long linear list of steps.

item.title: Manus
item.description: Manus gained attention as an agent that completes whole tasks instead of answering questions.
