You describe a goal, such as researching a market, comparing products, building a small site, or analyzing a spreadsheet, and Manus plans the work, opens a browser, writes and runs code in its own cloud environment, and produces deliverables like reports, slides, and files. You can watch what it does and step in, and it continues running in the background.

item.title: MarketMan
item.description:
MarketMan is back-of-house software for food service. Operators record what they buy and use, build recipes with ingredient costs, and see the cost of each dish. When prices change or usage varies, the system flags it, helping managers protect margins.

Ordering and invoicing are handled in one place. Staff place orders with suppliers, receive deliveries, and match invoices to what arrived, which catches errors and short shipments. Forecasting tools predict how much to order based on sales history, and integrations connect with point of sale and accounting systems.

item.title: MarketMuse
item.description:
MarketMuse approaches content from the perspective of topical authority. It scans your website and compares the topics you cover with what search engines expect from a site in your area, then shows gaps where new or improved content could help. Instead of focusing on single keywords, it helps plan clusters of related articles that together establish expertise.

Its tools turn that strategy into work. Content briefs list the subtopics, questions, and terms a piece should address, an optimization tool scores drafts against those expectations, and AI helps with drafting and updating existing pages. Metrics such as personalized difficulty estimate how hard a topic will be for your site specifically. Teams use the platform to prioritize where to invest effort.

item.title: Masterpiece Studio
item.description:
Masterpiece Studio began with virtual reality tools for sculpting, painting, and animating in 3D, making 3D creation more intuitive for artists. It later moved toward generative AI, with Masterpiece X, which generates 3D models from text or images. Users describe an object, and the system produces a mesh with textures that can be refined or used as a starting point for game assets, virtual worlds, and prototypes.

The aim is to make output useful in production. Generated models can be downloaded in common formats and used in game engines such as Unity and Unreal, or opened in Blender and other tools for editing. Additional features help with rigging and animation, so characters can be posed and moved without a complex setup. A no-code approach targets creators who do not have a modeling background, including developers and designers who need many assets.

item.title: Mathway
item.description:
Mathway helps students check and understand math. A user enters a problem or snaps a photo, and the app returns the answer and, with a subscription, the steps used to reach it. It covers algebra, trigonometry, calculus, statistics, and more.

Used well, step-by-step solutions help a student learn a method. Used carelessly, they let students copy answers without understanding, and teachers often restrict such tools. Automated solvers can also make errors, especially with word problems and unusual notation.

item.title: Maze
item.description:
Maze helps product teams learn from users. Designers import a prototype from Figma, set tasks for participants, and share a link to run a test that records clicks, paths, and success rates. Surveys, card sorts, and interview studies are supported as well, and a panel service can recruit participants.

AI speeds up analysis. It transcribes sessions, pulls out themes and quotes, and writes summaries of what the data shows, so teams spend less time sorting through recordings. Reports can be shared with stakeholders.

item.title: MeetGeek
item.description:
MeetGeek joins your calendar’s online meetings, records them, and produces a transcript and summary after each one. The summary lists decisions, action items, and key points, and highlights flag important moments. Notes are sent automatically to attendees or to tools like Slack, Notion, HubSpot, and Google Docs, which cuts down on manual write-ups.

Beyond a single meeting, it organizes knowledge across your calls. Hubs group meetings by team or topic, and you can search past conversations or ask questions about them. Meeting templates tailor summaries for sales calls, interviews, or team check-ins, and analytics show participation and talk time. Teams can get insights into patterns across customer calls.

item.title: Mematic
item.description:
Mematic makes meme creation quick on a phone. Users pick a template from a large library or upload their own image, add captions in the classic style, and share to social networks and messaging apps. The interface is built for thumb use, so formatting text is fast.

The app offers sticker and filter options, categories of trending templates, and tools for adding emoji and shapes. A premium subscription removes ads and watermarks and adds more templates and features.

item.title: Meme Generator
item.description:
Meme Generator, at memegenerator.net, lets users pick a template, add top and bottom text, and share the result. Its library includes classic image macros and newer formats, and users can upload their own images. A gallery shows popular memes made with the tool.

The AI features help with captions: a user chooses a template and the tool proposes text, which is useful for getting past the blank caption box. Sharing links and downloads are straightforward.

item.title: Meshcapade
item.description:
Meshcapade grew out of research at the Max Planck Institute on how to represent human bodies in 3D. Its core is SMPL, a parametric model that describes body shape and pose with a small set of numbers, which makes it efficient to generate and animate realistic humans. SMPL has become widely used in computer vision and graphics research, and Meshcapade commercializes the technology.

Its products turn images and video into 3D human data. Motion capture from ordinary video can extract body movement without suits or special cameras, and the output can be used in animation, games, virtual production, and sports analysis. Tools generate avatars with accurate body shapes for virtual try-on in fashion, health and fitness applications, and digital humans. An API lets developers integrate these capabilities, and plugins connect with popular 3D software.

item.title: Meta AI
item.description: Meta AI is the assistant that Meta put where its users already are. In WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, and Facebook, you can mention it in a chat or open it from the search bar to ask a question, get recommendations, or generate an image. There is also a standalone app and website with fuller features, including natural voice conversations, image creation and editing, and a feed where people share what they have made.

item.title: Metabase
item.description:
Metabase makes data approachable. Connected to a database or warehouse, it lets non-technical users build questions by clicking through filters and summaries, view results as charts, and assemble dashboards. Analysts can write SQL when they need it, and everything is shareable.

The AI assistant lets users describe what they want, and generates the query or chart, which helps people who do not know the data model. Embedded analytics lets companies place dashboards in their own products. Permissions and models keep data governed.

item.title: Metricool
item.description:
Metricool brings several marketing tasks into one dashboard. Users can plan and schedule posts across networks on a calendar, see analytics on posts, followers, and competitors, and manage Facebook, Instagram, Google, and TikTok ads reports. A link-in-bio tool, inbox for comments and messages, and web analytics help connect social activity to site traffic.

Reporting is a strong point. Customizable reports can be exported or scheduled for clients, and integrations connect with Looker Studio and other business intelligence tools, which suits agencies. AI features help write captions, suggest posting times, and generate content ideas, and a feature can plan a calendar from a brief. Plans cover multiple brands, so one account can manage several clients.

item.title: Microsoft Designer
item.description:
Microsoft Designer helps people make graphics quickly. You describe what you want, such as an invitation for a birthday party or a banner for a sale, and Designer produces several layout options with text, images, and styling, which you can edit. It offers templates for common formats, background removal, and tools for resizing a design for different platforms.

AI image generation is built in, powered by Microsoft’s and OpenAI’s image models, so you can create custom illustrations or photos to include in a design. It integrates with Microsoft 365 apps and Copilot, and is available on the web, as a mobile app, and inside tools such as Edge. Brand kits and shared templates are available on paid Microsoft 365 plans.

item.title: Microsoft Government Cloud
item.description:
Azure Government is a separate cloud region set up for US federal, state, and local agencies and their partners. It runs in data centers staffed by screened US personnel and is isolated from commercial Azure, which allows it to meet compliance regimes for sensitive government data.

Agencies use it for the usual range of cloud work, including hosting applications, analytics, and AI. Services such as Azure OpenAI and Copilot have been made available in versions that meet government requirements, which lets agencies use generative AI with data protections.

item.title: Microsoft Power Automate
item.description:
Power Automate connects apps and automates repetitive work. Users build flows that trigger on events, such as an email arriving or a form submission, and perform actions in hundreds of services. It works smoothly with Teams, SharePoint, Outlook, and Dynamics.

AI features extend it. Copilot lets people describe a flow in plain language, AI Builder processes documents and forms, and agent capabilities handle more open-ended tasks. Desktop flows use robotic process automation to control applications that have no API.

item.title: Microsoft Power Automate
item.description:
Power Automate helps people automate repetitive work without code. In a visual designer, users create flows that start from a trigger, such as an email arriving or a form being submitted, and then run actions like saving attachments, updating a spreadsheet, sending approvals, or posting to Teams. It connects to hundreds of services, with deep integration with SharePoint, Outlook, Excel, and Dynamics 365, and handles scheduled and event-driven tasks.

It also covers robotic process automation. Desktop flows record and replay actions on a computer, allowing automation of legacy applications that lack APIs. AI Builder adds capabilities such as reading text from documents, classifying content, and making predictions, and Copilot can build a flow from a plain-language description. Newer features support AI agents that use flows as tools.

item.title: Microsoft Translator
item.description:
Microsoft Translator covers the common translation needs. You can type or paste text, speak into a phone for conversation translation, translate images and documents, and use offline language packs when traveling. Multi-device conversation mode lets several people speak in different languages and see translations on their own screens, which suits meetings and travel.

It’s integrated throughout Microsoft products. Teams offers live captions and translated meetings, Office apps can translate documents and text, and Edge translates web pages. For developers and businesses, Azure AI Translator provides APIs for text, document, and speech translation, with custom models and glossaries, and options to run in containers.

item.title: Midjourney
item.description: Midjourney is one of the most popular image generators, valued for its distinctive aesthetic. You describe an image, and it returns variations that tend to look polished and painterly, with strong composition and lighting. It began on Discord, where users type commands in a shared channel, and now offers a web interface with an image editor, personal galleries, and organization tools. It’s widely used by illustrators, designers, concept artists, and marketers.

item.title: Mintlify
item.description:
Mintlify helps developer companies publish documentation that looks and works well. Teams write pages in MDX or Markdown, keep them in a Git repository, and Mintlify builds a fast, branded site with navigation, search, code samples, and API playgrounds generated from OpenAPI specs. Many well-known developer tools use it.

AI is part of both the reader and writer experience. An assistant on the docs site answers questions from the documentation, helping users find what they need, and docs are published in forms that AI coding tools can read, such as llms.txt and MCP servers. For writers, AI agents can draft pages, update docs when code changes, and flag outdated content. Analytics show what readers search for and where they get stuck.

item.title: Miro AI
item.description:
Miro provides an infinite shared canvas where teams place sticky notes, diagrams, documents, and images, and work together live or asynchronously. It’s used for brainstorming, retrospectives, user journey maps, roadmaps, and workshops, particularly for distributed teams. A large library of templates, integrations with tools such as Jira, Slack, and Google Drive, and facilitation features like timers and voting make it versatile.

AI features speed up creation and synthesis. Users can generate diagrams, flowcharts, and mind maps from a prompt, summarize and cluster hundreds of sticky notes into themes, and turn a board into a document or a prototype. Sidekicks are AI helpers with specific roles, such as a product manager or a retrospective facilitator, that give feedback and suggestions on the board. Flows connect several AI steps for repeatable processes.

item.title: Missinglettr
item.description:
Missinglettr automates a task many content creators neglect: promoting their articles over time. You connect your blog or paste a link, and the tool analyzes the post to pull out quotes, statistics, and highlights. It then generates a series of social posts, with images, scheduled across weeks and months, so a single article continues to attract visitors long after it’s published.

Other features round out the platform. A curation tool suggests relevant content from other sources to share, a social media scheduler handles regular posting, and analytics show engagement. Collaboration features allow agencies and teams to manage several brands. AI helps with writing captions and variations, and automated hashtag suggestions save time.

item.title: Mixmax
item.description:
Mixmax turns Gmail into a sales workspace. It tracks opens, clicks, and replies, lets you schedule messages, and adds a calendar tool so recipients can book meetings from your email. Templates and snippets speed up repetitive writing, and polls, surveys, and documents can be embedded. It is used by sales, recruiting, and customer success teams that live in their inbox.

Sequences are a main feature: automated multi-step email campaigns that send follow-ups until someone replies, with rules for pausing and routing. Integrations connect with Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach alternatives, Slack, and Zapier, so activity is logged in the CRM. AI helps draft emails, personalize at scale, and suggest next steps, and call recording and meeting notes have been added in some plans.

item.title: Modal
item.description:
Modal removes much of the setup around running compute. A developer writes Python, adds decorators that say what hardware and packages are needed, and Modal builds the container, starts it on demand, scales to many machines, and shuts it down when finished. Startup is fast, which makes it practical for bursty workloads.

Typical uses include model inference, fine-tuning, batch jobs, data processing, and running sandboxes for agents. Features such as web endpoints, scheduled jobs, volumes for storage, and notebooks cover a range of needs. Pricing is based on seconds of compute.

item.title: Monday.com
item.description:
Monday.com organizes work in colorful boards that resemble spreadsheets. Teams track projects, sales pipelines, marketing campaigns, and operations with columns for status, owners, dates, and more, and view the same data as a timeline, calendar, or chart. No-code automations handle routine updates and notifications.

The platform has expanded into products for sales CRM, service desks, and software development, built on the same foundation. AI assistants create boards from a description, summarize items and updates, write content, and extract information, and agents can take on tasks within workflows.

item.title: Moovly
item.description:
Moovly serves companies that need many versions of the same video. Using a template, teams can generate hundreds or thousands of variations that change names, products, languages, or data, such as personalized sales videos or product videos for each item in a catalog. A browser editor handles design, and an API automates production from spreadsheets or other systems.

Localization is a major theme. Moovly can add subtitles, translate scripts, and generate voiceovers in multiple languages using AI voices, helping companies serve international audiences, and AI tools assist with text-to-video and editing. It’s used in marketing, e-commerce, training, and communications, and offers brand controls and collaboration for large teams.

item.title: Morningstar AI
item.description:
Morningstar is known for independent research on funds, stocks, and markets. Its star ratings for mutual funds and ETFs became a standard reference, and analysts publish research and fair value estimates on companies. Individual investors use its website and premium subscriptions to screen investments and build portfolios, while advisors and institutions use products like Morningstar Direct for deeper analysis, portfolio construction, and reporting.

AI has been added to make research easier to navigate. Mo is a conversational assistant that answers investing questions using Morningstar’s research and data, summarizes reports, and explains concepts, with an emphasis on drawing from the company’s own vetted content to limit errors. Other uses include automated summaries of earnings calls and analyst notes, and data tools that help build screens and analyze holdings.

item.title: Mosaic
item.description:
Mosaic is aimed at finance teams that want a modern view of the business. It pulls data from accounting systems, sales tools, and HR platforms into a single model, so metrics like revenue, headcount, and cash are current and consistent. Teams build reports and board decks from live data.

Forecasting and scenario tools let teams test assumptions, such as hiring plans or pricing changes, and see the impact. AI allows users to ask questions in plain language and get analysis, and automates routine commentary and variance explanations.

item.title: Motion
item.description: Motion tries to take planning off your hands. You add tasks with deadlines, durations, and priorities, connect your calendar, and Motion places each task into open time on your calendar. If a meeting gets added or a task runs long, it rebuilds the schedule automatically so you always see a realistic plan for the day. The goal is to protect focus time and make sure deadlines are met without constant manual rearranging.

item.title: Moz Pro
item.description:
Moz was one of the earliest SEO software companies, and Moz Pro remains a staple for agencies and in-house marketers. Users research keywords, audit sites for technical problems, track rankings over time, and analyze links, with Domain Authority, Moz’s well-known score, used as a quick measure of a site’s strength.

The MozBar browser extension overlays metrics on search results and web pages, making competitor checks quick. Reporting tools produce client-ready summaries, and newer AI features suggest priorities and help with content. A separate local product manages business listings.

item.title: Munch
item.description:
Munch focuses on video repurposing. You upload a webinar, podcast, interview, or live stream, or connect a link, and it identifies segments likely to perform well as short clips. Rather than simply cutting at fixed intervals, it analyzes the transcript and content and compares it with trending topics and keywords, then proposes clips with captions, titles, and formatting for TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and LinkedIn.

Features that support the workflow include automatic captions, reframing to vertical or square, branded templates, and the ability to edit clips before exporting. Social copy and hashtags can be suggested, and a scheduler publishes clips to connected accounts. Marketing teams, agencies, podcasters, and course creators use it to get more from long content without manual editing.

item.title: Murf
item.description: Murf is known for its studio, but its voice features are a separate reason people use it. The voice changer converts a recording of your own speech into a different voice from the library, keeping your timing and emotion, which suits people who want a polished sound without hiring talent. Voice cloning can create a custom voice for a brand or presenter, typically with consent and verification, and is offered mainly for business customers.

item.title: Murf
item.description:
Murf is aimed at people who need a professional voiceover without hiring a voice actor or booking a studio. In its browser-based studio, you paste a script, choose a voice, and adjust pitch, speed, and emphasis. Voices come in many accents and languages and suit narration, e-learning, product videos, ads, and presentations. You can add background music, line the audio up with video or slides, and export the result.

The platform has expanded to related audio jobs. Dubbing translates a video or audio file into other languages and keeps it timed to the original. An API gives developers text-to-speech for their own apps, including fast, streaming voices for conversational use. Murf Agents power voice calls and chat for customer service and similar needs, and a voice changer converts one voice into another. Team workspaces help companies share projects and keep audio consistent.

item.title: Mutable AI
item.description:
Mutable AI was a startup building AI tools for programmers. Its VS Code extension offered code completion, refactoring, and chat that could answer questions about a project, and its AutoPilot feature aimed to carry out a described feature across a codebase. The team later became known for turning repositories into readable, wiki-style documentation, which helps developers understand unfamiliar code.

Google acquired the company, and the original Mutable AI site no longer works. The idea of generating a living wiki for a codebase continues in Google’s own products, where documentation tools built on that concept have appeared. Users of the earlier extension needed to move to other assistants, as the standalone service is gone.

item.title: n8n
item.description: n8n lets you build automations by connecting nodes on a canvas, similar to Zapier or Make, but with more room for code. Each node is a step: a trigger like a webhook or schedule, an action in an app, or a block that transforms data with JavaScript or Python. Hundreds of integrations are included, and a generic HTTP node covers the rest. Workflows can branch, loop, and call other workflows, so it handles anything from simple notifications to elaborate data pipelines.

item.title: Narrato
item.description:
Narrato helps teams manage the whole content process. A content calendar plans what to publish, assignments route work to writers and editors, and approval workflows track progress. The AI writer generates drafts, outlines, social posts, and ad copy in a team’s style, and SEO tools provide keyword suggestions and optimization scores.

Additional tools address agencies and publishers. Brief generation creates instructions for writers, a plagiarism checker and AI content detector help check originality, and a marketplace lets teams hire freelance writers for content that needs a human touch. Integrations publish directly to WordPress and other platforms, and an AI assistant helps with ideas and repurposing.

item.title: Navina
item.description:
Navina addresses chart review. Before a patient visit, a clinician or care team would normally dig through records from different sources. Navina collects data from the electronic health record, outside providers, and claims, summarizes it, and highlights what matters, such as conditions that may be undocumented or screenings that are overdue.

That helps with both quality of care and risk adjustment, which affects payment under value-based contracts. Insights appear in the clinician’s workflow so they can act during the visit. Health systems and value-based care groups are the main customers.

item.title: Netlify
item.description:
Netlify popularized the idea of pushing code to Git and having a site build and deploy automatically. Developers connect a repository, and Netlify builds on each change, gives every pull request a preview URL, and serves the site from a global network. Serverless functions and edge functions add dynamic behavior without servers.

The platform has added AI features. Agent Runners let AI agents such as Claude and Codex make changes to a site and open pull requests, and an AI-oriented gateway and tooling help developers use models inside their projects. Forms, identity, and storage services handle common needs.

item.title: Netomi
item.description:
Netomi builds AI agents for customer support. Large brands connect it to their help desks and back-end systems, and the agents answer questions, track orders, process returns, and handle other requests across channels. Where an agent cannot resolve something, it hands off to a person with context.

The platform learns from past tickets and company content, and is built with controls such as guardrails and testing for regulated and high-volume environments. Customers include airlines, retailers, and travel companies that field heavy, repetitive inquiries.

item.title: Neural.love
item.description:
Neural.love combines creation and repair tools in one web app. The generator creates images from text prompts with a choice of models and styles, while the enhancement tools improve existing pictures. Upscaling increases resolution, denoising cleans grainy photos, and restoration repairs scratches and faded color on old family pictures. Face enhancement can sharpen portraits, and colorization adds color to black-and-white images.

The platform is practical for photographers, genealogists, designers, and anyone with old or low-quality images. Users upload a file, choose the effect, and download the result, with credits consumed by each operation. An API lets developers add enhancement features to their own apps, and batch options handle many images. Generated images can be used in marketing and design, subject to the terms for each plan.

item.title: NeuralText
item.description:
NeuralText is an SEO content suite. Users find keywords, group them into clusters by intent, study what ranks for a term, and create content briefs that list topics and questions to cover. The AI writer then drafts articles or sections using those guidelines.

The tool aims to let one person handle research, planning, and drafting. A content editor scores text against the brief, and additional templates cover ads, product descriptions, and social posts.

item.title: Nintex
item.description:
Nintex helps organizations digitize their processes. Using a visual designer, business analysts build workflows that route requests, collect approvals, update systems, and send notifications, and they create forms to start those workflows. It integrates with Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Salesforce, and many other systems, which is where its roots lie, with many customers automating processes on SharePoint.

The platform has several parts. Process mapping tools document how work actually happens, automation tools execute workflows and robotic process automation, and document generation tools produce contracts and reports from data. AI features assist with building workflows from descriptions and extracting data from documents, and analytics show where processes slow down.

item.title: Nosto
item.description:
Nosto helps online stores treat every visitor differently. It tracks browsing and purchase behavior and uses it to recommend products, order category pages, personalize search, and show targeted messages. Merchants configure these experiences with a visual tool and rules, and the system learns what works.

Features include product recommendations across the site and in emails, a search engine that understands intent, and tools to personalize content by audience. Shopify, Magento, and other platforms are supported. Generative AI helps write product copy and campaign content.

item.title: NotebookLM Plus
item.description: NotebookLM Plus gives heavier users more room in NotebookLM, Google’s tool for working with your own documents. The free version lets you add sources, ask questions with citations, and generate study aids, but it limits the number of notebooks, sources, and daily queries. The Plus tier lifts those limits, so people with large projects, such as researchers, students writing theses, or analysts working across many documents, can keep more material in one place.

item.title: Notion
item.description:
Notion lets people build their own workspace from simple pieces. A page can hold text, headings, checklists, images, embedded files, and databases, and databases can be shown as tables, boards, calendars, or galleries. Teams use it for wikis, meeting notes, project tracking, product roadmaps, and personal organization, and templates help people get started. Real-time collaboration, comments, and permissions make it work for teams as well as individuals.

The product has grown beyond notes. Notion Calendar and Notion Mail connect scheduling and email to the workspace, and Sites turns pages into public web pages. Notion AI adds writing help, summaries, translation, and question answering across your workspace and connected tools like Slack and Google Drive, plus agents that perform tasks. AI meeting notes capture and summarize calls. See the Notion AI entry for details on those features.

item.title: Notta
item.description: Notta turns speech into text for people who sit through many conversations. You can record in the mobile or web app, upload audio and video files, or let its assistant join Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams calls. The transcript appears in the app with speaker labels and timestamps, and you can search it, edit it, and share it. It supports a large number of languages, which suits international teams, journalists, and researchers.

item.title: Noty.ai
item.description:
Noty.ai is a lightweight tool for people who want meeting notes without much setup. It records and transcribes online meetings, then creates a summary that highlights the main discussion points, decisions, and tasks. The goal is to let participants focus on the conversation instead of typing, and to give everyone a shared record afterward.

Its integrations make the notes easy to reuse. Summaries can be pushed to Notion and other workspace tools, and the transcript is searchable, so you can find what was said about a topic in a past meeting. A browser extension handles recording in Google Meet and Zoom, and a free plan lets individuals try the product.

item.title: Nuance DAX
item.description: DAX, short for Dragon Ambient eXperience, was developed by Nuance and later acquired by Microsoft. With patient consent, the system captures the conversation between clinician and patient, uses speech recognition and AI to turn it into a structured medical note in the format the clinician needs, and sends it to the electronic health record for review and signature. The goal is to cut the hours doctors spend on documentation and let them focus on patients.

item.title: Numerous
item.description:
Numerous brings language models into the spreadsheet. After installing the add-in, you use a formula such as =AI(“prompt”, cell) in a cell to ask the model to do something with the data: categorize customer feedback, write product descriptions, extract names from messy text, translate, or summarize. Filling the formula down a column performs the task on hundreds or thousands of rows, which would take hours by hand.

It aims to be approachable for people who know spreadsheets but not code. Prompts are written in plain language, results appear in cells where you can filter and calculate with them, and features help with common tasks like cleaning, tagging, and brainstorming. Marketers, e-commerce teams, researchers, and operations staff use it to process lists of items quickly.

item.title: Observe.AI
item.description:
Observe.AI is built for contact centers that handle huge numbers of customer interactions. Quality teams traditionally review a small sample of calls by hand. Observe.AI transcribes and scores all interactions automatically against a company’s quality and compliance criteria, flags issues such as missed disclosures or poor handling of angry customers, and surfaces trends across thousands of conversations.

It also supports agents during and after the call. Real-time guidance suggests what to say or reminds an agent of a required step, and post-call summaries cut the time spent on notes. Coaching tools turn scores into specific feedback for each agent, and dashboards help supervisors see which skills to work on. The platform has added AI agents that speak with customers directly for routine requests, handing off to humans when needed.

item.title: Obsidian
item.description: Obsidian treats notes as local files. Everything you write is a Markdown document in a folder on your computer, so you own the data and can open it with any other editor. You connect notes with links, and the app shows backlinks and a graph view of how ideas relate. People use it for personal knowledge management, research, writing, journaling, and project notes, and many build large networks of thousands of linked notes over years.

item.title: Okendo
item.description:
Okendo helps online stores build trust with reviews. After a purchase, it asks customers for reviews with photos and video, displays them on product pages, and syndicates them to Google. Surveys and attributes gather more detail about the customer and product fit.

Additional tools include a loyalty and referral program and a customer data layer. AI summarizes reviews into themes, analyzes sentiment, and suggests replies, helping merchants learn what customers like and dislike. Integrations connect with email, helpdesk, and ads tools.

item.title: Ollama
item.description:
Ollama made local AI simple. You install it, run a command such as ollama run with a model name, and it downloads the model and starts a chat in your terminal. It handles the details of quantization and GPU acceleration, so models like Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen, and many others run on ordinary laptops and desktops. Everything stays on your machine, so it’s private and works offline.

It is a building block for developers. Ollama exposes a local REST API, including an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so apps and tools can use your local models, and many projects such as Open WebUI, coding assistants, and agent frameworks integrate with it. Modelfiles let you customize system prompts and parameters, and recent versions add a desktop app, support for multimodal models, and optional cloud-hosted models for those too big to run locally.

item.title: ON1 Photo AI
item.description:
ON1 Photo AI aims to shorten the path from a raw photo to a finished image. It analyzes a picture and suggests adjustments, then applies tools such as NoNoise AI for removing grain, Sharpener AI for restoring detail, and Super Resolution for enlarging photos. Other tools handle sky replacement, background removal, portrait retouching, and object removal, and automatic masking selects subjects, skies, and other regions for local edits.

It fits into several workflows. It can open and process RAW files directly, work as a standalone app, or run as a plugin inside Lightroom, Photoshop, and other editors, which lets photographers use its AI tools without leaving their usual software. Presets provide quick looks, and batch processing handles many images at once. A separate ON1 Photo RAW product adds organizing and layer-based editing.

item.title: Open WebUI
item.description:
Open WebUI gives people a familiar chat interface for models they control. You run it on your own server or computer, connect it to local models through Ollama or to any OpenAI-compatible API, and get a polished web app with conversation history, model switching, prompt libraries, and voice input. It started as a front end for Ollama and has become a full platform.

Features target teams and power users. Retrieval-augmented generation lets users upload documents and chat with them, web search can add current information, and tools and functions extend what models can do. Administrators can manage multiple users, roles, and permissions, which suits organizations that want an internal AI assistant without sending data to a third party. It supports plugins and pipelines for custom behavior.

item.title: OpenAI Operator
item.description: Operator was OpenAI’s first widely available computer-using agent. It ran a browser in the cloud and looked at screenshots of web pages, then clicked, typed, and scrolled like a person to carry out a task such as ordering groceries, filling out a form, or booking a restaurant. You could watch it work, take control, and it paused to ask for confirmation before steps such as payments or entering sensitive details.

item.title: OpenAI Realtime API
item.description:
The Realtime API changes how voice applications are built. Older systems chained speech recognition, a language model, and speech synthesis, adding delay at each step. The Realtime API handles audio in and audio out directly in one model, so responses start sooner and can include tone, pauses, and interruptions that sound natural.

Developers connect over WebRTC or WebSockets to stream audio and receive speech, text, and tool calls. It supports function calling, so a voice agent can look up data or take actions, and it can be used for phone agents, in-app assistants, and language practice.

item.title: Opendoor
item.description:
Opendoor popularized the iBuyer model. A homeowner enters an address and details, receives an offer within days based on the company’s pricing model and an inspection, and can close on a timeline they choose. The company then repairs and resells the home. The process appeals to sellers who value speed and certainty over getting the highest price.

Technology is central to the business. Machine learning models estimate what a home is worth and how long it will take to sell, using data on the property and the local market, and these estimates determine offers and risk. Opendoor also offers listing options for sellers who prefer to sell traditionally, along with buyer services such as touring homes with self-guided access in some markets.

item.title: OpenHands
item.description:
OpenHands provides an open alternative to commercial coding agents. A user gives it a task, and the agent works in a sandbox with a terminal, an editor, and a browser, taking steps to complete the job and showing its work. It can resolve GitHub issues and open pull requests.

The project started as OpenDevin, an open-source response to the Devin demo, and grew into a community-driven platform run by All Hands AI. It supports models from many providers, has a command line tool and a web interface, and is used in research and benchmarks for coding agents.

item.title: OpenRead
item.description:
OpenRead is built for people who read a lot of research. After you import a paper, an AI assistant can answer questions about it, explain terms, summarize sections, and pull out items like methods, results, and limitations. A structured summary view lays out the main points in a consistent format, which helps when scanning many papers for a review.

The platform extends beyond a single paper. It helps search the literature, organize papers into collections, take notes alongside the text, and generate outlines or review drafts from selected sources. Support for multiple languages makes it useful for researchers who read in a second language, and translation features help with papers published in other languages.

item.title: OpenRouter
item.description:
OpenRouter solves the problem of juggling many AI provider accounts. A developer gets one API key and one endpoint, and can call any supported model by changing its name, using the same request format as OpenAI’s API. Billing is unified, with credits that work across providers, which makes it easy to try new models as soon as they appear, including open-source ones hosted by different companies.

Beyond routing, it adds useful features. Automatic fallbacks switch to another provider if one is down, routing options choose the cheapest or fastest provider for a model, and analytics show usage and cost. Public rankings show which models people use most, giving a view of real-world adoption. Users can bring their own provider keys and set data privacy preferences that control which providers may see their prompts.

item.title: Opus Clip
item.description:
Opus Clip automates a task that eats hours for podcasters, streamers, and marketers: cutting a long recording into shorts. You paste a link or upload a video, and the AI analyzes the transcript and visuals to find segments with a strong hook and a complete idea. It generates several clips, each with a title, captions, and a vertical layout that keeps the speaker in frame.

A virality score estimates how well each clip is likely to perform, based on patterns from social video, which helps you decide what to post first. You can edit the transcript, trim, change caption styles, apply brand templates, and add B-roll. Features such as ClipAnything let you search for a moment by describing it, and a scheduler publishes to connected social accounts.

item.title: Oracle SCM
item.description:
Oracle SCM Cloud brings the functions of a supply chain together in one cloud application suite. It covers planning demand and supply, buying from suppliers, managing inventory and warehouses, running manufacturing, handling orders and fulfillment, and moving goods through transportation and global trade, with product lifecycle management for design data. Because it shares data with Oracle’s finance and HR applications, companies can connect supply chain decisions to financial outcomes.

AI and analytics support the suite. Machine learning improves demand forecasts and supply plans, predictive models flag delays and quality risks, and generative AI assistants help users find information and complete tasks. Oracle has been adding AI agents that can handle routine actions across processes. The suite is delivered in the cloud and updated regularly.

item.title: Originality.ai
item.description:
Originality.ai was built for people who commission or publish written content and want to know whether it was written by AI. You paste text or scan a URL, and it returns a score estimating the likelihood the text was generated by models such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, alongside a plagiarism check against web sources. Content teams, SEO agencies, and website buyers use it to check contractors’ work.

Additional tools include a fact-checking aid, a readability analysis, and a feature that shows the writing history of a Google Doc to demonstrate how it was composed. A Chrome extension and API support integration with publishing workflows, and team accounts allow reviewing many pieces. The company publishes accuracy studies, although its results are disputed by others.

item.title: Otter.ai
item.description: Otter was one of the first widely used meeting transcription tools. You connect your calendar, and its assistant joins your Zoom, Google Meet, or Teams calls to record, transcribe, and label speakers. The transcript is available live, so participants can follow along, and afterward you get a summary, key points, and action items. Everything is searchable, so you can find what was said in a past meeting by keyword. It also works on phones for in-person conversations and lectures.

item.title: Otter.ai
item.description:
Otter.ai joins online meetings, transcribes the conversation as it happens, and produces notes people can search and share. Speakers are labeled, key points are summarized, and action items are pulled out, so attendees can focus on the discussion instead of taking notes.

Features include an assistant that can answer questions about a meeting or across past meetings, automatic sharing of notes with attendees, and integrations with calendars and collaboration tools. Mobile and web apps handle in-person conversations, lectures, and interviews.

item.title: Outreach
item.description:
Outreach is used by sales teams to run structured prospecting and follow-up at scale. Reps enroll leads in sequences that combine emails, calls, LinkedIn steps, and tasks, and the platform schedules each step, tracks replies, and logs activity to the CRM. Managers can see which messages and cadences perform best, and automated rules route leads and keep work organized.

Over time, Outreach has added revenue intelligence and AI. Conversation intelligence records and analyzes calls, deal health scoring flags risk, and forecasting tools combine activity and pipeline data to estimate outcomes. AI assistants summarize meetings, draft emails, suggest next steps, and increasingly act as agents that research accounts or manage parts of the pipeline.

item.title: Paige.AI
item.description:
Paige works on a part of medicine where AI could make a real difference: pathology, in which specialists examine tissue slides to diagnose cancer. Slides are scanned into very large digital images, and Paige’s algorithms analyze them, flagging areas that look suspicious and helping pathologists find cancer more efficiently and consistently. Its prostate cancer detection software was the first AI pathology tool to receive FDA clearance.

The company grew out of a collaboration with Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and built a large collection of digitized slides paired with clinical and molecular data. It developed foundation models trained on millions of slides to support a broad range of cancer analysis tasks, and offers a platform for laboratories to deploy AI tools alongside digital pathology systems.

item.title: Palantir Gotham
item.description:
Gotham helps organizations that work with sensitive and scattered data make decisions. It pulls information from many systems, such as databases, reports, sensor feeds, and documents, into a unified model of people, places, events, and relationships, called an ontology. Analysts can search, visualize connections, map activity, and collaborate on investigations, and operational users can plan and track missions.

The platform is used in defense, intelligence, and public safety. Capabilities include link analysis, geospatial views, timelines, and tools for managing access to classified or restricted data, and it can run in secure and air-gapped environments. Palantir’s Artificial Intelligence Platform adds large language models that work with the same data under access controls, allowing users to ask questions and automate analysis.

item.title: PandaDoc AI
item.description:
PandaDoc helps sales teams close deals faster. Users build proposals and quotes from templates in a drag-and-drop editor, add pricing tables with live calculations, embed videos and payment links, and send them to clients, who can review and sign electronically. Tracking shows when a document is opened and viewed, so reps know when to follow up.

Automation and integration make it practical for teams. It connects with CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot to populate documents with deal data and update records when documents are signed, offers approval workflows, content libraries, and a payment step. AI features help generate document content from a prompt, summarize contracts, suggest edits, and extract information, speeding up proposal creation.

item.title: Paper Digest
item.description:
Paper Digest helps researchers keep up with a flood of new papers. Instead of scanning listings of new submissions every day, a user sets up topics or keywords and gets a personalized digest with short AI-generated summaries of matching papers. This helps researchers spot relevant work quickly and decide which papers merit a full read.

The service also publishes curated summaries of papers from major conferences and journals, and offers a platform to search, summarize, and organize papers. Paper Digest builds on text summarization models to produce abstracts and key points, and it provides tools such as a reader and a way to generate a quick literature overview. Some features are open to everyone, while others sit behind a login or subscription.

item.title: Paperspace
item.description:
Paperspace rents GPU computing by the hour. Users launch virtual machines with GPUs for training models, running experiments, or heavy graphics, and connect remotely. Gradient adds managed Jupyter notebooks and workflows that make it easy to start without setting up servers.

DigitalOcean acquired Paperspace and has been integrating it with its cloud offerings, aiming to give developers and small teams access to GPUs with simple pricing. Students and independent researchers have long used it for coursework and experiments.

item.title: Pattern89
item.description:
Pattern89 set out to bring data to creative decisions. Advertisers produce many images and videos but often cannot tell which elements drive results. The platform analyzed an advertiser’s past ads and performance data, tagging the visual and text elements in each, such as colors, faces, products, and calls to action, and learned which combinations worked for a given audience and channel.

With that knowledge, it could score new creative before launch and suggest changes, and recommend which assets to prioritize. Marketers used it to reduce wasted spend on ads that were unlikely to work, and to give designers concrete guidance. Integrations with social ad platforms pulled in performance data.

item.title: Pencil
item.description:
Pencil helps marketing teams produce a steady stream of ads. You connect your brand assets and product information, and Pencil generates video and image ads with copy and voiceovers in different formats for platforms like Meta, TikTok, and YouTube. Teams can create many variations, which makes testing easier than designing each ad by hand.

The prediction layer is the distinctive part. Pencil scores creative on how likely it is to perform, using models trained on a large amount of ad performance data and refined with the account’s own results. It also helps track which messages and visuals win and feeds that back into the next round of creative. Integrations with ad platforms and Shopify bring in performance data and product catalogs.

item.title: Penpot
item.description:
Penpot is built for collaboration between designers and developers. It uses open web standards, so designs map to real code, and supports flexible layouts based on CSS grid and flex. Teams create prototypes, design systems, and shared components in a browser.

Being open source matters to some teams. They can host Penpot themselves, keep control of their data, and avoid vendor lock-in, and developers can inspect designs and get code in a familiar form. AI features and plugins extend the tool.

item.title: People.ai
item.description:
People.ai solves the data entry problem in sales. Instead of relying on reps to log everything, it connects to email, calendars, and phone systems and records contacts, meetings, and conversations, then matches them to the right accounts and opportunities in the CRM. That keeps records current and gives managers a more complete picture of how engaged each deal is.

On top of the data, it provides analytics and AI. Dashboards show activity, engagement with key contacts, and whether deals are at risk, and forecasting tools estimate which will close. AI agents can summarize accounts, answer questions about the pipeline in natural language, and prepare reps for meetings. The aim is to give sales leaders a reliable view without chasing updates.

item.title: Peppertype.ai
item.description:
Peppertype.ai started as a copywriting assistant and has grown into a broader content tool for marketers. Users pick a type of content, such as an ad, a product description, a blog outline, or a LinkedIn post, supply the topic and tone, and receive several drafts. Brand voice and knowledge settings help it reflect a company’s style, and templates cover many common marketing formats.

It is part of Pepper Content, a company that also runs a marketplace of freelance writers and managed content services, which is the source of the Peppertype name. That connection lets teams combine AI drafting with human writers and editors for higher-stakes content. Workflow tools support collaboration, review, and publishing, and the platform has added AI agents for tasks like research and repurposing content.

item.title: Perplexity
item.description: For research, Perplexity is useful because it shows its sources. Each answer comes with numbered citations to the pages it used, so you can open the link and check a claim before relying on it. You can narrow searches to particular kinds of sources, such as academic papers, and keep asking follow-up questions that build on the earlier ones. This makes it a quicker starting point than a list of search results for questions that need several sources.

item.title: Perplexity
item.description: Perplexity works more like a search engine than a chatbot. You ask a question, it searches the web in real time, and it writes a short answer with numbered citations you can click to check. That makes it good for current events, product comparisons, and fact-finding where you need to see where the information came from. Follow-up questions keep the context, and you can narrow searches to sources like academic papers or forums.

item.title: Perplexity AI
item.description:
Perplexity positions itself as an alternative to the list of links. You ask a question in natural language, it searches the web in real time, reads the pages, and writes a concise answer with citations to each source. That format is helpful for questions where you want a quick overview with a way to check the evidence, such as product comparisons, news, how-to questions, and research basics.

The experience supports continued exploration. Follow-up questions build on earlier context, and focus options narrow the search to categories such as academic sources or discussion forums. Pro Search runs more steps for complex questions, and Deep Research generates longer reports. The Comet browser brings the assistant into everyday browsing, and Spaces organize related research. Users can choose among several models in paid plans.

item.title: Perplexity Labs
item.description: Labs goes beyond answering a question. You describe a project, such as a market analysis, a financial model, or a small dashboard, and Labs works for several minutes, combining web research, code execution, and chart creation. It then returns finished assets: a written report, a spreadsheet, charts, or a simple web app that you can download or share. The tool uses a team of specialized steps behind the scenes, so the output is more like a deliverable than a chat reply.

item.title: Perplexity Pages
item.description:
Pages is a publishing layer on top of Perplexity’s research. After you explore a topic with the assistant, you can convert the thread into a structured page with headings, summaries, and citations to the sources it used. It organizes the material in the way a short article or study guide would be written, instead of leaving you with a conversation log.

You control the result. Sections can be rewritten, reordered, or removed, images can be added, and the page can be published with a shareable link or kept private. Educators use Pages to create study guides, students for report drafts, and professionals for quick explainers on topics they research often. Because the citations travel with the content, readers can check where claims came from.

item.title: Perplexity Sonar
item.description:
Sonar lets developers build apps that answer questions using current web information. Instead of relying only on a model’s training data, a request to Sonar searches the web, reads relevant pages, and returns a response with citations. That grounding is useful for assistants, research tools, news summaries, and any product where freshness and sources matter.

There are several variants. The standard Sonar models are fast and low-cost, Sonar Pro handles more complex queries with more sources, Sonar Reasoning adds step-by-step analysis, and Sonar Deep Research runs multi-step research jobs and writes longer reports. A Search API offers ranked web results for developers who want to feed content to their own models. The API follows a format familiar to users of OpenAI’s, so adoption is simple, and options control which domains to search and how recent results should be.

item.title: Persado
item.description:
Persado focuses on the specific words in marketing messages. Its premise is that the choice of language, including emotions, calls to action, and phrasing, affects whether people respond, and that machine learning can learn what works. Marketers give it a campaign goal and brand guidelines, and it generates message variations and predicts which will perform best, based on its library of language and results from past campaigns.

Large brands in finance, retail, and telecommunications use Persado to optimize email subject lines, ads, and push notifications at scale. It integrates with marketing platforms, tests variants, and learns from the results to improve future messages. More recently, the company has added generative AI tools for drafting and personalizing content within brand guardrails.

item.title: Personetics
item.description:
Personetics supplies the intelligence behind money management features in banking apps. Banks connect transaction data, and the platform generates timely, personalized messages and suggestions, like warning a customer that a bill will overdraw their account or noticing a good time to save.

The aim is a more engaging and useful banking relationship. Personetics works with large banks around the world and presents itself as a way to turn data into proactive guidance. AI generates the insights and chooses when and how to show them.

item.title: Personio
item.description:
Personio centralizes HR work. Companies keep employee data, manage leave and attendance, handle recruiting from job posting to offer, prepare payroll, and run reviews, in one system designed around European employment rules. Self-service features let employees update their own data and request time off.

AI features help with common tasks. They draft job descriptions, assist with screening candidates, answer HR questions from company policy, and automate workflows. Reports show headcount, turnover, and other metrics.

item.title: Phidata
item.description:
Phidata began as a Python framework for turning language models into agents. Developers define an agent with instructions, tools, memory, and a knowledge base, and the framework handles running it, storing history, and retrieving documents. It also supports teams of agents that work together.

The project was renamed Agno, and the same team and codebase continue under the new name, so documentation and packages now refer to Agno. Newer releases focus on speed, a lightweight design, and production features such as a runtime for serving agents.

item.title: Phind
item.description: Phind was built for programmers who had questions that a standard search engine handled poorly. A developer could ask how to fix an error, compare libraries, or write a function, and Phind searched the web and documentation, then wrote an answer with code snippets and links to its sources. It used its own coding-focused models and later offered an IDE extension and a chat interface for follow-up questions, and it was popular as a free alternative to general chatbots.

item.title: Phrase
item.description:
Phrase helps companies translate software and content into many languages. Developers connect repositories and design tools, and new text is sent to translators or machine translation, then returned to the product when approved. Translation memory reuses earlier work and glossaries keep terminology consistent.

The platform brings together several products that grew from a merger: a translation management system, a string management tool for software teams, and a computer-assisted translation editor. AI translation engines and quality estimation reduce the amount of human review needed for lower-risk content.

item.title: Pi
item.description:
Pi was built to be a kind and curious conversational partner instead of a productivity tool. Its responses are short, warm, and conversational, and it often asks follow-up questions, which made it a favorite with people who wanted to talk through ideas, plans, or feelings in a low-pressure setting. It supports voice conversations with several voices, which suits casual use.

Inflection AI, founded by former DeepMind and LinkedIn leaders, launched Pi with the aim of making a personal AI. The company later saw its founders and much of its team join Microsoft, and it pivoted to licensing its models to enterprises. Pi remains online as a free consumer product at pi.ai and in apps, but active development has slowed, and the messaging integrations it once had are gone.

item.title: Picsart AI
item.description:
Picsart began as a mobile photo editor and grew into a broad creative suite. Users edit photos with filters, collages, stickers, and text, make videos, and design social posts from templates. A community lets people share and remix content, which helped it spread among younger creators and small businesses.

AI is now central. Tools generate images from prompts, remove backgrounds and objects, expand pictures, replace elements, enhance and upscale photos, and create stylized avatars. Text-to-video and animation tools turn ideas into clips, and an AI writer helps with captions. Picsart also provides APIs and plugins so other platforms can use its image tools, and teams can use brand kits and shared workspaces.

item.title: Pictory
item.description:
Pictory is aimed at marketers and content creators who want video without editing skills. You paste a script or a blog URL, and the AI splits the text into scenes, picks stock clips and images for each, adds captions and music, and generates a voiceover. You can then edit scenes, swap visuals, and adjust the text with a simple storyboard-style editor.

Other features extend the same idea. Pictory can summarize a long video, such as a webinar or Zoom recording, into a short highlight reel, create captions, and generate text-to-video clips. A brand kit keeps colors and logos consistent, and integrations let teams pull content from articles. Typical uses are social media videos, explainers, and repurposing blog posts for video platforms.

item.title: Pieces for Developers
item.description: Pieces helps developers avoid losing things they have already found. It runs a local service that captures and organizes code snippets, links, screenshots, and notes, enriches them with context such as where they came from, and makes them searchable. Plugins for VS Code, JetBrains, browsers, and other tools save snippets in a click and bring them back when you need them, so you don’t need to search again for how you solved something last month.

item.title: Pika Labs
item.description: Pika grew popular by making AI video fun and easy for people with no editing experience. You type a prompt or upload an image, and it generates a short clip in a few moments. Its signature features are effects that change objects in playful ways, such as melting, squishing, inflating, or turning something into cake, which spread quickly across social media. The interface is simple and mobile-friendly, which suited creators who make clips for TikTok and Instagram.

item.title: Pika Labs
item.description:
Pika makes short video easy. A user types a prompt, uploads an image, or provides a clip, and Pika generates or modifies footage. It is known for playful effects, like making objects melt or inflate, as well as realistic motion and camera control.

Creators use it for social posts, ads, and concept work. Features include editing parts of a video, extending clips, adding sound, and lip sync. The platform has expanded to support multiple underlying models and mobile apps.

item.title: Piktochart
item.description: Piktochart is aimed at people who need to present information visually but are not designers. You choose a template for an infographic, report, presentation, or poster, edit the text and images, and add charts and maps that you can link to data. Visual blocks, icons, illustrations, and a library of graphics make it quick to produce clean results, and the tool exports to image and PDF formats or shares online.

item.title: Pilot
item.description:
Pilot offers accounting as a service. A company connects its bank accounts and tools, and Pilot’s team and software keep the books, close each month, prepare financial statements, and handle tax filings. Clients get a dedicated bookkeeper and a dashboard.

Automation takes on the repetitive work, such as categorizing transactions, while humans check results and answer questions. Add-on services include CFO advice, R&D tax credits, and sales tax support.

Pilot is priced by monthly fee based on complexity, and aimed at startups and small to mid-sized businesses. It is a service, not self-serve software. Alternatives include Bench (which shut down and was acquired by Employer.com), Puzzle, Digits, Xero with an accountant, and QuickBooks Live. Pilot suits startups that want outsourced accounting.

item.title: Pinecone
item.description:
Pinecone provides the storage and search layer for applications that work with embeddings, which are numerical representations of text, images, or other data. A developer converts documents into vectors, stores them in Pinecone, and later retrieves the ones closest in meaning to a query. That pattern powers retrieval-augmented generation, where a language model answers using relevant stored passages, as well as semantic search and recommendation systems.

The service is fully managed and serverless, so developers don’t provision servers or manage indexes by hand, and it scales with usage. It supports metadata filtering, hybrid search that combines keyword and semantic methods, namespaces to separate data, and tools for generating embeddings and reranking results. Pinecone also offers an assistant product that handles document chat with minimal setup, and integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and the major model providers.

item.title: Pipedrive
item.description: Pipedrive is designed by and for salespeople, with the pipeline at the center. Deals appear as cards that move across stages, from first contact to closed, so reps can see at a glance what needs attention. Each deal has activities, emails, notes, and files attached, and the system reminds you of follow-ups so nothing slips. Compared with big CRM suites, the interface is clean and quick to learn, which suits small and growing sales teams.

item.title: Pitch
item.description:
Pitch aims to make presentations that look good without wrestling with layouts. It provides modern templates, smart slide types, and a brand-aware design system that keeps a team’s decks consistent. Collaboration works like a shared document: several people edit at once, leave comments, and track versions, which suits startups, agencies, and sales teams that produce decks together.

Distinctive features include presentation analytics and sharing. You can send a deck as a link and see who viewed it and for how long, which is helpful for investor and sales decks, and recordings let you narrate a deck for asynchronous sharing. AI tools generate slide drafts from a prompt, rewrite text, and create visuals, and the platform integrates with tools like Slack, HubSpot, and Google Drive.

item.title: PitchBook
item.description:
PitchBook tracks private markets. Its database covers companies, funding rounds, investors, funds, acquisitions, and valuations, and analysts use it to find targets, benchmark deals, and research sectors. Reports and data feeds support investment decisions and strategy work.

AI tools help users query the database in natural language, summarize companies and markets, and speed up research tasks. Integrations with Excel and CRM systems bring data into daily workflows. The company also publishes market research.

item.title: Pixelcut
item.description:
Pixelcut focuses on product images. A seller photographs an item, removes the background in one tap, and places the product on a clean or styled backdrop. AI can generate scenes that suit a product, add shadows, and upscale low-resolution pictures.

Batch tools process many images, and templates help create ads, social posts, and listing graphics. The mobile app is popular with small sellers who shoot products with a phone.

Pixelcut has a free tier and paid plans. AI-generated scenes should still show the product accurately to avoid returns. Alternatives include Photoroom, Canva, Pebblely, Remove.bg, and Adobe Express. Pixelcut suits small online sellers.

item.title: Plaid
item.description: Plaid connects apps to bank accounts. When you link an account in a budgeting app, investment platform, or payments service, Plaid’s interface asks you to sign in to your bank, and the app then receives only the data you permit. Developers use Plaid’s APIs to verify account ownership, check balances, read transaction history, confirm identity, assess income and assets for lending, and initiate transfers, without building separate integrations with thousands of banks.

item.title: Planet Labs
item.description: Planet Labs built its business on frequency. Rather than a few large satellites, it operates a large number of small ones, so it can photograph almost every part of the land surface regularly. That consistency allows users to watch change over time: crops growing, forests being cleared, ice melting, construction progressing, or ships moving. The imagery has a lower resolution than the sharpest commercial satellites but far greater frequency, and some higher-resolution satellites supplement it.

item.title: Planner 5D
item.description:
Planner 5D lets anyone design interiors. A user draws walls and rooms, adds furniture from a large catalog, and views the result in 3D from any angle or as a realistic render. It is aimed at homeowners and hobbyists planning remodels, with simple controls.

AI features generate design suggestions from a room photo, restyle spaces, and build floor plans from sketches. A community gallery provides projects to copy and adapt. Mobile and web apps share projects.

item.title: PlantNet
item.description: Pl@ntNet lets anyone identify a plant by taking a photo. You photograph a leaf, flower, fruit, or bark, and the app compares it with a large reference collection and returns a list of likely species with confidence scores and similar images. It covers wild plants and many cultivated ones, with regional floras for different parts of the world, and works best when you provide several views of the same plant.

item.title: Plasmic
item.description:
Plasmic connects visual design with real code. Developers register their React components in Plasmic, and designers and marketers can then drag those components onto a canvas, adjust styling and content, and publish pages without waiting for a code release. Alternatively, Plasmic can build entire pages and sites itself, and its output integrates with frameworks like Next.js, Gatsby, and plain React.

Features help teams collaborate. A CMS stores content, responsive design controls handle layouts across devices, and the editor includes interactions, animations, and data bindings. Teams can use it to build landing pages, marketing sites, and web apps, while developers stay in control of the underlying components. Code can be exported or used with a runtime, which reduces lock-in.

item.title: Playground AI
item.description:
Playground started as a place to experiment with image models in a friendly interface. You enter a prompt, choose a model and style, and generate images, then refine them in a canvas that lets you edit parts of a picture, combine elements, and iterate. It was positioned as a flexible tool for artists, designers, and marketers, with a free daily allowance that made it popular for experimentation.

The company has also developed its own image models, which it has promoted for following prompts closely and rendering text, along with tools for creating logos, posters, and social graphics. Image-to-image, upscaling, and editing by instruction help refine results. Users can browse a community feed to see what others are making and borrow ideas.

item.title: Plus AI
item.description:
Plus AI takes the approach that you shouldn’t have to leave your slide editor to use AI. After installing the add-in in Google Slides or PowerPoint, you describe the presentation you want, and it drafts an outline and slides in the editor, which you can then adjust like any other deck. It can also build from a document, a set of notes, or a web page.

Editing features save time on existing decks. The remix tool can restyle or rework slides, and the rewrite function changes tone or length of text on a slide. It can convert content into a different layout, summarize, and create speaker notes. Because the output is native slides, the file remains fully editable and compatible with company templates and brand assets.

item.title: Poe
item.description:
Poe gives access to many AI models without separate accounts. A single app and website lets you switch between leading chatbots, image generators, and video tools, compare answers, and keep your conversations in one place. This is helpful for people who want to try different models and use whichever works best for each task.

Creators can build bots on top of models with custom prompts and knowledge, and publish them for others, with ways to earn revenue based on usage. The platform also offers an app builder and an API so developers can use Poe’s models in their projects. Group chats let multiple bots and people interact in one conversation.

item.title: Polycam
item.description:
Polycam makes 3D scanning accessible. A user walks around an object or room with their phone, the app captures images or LiDAR depth data, and processing creates a textured 3D model. Models can be measured, shared, and exported for use in design, games, or construction.

Modes include photo-based capture for detail, LiDAR for room scans and floor plans, and tools to build models from photos taken with any camera. Newer features include Gaussian splatting for realistic views and AI tools for generating models from images.

item.title: PostHog AI
item.description:
PostHog bundles the tools product teams use to understand and improve their software. After adding its SDK, you can track events, build funnels and retention charts, watch session recordings, run experiments, release features gradually with flags, collect feedback through surveys, and analyze data with SQL. Having these in one product, with a shared data set, avoids the cost and complexity of stitching several tools together.

AI features include an assistant that can answer questions about your data, write queries, create charts, and summarize insights in plain language, and tools for monitoring AI applications such as tracing model calls and costs. Because PostHog is open source, it can be self-hosted for data control, or used through PostHog Cloud, and a pipeline can send data to other destinations.

item.title: Power BI
item.description: Power BI turns raw data into visual reports. You connect to sources such as Excel files, SQL databases, cloud services, and Microsoft Fabric, shape the data, define relationships and calculations, and build dashboards with charts, maps, and slicers. Reports can be published to the Power BI service, shared with colleagues, refreshed on a schedule, and embedded in other applications. Because it fits neatly with Excel, Teams, SharePoint, and Azure, it is the default BI tool for many Microsoft-centered companies.

item.title: Powtoon
item.description:
Powtoon helps people make animated videos without an animation background. You start from a template for an explainer, training video, or presentation, edit the text and scenes, and choose characters, props, and backgrounds from a library. A timeline lets you control timing, and you can add voiceovers, music, and screen recordings. It is used for onboarding, corporate communication, education, and marketing.

AI tools reduce the work of getting started. A text-to-video feature creates a draft from a script or topic, AI can write scripts, and text-to-speech generates narration in many languages. Avatars can present, and translation features help localize videos. Branding tools keep colors, fonts, and logos consistent, and collaboration features let teams review and approve content.

item.title: Privy
item.description:
Privy gives small stores a way to capture and convert visitors. Pop-ups and banners collect emails and texts with offers, automated emails recover abandoned carts, and campaigns promote products to subscribers. Everything runs from one dashboard connected to the store.

AI assists with writing and targeting, such as drafting emails and choosing segments. Templates and recipes simplify setup for merchants without a marketing team, and analytics show revenue from each campaign.

item.title: Productivity Directory
item.description:
Productivity Directory collects tools that help people work better. Instead of listing every AI product, it focuses on productivity: task managers, calendars, note apps, automation, meeting assistants, and writing aids. Each listing has a short description, a category, and a link, so visitors can browse by need and compare similar tools quickly.

Directories like this serve people early in their search. A user who wants to improve how they plan their day or take meeting notes can see what exists and narrow down options before visiting individual sites. Editors choose which products to include, which gives it a more focused feel than massive catalogs, and new tools are added over time.

item.title: Promethean AI
item.description:
Promethean AI addresses the labor involved in building 3D environments.
