An artist describes what they want in a scene, such as a cluttered study or a forest clearing, and the assistant selects assets from a library, places them with sensible arrangement and variation, and assembles a draft environment. The aim is to automate repetitive dressing and layout so artists can focus on art direction.

The tool learns from the studio’s own assets and preferences, so output stays consistent with the project’s look, and it integrates with common creative software and engines. It was aimed at game studios, film and virtual production teams, and architectural visualization, where large environments must be filled with believable detail.

item.title: Proposify
item.description:
Proposify helps agencies and service companies create and send proposals. Teams build templates with sections, pricing tables, and brand styling, assemble a proposal quickly, and send it to clients who can review, comment, and sign electronically. Notifications show when a proposal is opened.

AI features help with writing content and suggest improvements based on what has worked in past proposals. Analytics reveal how long clients spend on each section, informing follow-ups. Integrations connect with CRMs and billing.

item.title: ProWritingAid
item.description:
ProWritingAid is built for writers who want to improve their craft. As well as catching spelling and grammar errors, it generates reports on overused words, sentence length variation, clichés, passive voice, pacing, dialogue, and readability, which editors and novelists use to revise drafts. The detailed feedback is aimed at long-form writing more than quick messages.

It offers integrations with Microsoft Word, Google Docs, Scrivener, and browsers, and includes a plagiarism checker in higher plans. Newer features use AI to rephrase sentences, suggest rewrites, and offer feedback on structure, and writers can set a house style or custom rules. A lifetime purchase option has been a distinguishing choice compared with subscription-only competitors.

item.title: Qodo AI
item.description:
Qodo started as CodiumAI with a focus on tests, and has expanded to quality across the development process. In the IDE, it analyzes a function, understands its behavior, and generates unit tests that cover normal cases, edge cases, and failure modes, which helps developers raise coverage without writing everything by hand. It also offers chat and code suggestions that take the project context into account.

The review side is a major part. Qodo Merge, built on an open-source tool called PR-Agent, comments on pull requests with summaries, potential bugs, security issues, and suggested fixes, and can learn a team’s standards so reviews reflect internal rules. Multi-agent review systems and a context engine aim to understand large codebases, which matters for enterprise teams with many repositories. Integrations cover GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and major IDEs.

item.title: Quizlet AI
item.description:
Quizlet is a long-running tool for learning through flashcards. Students create or find sets of terms and definitions, then study them with modes such as flashcards, learn sessions that adapt to what you miss, matching games, and practice tests. A huge library of user-created sets covers school subjects, languages, and professional exams, and teachers use it to build class activities.

AI has added help with creating and understanding material. Tools can generate flashcards or quizzes from uploaded notes, textbook pages, or slides, saving the effort of typing each card. An AI tutor can explain a concept, quiz you, and give step-by-step help, and features track progress and suggest what to review. Study guides and summaries can be produced from your own materials.

item.title: Qwilr
item.description:
Qwilr replaces static PDF proposals with web pages. A seller builds a proposal from blocks, such as text, images, videos, pricing tables, and acceptance sections, and sends a link. Buyers can adjust options in a pricing table, and sign online, which shortens the path to closing.

Analytics show who viewed the page, how long they spent on each section, and when they came back, which guides follow-up. Templates keep branding consistent, and integrations push data into CRMs. AI drafts content from notes and suggests improvements.

item.title: Railway
item.description:
Railway makes hosting feel easy. A developer connects a GitHub repository, and Railway detects the language, builds the app, and runs it, with databases like Postgres, Redis, and MySQL added in a click. Environments, variables, and networking are managed in a visual canvas.

Usage-based pricing and preview environments suit small teams, startups, and side projects. Many AI app builders and hobbyists use it to deploy back ends quickly. Features include cron jobs, volumes for storage, and private networking.

item.title: Raw Shorts
item.description:
Raw Shorts aims to make animated explainers accessible to non-designers. You paste a script, an article, or an idea, and the AI breaks it into scenes, chooses animated templates, characters, and icons, and adds a voiceover and music. You can then edit scenes, change visuals, adjust timing, and brand the video with your colors and logo before exporting.

It’s used for marketing explainers, training videos, social clips, and educational content. A library of animated styles, text-to-speech voices in many languages, and options for adding your own media let teams produce a polished video in a short time. Newer features include generating videos from blog posts or presentations.

item.title: Raycast AI
item.description:
Raycast puts a command bar on your keyboard. Press a hotkey, type a few letters, and you can launch apps, search files, run calculations, manage windows, paste snippets, control music, and use hundreds of extensions that connect to tools such as GitHub, Linear, Notion, and Slack. Power users value how much it can cut mouse use and context switching.

Raycast AI adds chat and commands powered by leading language models. You can ask a question, rewrite selected text, summarize a page, translate, or run custom AI commands from any app, and switch among models from different providers. AI Extensions let the assistant act through extensions, such as creating an issue or checking a calendar, and Model Context Protocol support connects it to more tools. Chats and presets are synced across devices.

item.title: Readwise Reader
item.description:
Reader is a single inbox for things you want to read. You can save web pages, subscribe to newsletters at a dedicated email address, follow RSS feeds, upload PDFs and ebooks, and import videos with transcripts. Everything appears in a clean reading view, with tools for highlighting, tagging, and taking notes, and it works across web, mobile, and browser extensions.

The connection with Readwise makes it more than a reading list. Highlights flow into Readwise, which resurfaces them through spaced repetition so you remember what you read, and exports them to Notion, Obsidian, Roam, and other note apps. Ghostreader is the AI assistant that can summarize a document, define terms, answer questions about it, and generate custom prompts, and it also supports text-to-speech and features for catching up on a backlog.

item.title: Real-ESRGAN
item.description:
Real-ESRGAN takes a small, blurry, or compressed image and produces a larger, cleaner version. It was trained on synthetic damage that imitates real-world degradation, such as blur, noise, and compression artifacts, so it handles messy sources better than older upscalers that assumed clean images. The results often look natural, with sharper edges and textures, although the model adds plausible detail instead of recovering what was truly there.

The project provides several models, including one for general photos and one for anime and illustrations, plus tools for video that process frames. Portable builds run on Windows, macOS, and Linux using Vulkan, so no complicated setup or Nvidia GPU is needed, and Python code lets developers integrate it. It is often paired with GFPGAN for face restoration. Many commercial upscaling tools and apps use Real-ESRGAN or models derived from it.

item.title: Recharge
item.description:
Recharge enables subscribe-and-save models for online stores. Merchants on Shopify and other platforms set up subscription products, let customers manage deliveries and payments in a portal, and bill on schedule. It is common in consumables such as food, supplements, and beauty products.

Analytics show retention, churn, and revenue, and tools help reduce cancellations. Smart payment retries recover failed charges, and AI models predict which subscribers may leave so merchants can intervene with offers or pauses.

item.title: Redfin
item.description:
Redfin helped modernize home search. Its site and app show listings with details, photos, and maps, along with estimated home values, price history, and tools to compare neighborhoods. A key difference from traditional brokerages is that its agents are salaried employees instead of paid mostly on commission, and Redfin has competed on lower listing fees and a customer-focused model.

Technology plays a large role. Its valuation model, the Redfin Estimate, uses machine learning on recent sales and listing data to estimate home values, and tools offer alerts, tours scheduling, and offers online. AI features help with search and recommendations. Rocket Companies, the owner of Rocket Mortgage, acquired Redfin, bringing mortgage and agent services together under a combined offering, including financing incentives when buyers use both.

item.title: Remini
item.description:
Remini gained a following for photo restoration. A user uploads an old family photo or a blurry picture, and the AI sharpens it, repairs damage, and enhances faces. It can also upscale images and colorize black-and-white ones.

The app expanded into AI-generated portraits and avatars from selfies, which went viral at times. Video enhancement is also offered. It runs mainly on phones, with processing in the cloud.

Remini has a free tier with ads and limits, and paid plans, and has faced criticism over subscription practices. Enhancement invents plausible detail, so faces may change from the original. Photos are uploaded, so check the privacy policy. Alternatives include Topaz Photo AI, Let’s Enhance, Photoshop’s neural filters, VanceAI, and Palette.fm. Remini suits people restoring family photos.

item.title: RemNote
item.description: RemNote is built for students who want to learn what they write. In a typical note app, notes sit in a folder and are rarely reviewed. In RemNote, you mark terms and definitions inside your notes, and the app turns them into flashcards automatically, then schedules reviews with a spaced repetition algorithm so facts move into long-term memory. Notes are organized in an outline, and each line can link to others, which helps build a connected knowledge base.

item.title: Renderforest
item.description:
Renderforest bundles several creative tools for small businesses. Its video maker offers thousands of templates for intros, explainers, promos, and social videos, with a drag-and-drop editor, stock footage, and music. A logo maker, website builder, and mockup tools round out the suite, so a new business can produce basic branding materials in one place.

AI features speed up creation. Text-to-video tools generate videos from a script or prompt, an AI logo generator proposes designs from a business name, and voiceover and animation helpers add narration and movement. Templates for explainer videos, promos, slideshows, and animated infographics make it quick to produce content for marketing and social media.

item.title: Replica Studios
item.description:
Replica Studios was an Australian startup that made AI voices aimed at creative productions. Its library offered voices of professional actors who had agreed to license their performances, and its tools let game developers and filmmakers generate dialogue with emotion and style. Integrations for game engines such as Unreal and Unity made it easy to put placeholder or final voices into a project, and it also supported voice conversion.

The company drew attention for working with actors instead of against them. It signed an agreement with the actors’ union SAG-AFTRA on terms for licensing digital voice replicas in games, which some actors welcomed and others criticized as inadequate. That debate was part of a wider fight over how AI voices should be used in entertainment, which continues.

item.title: Replika
item.description: Replika is one of the earliest AI companion apps. You create an avatar, choose a name and appearance, and begin chatting. Over time the AI builds a memory of your interests, relationships, and preferences, and the avatar responds in a way that reflects that history. Users talk to it about their day, vent about problems, practice conversations, or just keep company. It offers text chat, voice calls, and an augmented reality mode that places the avatar in your room.

item.title: Replit
item.description:
Replit began as an online code editor and runtime that supported dozens of languages with no installation. Open a browser tab, start a project, and your code runs immediately on Replit’s servers. That made it popular in schools, coding bootcamps, and with beginners, and its multiplayer editing lets several people work in the same project at once. Projects are hosted, so sharing or deploying an app takes a click.

The current focus is Replit Agent, which builds software from natural language. You describe an app, and the agent writes code, sets up the environment, installs packages, creates a database, tests the result, and deploys it. You can keep chatting to refine features or fix bugs, or open the code and edit it directly. The aim is to let people without programming experience make working apps, and to let developers move faster. A mobile app lets you build and test from a phone.

item.title: ResearchRabbit
item.description:
ResearchRabbit helps researchers find papers they would not discover through keyword search. You add a few papers to a collection, and the tool suggests related earlier work, later work that cites them, and papers by connected authors, showing the connections in visual graphs. As you add more papers, recommendations get more specific, which makes it behave like a recommendation engine for research.

Collections keep projects organized, and alerts notify you when new papers match your interests. You can see networks of authors, explore how a field evolved, and export references to managers like Zotero. It is popular with students and academics who are starting a literature review or entering a new topic, and who want something more exploratory than a search box.

item.title: Resemble AI
item.description: Resemble AI builds voices for products and productions. You provide recordings of a speaker, with consent, and the platform trains a voice model that can read any text in that voice, or convert one person’s speech into another voice in real time. Companies use it for branded voices, localization, games, call centers, and media. An API makes it possible to generate speech in applications, and the system supports multiple languages and emotional control.

item.title: Resume.io
item.description:
Resume.io helps job seekers create a polished resume quickly. You choose a template, fill in your experience, education, and skills in a guided form, and see the layout update. The templates are designed to be clean and readable by applicant tracking systems, and you can adjust colors and fonts, reorder sections, and download the result as a PDF. Cover letter and CV builders follow the same approach.

AI features help with the hard part, which is the wording. The assistant suggests bullet points for a job title, drafts a professional summary, and can tailor a resume to a job description. A resume checker highlights weaknesses, and a job tracker helps manage applications. The tool also provides guides and examples for different professions.

item.title: Retool AI
item.description:
Retool is designed for engineers who need to build internal software quickly. Developers connect databases, APIs, and services, drag components such as tables, forms, and charts onto a canvas, and write queries and logic in SQL and JavaScript where needed. The result is an application for operations, support, or finance teams to manage data, approve requests, or run workflows, built in hours instead of weeks.

AI is integrated across the platform. A generative assistant can create an app from a description, write queries, and generate components, and Retool offers AI actions to classify, summarize, and extract information as parts of apps and workflows. Retool Agents let teams build agents that use their data and tools, and workflows automate scheduled and event-driven tasks. Enterprise controls cover permissions, audit logs, and self-hosting.

item.title: Rev
item.description:
Rev started as a human transcription marketplace and added automatic transcription as speech recognition improved. Users upload audio or video, and receive a transcript within minutes from the AI service, or within hours from human transcribers who deliver higher accuracy. The choice lets you trade cost and speed for precision, which matters for legal proceedings, journalism, and broadcast captions.

Beyond transcripts, Rev offers captions and subtitles in many languages, translation, and a web editor for correcting and exporting text. Meeting tools record calls and produce notes, and an API supports developers who want to add transcription to products. Accessibility compliance is a big use, because captions help meet legal requirements for education and media.

item.title: Reverso
item.description:
Reverso is known for context. Beyond a plain translation, it shows examples of the word or phrase used in real texts, such as books, subtitles, and documents, with the original and translation side by side. That helps learners and translators choose the right expression, understand nuance, and see how phrases are typically used in each language.

The product includes several tools. A translator handles text and documents, Reverso Context is the example search, and a grammar and spell checker works across languages. Verb conjugators, vocabulary lists, and flashcards support learning, and AI features paraphrase and improve text. Browser extensions and mobile apps make it available while reading or writing.

item.title: Rezi
item.description:
Rezi focuses on a specific worry: that automated screening software will reject a resume before a person reads it. The builder uses a simple, single-column layout and standard section names that parsing software reads reliably. As you write, a score shows how well the resume matches ATS best practices, with checks on length, formatting, action verbs, and keywords from a target job posting.

AI helps with content. It can generate bullet points from a role and tasks, rewrite weak phrases into stronger ones, and tailor a resume to a job description. It also drafts cover letters and has features for tracking applications and tuning your LinkedIn profile. The interface is plain, with less design flair than many competitors, which is intentional.

item.title: Rippling
item.description:
Rippling combines employee data with the systems that depend on it. When a person joins, Rippling creates their payroll record, sets up benefits, provisions laptops and software accounts, and orders equipment, using one source of truth. Changes in the employee record cascade across the systems.

Modules cover HR, payroll in many countries, time and attendance, benefits, device and app management, and corporate cards and expenses. A workflow engine lets admins automate approvals and tasks, and AI assistants answer questions and draft content.

item.title: Rive
item.description: Rive aims to make animation behave like part of an app. In its editor, designers draw vector shapes, rig them with bones, and animate them on a timeline. The key difference from video or GIF is the state machine: animations can have states and transitions that react to inputs, such as a button being pressed, a character getting closer, or a progress value changing. This lets one asset handle many behaviors.

item.title: Riverside
item.description: Riverside solves a familiar remote-recording problem: video calls compress audio and video, so the recording sounds and looks poor. Riverside records each person’s microphone and camera on their own device and uploads the files in the background. The result is uncompressed audio and up to 4K video, with each participant on a separate track, unaffected by a weak internet connection during the call. Hosts and guests join through a browser link without installing anything.

item.title: Roam Research
item.description:
Roam helped popularize networked note-taking. Notes are organized as outlines of bullet blocks, and you link to other pages by typing double brackets. Every link creates a backlink on the page it points to, so you can see everywhere a concept is mentioned. Daily notes serve as a default home for new thoughts, and over time, links build a web of connected ideas without a rigid folder structure.

Its power comes from working at the block level. Any bullet can be referenced or embedded elsewhere, queries pull together blocks that match conditions, and attributes add structured data to notes. A graph view and a plugin ecosystem add visualization and automation, and keyboard-driven editing makes it fast for those who master it. Researchers, writers, and knowledge workers have used it for long-term thinking.

item.title: Roboflow
item.description:
Roboflow helps teams build computer vision applications without starting from scratch. You upload images or video, label objects with AI-assisted annotation tools, and Roboflow handles formatting, augmentation, and splitting data into training sets. It then trains or fine-tunes models such as YOLO and other popular architectures, and shows performance metrics so you can see where the model fails and what data to add.

Deployment is a main focus. Models can run through a hosted API, on your own servers, or at the edge on devices such as NVIDIA Jetson or a mobile phone. Workflows let you chain models with logic and actions, for example detecting a defect, counting items, and sending an alert to a system. Roboflow Universe is a public collection of datasets and pretrained models shared by the community, which gives a fast start for common tasks.

item.title: Rosetta Stone
item.description: Rosetta Stone teaches by immersion. Instead of translating from your own language, lessons pair images with words and phrases in the target language, so you learn by association, the way children pick up a first language. Lessons build from simple vocabulary to conversation, with exercises on listening, reading, writing, and speaking. It has been a recognized name in language learning for decades and sells courses in about two dozen languages.

item.title: RunPod
item.description:
RunPod rents GPU computing in several forms. Users launch pods with a chosen GPU for development and training, or deploy serverless endpoints that scale with traffic for inference. Templates for common tools like Stable Diffusion and popular language model setups speed up starting.

Storage volumes persist data across sessions, and a community cloud offers lower prices on capacity from independent hosts alongside a secure cloud with data center hardware. Per-second billing suits bursty work.

item.title: Runway
item.description:
Runway builds tools for creative professionals. Its generative video models create clips from text or images, and a suite of editing tools handles tasks like removing backgrounds, changing motion, extending shots, and applying styles. Everything runs in the browser.

The company began with accessible video editing and became a leader in generative video, working with artists and studios. Newer models offer longer clips, better consistency, and controls for camera and motion, and the platform includes workflows for combining generation with traditional editing.

item.title: Runway
item.description: Runway is one of the original AI video companies, and it built its tools with filmmakers and artists in mind. The core of the product is its Gen video models, which create short clips from a text prompt, a still image, or both. Reference images help keep a character or setting consistent from one shot to the next, which is the hard part of making anything longer than a single clip. The company started as a set of browser-based editing tools, and some of that remains, such as background removal, motion tracking, and inpainting.

item.title: Runway Gen-3
item.description:
Gen-3 Alpha improved on earlier versions with finer detail, better handling of motion, and more consistent results across frames. Users could generate clips of several seconds from a prompt, an image, or both, with controls for camera movement and style.

It was trained on both images and video, aiming to understand how things move, and supported features such as image-to-video and video-to-video. Filmmakers and agencies used it for concept work, ads, and visual effects experiments.

item.title: Salesforce
item.description: Salesforce is the CRM that large companies tend to run their sales and customer operations on. It tracks leads, accounts, opportunities, and support cases, and it is sold as separate clouds for Sales, Service, Marketing, and Commerce, with Slack, Tableau, and MuleSoft added for collaboration, analytics, and integration. Underneath is a platform that lets companies build custom objects, workflows, and apps, which is why Salesforce setups can look very different from one company to the next.

item.title: Salesforce Einstein
item.description:
Einstein brought AI to Salesforce customers well before generative AI became popular. Predictive features score leads and opportunities, forecast revenue, recommend next best actions, and flag at-risk accounts, using each company’s own CRM data. Einstein Discovery finds patterns and suggests what drives outcomes, and bots and analytics features extend the same ideas to service and marketing.

With generative AI, Einstein has expanded to write emails, summarize records and cases, and generate service replies, grounded in customer data and protected by the Einstein Trust Layer, which masks sensitive information and prevents customer data from being used to train outside models. The conversational assistant evolved into Agentforce, which builds autonomous agents on the same foundation, so Einstein now refers to a mix of older predictive features and the generative AI infrastructure.

item.title: SalesLoft
item.description:
Salesloft helps sales teams organize outbound and follow-up work. Reps follow cadences, which are structured sequences of emails, calls, and social touches, and the platform tells them who to contact next and records each activity in the CRM. Managers can see which messages and sequences generate replies and meetings, and coach reps with call recordings and analytics.

The platform has expanded into revenue orchestration. Conversation intelligence records and summarizes calls, deal management tracks stage progress and risk, and forecasting tools combine pipeline data with engagement signals. Salesloft acquired Drift for conversational marketing and has combined with Clari, a revenue forecasting company, to build a broader revenue platform. AI assistants prepare meeting briefs, draft messages, and suggest next steps.

item.title: SaneBox
item.description:
SaneBox tackles inbox overload without replacing your email app. It connects to your existing account and analyzes your behavior, such as who you reply to and which messages you open, then moves less important mail into a folder called SaneLater. Newsletters, notifications, and cold outreach end up there, and you get a digest to skim when you choose. The important mail stays in your inbox.

Several tools help you stay in control. SaneBlackHole sends unwanted senders away permanently with a single drag, snooze folders let you hide a message until later, and reminders alert you if a recipient has not replied. A Do Not Disturb feature holds mail for a period. Because it works on the server, it functions with Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, Yahoo, and other providers, and on all your devices.

item.title: SAP Ariba
item.description:
SAP Ariba helps large organizations buy what they need in an organized way. Procurement teams use it to find and evaluate suppliers, run sourcing events, manage contracts, process purchase orders and invoices, and monitor supplier risk. The Ariba Network connects buyers and suppliers electronically, so orders and invoices flow between systems without manual entry.

AI is being added to reduce manual work. SAP’s assistant, Joule, can help users search for information, draft sourcing documents, and answer questions about spend, and features analyze contracts, recommend suppliers, and flag unusual transactions. Integration with SAP’s ERP and other systems provides a connected view of purchasing, and spend analytics reveal savings opportunities.

item.title: Sassbook AI
item.description:
Sassbook AI is a small suite of text tools. The AI story writer takes a premise and creates a narrative, with options to continue and steer the plot, aimed at hobby writers and students looking for ideas. Other tools summarize long text into shorter versions, paraphrase passages in different styles, and generate headlines and titles.

The tools work in a browser with a simple interface. Users paste text or enter a prompt, choose settings such as length or style, and get results they can edit. It also includes a plagiarism check and a few utilities for writers. The target audience includes bloggers, students, and casual writers who need quick help.

item.title: Scale AI
item.description:
Scale AI built its business on a simple observation: AI models need huge amounts of well-labeled data, and quality control at scale is hard. It combines software with a large network of human contributors and experts to annotate images, video, text, and sensor data. Early customers included self-driving car developers, and the company grew by supplying training data to the biggest AI labs.

Today much of its work involves large language models. Scale provides human feedback data used in reinforcement learning, expert-written examples for fine-tuning, and evaluations that test models for accuracy and safety. Its tools help companies manage data pipelines, and a generative AI platform lets enterprises customize models on their own data. Public-sector work includes AI systems for defense and government agencies, and the company runs public leaderboards that rank models on hard tests.

item.title: Scalenut
item.description:
Scalenut combines SEO research with AI writing. A user enters a keyword, and the platform analyzes search results to suggest topics, questions, and structure, then produces an outline and draft article, optimized for search. A one-click mode called Cruise creates a full article by following the steps of research, outline, and writing automatically.

Other features support content marketing. A keyword planner clusters terms into topics, an optimization score guides edits, and tools help with rewriting, product descriptions, and social content. The platform includes brand voice settings, a plagiarism checker, and a feature for tracking content performance. Teams can collaborate and manage projects in the app.

item.title: Scenario
item.description:
Scenario is built around consistency, which is the main challenge of using generative AI in game production. A studio uploads examples of its art, and Scenario trains a custom model that learns the style, so the characters, props, and environments it generates look like they belong in the same game. Artists can use it to create concepts, variations, and finished assets faster.

The platform covers more than still images. It can generate sprites, textures, icons, and UI elements, create variations of existing pieces, convert images into 3D models, and offers workflows for upscaling and cleaning outputs. An API and plugins connect it to game engines and pipelines, and team features support collaboration and asset management. The focus is on production use by studios and indie developers.

item.title: Scholarcy
item.description:
Scholarcy tries to make reading faster. You give it an article or upload a PDF, and it breaks the document into a summary card with key points, the main findings, study design, limitations, and important terms. It extracts figures, tables, and references, and links the references so you can follow them. The format helps readers decide whether a paper is worth a full read.

A browser extension summarizes papers on publisher websites, and a library stores summaries with notes and tags. Export options send content to reference managers and note apps, and a feature can generate flashcards for study. Students and researchers use it to process large reading lists, create literature review notes, and check key details quickly.

item.title: Scinapse
item.description:
Scinapse is a search tool for scientific literature. It indexes a large body of scholarly papers across disciplines and ranks results with machine learning that considers relevance, citations, and recency. Users search by topic, title, or author, filter by year, journal, and field, and read abstracts with links to the publishers or open-access copies.

Features go beyond a basic list. Author pages show a researcher’s publications and citation profile, paper pages show who cited a work and related papers, and collections let you save papers to read later. Alerts notify you about new papers on a topic or from an author. The site was created by a Korean research technology company and is free to use, supported by its broader services for researchers.

item.title: SciSpace
item.description: SciSpace, formerly known as Typeset, is built around the problem of reading dense research. Upload a PDF or open a paper from its database, and an AI copilot lets you highlight a passage, a table, or an equation and ask for an explanation in simpler terms. You can also ask questions about the whole paper, request a summary, or get the key methods and results. It is helpful for students and researchers entering an unfamiliar field.

item.title: Scribbr
item.description:
Scribbr started as a proofreading and thesis editing service and built free tools for students. The citation generator formats references in common styles, the paraphraser rewrites text, and the grammar checker catches errors. A plagiarism checker compares text against sources, and an AI detector estimates machine-written text.

Students use these tools while writing essays and theses. Paid services include human editing by professional editors, which is a differentiator from purely automated tools. Guides explain academic writing topics.

item.title: SeaArt
item.description: SeaArt gives users a rich set of image generation tools in a friendly interface. You write a prompt, choose among many models and styles, and generate images, with options such as ControlNet to guide pose or composition and LoRA models to apply particular styles or characters. A library of community-shared models, workflows, and characters lets users build on others’ work, and a node-based workflow editor offers more advanced control for those who want it.

item.title: Semantic Scholar
item.description: Semantic Scholar is a research search engine built by the Allen Institute for AI, a nonprofit research organization. It covers hundreds of millions of academic papers across science, medicine, engineering, and the social sciences, and it is free. Unlike a plain keyword search, it uses language models to understand what papers are about and how they connect, which helps surface relevant work that does not use the exact words you typed.

item.title: Sembly AI
item.description:
Sembly joins your online meetings, records them, and produces a transcript with a structured summary. The summary highlights the main points, tasks, decisions, and risks mentioned, so teams can see what needs follow-up without rewatching. It also supports in-person meetings through its mobile app and uploads of audio files, and works in many languages.

Beyond single meetings, Sembly helps organize knowledge. Workspaces and meeting libraries let teams search past conversations and ask questions across them, and templates adjust the notes for different meeting types such as sales calls or interviews. Integrations push summaries and tasks into Slack, Notion, Asana, Jira, HubSpot, and other tools. Analytics track patterns like meeting time and topics.

item.title: Semgrep
item.description:
Semgrep scans code for patterns. Rules look like the code they match, which makes them easier to write than traditional analyzers’ queries. Teams use community rules for common vulnerabilities and write custom ones for their own standards, running scans in CI and on developers’ machines.

The commercial platform adds dependency scanning, secrets detection, and a triage assistant that uses AI to explain findings, suggest fixes, and filter likely false positives. It integrates with pull requests and issue trackers.

item.title: SEMrush
item.description:
Semrush bundles many marketing tools in one subscription. Users research keywords, audit websites, track rankings, analyze backlinks, spy on competitors’ traffic and ads, and plan content, all from a shared dashboard. It is widely used by agencies and in-house teams.

AI features help with writing and analysis. A writing assistant drafts and optimizes content, AI tools summarize data and suggest actions, and newer products track how brands appear in AI-generated answers from chat assistants, a growing concern for search marketers. Reports and integrations suit client work.

item.title: SEMrush
item.description: Semrush is among the most widely used toolkits for search marketers. Its core is a big database of keywords and domains, so you can see which terms a competitor ranks for, how much traffic a page gets, who links to it, and where your own site stands. Keyword research, position tracking, site audits, and backlink analysis cover the regular work of search optimization. Separate tools handle paid search, content planning, local listings, and social media.

item.title: ServiceNow
item.description:
ServiceNow began as an IT service management tool and became a general workflow platform for large organizations. Employees and customers submit requests, such as a laptop problem, a payroll question, or a customer complaint, and the platform routes, tracks, and resolves them using defined workflows. Companies use it as a system of record and action across IT operations, HR, legal, security, and customer service.

AI is central to its current strategy. Now Assist adds generative AI to summarize cases, draft replies, and help agents find answers, and AI agents can take on tasks such as triaging incidents and fulfilling requests with minimal human intervention. The company acquired Moveworks, whose employee assistant is intended to become the front door to the platform, and offers tools to govern and monitor agents across the enterprise.

item.title: Sheet+
item.description:
Sheet+ is for spreadsheet users who know what they want but not the syntax. You describe the calculation, such as the total of sales for a region in a given month, and Sheet+ produces the formula with an explanation. You can paste a formula you don’t understand and get a plain-language breakdown, or paste an error and receive suggestions for fixing it.

It extends to related tasks. It can write Google Apps Script automation from a description, generate regular expressions, and create SQL queries, and integrates with Sheets through an add-on so you can work without leaving the spreadsheet. It’s popular with small business owners, analysts, and anyone who finds formulas intimidating.

item.title: Shopify
item.description: Shopify lets someone start an online store without building the software behind it. You choose a theme, add products, set up payments and shipping, and the platform handles hosting, the checkout, and tax and currency settings. The same system also covers in-person sales through point-of-sale hardware, so a shop can manage online and physical inventory together. Everything from a one-person side business to large brands runs on it, and Shop Pay, its accelerated checkout, is used well beyond Shopify’s own stores.

item.title: Shortwave
item.description:
Shortwave is a Gmail client that rethinks the inbox. Related messages are grouped into threads, newsletters and receipts can be bundled so they do not clutter the main view, and snooze, scheduling, and split inboxes help you process email faster. It works on Mac, Windows, iOS, Android, and the web, and connects to your Gmail account.

AI is central. You can ask the assistant questions about your email, such as what a client asked for last month or when a trip was booked, and it searches and answers using your messages. It summarizes long threads, drafts replies in your tone, and can take actions like organizing, labeling, and scheduling. The goal is to cut the time spent finding and writing.

item.title: SideChef
item.description:
SideChef is built for people who want help in the kitchen. Each recipe is broken into short steps with photos or video, so you can follow along while cooking, and hands-free voice control and timers keep you moving without touching your phone with messy hands. Recipes cover a wide range of cuisines and diets, and you can scale servings, swap ingredients, and save favorites.

Planning features reduce the work around cooking. Meal plans suggest weekly menus based on tastes and dietary needs, and shopping lists are built automatically from chosen recipes, with options to order groceries through delivery partners. The app also works with smart kitchen devices, and AI helps personalize recommendations and adjust plans over time.

item.title: SimilarWeb
item.description:
Similarweb lets you look at the performance of sites you do not own. Enter a domain, and it shows estimated monthly visits, traffic sources such as search, social, and direct, top keywords, referring sites, audience demographics, and engagement metrics like time on site. Data comes from a mix of panels, partnerships, and public sources, modeled to produce estimates. This helps in benchmarking competitors and finding growth opportunities.

The platform covers more than websites. It tracks app usage and downloads, advertising, and market segments, and ranks sites within categories. Recent additions include tracking how brands and sites are cited and visited through AI chatbots, reflecting the way people increasingly use AI assistants instead of search. Investors use the data to spot trends in company performance before financial reports, and sales teams use it to find leads.

item.title: simpleshow
item.description:
simpleshow is known for its hand-drawn, paper-cutout explainer style. A user pastes a script or topic, and the engine suggests images and structure, generates a video with narration, and lets the user edit scenes. The goal is to make complex subjects clear for training and communications.

Companies use it for onboarding, compliance, product explanations, and internal updates. The platform is aimed at non-designers and provides templates and a library of illustrations.

item.title: Siri
item.description: Siri is the assistant that comes with every Apple device. You say “Hey Siri” or hold a button, then ask it to send a message, set a timer, call someone, play music, adjust a setting, or control HomeKit devices. It works across Apple’s hardware, so the same assistant is on your wrist, in your car through CarPlay, and on a smart speaker. Its biggest advantage is how deeply it ties into the system, since it can act on messages, calendars, reminders, and photos without extra setup.

item.title: Sisense
item.description:
Sisense helps organizations analyze data and share insights. Analysts connect data sources, build models and dashboards, and users explore results in a browser. Its strength is embedding: software companies place Sisense charts and analytics inside their products for customers.

AI features include asking questions in plain language, forecasting, and automatic detection of unusual patterns, plus a generative assistant that builds dashboards. The platform works with cloud data warehouses and offers an API-first approach.

item.title: Sketch
item.description:
Sketch helped define modern interface design. Designers create screens with vectors and reusable symbols, build design systems, and prototype interactions. Its Mac-native app is fast and has a large plugin ecosystem.

Collaboration moved to the web, where teammates view, comment, and hand off designs, and a Windows-compatible web editor extends access. AI features help generate placeholder content, adjust layouts, and speed up repetitive work.

Sketch is sold by subscription. Figma has taken much of its market because of browser-based collaboration. Alternatives include Figma, Penpot, Adobe XD (no longer developed), Framer, and Affinity Designer. Sketch suits Mac-based designers who prefer a native tool.

item.title: SketchUp
item.description: SketchUp is known for being easy to learn. Its core idea is pushing and pulling flat shapes into 3D forms, which makes it quick to sketch a building, a room, or a piece of furniture. Architects use it for early design, interior designers for layouts, and construction and woodworking professionals for planning and shop drawings. The 3D Warehouse offers a huge library of free models of furniture, fixtures, and building components.

item.title: Slidebean
item.description:
Slidebean separates writing from design. You enter text for each slide in an outline-style editor, choose a slide type such as problem, solution, market, or team, and the software lays it out, selecting fonts, spacing, and graphics so the result looks professional. That means founders can focus on the message and avoid spending hours on layout. AI features help draft slide content and improve wording.

Because it was built for startups, Slidebean adds extras beyond slides. It offers pitch deck templates based on successful funding decks, tools to share decks and see who viewed them, and a financial model builder for projections. The company has also offered pitch deck design and fundraising services for founders who want expert help.

item.title: SlidesAI
item.description:
SlidesAI works inside Google Slides. You paste in text, such as an essay, notes, or an article, or enter a topic, and the add-on creates a set of slides with titles, bullet points, and layout. It lets you pick a presentation style, color theme, and the number of slides, and can add relevant images. The result is a draft that you edit like any other Google Slides deck.

Additional features support content work. It can summarize long text into key points, paraphrase for clarity, and generate text for slides from a prompt. Because the output is a native Slides file, it can be shared, collaborated on, and presented as usual. It’s popular with students, teachers, and professionals who need a quick starting point.

item.title: Smartcat
item.description:
Smartcat brings machine and human translation together. A company uploads documents or connects content sources, receives AI translation immediately, and can request human review from freelance linguists or agencies in its marketplace, all with translation memory and glossaries.

Workflow tools manage projects, deadlines, and payments, and the platform supports many file types and integrations. AI agents handle tasks such as quality checks, and the pricing model aims to keep costs lower than traditional agencies.

item.title: Smartly.io
item.description:
Smartly, formerly Smartly.io, serves brands and agencies that run large ad programs. Its platform connects to major social networks and lets teams build and launch many campaigns from one interface, apply rules, and update thousands of ads at once. For retailers with big catalogs, dynamic ads are generated automatically from product feeds, adjusting to inventory and price.

The product emphasizes creative and optimization. Creative automation produces many ad variations in different sizes and languages from templates, which helps with testing and localization. Predictive budget allocation shifts spend among campaigns based on performance, and reporting brings results across platforms together. Newer generative features help create and adapt creative assets, with brand controls.

item.title: Smartsheet AI
item.description:
Smartsheet is built around the grid. Teams manage projects, requests, and processes in sheets that look like spreadsheets but add features such as attachments, comments, dependencies, and approvals. The same data can be viewed as a Gantt chart, calendar, board, or form, and reports and dashboards summarize progress for leaders. It’s used for project plans, marketing calendars, intake processes, and portfolio tracking in many large organizations.

Automation and AI reduce manual work. Rules can send alerts, request approvals, or update fields when conditions are met, and AI helps by generating formulas from plain language, summarizing sheets, creating content, and analyzing data to find trends. Newer features allow building workflows and agents with natural language. Integrations connect with Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Slack, Salesforce, and more.

item.title: SmolAgents
item.description: SmolAgents is designed to be easy to read and use. The core logic fits in a small amount of code, and building an agent takes a few lines: you pick a model, give it tools, and run a task. Its signature idea is the code agent, where the model writes its actions as Python code instead of structured tool calls. This lets it combine steps, use loops and variables, and handle multi-step problems efficiently, and the approach often needs fewer steps than traditional methods.

item.title: Snyk AI
item.description:
Snyk puts security checks into the development workflow. Developers connect repositories and CI pipelines, and Snyk scans their own code, third-party libraries, container images, and cloud configuration for known vulnerabilities and insecure patterns, then reports issues with guidance. Findings appear in the IDE, pull requests, and dashboards, and automatic fix pull requests can upgrade vulnerable dependencies.

AI plays a central role. DeepCode AI, trained on security data, analyzes code and generates suggested fixes, and Snyk has developed tools to scan code written by AI coding assistants and to guard agents using the Model Context Protocol. As developers use assistants to write more code, automated security review becomes more important, and Snyk positions itself as a safety layer.

item.title: SocialBee
item.description:
SocialBee organizes posting by category, such as promotions, tips, and behind-the-scenes, so a profile keeps a deliberate mix rather than random posts. Evergreen content can be recycled automatically, and a calendar shows what is scheduled.

AI helps generate posts, captions, and images, and its Copilot suggests a strategy and content plan from a business description. Team features support approvals and client work, and analytics report performance.

SocialBee is paid, with plans by profiles. Alternatives include Buffer, Later, Publer, Hootsuite, and Metricool. SocialBee suits small businesses and agencies.

item.title: Socratic by Google
item.description:
Socratic began as a startup and was acquired by Google, which relaunched it as a free app for students. A learner took a photo of a homework problem, and the app identified the concept and pointed to videos, explanations, and step-by-step guidance from across the web instead of just giving an answer.

It covered subjects such as math, science, and literature, and used machine learning to match questions to educational content. The goal was to help students understand a topic, not only to produce a solution.

item.title: Softr
item.description:
Softr turns data into software. A user connects Airtable, Google Sheets, or its own database, and builds pages with blocks such as lists, forms, dashboards, and charts. Logins and permissions control which users see which records.

Typical products include client portals, directories, simple CRMs, and internal tools. The AI builder creates an app from a description, and workflows automate actions. Hosting and a custom domain are included.

Softr has a free plan and paid tiers by users and features. Complex logic is limited compared with full code. Alternatives include Glide, Pory, Stacker, Bubble, and Retool. Softr suits non-developers building apps on spreadsheets and databases.

item.title: Sonix
item.description:
Sonix focuses on fast, accurate machine transcription with a polished editor. You upload a file or connect a source, and get a transcript with timestamps and speaker labels, which you can edit while listening and the text highlights as the audio plays. It supports over forty languages and can translate transcripts into many more. Journalists, researchers, podcasters, and video producers use it to turn recordings into searchable text.

Additional tools support publishing. Sonix exports subtitles and captions in standard formats, offers a media player that embeds the transcript, and provides search across all your files. Integrations and an API connect it with video editors like Premiere Pro and Final Cut, and Zoom. Teams can share folders and custom vocabulary to improve accuracy on specialized terms.

item.title: Sourcegraph Cody
item.description: Cody grew out of Sourcegraph’s code search, which indexes entire repositories and lets developers find and understand code across many projects. That context was its main advantage: instead of guessing from the open file, Cody could draw on the broader codebase to answer questions, write code that matched existing patterns, and explain how parts of a system fit together. It worked in VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and the web, with chat, autocomplete, and commands to edit and test code.

item.title: Spark Mail
item.description:
Spark is an email client that works with Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Yahoo, and other accounts. Its Smart Inbox sorts messages into categories, putting people and important mail first and keeping newsletters and notifications out of the way. Features such as snooze, send later, follow-up reminders, and quick replies make it faster to process mail, and a unified inbox combines accounts.

Collaboration is a differentiator. Teams can share emails, comment privately on messages, and draft replies together before sending, which suits small teams who handle shared mailboxes. AI features in the paid tier help write and rewrite emails, summarize long threads, and suggest replies, and a feature can search by asking questions. The app is available on Apple devices, Android, and Windows.

item.title: Speechify
item.description: Speechify turns reading into listening. You import text from the web, a PDF, an email, or a photo of a page, and the app reads it aloud at the speed you choose, highlighting the words as it goes. That makes it useful for catching up on articles while commuting, for studying, and for people with dyslexia or other reading differences, who often find audio easier to process. Apps for iOS, Android, Chrome, and the web sync your library.

item.title: Spline
item.description:
Spline brings 3D to web designers. In a browser editor that feels more like Figma than Blender, you create shapes, materials, lighting, and animations, then add interactions such as hover effects and clicks. Scenes can be published as links, embedded in websites, or exported to code, and they run in real time in the browser. It’s used for product landing pages, interactive hero sections, games, and design prototypes.

Collaboration and AI features set it apart from traditional 3D tools. Multiple people can edit a scene at once with comments and version history. AI tools can generate 3D objects and textures from text, help with animation, and create scenes from prompts. Physics, particles, and state-based interactions add depth, and integrations with Figma let designers bring in 2D elements.

item.title: Spotify for Podcasters
item.description:
Spotify for Podcasters grew from Anchor, an app that made podcasting free and easy. Creators can record from a phone or computer, upload episodes, and publish to Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and other directories from one place, with no hosting fees. Tools include simple editing, music and sound effects, and a way to bring in guests remotely.

The creator tools have expanded to include video podcasts, which Spotify has promoted heavily, along with analytics on audience size, demographics, and listening behavior. Monetization options include ad insertion, listener subscriptions, and partner programs for eligible shows. The brand has been folded into Spotify for Creators, which covers audio and video content creators on the platform.

item.title: Sprout Social
item.description:
Sprout Social is built for teams that manage social media as a function, not a side task. A calendar plans and schedules content across networks such as Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X, and TikTok, and approval flows keep drafts under review before they go out. A smart inbox gathers messages, comments, and mentions from every channel into one stream that can be assigned, tagged, and replied to by a team.

Analytics are a major selling point. Reports show how posts perform, how audiences grow, and how competitors compare, and they can be exported or shared with clients and executives. Listening tools track brand mentions, topics, and sentiment across social and the web, which helps with crisis monitoring and market research. Influencer marketing and employee advocacy tools extend into related work. AI Assist helps write posts, change tone, and draft replies, and it can summarize sentiment from conversations.

item.title: Square
item.description:
Square is known for its card readers and registers. A small business accepts payments in person, online, or by invoice, tracks inventory, and manages staff and payroll from a single account. Hardware ranges from a simple reader to full countertop systems.

Additional services include appointments, loyalty programs, marketing, and small business loans based on sales. AI assistance writes item descriptions, generates insights from sales data, and answers business questions.

Square charges processing fees per transaction and sells hardware, with paid software tiers for advanced features. It has a free plan for basic use. Alternatives include Toast for restaurants, Clover, Shopify POS, Stripe Terminal, and SumUp. Square suits small retail and food businesses.

item.title: Stability AI
item.description:
Stability AI helped start the open-source image generation boom with Stable Diffusion, a model anyone could download, run, and modify. The release spurred a huge community of tools, fine-tunes, and applications, and changed expectations about access to generative models.

The company has since released a family of models, including newer image generators, Stable Video Diffusion, Stable Audio for music and sound, and 3D tools. It sells API access and commercial licenses, and partners with enterprises, and with media and entertainment companies.

item.title: Stable Video Diffusion
item.description:
Stable Video Diffusion extends the Stable Diffusion approach to motion. A user supplies a still image, and the model generates a few seconds of video that animates the scene. It was released with open weights, so researchers and hobbyists could run and adapt it.

Many later tools and workflows built on it, adding controls, longer clips, and fine-tunes. It helped prove that open video models were feasible, though newer models from other labs have surpassed it in length and quality.

item.title: Stamped.io
item.description:
Stamped helps online stores build trust. After a purchase, it emails customers asking for reviews, collects star ratings with photos or videos, and displays them on product pages and in search results with structured data. Social proof improves conversion rates, and review requests can be automated and timed, with options to send coupons for leaving a review.

The platform also offers loyalty and referral programs. Customers earn points for purchases and actions, redeem rewards, and refer friends, which encourages repeat business. AI features summarize reviews into key themes, surface what customers love or dislike, and help merchants respond. Reports show review volume, ratings, and the effect on sales, and integrations connect with email, helpdesk, and ads tools.

item.title: Stampli
item.description:
Stampli keeps the conversation about an invoice attached to the invoice. When a bill arrives, teams discuss it in context, approvers sign off, and the payment goes out, with no hunting through email threads. It connects to accounting systems and does not require replacing them.

Billy the Bot reads invoices, suggests coding and approvals based on past behavior, and flags anomalies. Payment tools handle payments and cards, and the platform provides audit trails and reporting.

item.title: StarryAI
item.description:
StarryAI brought AI art generation to phones. In the app, you enter a text prompt, pick an art style or model, and receive images within a minute or so. Styles range from fantasy and anime to realism and abstract, and you can use an image as a starting point for variations. It’s aimed at hobbyists and creators who want art for wallpapers, profile pictures, book covers, or game concepts.

Features support experimentation. You can control aspect ratio, choose among models, and upscale results, and a gallery shows creations from other users for inspiration. Different pricing tiers offer more credits and faster generation, and the terms for commercial use vary by plan, with ownership of outputs depending on the subscription.

item.title: Stepsize
item.description:
Stepsize addressed the problem of technical debt that never gets recorded. Developers flag issues directly in code while they work, and Stepsize collects them in a backlog that can be prioritized and linked to issue trackers. Managers see where debt concentrates and plan time to address it.

The company has since introduced Stepsize AI, a product that generates reports on development progress from engineering tools, and its materials describe AI collaboration for software projects. Teams should check which products are currently offered.

item.title: Steve AI
item.description:
Steve AI is a text-to-video tool aimed at people who need videos without filming. You paste a script, an article, or a prompt, and the platform creates a video with scenes, characters or stock footage, text, voiceover, and music, which you can edit. It offers animated styles and live-action style videos built from stock clips.

It supports many typical use cases. Marketers create explainers and promos, educators make lesson videos, and social media managers turn blog posts into short clips. Options include different aspect ratios, branding, and a library of characters and backgrounds. Voiceover and avatar features add narration in various languages.

item.title: Stitch Fix
item.description:
Stitch Fix popularized personal styling by mail. A client fills out a style profile, and a stylist assisted by algorithms selects pieces, ships them in a box, and the client keeps what they like and returns the rest. Feedback improves later selections.

Data science is central to the company. Algorithms analyze preferences, item attributes, and inventory to predict what each customer will like, while stylists add judgment. Generative AI tools support outfit suggestions and visual try-on, and customers can also shop directly.

item.title: StockImg AI
item.description:
StockImg AI turns a description into a usable image. Instead of searching a stock library for something close to what you imagine, you type what you want and the tool creates it. It offers separate generators geared to common needs: logo designs, ebook and book covers, posters, wallpapers, illustrations, and app screen mockups. Each has settings suited to its format, such as aspect ratios for covers and posters.

The tool also includes editing functions. You can adjust and regenerate images, remove backgrounds, and explore variations. Self-publishers, small businesses, bloggers, and social media managers use it to get covers and graphics without hiring a designer or paying for licenses. The output is meant to be unique to your prompt, which avoids the problem of the same stock photo showing up in many places.

item.title: StudySmarter
item.description:
StudySmarter helps students prepare for exams. You upload lecture notes, a PDF, or a textbook chapter, and the app generates flashcards and summaries from the content. Quizzes test what you have learned, spaced repetition schedules reviews, and a study planner breaks your exam preparation into manageable sessions. A large library of shared flashcards and notes from other students covers school and university subjects.

AI features act as a study partner. An assistant can explain concepts, answer questions, and generate practice problems, and the app can create mind maps and summaries from uploaded materials. Progress tracking shows what you know and what needs more review. The app was founded in Germany and is used in many countries, with content aligned to various curricula.

item.title: SubtitleBee
item.description:
SubtitleBee automates subtitles. You upload a video, choose the spoken language, and the tool transcribes it and creates timed captions, which you can edit in a simple editor. It supports many languages and can translate subtitles into others, helping creators reach international audiences. Typical users are YouTubers, social media managers, educators, and marketers, who need captions because many viewers watch with the sound off.

Style options let captions fit a brand: you can change fonts, colors, positions, and highlight words as they are spoken, which is a popular look on short-form video. Subtitles can be exported as files for use in other editors or burned into the video itself. Plans are tied to the amount of video processed, and the product is in a crowded category.

item.title: Suki AI
item.description:
Suki reduces the paperwork burden on doctors. With patient consent, its ambient system listens to the visit, converts the conversation into a structured clinical note in the specialty’s format, and places it in the electronic health record for review. Clinicians can also dictate or use voice commands to look up information, queue orders, and complete tasks hands-free.

The assistant extends beyond notes. It suggests billing codes based on the documentation, helps with information retrieval from the chart, and supports different specialties with tailored templates. Integration with major record systems is a priority, since adoption depends on fitting into existing workflows. Healthcare organizations use it to reduce time spent on documentation and clinician burnout.

item.title: Sunsama
item.description:
Sunsama is built around the idea that planning your day deliberately reduces overwhelm. Each morning, a guided ritual walks you through gathering tasks from different sources, choosing what you can realistically do, estimating the time each will take, and placing them on your calendar. The app shows your total planned hours against the day’s available time, which discourages overcommitting.

It connects to many other tools. Tasks from project managers, issue trackers, email, and Slack can be brought into your daily view without leaving Sunsama, and calendar events appear alongside them. An end-of-day shutdown ritual lets you review what you finished and move unfinished tasks forward. AI features help with suggestions for scheduling, summaries, and organizing tasks.

item.title: Supabase AI
item.description:
Supabase provides what an application needs behind the scenes. It gives developers a hosted Postgres database with auto-generated APIs, user authentication, file storage, real-time updates, and serverless edge functions, all manageable from a web dashboard. It’s often described as an open-source alternative to Firebase, with the advantage of using standard SQL and a portable database.

For AI, Supabase supports the pgvector extension, which stores embeddings in Postgres and enables similarity search, so developers can build semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation without a separate vector database. Edge functions can call language models, and an AI assistant in the dashboard helps write SQL and design schemas. It has become a popular backend for AI app builders such as Lovable and Bolt.

item.title: Superhuman
item.description:
Superhuman became known as the fastest email client. It’s designed so you can process your inbox with the keyboard, using commands for archiving, replying, snoozing, and reminders, and everything loads instantly. The interface is minimal, with Split Inbox sections that separate important mail from newsletters and notifications. Features such as send later, follow-up reminders, read statuses, and a command palette are built into the workflow.

AI is now part of the experience. It drafts replies in your voice, summarizes long threads, searches your mail in plain language, and can write emails from short prompts. The company that owns Superhuman acquired it, changed its own name to Superhuman, and groups it with Grammarly’s writing assistant and the Coda workspace in a combined suite.

item.title: Supermaven
item.description: Supermaven was a coding assistant that focused on one thing: fast, accurate autocomplete. Its main claim was an unusually large context window, which let it consider much more of your project than most completion tools when suggesting the next lines. Developers liked how quickly suggestions appeared, and extensions for VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and Neovim made it easy to try. A free tier and a low-priced paid plan helped it spread.

item.title: Supernormal
item.description:
Supernormal aims to make meeting notes require no effort. A bot joins your scheduled meetings, records and transcribes them, and creates notes organized by templates for different types of meetings, such as sales calls, interviews, one-on-ones, and standups. The notes list decisions, action items, and key points, and are shared with attendees or saved to the tools your team uses.

The product works across platforms, including Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams, and also supports in-person meetings. Integrations push notes to Slack, Notion, HubSpot, Salesforce, and Google Docs. Search and chat features let you look back at past meetings and ask questions, and customization options allow you to adjust the format of the notes.

item.title: Surfer SEO
item.description: Surfer helps writers create content that matches what already ranks. You enter a keyword and it analyzes the top search results, then suggests the terms, headings, length, and structure those pages share. As you write in its editor, a content score updates, giving a quick sense of how well your page covers the topic. Writers and SEO teams use it to guide drafts and to update old posts that have dropped in rankings.

item.title: Swimm
item.description:
Swimm tackles documentation that rots. Developers write docs that reference specific code, and Swimm tracks those references. When the code changes, it detects the affected docs and either updates them automatically or alerts the owner.

AI helps generate documentation from code and answer questions about a codebase, which helps new hires learn a system. Integrations with IDEs and code hosts put docs where developers work. Large teams with legacy systems are the main audience.

item.title: Synthesia
item.description:
Synthesia produces videos with digital presenters. Users select from a library of avatars or create a custom one, paste a script, choose a voice and language, and receive a finished video. The editor handles slides, text, and media.

Companies use it for training, onboarding, product explainers, and communications, often replacing costly shoots. Translations let one video serve many markets. Recent features add interactive videos, screen recording, and avatars with more expressive delivery.

item.title: Synthesia
item.description:
Synthesia lets companies produce videos without cameras, studios, or actors. A user writes or pastes a script, selects an AI avatar from a library of presenters or creates a custom one, and the platform generates a video with natural speech and lip movement. Scenes, slides, screen recordings, and media can be combined, and editing the script and regenerating takes the place of a reshoot.

The platform is built for business use. It supports a large number of languages, so one video can be localized quickly, and offers templates, brand kits, and collaboration features. Interactive and agent-style avatars can respond to viewers, and an API lets teams automate video creation. Enterprise features cover security, compliance, and consent controls, since custom avatars require permission from the person depicted. Companies commonly use it for learning and development, onboarding, product explainers, and sales content.

item.title: Tableau
item.description:
Tableau is known for making data exploration feel visual and quick. Analysts connect to databases, spreadsheets, and cloud data warehouses, then drag fields onto a canvas to build charts, maps, and dashboards without writing code. It handles large data volumes well, and its interactivity lets viewers filter, drill down, and compare in ways static reports cannot. It is widely used in finance, healthcare, retail, government, and education.

Salesforce owns Tableau and has built AI into it. Tableau Pulse sends personalized, plain-language insights about key metrics to the people who care about them, and flags unusual changes without anyone opening a dashboard. Tableau Agent helps users build visualizations and analyze data by chatting with the tool. Tableau Prep cleans and combines data, and the platform integrates with Salesforce data and its Data Cloud.

item.title: Tabnine
item.description:
Tabnine was one of the earliest AI code completion tools, and it built its identity on privacy and control. It works inside VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and other editors, suggesting lines and functions, answering questions in chat, writing tests and documentation, and explaining code. A distinguishing choice was letting companies run it in their own environment, including fully disconnected networks, and keeping code out of any third party’s training.

Its enterprise pitch centers on context. Tabnine can learn from a company’s repositories, style guides, and standards so suggestions match internal conventions, and administrators can choose which models are used, including options hosted in-house. It offers attribution and provenance controls for companies worried about generated code resembling open-source projects with restrictive licenses. Agents extend it to larger tasks such as code review and test generation.

item.title: Tactiq
item.description:
Tactiq takes a lightweight approach to meeting notes. Instead of sending a recording bot into the call, it runs as a browser extension that captures the meeting’s captions and audio on your device. A live transcript appears in a sidebar as people speak, and you can highlight key moments as the meeting happens. That makes it less intrusive in calls where an unfamiliar bot would raise eyebrows.

After the meeting, AI features produce summaries, action items, and custom outputs from prompts, such as a follow-up email or a status update. The transcript is saved in your account and can be exported to tools like Notion, Google Docs, Slack, and HubSpot. Templates adapt the output for different meeting types, and a search function finds past conversations.

item.title: Talkdesk
item.description:
Talkdesk provides the software contact centers use to handle calls and messages. Customers reach an agent by phone, chat, or messaging, and the platform routes them, records interactions, and reports on performance. Cloud delivery makes setup quicker than legacy systems.

AI is part of each layer. Virtual agents resolve common requests, agent assist suggests replies and surfaces knowledge during calls, quality tools score conversations automatically, and forecasting helps schedule staff. Industry versions serve healthcare, financial services, and retail.

item.title: Tana
item.description:
Tana combines outlining with databases. Everything is a node in an outline, and tagging a node with a Supertag gives it fields and behavior, so a note about a person, a book, or a project becomes structured and can be queried and viewed in many ways. Backlinks connect related ideas.

AI is integrated into the workflow. It can transcribe meetings and turn them into tagged notes, fill in fields, and answer questions across a workspace, and it can act on commands users define. Voice capture makes it easy to record ideas on the go.

item.title: Taskade
item.description:
Taskade merges project management and AI. A project can be viewed as a list, board, calendar, table, or mind map, and everything can be edited collaboratively in real time. Chat and video calls are built into the workspace so a team can discuss and track tasks in one place. It is flexible enough for personal to-do lists, team projects, wikis, and meeting notes.

AI agents are central. Users can create agents with specific roles and knowledge, such as a research assistant, a project manager, or a support bot, and let them generate content, break down projects, and respond to questions. Automations connect actions across tools and trigger agents on schedules or events, and templates cover common uses like content planning and sales processes. You can also generate whole projects from a prompt.

item.title: Tempus AI
item.description:
Tempus builds a bridge between lab results and clinical decisions. It sequences tumors and other samples, combines the results with clinical data, and provides physicians with reports to help guide treatment choices, such as matching patients to targeted therapies or clinical trials. Over time, the company has assembled a large library of linked clinical and molecular data.

That data supports a second business: working with pharmaceutical companies. Tempus licenses de-identified data and builds models to help discover and develop drugs, find suitable patients for trials, and analyze outcomes. It has expanded through acquisitions into digital pathology with Paige and into radiology with the former Arterys platform, aiming to combine images, genomics, and clinical records into foundation models.

item.title: Textio
item.description:
Textio focuses on how words affect people at work.
