Its model, trained on large amounts of text paired with outcomes like application rates, flags language in a job posting that may discourage certain candidates, such as gendered phrases or jargon, and suggests alternatives that attract a broader and larger pool. Recruiters get a score and specific edits as they write.

The platform extends to employee communications. Textio helps managers write clearer, fairer performance reviews and feedback by spotting vague, biased, or unhelpful phrases, and supports recruiting emails and other HR writing. Generative AI features help draft job posts and feedback from a few inputs while applying the same guidance. Integrations work within applicant tracking systems and email tools.

item.title: The Yes
item.description:
The Yes used a swipe-based onboarding to learn a shopper’s taste in fashion and then curated a feed of products from many brands. Its algorithm tried to act like a personal stylist, adjusting to what a user liked and avoiding what they skipped.

Founded by a former Stitch Fix executive, the company was acquired by Pinterest, which folded the team and its taste-based personalization ideas into Pinterest’s shopping features. The standalone app and site were closed.

item.title: ThoughtSpot
item.description:
ThoughtSpot built its product around search. Instead of building reports by dragging fields, business users type a question such as sales by region last quarter, and ThoughtSpot generates the right chart from the connected data warehouse, with the ability to drill down and refine. This lowers the barrier for people who are not analysts and reduces the queue of requests for data teams.

Generative AI has expanded the approach. Spotter acts as an AI analyst that understands questions in conversation, runs analyses, explains results, and proposes follow-up questions, while agents can answer questions inside other tools. Liveboards combine charts into shareable dashboards that update from live data, and an embedded analytics offering lets companies put these capabilities in their own products.

item.title: Tipalti
item.description:
Tipalti automates accounts payable for growing companies. Suppliers and partners onboard through a portal that collects tax forms and payment details, invoices are captured and approved, and Tipalti pays them in the local currency and method across many countries.

Compliance is a main benefit: the platform handles tax documentation, sanctions screening, and reporting, which is hard for companies paying people worldwide. AI reads invoices, flags anomalies, and helps reconcile payments in accounting systems.

item.title: tl;dv
item.description:
tl;dv, short for “too long; didn’t view,” saves people from rewatching meetings. A bot joins your calls to record and transcribe them in many languages, and you can mark highlights during the call. Afterward, the recording is available with an AI-generated summary and a list of action items, plus timestamps so you can jump to the part that matters. Clips can be shared with people who missed the meeting.

The tool is popular with sales and product teams. It can fill in CRM fields in tools like HubSpot and Salesforce, produce reports across many meetings to spot patterns such as customer objections, and send notes to Slack and Notion. Templates tailor summaries to sales calls, user interviews, and team meetings, and search lets you find topics across your library.

item.title: Toast
item.description:
Toast serves the restaurant industry. Servers take orders on handheld devices, kitchen displays route tickets, guests pay at the table or online, and managers track sales, labor, and inventory. Online ordering, delivery integrations, and loyalty programs are part of the ecosystem.

Data and AI support operations. Sales forecasts help schedule staff, menu analytics show what sells, and assistants help write menu descriptions and answer business questions. Payroll and team management tools extend the suite.

item.title: Todoist
item.description: Todoist is a clean, fast task manager. You add tasks by typing in plain language, like “send report every Friday at 3pm,” and it turns that into a recurring due date. Tasks can be organized into projects and sections, given priorities and labels, and viewed as a list, board, or calendar. Filters let you build views such as everything due today across all projects. It syncs across phones, computers, browsers, and email clients.

item.title: Together AI
item.description:
Together AI focuses on open models. Developers call popular open-weight models for text, code, images, and more through an OpenAI-compatible API, and the platform’s optimized inference stack delivers speed and competitive prices. It includes serverless endpoints for quick use, dedicated endpoints for steady workloads, and batch processing to reduce cost.

The company also supports customization and training. Teams can fine-tune models on their data, including with reinforcement methods, and rent GPU clusters for large training runs, with an emphasis on cutting-edge hardware. Together’s researchers have contributed techniques such as FlashAttention that improve model efficiency, which feeds into its products.

item.title: Together AI
item.description:
Together AI hosts open models such as Llama, Qwen, and DeepSeek, and offers a developer-friendly API compatible with common formats. Its inference stack is tuned for speed, and options range from pay-per-token serverless access to dedicated endpoints for steady workloads.

Customization is a second focus. Teams can fine-tune models on their data, train at scale on GPU clusters, and run batch jobs at lower cost. The company’s research contributions in efficient attention and inference feed into its products.

item.title: Tome
item.description:
Tome became a popular early example of generative AI for presentations. A user described a topic, and Tome produced a complete, designed narrative with text, images, and layout, which could be edited in a flexible, canvas-like format. It was positioned as a more modern, storytelling-focused alternative to PowerPoint, and gained millions of users, with attention from students, founders, and professionals.

The company later decided to retire the presentation product and pivot to something different, a sales-focused application. Users were given a period to export their work before the service closed. The pivot reflected a challenge facing many AI tools: general features are quickly matched by larger products, and a standalone app needs a defensible niche.

item.title: Topaz Photo AI
item.description:
Topaz Photo AI aims to fix the technical flaws in photos with little effort. When you open an image, it analyzes the content and suggests corrections, using models for noise reduction, sharpening, and increasing resolution. It handles problems like grainy high-ISO shots, soft focus, and motion blur, and can enlarge photos while adding believable detail. Many wildlife, sports, and event photographers use it to rescue difficult images.

The tool also offers face recovery, light adjustment, color balance, and a way to apply different adjustments to selected subjects. It can be run as a standalone application, as an external editor from Lightroom, or as a plugin for Photoshop, and processes batches of images. Models run locally on your computer and benefit from a good graphics card.

item.title: Topaz Video AI
item.description:
Topaz Video AI improves footage after it has been shot. Its models upscale low-resolution video to HD or 4K, remove noise and compression artifacts, and sharpen soft footage. Frame interpolation creates additional frames to make slow motion smoother or convert a low frame rate to a higher one, and stabilization steadies shaky shots. Archivists restoring old film and videographers rescuing difficult footage use it often.

Different models are tuned for different problems, such as live action, animation, or low-quality sources. Newer diffusion-based models aim for higher-quality enhancement of detail, at the cost of heavy processing. The app lets you preview results on short clips before processing a whole video, supports batch processing and command-line use, and exports to common formats, with some cloud options for heavy models.

item.title: Tray.io
item.description:
Tray.io builds on the idea of integration-platform-as-a-service. Teams use a visual builder to create workflows that connect SaaS applications, databases, and internal systems, with powerful logic, error handling, and the ability to write code where necessary. Hundreds of connectors and a universal connector for APIs cover common enterprise tools such as Salesforce, Workday, and Slack.

The company has moved toward AI agents. Its Merlin AI tools let teams build agents that use the connected systems as tools, so an agent can look up a customer, update a record, and send a message, with governance over what it can access. Embedded integration products let software companies offer customer-facing integrations in their own products.

item.title: Turnitin
item.description:
Turnitin compares student submissions against a large database of papers, publications, and web content, producing a similarity report for instructors. It integrates with systems such as Canvas, Blackboard, and Moodle, so checking fits into grading.

An AI writing indicator estimates how much of a submission may be AI generated. AI detection is imperfect: false positives and negatives occur, and results are best used as a prompt for conversation, not proof. Feedback and grading tools add other functions.

item.title: Udemy
item.description:
Udemy opened online teaching to anyone. Instructors create video courses on a huge range of topics, from Python programming and UX design to photography and personal finance, and learners buy them individually, often at steep discounts. Courses can be watched at your own pace for life, and ratings and reviews help buyers choose. Quality varies widely, as there is little gatekeeping.

For companies, Udemy Business provides a curated library of courses with analytics and learning paths, which many organizations use for employee training. AI features include assistants that answer questions about course content, recommend lessons, and help instructors build courses, and role-play practice tools for skills training. Udemy has emphasized AI and technology skills, which are among its most popular categories.

item.title: UiPath
item.description:
UiPath popularized robotic process automation, in which software robots mimic what a person does on a screen. Developers build automations in a studio by recording and arranging steps such as clicking, copying data between systems, and filling forms, and run them on servers or desktops. This is valuable for companies with legacy systems that lack APIs, since bots can work through the same interfaces people use.

The platform has expanded into AI. Document understanding extracts data from invoices and forms, process mining reveals which workflows are worth automating, and agent tools let AI agents plan and carry out tasks, orchestrated alongside robots and people. The Maestro orchestration layer coordinates agents, robots, and human steps, and governance features control access and auditing.

item.title: Unbounce AI
item.description:
Unbounce helps marketers create landing pages that convert. A drag-and-drop builder and templates make it possible to publish pages without developers, with popups and sticky bars to capture leads on websites. Marketers connect pages to ad campaigns and test variants to find what performs best.

AI is a core part. Smart Copy generates headlines and body text from a brief, and Smart Traffic uses machine learning to send each visitor to the variant they are most likely to convert on, based on their attributes, which can improve results faster than a standard A/B test. Newer tools analyze pages and suggest improvements, and AI builder features create a page from a prompt.

item.title: Undermind
item.description: Undermind is designed for the situation where a simple search leaves you wondering what you missed. You describe your research question in plain language, including constraints and nuance, and the agent runs a deep search: it queries multiple sources, reads abstracts and text, follows citations, and refines its search based on what it finds. After some minutes, it delivers a ranked list of relevant papers with explanations of why each matches.

item.title: Upscayl
item.description: Upscayl makes AI upscaling available to anyone. You drag in a low-resolution image, choose a model, and the app enlarges it by two, three, or four times with added detail, saving the result to your computer. It includes models tuned for general photos, digital art, and sharpening, and supports batch processing for many files. Because it runs on your own hardware, there is no per-image fee, and your images stay private.

item.title: Vapi
item.description:
Vapi handles the hard parts of voice agents. Developers define an assistant with a prompt and tools, connect a phone number, and Vapi orchestrates speech-to-text, the language model, and text-to-speech, with handling for interruptions and turn-taking. Bring-your-own provider choices allow swapping components.

Use cases include customer support lines, appointment scheduling, outbound calls, and voice assistants in apps. The platform includes testing, analytics, and call transfer features.

Vapi is billed by minutes plus provider costs. Voice calls are regulated, and callers should know they are speaking with an AI. Alternatives include Retell AI, Bland AI, Synthflow, Twilio ConversationRelay, and LiveKit. Vapi suits developers building voice agents.

item.title: Vast.ai
item.description:
Vast.ai connects people who need GPU compute with those who have spare capacity. Hosts, from individuals with gaming rigs to data centers, list machines with details and prices, and users search by GPU type, memory, location, and reliability, then launch containers on them. The competition among hosts keeps prices lower than on-demand rates from large cloud providers.

The platform provides tools for launching Docker-based environments, Jupyter notebooks, and templates for popular AI frameworks, and offers interruptible instances at deeper discounts as well as on-demand options. A range of GPUs is available, from consumer cards to data center models, which suits experimentation, rendering, fine-tuning, and inference for budget-conscious teams.

item.title: Vectorizer.ai
item.description:
Vectorizer.ai converts bitmap images into vectors, which are scalable files used for logos, print, and cutting machines. Upload a low-resolution logo or illustration, and the service traces the shapes into paths and fills, returning an SVG, EPS, PDF, or DXF that can be resized without losing sharpness. The AI approach produces cleaner curves and fewer stray points than older tracing tools, with controls to adjust the level of detail.

Designers use it to recover logos from low-quality files, sign makers and crafters use it to prepare artwork for vinyl cutters and laser engravers, and developers add it to workflows through an API. It handles flat-color artwork best, such as logos and icons, and it works less well on photographs, which turn into complex tracings with many shapes. A preview lets you see the result before paying.

item.title: VEED.io
item.description:
VEED is an online video editor that makes common edits simple. You upload clips, trim and arrange them on a timeline, add text, music, and effects, and export in formats for different platforms. It includes a screen and webcam recorder for tutorials and messages, templates for social videos, and stock media. Everything runs in the browser, which allows collaboration without installing software.

AI features are a big part of the draw. Auto subtitles transcribe and style captions in many languages, background removal and noise cleanup polish footage, eye contact correction makes you appear to look at the camera, and AI avatars and voices generate presenter videos from scripts. Tools for translation and dubbing help reach other markets, and an assistant can clean up speech by removing filler words and silences.

item.title: Venice AI
item.description: Venice AI builds its pitch around privacy and freedom of use. The company states it does not log or store conversations on its servers, and that chats are kept in the user’s browser, which appeals to people uneasy about their prompts being retained or used for training. It runs open-source models, so users can pick from several language models and an image generator, and the platform applies fewer content restrictions than many mainstream services.

item.title: Venngage
item.description:
Venngage targets people who need to communicate information visually. Users start from thousands of templates for infographics, reports, flyers, presentations, and social graphics, replace the content, and customize colors, icons, and charts. Data can be imported to generate charts, and the tool includes maps and diagrams for explaining processes and comparisons.

It differentiates itself with business features. Brand kits apply logos, fonts, and colors automatically, team workspaces allow collaboration and approvals, and an accessibility checker flags color contrast and other issues. AI tools generate infographic designs from text, write copy, and suggest improvements, and designs can be exported or shared with analytics.

item.title: Vercel AI
item.description:
Vercel makes deploying web applications simple. Developers connect a repository, and every push builds and deploys to a global network, with preview URLs for each change. It is the home of Next.js and used by many teams for sites and apps.

For AI, Vercel provides the AI SDK, which standardizes streaming, tool calling, and structured output across model providers, plus an AI Gateway for routing requests and tracking cost. Its v0 tool generates interfaces from prompts, and agents and sandboxes support more advanced workflows.

item.title: Vertex AI
item.description: Vertex AI is where Google Cloud customers build with AI. At its center is Model Garden, a catalog that includes Google’s Gemini, Imagen, and Veo models, open models like Llama and Gemma, and models from partners such as Anthropic. You can call a model through an API, test it in a studio, and then deploy it with Google Cloud’s security, networking, and compliance controls. Data stays under the customer’s governance, which matters for regulated industries.

item.title: Vidyo.ai
item.description:
Vidyo.ai set out to save creators the time of cutting short clips from podcasts, webinars, and long videos. You upload a video or paste a link, and the AI analyzes the content to find segments that could stand alone, then produces clips with captions and a vertical layout. You can edit the transcript, adjust the clip boundaries, and customize caption styles before exporting.

The company has rebranded to quso.ai, expanding from a clipping tool into a broader social content platform. It now includes features for scheduling posts across social networks, analytics on performance, and AI helpers for creating captions and ideas. Accounts and plans carried over from Vidyo.ai, and the core clipping features continue.

item.title: Visily
item.description:
Visily is built for people who need to mock up interfaces quickly without learning a full design tool. You can upload a screenshot of an app, a hand-drawn sketch, or a description of a screen, and the AI creates an editable wireframe made of real components. A library of templates, UI kits, and smart components helps assemble screens for web and mobile products.

Collaboration is part of the appeal. Teams can edit together, leave comments, and share clickable prototypes with stakeholders, and designs can be exported or moved into Figma for refinement. Product managers, business analysts, and founders use it to communicate ideas visually and gather feedback early, before engineering work starts.

item.title: Visme AI
item.description:
Visme is aimed at people who need to present information visually without design skills. It offers a drag-and-drop editor with thousands of templates for presentations, infographics, reports, charts, social media posts, and documents. Data widgets create charts and graphs from spreadsheets, and interactive elements such as links and animations can be added. Brand kits keep colors, fonts, and logos consistent across a team.

AI features speed up creation. An AI designer can generate a presentation or document from a prompt, write and rewrite text, create images, and suggest layouts. Teams can collaborate in real time with comments and workflows, and content can be exported as PDF, PowerPoint, or HTML, or shared by link with analytics. Visme is often used by marketers, educators, consultants, and communications teams.

item.title: Voicemod
item.description: Voicemod changes how you sound as you speak. You choose a voice effect, such as a robot, a deep voice, or a character, and the app processes your microphone audio in real time. It works as a virtual microphone, so apps like Discord, Zoom, OBS, and many games treat it like a normal mic. Gamers and streamers use it for fun and for roleplay, and some people use it for privacy.

item.title: Vue.ai
item.description:
Vue.ai is built for retailers with large catalogs. Computer vision reads product images and assigns attributes such as color, pattern, neckline, fabric, and occasion, which saves teams from tagging thousands of items by hand. Those tags feed search, filters, and merchandising, so shoppers find items that match what they want.

The same data drives the customer-facing side. Recommendation engines suggest items based on browsing and purchase behavior, visual search lets shoppers upload a photo to find similar products, and styling tools suggest outfits that go together. Merchandisers can also see how products perform and adjust collections and layouts.

item.title: Vyond
item.description:
Vyond focuses on business animation. Users build videos from libraries of characters, props, and backgrounds, choosing actions and expressions for each character and arranging scenes on a timeline. The style is a recognizable cartoon format popular in corporate training, compliance courses, and explainer videos, and the tool makes it possible to produce them without animation skills.

AI features reduce the work of getting started. A text-to-video capability generates a draft video from a script or prompt, including scenes, characters, and voiceover, which you can then edit. Other tools produce voices in many languages, help with translations, and match lip sync. Branded templates and shared libraries help teams keep their videos consistent, and enterprise features cover security and administration.

item.title: W&B Weave
item.description:
Weave addresses a common problem with LLM apps: it is hard to know what they are doing. Adding a few lines of code logs each call with its inputs, outputs, latency, cost, and the surrounding function calls, so a developer can inspect a failing response step by step instead of guessing. The traces cover nested calls, which matters for agents that chain several models and tools.

It also handles evaluation. Teams build datasets of test cases, define scorers (including LLM judges), and run experiments to compare prompts, models, and app versions before shipping. Results are tracked over time, which makes it easier to tell whether a change actually helped. Online evaluations can score live traffic and flag regressions in production.

item.title: Waifu2x
item.description: Waifu2x was one of the first widely used AI image upscalers. Created for anime and illustration, it uses convolutional neural networks to double the size of an image while reducing noise and compression artifacts. A free web demo made it easy to try, and downloadable versions let people run it locally, including ports that work on many graphics cards through Vulkan. It became a standard tool for enlarging fan art, wallpapers, and screenshots.

item.title: Warp
item.description:
Warp rethinks the command line interface. Each command and its output appear as a block that you can copy, share, search, or collapse, and the input behaves like a text editor with cursor movement, multiple cursors, and autocomplete. That makes the terminal friendlier to people who find traditional shells unforgiving, without removing the shell itself.

AI is built in. You can type a request in plain language and get the matching command, ask why an error happened, and hand longer tasks to an agent that plans steps, runs commands with your approval, and fixes problems as they come up. Warp Drive stores saved commands and workflows that teams can share, and the terminal also works with other coding agents running inside it.

item.title: Watershed
item.description:
Watershed focuses on carbon accounting for large companies. Organizations connect data from finance systems, energy bills, travel, and suppliers, and the platform converts that activity data into greenhouse gas emissions across all scopes, including the harder-to-measure supply chain. The methods follow recognized standards and are designed to stand up to audits, which matters as more companies face disclosure rules.

Beyond measurement, the platform supports action. Companies set targets, model reduction scenarios, and track progress, and tools for engaging suppliers help gather better data and cut emissions in the value chain. Reporting features produce disclosures for frameworks and regulations, and AI helps classify purchases, fill gaps in data, and prepare reports, which reduces the manual effort that carbon accounting requires.

item.title: Wave.video
item.description:
Wave.video bundles several tools that marketers often use separately. The editor handles videos from templates, with stock footage, music, and text animations for social posts, ads, and promos. A recorder captures your screen or webcam, a live streaming studio broadcasts to multiple platforms, and a hosting service stores and embeds videos with customizable players and calls to action.

AI features help produce videos faster. Tools convert text or a blog post into a video draft, generate captions and subtitles, resize videos for different social formats, and create voiceovers. Brand kits keep colors and logos consistent, and integrations link with email platforms and social networks. It’s targeted at small businesses, agencies, and content teams.

item.title: Weather.ai
item.description:
Weather.ai positions itself as a forecast service built on machine learning rather than only traditional physics models. It aims to give hourly and daily forecasts for specific locations, which is the kind of hyperlocal output people want for planning a run, a trip, or an event. The site focuses on readable forecasts, and an API is available for developers.

Machine learning is now common in weather prediction. Large research efforts from Google DeepMind, NVIDIA, and others have shown that models trained on decades of observations can produce competitive forecasts quickly, and many startups sell tailored predictions built on this work. Services in this space usually combine public data from national weather agencies with their own models and corrections.

item.title: WeatherBug
item.description:
WeatherBug built its name on a dense network of weather stations, often at schools and other local sites. That gives it temperature, wind, and rain readings from places closer to you than a distant airport sensor, which helps when conditions change quickly, such as during a storm. The app combines that observation data with forecast models for hourly and multi-day outlooks.

Its mobile app is the main product. Users get radar maps, lightning detection, and alerts for severe weather and rainfall, along with air quality and pollen information in some regions. A subscription removes ads and unlocks extra features, and some of the forecasting uses machine learning to adjust model output for local conditions.

item.title: Webflow
item.description:
Webflow sits between simple site builders and hand-coded sites. Designers work on a canvas that mirrors how the web works, setting classes, flexbox and grid layouts, and breakpoints, and the platform produces production code and hosts the result. That gives far more control than template-based builders, which is why agencies and in-house design teams like it.

The platform includes a CMS for blogs and collections, e-commerce, interactions and animations, localization, and tools for marketers to edit content without breaking the design. AI features generate sections and copy, suggest changes, and help with site structure and SEO. Developers can add custom code and use an API to connect Webflow to other services.

item.title: WellSaid Labs
item.description:
WellSaid focuses on voiceovers for businesses. In its web studio, you type or paste a script, pick a voice, and generate narration with control over pacing, pronunciation, and emphasis. The voices are built from recordings by professional voice actors who agreed to the use, which gives companies a clear license position. Typical projects include training courses, explainer videos, product tours, corporate announcements, and audio for apps.

For larger teams, collaboration and control matter. Projects can be shared, commented on, and reviewed, and custom pronunciation settings keep brand names and technical terms consistent across a library of content. An API lets developers add speech to their own products, and integrations connect WellSaid to e-learning and creative tools. Enterprise plans emphasize security, privacy, and compliance, and custom voices can be created for a brand.

item.title: Whimsical AI
item.description:
Whimsical puts several lightweight visual tools in one place. You can draw flowcharts and sequence diagrams, sketch low-fidelity wireframes, brainstorm on mind maps, write docs, and arrange sticky notes on a board. The tools are designed around speed, with keyboard shortcuts, snapping, and a clean look that makes rough thinking easy to share.

AI features reduce the setup. Describe a process and Whimsical can draft a flowchart, turn a topic into a mind map, or produce a first-pass wireframe, which you then edit by hand. Teams use it for planning, product specs, and explaining systems, and sharing is simple with links, comments, and embeds in tools like Notion and Confluence.

item.title: Whisk
item.description:
Whisk started as an independent app for collecting recipes. You could save dishes from any food site into one library, group them into collections, plan meals for the week, and turn the ingredients into a shopping list that could be sent to grocery delivery services. A browser extension made saving a recipe a single click.

Samsung bought the company and renamed the app Samsung Food, and the whisk.com address now leads to the new brand. The app keeps the same core features and adds AI help, such as adjusting a recipe to dietary needs, suggesting meals from what you have, and generating plans. It also connects with Samsung’s smart appliances, though it works without them on phones and the web.

item.title: Wix ADI
item.description:
Wix ADI, short for Artificial Design Intelligence, was an early attempt at automatic site building. A user answered questions about their business and style, and ADI generated a layout with text, images, and a structure suited to the industry. It let people with no design skills get a website online in minutes, long before generative AI was common.

ADI sites had limits. They used a simpler editor than the main Wix Editor, which made it hard to customize them or to add advanced features. Wix has since retired the product: ADI sites are no longer supported and existing ones were moved into the standard Wix Editor, so owners can keep editing them there.

item.title: Wolfram Alpha AI
item.description: Wolfram Alpha doesn’t search the web. It computes answers. Ask it to integrate a function, convert units, compare populations, or show the weather on a given date, and it uses curated data and algorithms, written in the Wolfram Language, to produce a result with steps, charts, and data. That makes it reliable for math, physics, chemistry, statistics, and factual queries with definite answers, which is where language models often make mistakes.

item.title: WooCommerce
item.description:
WooCommerce is the most widely used way to run a store on WordPress. You install the plugin, add products, set up payments, shipping, and taxes, and manage orders from the WordPress dashboard. Because it is open source, you own the store and the data, host it where you want, and can modify anything with code or extensions.

The ecosystem is its strength. Thousands of themes and extensions add subscriptions, bookings, memberships, marketplaces, and connections to accounting and marketing tools. AI extensions can write product descriptions, suggest recommendations, and help with support, and Automattic’s own tools plus third-party plugins fill the gaps. Many agencies build custom stores on top of it.

item.title: WordAI
item.description:
WordAI is an article rewriter. You paste in text, and the tool produces a reworded version that keeps the meaning but changes the sentences and structure. It was one of the earlier products built around natural language processing for this job, as opposed to older spinners that swapped in synonyms and produced awkward results.

People use it to adapt copy for different audiences, create alternate product descriptions, or refresh older posts. Settings control how much it changes, and you can review and edit the output. It sits alongside the Spin Rewriter and Chimp Rewriter type tools, and now competes with general AI assistants that can rewrite on request.

item.title: Wordsmith
item.description:
Wordsmith turns data into text. Users define templates and logic, connect a data source, and the platform writes a narrative for each record, such as a financial summary, a sports recap, or a personalized report. The output is consistent and can be produced in volume.

It predates today’s chat models. Rule-based natural language generation gives predictable text, which suits regulated reporting where exact control matters, while large language models offer flexibility and fluency but less predictability.

item.title: Workato
item.description:
Workato is an integration and automation platform. Teams build recipes that link applications such as Salesforce, Workday, and Slack, trigger actions, and move data. Business users can create simple automations while IT governs the platform.

The company has added AI across the product. Users describe a workflow in plain language and Workato builds a draft, document understanding extracts data, and agents handle tasks with enterprise controls. Governance, security, and monitoring suit regulated companies.

item.title: Workday
item.description:
Workday began as cloud HR software and expanded into financials. Large employers use it to keep employee records, run payroll and benefits, manage recruiting and performance, plan headcount and budgets, and close the books. Having HR and finance on one data model helps companies tie workforce decisions to costs.

AI shows up across the suite. It suggests candidates and skills matches, flags attrition risks, helps managers with planning, and drafts job descriptions and summaries. Workday has also introduced AI agents that take on tasks inside its apps, along with an agent management layer so that companies can control what those agents may do. It has bought AI companies to extend this, including some that build agent platforms.

item.title: Writerly
item.description:
Writerly is aimed at teams that want AI-written content to sound like them. Instead of generating generic text, it lets users supply samples of their existing writing and style guidelines, then drafts articles, emails, and social posts that follow that voice. That approach is common among brand-focused writing tools, and matters most for companies with several writers.

Features reported in directories include templates for common content types, collaboration for editors and reviewers, and options to reuse past content. Teams often use this kind of tool to keep messaging consistent across channels and to speed up first drafts, with humans editing for accuracy and judgment.

item.title: Writesonic
item.description:
Writesonic started as a template-based copywriter and has widened into a content and marketing suite. Users pick a tool for blog articles, ad copy, product descriptions, emails, or social posts, give a brief, and get a draft. A long-form article writer can produce SEO-minded posts from a keyword with outlines and sources, and a chat assistant answers questions and drafts on demand.

Recent additions center on search visibility. Writesonic has tools to see how a brand is mentioned in AI answer engines such as ChatGPT and Perplexity, plus recommendations for improving content. It also offers brand voice settings, an editor with SEO scoring, and integrations with WordPress and other platforms.

item.title: Writesonic
item.description: Writesonic began as a template-driven AI writer for marketing copy. You choose a type of content, such as a blog post, ad, product description, or social caption, fill in some details, and get a draft. A longer-form article writer builds full posts with an outline, headings, and optional SEO guidance, and a chat assistant answers questions and can search the web. A browser extension and integrations with WordPress and other tools help get content published.

item.title: x.ai
item.description: x.ai took a distinctive approach to scheduling. Instead of an app or a booking link, you copied its assistant, Amy or Andrew, on an email thread, and it handled the back-and-forth of finding a time with the other people. It read your calendar, proposed times in natural language, replied to the guests, and sent calendar invitations. Because everything happened by email, the other person did not need to install or log in to anything.

item.title: Yelp
item.description:
Yelp built its business on reviews. Users write about their experiences with restaurants, home services, medical offices, and other local businesses, rate them, and upload photos. Search results combine ratings, distance, price, and filters such as open now or takeout, which helps people choose. In the United States, it is a major source for restaurant and service recommendations.

Businesses can claim their listing, add information, respond to reviews, and run ads, and some features support booking, waitlists, and requesting quotes from local professionals. AI has been added to the product: assistants help users find places through conversation, summaries condense long review histories, and tools detect and filter spam and fake reviews through a recommendation software that sorts reviews by reliability.

item.title: Yodlee
item.description:
Yodlee lets financial apps pull in customers’ account data. A budgeting tool, lender, or wealth platform can use Yodlee’s APIs to link to thousands of financial institutions, retrieve balances and transactions, and keep them updated. That saves each company from building separate connections to every bank.

Beyond raw data, Yodlee enriches transactions. Machine learning cleans merchant names, assigns categories, and flags patterns, and analytics products use aggregated data to describe consumer spending trends. Account verification and income checks help lenders confirm information, and the company supports open banking rules in regions where they exist.

item.title: Yotpo
item.description:
Yotpo helps online stores build trust and repeat business. It collects reviews with photos, shows them on product pages and in search, and runs loyalty programs and referral offers. SMS and email tools extend marketing.

AI summarizes reviews into themes, flags issues, and drafts responses, and analytics tie content to conversion. Integrations cover Shopify, BigCommerce, and other platforms.

Yotpo has a free tier and paid plans that scale with orders. Alternatives include Okendo, Judge.me, Stamped.io, Klaviyo, and Trustpilot. Yotpo suits growing online stores.

item.title: You.com
item.description:
You.com is a search engine that mixes web results with AI-generated answers. You ask a question and receive a conversational response with links to sources, along with traditional results and apps for tasks like coding or image creation. A privacy focus has been part of its positioning, with a private mode and a commitment to not selling personal data.

The product has moved toward agents and enterprise search. Research and agent modes run multi-step investigations and produce longer reports, a custom agent builder lets people create assistants for specific tasks, and the platform lets users switch among models from different providers. For developers and businesses, You.com offers APIs that deliver live web search results formatted for AI applications, which several AI companies use to ground their answers.

item.title: Yuka
item.description:
Yuka makes reading labels simpler. You scan the barcode of a food or personal care product with your phone, and the app returns a score with color coding and an explanation of what affects it. For food, the score considers nutritional quality, additives, and whether the product is organic. For cosmetics, it flags ingredients seen as risky.

The app is built to help shoppers choose. When a product scores poorly, Yuka suggests better alternatives in the same category, and you can keep a history of what you scanned. It does not accept advertising or payments from brands for ratings, and it funds itself through its premium subscription, which adds features like searching without a barcode and offline use.

item.title: Zapier
item.description:
Zapier lets people automate work between apps without programming. A Zap starts with a trigger, such as a new form entry, and performs actions in other apps, like adding a row to a spreadsheet and sending a Slack message. It connects thousands of products.

AI has become part of the platform. Users describe an automation in plain language, add AI steps that summarize or classify data, and build agents that act across apps. Tables, forms, and interfaces let teams build small apps around their automations.

item.title: Zapier
item.description:
Zapier handles the plumbing between business apps. A workflow listens for an event in one tool and does something in another, with filters, paths, and delays to model real processes. Templates cover common needs in sales, marketing, and operations.

Newer capabilities include AI actions that read and write text, agents that carry out multi-step tasks, and an MCP offering that exposes Zapier actions to AI assistants. Teams can monitor runs, handle errors, and manage access centrally.

item.title: Zapier
item.description: Zapier connects the apps a business already uses and lets them pass data to each other without code. You build a Zap with a trigger, such as a new form submission, and one or more actions, such as adding a row to a spreadsheet, posting in Slack, and creating a CRM contact. It supports thousands of apps, from Gmail and Salesforce to niche tools, which is the main reason people choose it over building integrations by hand. Filters, paths, and delays let a Zap branch and wait, and a multi-step workflow can handle surprisingly complicated processes.

item.title: Zed AI
item.description:
Zed is built for speed. Its editor, written in Rust, starts quickly and stays responsive on large projects, and multiplayer editing lets several people work in the same file with voice and chat.

AI is built in rather than added by extension. Users chat with models in an assistant panel, ask for inline edits, and run an agent that edits code across files, with support for several providers and local models. Edit predictions suggest the next change as you type, and the Agent Client Protocol lets other agents run inside.

item.title: Zendesk
item.description:
Zendesk is one of the most widely used help desk systems. Customer messages from email, web chat, phone, WhatsApp, and social media become tickets in a shared workspace, where they can be routed, prioritized, and tracked against service targets. A help center and community forum let customers find answers themselves, and reports show response times and satisfaction. It scales from small support teams to large contact centers.

The current product is built around AI. AI agents take on requests from start to finish, answering from help articles and past conversations, and taking actions in connected systems when allowed. A copilot assists human agents by suggesting replies, summarizing long threads, and flagging urgent or unhappy customers. The platform has added contact center, workforce management, and quality assurance tools, and an employee service product that applies the same ideas to internal IT and HR requests.

item.title: Zeni
item.description:
Zeni provides outsourced finance for startups. Companies connect their bank accounts, and Zeni handles bookkeeping, accounts payable, tax, and CFO services, with a dashboard showing cash, burn, and runway in real time. Humans check the AI’s work.

The service replaces a part-time accountant or finance hire for early-stage companies. Monthly reports help founders and investors understand the business.

Zeni is a subscription service. Alternatives include Pilot, Bench, Puzzle, Digits, and a traditional accountant. Zeni suits startups wanting outsourced finance.

item.title: Zest AI
item.description:
Zest AI helps lenders approve more borrowers safely. Its models use many variables to estimate credit risk, aiming to include people thin credit files would exclude while keeping losses in check. Lenders deploy the models in their own decisioning workflows.

Explainability is central, since regulators require lenders to give reasons for adverse decisions. Zest provides tools to explain scores and to test models for disparate impact across groups. Credit unions and community banks are among its customers.

item.title: Zety
item.description: Zety walks job seekers through making a resume. You choose a template, answer prompts about your experience and education, and see a preview that updates as you type. The builder suggests wording for job duties and skills, which is helpful if you struggle with the phrasing, and it formats everything cleanly for PDF or Word download. It also builds cover letters and offers a library of guides and examples for different industries.

item.title: Zillow
item.description:
Zillow is where many people begin looking for a home. Listings for sale and rent appear on maps and lists with photos, price history, taxes, and school details, and users can filter by price, size, and features, save searches, and get alerts when matching homes appear. Agents and landlords pay to advertise or manage listings.

Its signature feature is the Zestimate, an automated estimate of a home’s value based on public records, market data, and a machine learning model. It is useful as a rough guide but can be off for individual homes, and sellers should not treat it as an appraisal. Zillow also offers mortgage and agent referral services, rental tools, and an AI-powered search that accepts natural language descriptions.

item.title: ZipRecruiter
item.description:
ZipRecruiter works on both sides of hiring. An employer writes a job once, and ZipRecruiter posts it across a network of job boards and sends it to potential candidates through email and notifications. Job seekers create a profile or upload a resume, browse listings, set alerts, and apply with a click, and the platform recommends jobs based on their interests and activity.

Matching technology is central. The system learns from employer and candidate behavior to recommend candidates to employers and jobs to seekers, and employers can invite candidates to apply. Tools help screen applicants, schedule interviews, and communicate in one place. AI features assist with writing job descriptions and surfacing strong matches, and an employer dashboard tracks responses.

item.title: Zoho
item.description:
Zoho builds a wide range of business applications on its own platform. Companies can use Zoho CRM for sales, Books for accounting, Desk for support, Projects for work tracking, Mail for email, People for HR, and dozens of other apps, many of which integrate with one another. Zoho One bundles the whole suite for a single per-user price.

Zia is the AI layer. It predicts which leads are likely to convert, detects anomalies in data, drafts replies, and answers questions in natural language, and Zoho has added a generative assistant and agents that can act across apps. The company also supports the option of running models on its own infrastructure for customers who want data kept in their region.

item.title: Zoho CRM
item.description:
Zoho CRM covers the normal work of sales: tracking leads and contacts, managing deals through a pipeline, logging calls and emails, and forecasting revenue. It supports multiple channels, including phone, email, live chat, and social media, and lets you build custom modules and fields so it can reflect how a business actually sells. Workflow rules, assignment rules, and blueprints enforce a consistent sales process without manual follow-up.

Zia is the AI layer. It scores leads by how likely they are to convert, predicts which deals will close, spots unusual activity, and recommends the best time to contact a prospect. It can answer questions in plain language, summarize records, and help draft emails. Because Zoho builds its own models, it positions this as a cost-effective alternative to enterprise AI add-ons. Integrations connect with Zoho’s other products such as Campaigns, Books, and Desk, and with outside tools through a marketplace.

item.title: ZoomInfo
item.description:
ZoomInfo provides one of the largest databases of business contacts and companies. Sales and marketing teams search by title, industry, company size, location, and technology to build lists, and see verified email addresses, direct phone numbers, org charts, and firmographic details. Intent data shows which companies are researching topics related to a product, helping teams reach out when interest is high.

The platform has expanded from data into a workflow product. It includes tools for sales engagement, marketing advertising, conversation intelligence through Chorus, and enrichment that keeps CRM records up to date automatically. AI features include assistants that research accounts, draft outreach, and recommend who to contact, and agents that handle prospecting tasks. It integrates with Salesforce, HubSpot, and other systems.

item.title: Zotero
item.description:
Zotero saves references with a click. A browser connector captures a paper or web page along with its citation details and PDF, and the library organizes items in collections with tags and notes. Word and Google Docs plugins insert citations in thousands of styles.

Group libraries support collaboration, and the open ecosystem has plugins for annotation, syncing, and AI summaries and search. Because it is community driven and non-profit, users keep control over data.

item.title: Zowie
item.description:
Zowie focuses on online retail support. Its AI agent connects to a store’s order system, answers questions about delivery and returns, processes simple actions, and hands off tricky cases to staff. It works across chat, email, and messaging channels.

The platform emphasizes decision-making that follows a brand’s policies, and gives support managers tools to review and adjust behavior. Analytics show resolution rates and topics.

Zowie is sold on subscription. Alternatives include Gorgias, Intercom Fin, Ada, Netomi, and Zendesk AI agents. Zowie suits e-commerce support teams.

item.title: Notion
item.description: Notion works as a set of building blocks. A team can create a company wiki, a project tracker with a board view, a product roadmap, a meeting notes database, and a documentation site, all in one workspace with permissions and comments. Databases are central: the same set of records can be viewed as a table, board, calendar, or timeline, and linked to other databases, which makes it possible to build custom systems without code.

item.title: 01.AI
item.description:
01.AI started with the goal of building leading large language models. Its Yi series, released with open weights, performed strongly on benchmarks for its size and supported long context and Chinese and English. Developers around the world downloaded and fine-tuned the models, and the company also offered an API and consumer products. Kai-Fu Lee, a well-known AI executive and investor, led the company.

The company’s strategy changed as the cost of competing at the frontier rose and powerful open models from other Chinese labs became available. It reduced its investment in pretraining its own large models and moved toward selling AI solutions to businesses, using other models where appropriate. Reports describe a focus on enterprise data infrastructure and a path toward a public listing.

item.title: ABBYY
item.description:
ABBYY has worked with optical character recognition for decades. Its FineReader software converts scanned pages and PDFs into editable text, and its enterprise products read invoices, contracts, IDs, and forms at scale. Machine learning classifies the type of document, locates key fields such as invoice totals and dates, and extracts the data in a structured form that other systems can use.

The platform has expanded into intelligent document processing. Pre-trained skills handle common document types without training, while companies can build custom models for their own forms. Validation tools route low-confidence results to human review, and integrations connect with robotic process automation, ERP, and content management systems. ABBYY has added generative AI features and tools for making documents ready for use by language models, as companies seek to feed documents into AI workflows.

item.title: ACE Studio
item.description: ACE Studio lets musicians create vocals without a singer. You enter a melody in a piano-roll editor along with lyrics, choose a voice model, and the software sings it, with controls for vibrato, breath, dynamics, and expression that make the performance sound human. It works as a standalone app or as a plugin inside digital audio workstations such as Ableton, Logic, and FL Studio. Songwriters use it for demos and finished tracks.

item.title: Aide
item.description: Aide was an AI-first code editor from the London startup CodeStory. It was a fork of VS Code, so it looked familiar and could use extensions, but it added a layer of AI that understood the project. You could chat about the codebase, ask for changes across several files, and get completions informed by wider context. It was released as open source under the AGPL license, and the project drew substantial interest from developers looking for an alternative to Cursor.

item.title: Aisera
item.description: Aisera provides AI agents for internal and external service desks. Employees can ask for help with IT issues, such as resetting a password or requesting software, or HR questions, such as time off policies, and the agent resolves the request by taking actions in connected systems instead of simply pointing to articles. For customers, similar agents handle support inquiries. The goal is to reduce the number of tickets that reach human staff.

item.title: Aleph Alpha
item.description: Aleph Alpha was Europe’s attempt to build a homegrown large language model company. Its Luminous models offered multilingual text generation and could handle images alongside text, with an emphasis on explainability, so users could see which parts of a source supported an answer. The company pitched itself to public sector agencies, banks, and industrial companies in Europe that wanted AI under their own control and in line with European regulation.

item.title: Alexa AI
item.description:
Alexa popularized the smart speaker. You speak to an Echo device to play music, set timers, control lights, check weather, shop on Amazon, and ask questions. Over the years, it grew into a platform with thousands of skills from third parties and support for a huge range of smart home devices. It’s built into many speakers, TVs, cars, and appliances.

Alexa+ is the next generation. Built on large language models, including Amazon’s own Nova and models from other providers, it holds more natural conversations, understands context across a dialogue, and can handle multi-step requests such as planning an evening, booking a reservation, or coordinating a family calendar. It can act across services, remember preferences, and work with smart home devices more flexibly, and a web and app experience complements the voice interface. Some promised features arrived later than first shown.

item.title: Alpha3D
item.description: Alpha3D addresses a bottleneck in 3D content: modeling each object by hand is slow and expensive. Instead, you upload a photo of a product or describe an object in text, and the platform generates a 3D model, typically within minutes. The models can be downloaded in common formats such as GLB for use in game engines, web viewers, and AR experiences. The company positions it for retail, gaming, and virtual try-on.

item.title: Animoto
item.description:
Animoto was built for people who need a video quickly and do not know editing software. A user uploads photos and video clips, picks a template and a song, and the tool arranges them into a polished video with text and transitions. A storyboard view lets you rearrange scenes and change styles.

It aims at small businesses, real estate agents, educators, and social media marketers. Templates fit common formats such as promos, slideshows, and testimonials, and brand tools apply logos and colors. Videos can be shared online or exported for ads and websites. Newer AI features speed up layout and text creation.

item.title: Arize AI
item.description:
Arize helps teams see what their models are doing after deployment. For classic machine learning, it tracks performance, detects when input data drifts away from training data, and helps identify which segments of users a model is failing. Alerts point teams to problems before they affect the business.

For LLM applications, it traces each request through the chain of prompts, retrieval, and tool calls, and runs evaluations that score responses for relevance, hallucination, and safety. This helps developers find why an answer was wrong and test fixes. Arize Phoenix, the company’s open-source tool, offers tracing and evaluation that can run locally.

item.title: Artisan AI
item.description:
Artisan describes its products as autonomous teammates rather than assistants. Ava, the AI BDR, works through the outbound sales process: building a list of prospects from a database, researching each, writing personalized messages, sending them, and handling follow-up. The company aims mainly at startups and small teams that cannot hire a full sales development group.

Ava connects to a company’s email, CRM, and calendar, and can book meetings that appear for human salespeople. The company also talks about expanding to other roles. Automation can increase outreach volume, but results depend on how well the target list and message match the market.

item.title: Ashby
item.description:
Ashby brings together tools that recruiting teams often buy separately. The core is an applicant tracking system for jobs, candidates, and interview plans. Around it sit scheduling that coordinates interviewers automatically, a CRM for sourcing and nurturing talent, and an analytics layer that shows pipeline health, time to hire, and source effectiveness.

AI features handle repetitive work, such as summarizing candidates, drafting outreach, and taking notes in interviews. Structured scorecards and interview plans promote consistent evaluation, and reporting is built into the product rather than added on, which analytics-minded recruiting teams like.

item.title: Attio
item.description:
Attio starts from the idea that every company sells differently. Instead of fixed objects like leads and opportunities, teams build their own structures, such as customers, partners, or investors, and link them. The interface feels more like a spreadsheet and a database than a traditional CRM, so it is easier to reshape.

Data fills in with little typing. Attio connects to email and calendar to log interactions, enriches company and contact details, and shows the strength of relationships. AI features summarize accounts, answer questions about the pipeline, and fill in fields from conversations. Workflow automation moves records, sends notifications, and updates data.

item.title: Augment Code
item.description:
Augment Code is built for teams with big, long-lived codebases. Its main idea is deep context: the tool indexes the repository and related documentation, so suggestions reflect the project’s own APIs, conventions, and architecture, not generic patterns. That reduces the made-up function calls common with less informed assistants.

It works in the editor with chat, inline completions, and next-edit suggestions that anticipate where you will change code next. Agent features take on larger tasks such as implementing a feature or fixing a bug across files, with the developer reviewing changes. A command line tool and integrations extend it into other workflows, and enterprise options address security and data handling.

item.title: Beamery
item.description:
Beamery treats talent like a relationship, not a one-off hire. Recruiters build pools of potential candidates, track interactions, run campaigns to stay in touch, and see who might fit upcoming roles. The same system can surface current employees for internal moves, which helps companies fill jobs from within.

Its AI builds around skills. It infers skills from resumes and profiles, maps them to a company’s roles, and recommends matches for jobs and development. Workforce planning tools help leaders see skill gaps and plan hiring or training. Integrations connect with applicant tracking systems such as Workday and SuccessFactors.

item.title: Beehiiv
item.description:
Beehiiv is built for people who run newsletters as a business. Writers compose and send posts, manage subscriber lists, and publish a website for the archive. Growth tools include referral programs, recommendations between newsletters, and landing pages, which help build an audience without outside ads.

Monetization is a central feature. Creators can sell paid subscriptions, run ads through the Beehiiv ad network, add sponsors, and offer digital products. Analytics show opens, clicks, and which posts convert readers. An AI assistant helps with drafts, subject lines, and ideas, and automation handles welcome sequences.

item.title: Bloomreach
item.description:
Bloomreach serves online retailers. Its discovery product powers site search, category pages, and recommendations, using machine learning to understand what shoppers mean, rank products, and personalize results. Merchandisers can set rules and see how changes affect sales.

The platform also includes engagement tools. A customer data platform unifies behavior across channels, and marketing automation sends email, SMS, and push messages triggered by actions. Content management supports headless sites. AI assistants help marketers build campaigns and analyze performance.

item.title: Botpress
item.description: Botpress started as an open-source tool for building chatbots with visual flows, and it grew into a platform around large language models. Developers and technical teams build agents that talk with customers on websites and messaging channels, connect to knowledge bases, and call APIs to do things like check an order or update an account. A visual builder and code options sit side by side, so non-engineers can adjust conversations while developers handle integrations.

item.title: Braze
item.description:
Braze helps brands talk to customers on the channels where they spend time. Marketers segment users by behavior, design journeys in a visual canvas, and send messages triggered by actions such as opening an app, abandoning a cart, or reaching a milestone. Real-time data means messages respond to what is happening now.

AI features improve targeting and creation. Predictive models estimate who might churn or buy, optimization chooses the best send time and channel for each person, and generative tools help write subject lines and copy. Analytics measure the effect of campaigns on retention and revenue.

item.title: Brex
item.description:
Brex built a corporate card and spend platform for startups and growing companies. Businesses issue cards to employees with set limits, and expenses are captured and matched automatically, with receipts collected through the app and policies enforced in real time. Finance teams get visibility into spending and can close their books faster than with manual expense reports.

The platform grew into a broader finance system. It includes bill payments, reimbursements, travel booking, banking features, and budgeting, with integrations to accounting software such as NetSuite and QuickBooks. AI agents handle tasks such as filling out expense reports, checking receipts for policy violations, and answering finance questions, aiming to reduce time spent on back-office work.

item.title: Browserbase
item.description:
Browserbase gives software a browser it can control. Running browsers at scale is difficult, with problems like memory use, bot detection, and session management. Browserbase hosts them in the cloud and exposes them through APIs and libraries such as Playwright and Puppeteer, so an agent can open pages, click, fill forms, and extract data.

The platform includes features that agents need: session recording and replay to see what happened, proxies and stealth options to reduce blocking, handling of logins and cookies, and the ability to run many sessions in parallel. An open-source framework, Stagehand, lets developers drive the browser using natural language instructions combined with code.

item.title: Cassidy AI
item.description:
Cassidy lets non-technical teams build AI workflows. A user connects sources such as documents, wikis, and apps, then designs assistants and multi-step workflows in a visual builder: take an input, retrieve company knowledge, draft an output, and send it onward.

Typical uses include drafting proposals and emails in the company’s voice, summarizing meetings, researching accounts, answering internal questions, and processing forms. Different model providers can be used, and permissions control who can see which sources. Teams share assistants so a good workflow becomes a reusable tool.

item.title: Chroma
item.description:
Chroma is a vector database aimed at developer simplicity. It stores embeddings, which are numerical representations of text, images, or other data, along with metadata and the original documents. Applications query it to find items similar in meaning to a given input, which is the core of semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation.

It is easy to start: a few lines of Python or JavaScript create a collection, add documents, and run queries, and it can run in memory inside a program, as a local server, or in a hosted cloud service. It integrates with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and other frameworks, which made it a common choice for prototypes.

item.title: Cleanlab
item.description:
Cleanlab starts from the idea that model quality depends on data quality. Real datasets contain mistakes: images with wrong labels, duplicated examples, and outliers. Cleanlab’s open-source library uses statistical methods and model predictions to find the examples most likely to be wrong, so a team can correct them instead of reviewing everything.

The commercial platform, Cleanlab Studio, extends this with a no-code interface for cleaning and improving datasets and training models on the result. The company has also moved into reliability for generative AI, offering tools to score the trustworthiness of language model outputs and catch hallucinations in production systems.

item.title: ClearML
item.description:
ClearML helps machine learning teams keep their work organized and reproducible. Adding a couple of lines of code to a training script logs parameters, metrics, code versions, and outputs to a central server, so experiments can be compared and repeated. This replaces scattered notebooks and manual notes.

The suite goes beyond tracking. It includes dataset versioning, a task queue that sends jobs to available machines, pipelines that chain steps together, and model serving. For companies with expensive GPUs, resource scheduling shares hardware across teams. ClearML also supports orchestration for large language model workflows.

item.title: CleverTap
item.description:
CleverTap serves brands with mobile apps and large user bases. It collects behavioral data such as app opens, purchases, and feature use, builds segments, and lets marketers send push notifications, email, SMS, WhatsApp, and in-app messages. Journeys can be designed visually so that actions trigger the next message.

AI is used for prediction and optimization. Models estimate which users are likely to churn or convert, choose the best time and channel for each message, and recommend products. A proprietary database designed for large volumes of event data keeps analysis fast, and analytics show retention, funnels, and campaign results.

item.title: Close
item.description:
Close takes the position that sales reps should do their work from one screen. Calls, emails, and texts happen inside the CRM and are logged automatically, so there is less manual data entry and a complete history on each lead. Power dialers let reps work through lists quickly.

Sequences automate multi-step outreach that mixes email, calls, and texts, and workflows keep pipelines moving. AI features transcribe and summarize calls, suggest follow-ups, and score leads, which helps managers coach and helps reps decide where to spend time. Reporting shows activity and results by rep.

item.title: Cloudflare Workers AI
item.description:
Workers AI brings model inference close to users. A developer writes a Cloudflare Worker, calls a model through a binding or REST API, and Cloudflare runs it on GPUs in its data centers around the world. There are no servers to manage, and the platform scales automatically.

The catalog includes open models for chat and text generation, embeddings, image generation, speech recognition, translation, and classification. Developers combine it with other Cloudflare products, such as Vectorize for vector search, D1 for databases, R2 for storage, and AI Gateway for monitoring, to build full applications at the edge.

item.title: Codecademy
item.description:
Codecademy teaches coding by doing. Lessons present a short explanation beside an editor where learners write code and see results right away, which makes it approachable for beginners. Courses cover languages such as Python, JavaScript, and SQL, as well as web development, data analysis, and machine learning.

Career paths and skill paths structure the learning, with projects and quizzes to check progress. An AI assistant helps learners who are stuck by giving hints and explaining errors, while avoiding simply handing over answers. Business plans let companies train teams, and Skillsoft acquired Codecademy to add it to its corporate learning catalog.

item.title: Codemod
item.description:
Codemod targets a chore every large codebase faces: changing the same pattern in hundreds or thousands of places. Codemods are scripts that rewrite code programmatically, for example moving from one version of a framework to the next. The platform provides a registry of community codemods, tools to run them, and a way to write new ones.

AI makes creating codemods easier. A developer describes a migration, and the tool helps produce the transformation and test it on examples, then applies it across repositories and opens pull requests for review. This turns weeks of manual edits into a reviewable change.

item.title: Comet ML
item.description:
Comet helps machine learning teams track and compare their work. A few lines of code log metrics, parameters, code, and datasets from training runs to a dashboard, where experiments can be compared and reproduced. A model registry stores approved versions and their lineage.

Production monitoring watches deployed models for drift and performance changes. For generative AI, Comet created Opik, an open-source tool for tracing and evaluating language model applications, which brings it into the same space as other LLM observability products.

item.title: Constructor
item.description:
Constructor serves online retailers that want search and discovery to drive revenue. Its engine powers site search, category pages, and recommendations, ranking products using both shopper behavior and business goals such as margin or inventory. Merchandisers can steer results with rules while the system learns from clicks and purchases.

Additional tools include product quizzes that guide shoppers to the right item, personalization that adapts to each visitor, and analytics that show how discovery affects sales. Generative AI features allow conversational shopping assistants that answer questions and suggest products.

item.title: ContractPodAi
item.description:
ContractPodAi was built for corporate legal departments that handle large volumes of contracts. Its platform covers the lifecycle: drafting from templates, routing for approval, negotiation, signature, storage in a searchable repository, and tracking of obligations and renewals. It connects with systems such as Salesforce, Microsoft 365, and ERP tools so contracts sit within the business processes they relate to.

The company has rebranded as Leah, after the name of its AI product, and now describes itself as an agentic AI platform. Its AI agents review contracts against playbooks, flag risks and deviations, extract key terms, answer questions about a contract portfolio, and handle repetitive tasks across legal, procurement, and finance. The change reflects a wider move in legal technology from software that stores documents to software that does the first pass of the work.

item.title: ContractSafe
item.description:
ContractSafe addresses a basic business problem: contracts scattered across inboxes, shared drives, and filing cabinets. Teams upload agreements into one searchable repository, and the system reads them to pull out key details such as parties, effective dates, renewal terms, and notice periods. Because the text is searchable, finding a specific clause across hundreds of contracts takes seconds instead of hours.

Automation helps avoid missed deadlines. ContractSafe can send alerts before a contract renews or expires, so teams can renegotiate or cancel in time instead of being locked into automatic renewals. Permissions control who can see sensitive agreements, and reports summarize the portfolio by type, value, and upcoming dates. Integrations connect with tools such as Salesforce and Microsoft or Google storage, and an audit trail records activity.

item.title: Convai
item.description:
Convai makes game characters that respond to what players say. A developer defines a character’s personality, backstory, and knowledge, and Convai handles listening to speech, generating replies with a language model, speaking them with a synthetic voice, and driving lip sync and gestures. Plugins integrate with Unity, Unreal Engine, and other platforms.

Characters can also take actions in the game world, such as navigating or interacting with objects, based on conversation. Use cases include immersive games, training simulations, virtual tours, and educational experiences where open-ended dialogue adds value over scripted lines.

item.title: Copper
item.description:
Copper integrates with the tools its users already work in. Because it lives inside Gmail and connects with Google Calendar, Drive, and Docs, contacts and conversations are logged automatically, so reps do not have to copy information into a separate system.

The CRM covers the usual sales functions: contacts, companies, deals, pipelines, tasks, and reporting. Project management features track work after a deal closes, which suits agencies and service firms. AI features help summarize communication and suggest follow-ups, and workflow automation moves deals through stages.

item.title: Copysmith
item.description:
Copysmith targets online retailers that need lots of product copy. A merchant can generate descriptions for many products from a spreadsheet or catalog, create ad headlines and text, and draft emails and social posts. Bulk generation saves time when a store has hundreds of items.

Integrations connect it to Shopify and Google Ads, so content can flow into the tools where it is used. Team features allow collaboration and approval, and brand settings keep tone consistent. Some tools support SEO optimization by suggesting keywords.

item.title: Cosine
item.description:
Cosine aims to act like a teammate on a codebase. It indexes the repository, then takes tasks such as fixing a bug or adding a feature, planning the work, editing multiple files, and running tests. It explains its reasoning along the way so a developer can follow and step in.

The company trains its own models, called Genie, specialized for software engineering using data on how developers work. Tools include a command line interface, an editor extension, and a web app, and it integrates with GitHub for pull requests. It also offers deployments for organizations with security needs.

item.title: Coupa
item.description:
Coupa gives companies control over what they spend. Employees request purchases through approved channels, procurement manages suppliers and contracts, and accounts payable processes invoices and payments. Having it in one system improves visibility and helps enforce policy.

The company’s distinctive asset is aggregated data. With permission, Coupa analyzes anonymized spend across its customer base to benchmark prices, identify supplier risk, and recommend savings. AI features help with spend classification, contract review, and answering questions about spending, and supplier networks connect buyers with vendors.

item.title: CSM AI
item.description:
CSM turns simple inputs into 3D assets. A user uploads a picture, types a description, or draws a sketch, and the system produces a 3D model with textures that can be exported to common formats. It supports game developers, designers, and creators who need assets quickly.

Beyond single objects, it offers tools for character creation and animation preparation, and an API lets developers build 3D generation into their own apps. The output is often a starting point that artists clean up, since generated meshes can have topology problems that matter for animation and games.

item.title: Darktrace
item.description: Darktrace takes a different approach from signature-based security.
